title: isVectorSearchSupported async — calling without await makes guards dead code
content:
Production bug pattern (fixed 2026-07-09, branch `user-memory-v2`, `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py`):

`BaseSQLProvider.isVectorSearchSupported()` (and other provider methods like `getProvider`) are `async def`. Calling them WITHOUT `await` in a guard, e.g. `if not sqlProvider.isVectorSearchSupported():`, evaluates a coroutine object's truthiness. A coroutine is ALWAYS truthy, so `not <coroutine>` is ALWAYS `False` — the guard branch becomes unreachable dead code. It also emits `RuntimeWarning: coroutine '...isVectorSearchSupported' was never awaited`.

This bit `_upsertVecMemoryEmbedding` (the vector-support guard silently never short-circuited). Every OTHER call site in the same file correctly uses `await sqlProvider.isVectorSearchSupported()`. Fix was simply adding `await`.

GENERAL RULE: any provider method accessed as `sqlProvider.<asyncMethod>()` must be awaited. When writing or reviewing a guard around `isVectorSearchSupported()` / `getProvider()` / similar, check for `await`. The test-mocking variant of this gotcha (MagicMock returns a plain bool that can't be awaited → `TypeError: 'bool' object can't be awaited`) is the mirror image and was recorded separately.

Also fixed in the same pass: `_upsertVecMemoryEmbedding`'s docstring had drifted — it claimed `Returns: None` and `Raises: Re-raised after logging`, but the actual signature is `-> bool` and the code catches exceptions and `return False` (never re-raises). `saveMemoryEmbedding` checks BOTH the bool return (`if not await self._upsertVecMemoryEmbedding(...): return False`) and wraps in try/except, so it tolerates either failure mode.

title: deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings ↔ getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings column-reset contract (model-drift linchpin)
content:
Data-flow / architecture contract for the memory-embedding regen cron in `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py`.

The regen cron's stale-detection is PROVENANCE-COLUMN based, not vec0-row based. `getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings(chatId, modelName, dimensions, limit)` surfaces rows where `embedding_model IS NULL OR embedding_model != :modelName OR embedding_dimensions IS NULL OR embedding_dimensions != :dimensions`. Therefore, for the regen loop to pick up stale rows, the `embedding_model`/`embedding_dimensions` columns on `user_memories` MUST be NULLed out — the mere absence of a vec0 row is NOT enough.

`deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings(chatId, currentModel, currentDimensions) -> int` is the MODEL-DRIFT cleanup step that runs FIRST in the regen sequence. It MUST do BOTH:
  (a) delete the stale vec0 rows from `vec_user_memories_{N}` tables, AND
  (b) `UPDATE user_memories SET embedding_model=NULL, embedding_dimensions=NULL WHERE <stale predicate>`.

If (b) is skipped (this was the refactoring bug), `getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings` never re-surfaces the stale rows → the regen cron's stale-detection loop is SILENTLY BROKEN (rows stay with old-model provenance forever, never re-embedded). This is the model-drift complement to the content-drift path: `updateMemory` nulling those columns on content edits (recorded in the "content edits invalidate embeddings" memory) is the SAME invariant.

Stale predicate (shared by the COUNT and the UPDATE so they stay in lockstep):
`chat_id = :chatId AND embedding_model IS NOT NULL AND (embedding_model != :currentModel OR embedding_dimensions != :currentDimensions)`
— guarded by `embedding_model IS NOT NULL` so never-embedded rows (already NULL) aren't touched (they're surfaced by getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings already).

CONVENTION: when `currentDimensions` is Optional (dim-less embedding models), branch explicitly on `currentDimensions is None` to build the WHERE string rather than relying on SQL three-valued `col != :dim` (where `:dim=None` → NULL → falsy). This mirrors the `chat_embeddings.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings` precedent and avoids subtle NULL-comparison bugs across SQLite/PostgreSQL/MySQL. The COUNT and UPDATE share ONE predicate string.

Implementation note: COUNT uses `SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt` → `row["cnt"]` (int cast), same shape as `bayes_storage.py`'s `as vocab_size`.

title: Test mocking gotcha: mock generateEmbedding/resolveModel directly, not getLLMManager, after 85aa945 refactoring
content:
After the memories-feature refactoring (commit 85aa945), testing code that resolves embedding models has a non-obvious trap.

**The problem:** The old test helper pattern was `_stubEmbeddingModel(handler, model)` which set `handler.llmService.getLLMManager = Mock(return_value=Mock(getModel=Mock(return_value=mockModel)))`. This worked when production code called `self.llmService.getLLMManager().getModel(name)` directly. But the refactored code now calls `self.llmService.resolveModel(ChatSettingsKey.EMBEDDING_MODEL, chatSettings=..., defaultKey=...)` (internal/services/llm/service.py:1151), which internally calls `chatSettings[key].toModel()` (service.py:1177-1180), which calls the MODULE-LEVEL `getLLMManager()` function in `internal/bot/models/chat_settings.py` (line 22). That module-level function has its own `_llmManager` cache (line 19, set once at line 38, never reset by conftest's `LLMService._instance = None` fixture). So an instance-level mock on `handler.llmService.getLLMManager` is invisible to the `toModel()` path.

**The fix:** Mock `handler.llmService.generateEmbedding` and/or `handler.llmService.resolveModel` directly at the `handler.llmService` attribute level. Example:

```python
def _stubGenerateEmbedding(handler, *, result=None):
    mock = AsyncMock(return_value=result)
    handler.llmService.generateEmbedding = mock  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    return mock
```

Pass `result=("test-embed-model", [0.1, 0.2, 0.3])` for a successful embedding (returns `Tuple[modelName, floats]`), or `result=None` for the model-not-found / embedding-disabled case.

This pattern is verified in use in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search.py` (TestEmbedAndSaveMessage and the TestDtCronJob embed-loop tests at lines 998, 1014, 1038, 1286, 1347 mock `handler.llmService.generateEmbedding` directly).

NOTE: `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py` is the current handler file (renamed from `user_data.py`). The old `embedAndSaveMemory` free function and its module `internal/bot/common/memory_embedding_utils.py` were DELETED in commit 85aa945 — do not attempt `patch("internal.bot.common.handlers.user_data.embedAndSaveMemory", ...)` or `patch("...memory_embedding_utils.embedAndSaveMemory", ...)`; both raise AttributeError at runtime.

title: deleteMemory repo method cascades to deleteMemoryEmbedding internally (embedding cleanup is repo-level)
content:
Architecture detail (verified 2026-07-14): The `UserMemoriesRepository.deleteMemory` method (`internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py:239`) internally cascades to embedding cleanup — it calls `await self.deleteMemoryEmbedding(chatId, userId, memoryId, vecOnly=False)` at line 327.

The `vecOnly=False` is load-bearing: it means BOTH the vec0 row is deleted AND the provenance columns (`embedding_model`/`embedding_dimensions`) are nulled. This is required because `deleteMemory` is a SOFT-delete (sets `deleted_at`); without nulling provenance, `getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings` would re-surface the soft-deleted row for re-embedding. (See memory 7649c2fc for the deleted_at filter asymmetry this relies on.)

**Consequence for handlers and tests:** The handler `_llmToolDeleteMemory` by-id path only calls `db.userMemories.deleteMemory(chatId, userId, memory_id)` — it does NOT separately call `deleteMemoryEmbedding`. The embedding cleanup is owned by the repo method, not the handler.

**Test gotcha:** In tests that mock the repo (e.g. replacing `handler.db.userMemories` with a bare `Mock`), `deleteMemory` becomes an `AsyncMock` that does NOT cascade. So asserting `mockRepo.deleteMemoryEmbedding.assert_awaited_once()` at the handler level is WRONG — the cascade lives inside the real (mocked-away) repo method. The correct handler-level assertion is `mockRepo.deleteMemory.assert_awaited_once_with(chatId, userId, memoryId)`. The cascade itself is covered at the repo level in `tests/database/repositories/test_user_memories.py`.

title: _runRefinement template: {existingUserData}/{existingSummary} placeholders intentionally removed
content:
The memories refactoring intentionally removed the `{existingUserData}` and `{existingSummary}` placeholders from the memory-refinement template (`MEMORY_REFINE_USER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE`) format call. Only `{existingMemories}` and `{messages}` are now passed to `userPromptTemplate.format(...)` in `UserMemoriesHandler._runSingleRefinement` at `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py:1282-1285`.

**Operational gotcha:** A deployed per-chat override of `MEMORY_REFINE_USER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE` that still references the old `{existingUserData}` or `{existingSummary}` placeholders will raise `KeyError` inside `_runSingleRefinement`. This is caught by the method's outer `try/except`, so it fails silently — refinement simply stops for that user with no crash. Operators upgrading past this refactoring should audit any custom template overrides and migrate them to use `{existingMemories}`.

The backward-compat aliases were deliberately NOT restored (the inline comment at lines 1277-1280 documents this).

title: Tags filter in searchMemories now SQL LIKE (supersedes Python set-intersection post-filter)
content:
CORRECTION to memory 0713dca6 (2026-07-07), which documented `searchMemories` tags filtering as a **Python set-intersection post-filter running AFTER SQL `LIMIT ... OFFSET ...`** (`results = [r for r in results if requestedTags & set(r.get("tags") or [])]`), and the resulting pagination-interaction bug.

As of the memories refactoring (commit 85aa945, 2026-07-09), the tags filter was changed BACK to **SQL `LIKE`** in `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py`:
- `_filterOnlySearchMemories` (~lines 716-725) builds `tags LIKE :tagsN` clauses.
- `_semanticSearchMemories` (~lines 907-917) also uses `tags LIKE`.

Tags are now stored via provider auto-serialization (list → JSON TEXT). The matching is SQL `LIKE` (`%tag%`-style), not exact Python set-intersection.

**Impact on the pagination gotcha (0713dca6):** Because `LIKE` runs in the SQL `WHERE` clause (before `LIMIT/OFFSET`), the offset-interaction bug that 0713dca6 documented should now be RESOLVED at the repository level. However, 0713dca6's wizard-level workaround in `_renderMemoryList` (fetch a generous batch at offset 0, paginate in Python when a tag filter is active) was deliberately left in place. That workaround is now likely unnecessary/harmless and should be audited — the next person touching the wizard should verify whether the Python-side pagination can be dropped now that tags filtering is SQL-level.

**Tags serialization caveat:** memory f30a9bc2 flagged "tags serialization likely broken" because `addMemory` passes a raw list to a TEXT column. The refactoring relies on provider auto-serialization to convert the list to JSON TEXT. Verify this actually works end-to-end if debugging tag search.

title: searchMemories API: callers pass List[float] not bytes; embeddingModel selects vec0 table (serialisation is internal)
content:
The `UserMemoriesRepository` search API contract (internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py), finalised during the user-memories refactoring (2026-07-09):

**`searchMemories(chatId, userId, queryEmbedding: Optional[List[float]]=None, *, ..., embeddingModel: Optional[str], ...)`** — the public entry point. Two modes, selected by:
- Filter-only mode: `queryEmbedding is None OR embeddingModel is None` → plain SQL scan of `user_memories` with optional threadId/type/tags/permanent filters.
- Semantic mode: both `queryEmbedding` (a non-empty `List[float]`) AND `embeddingModel` set → native vec0 search over `vec_user_memories_{dim}`, JOIN back to `user_memories` by `memory_id`; `score = 1.0 - distance`.

**`_semanticSearchMemories(..., queryEmbedding: List[float], *, ..., embeddingModel: str, ...)`** — the internal semantic implementation. Takes `List[float]` directly.

**KEY DESIGN DECISION (diverges from chat_search.py precedent):** Callers pass `List[float]`, NOT pre-serialised float32 bytes. The float32 BLOB serialisation (`array.array("f", floats).tobytes()`) happens INSIDE the repo (`_semanticSearchMemories` / `_upsertVecMemoryEmbedding`), not at call sites. This is the opposite of the chat_history/embeddings path where `array.array("f", vec).tobytes()` is done by callers/repositories explicitly. The `embeddingModel` name selects which model-partitioned vec0 table to search (vec0 is partitioned by dimension `vec_user_memories_{dim}`); there is NO `dimensions` parameter — the dimension is derived from the embedding list length / tracked via `embedding_model`/`embedding_dimensions` provenance columns on the `user_memories` row itself.

NOTE: An earlier version of this API took `queryEmbedding: bytes` (pre-serialised) plus a `dimensions` int param; that was refactored away. Docstrings referencing `bytes`/`dimensions` were stale and fixed in this session. The `getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings`/`deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings` methods at the bottom of the file legitimately have a real `dimensions`/`currentDimensions` parameter (model-drift regeneration) — those are NOT stale.

title: make lint pipeline: flake8 → isort → import-main check → pyright (all Python-only, no markdown linter)
content:
`make lint` runs FOUR commands in the Makefile `lint` target (order matters):

1. `flake8 .` — Python parser; only processes `.py`/`.pyi`.
2. `isort --check-only --diff .` — sorts imports in Python files only.
3. **`import main` circular-import check** (added 2026-07-09 after the `85aa945` refactor introduced a startup-breaking cycle `database/models.py` → `internal.bot.models` → `ensured_message` → `internal.database` that flake8/isort/pyright couldn't detect, since none execute imports). Implemented as:
   ```makefile
   @echo "Checking for circular imports..."
   $(PYTHON) -c "import main" || (echo "FAIL: circular import detected (or main.py cannot be imported)" && exit 1)
   ```
   `main.py` has an `if __name__ == "____main__":` guard so `import main` exercises only the import graph, not the bot runtime. On failure, Python's traceback (which pinpoints the cycle) prints first, then the friendly FAIL message.
4. `pyright` — `typeCheckingMode=basic`, excludes `ext/`, scopes to `.py`/`.ts`/`.js`.

ALL FOUR are Python-only. There is **NO markdown linter** wired anywhere in the Makefile or CI. The `check` target adds `black --check` — also Python-only.

**Convention for Makefile edits:** use the `$(PYTHON)` variable (= `./venv/bin/python`) for internal consistency within the Makefile, even though AGENTS.md's hard rule says to invoke `./venv/bin/python3` at the shell. The Makefile already defines and uses `$(PYTHON)` for all Python invocations; matching that is preferred over the literal `./venv/bin/python3`. Makefiles REQUIRE tabs (not spaces) for recipe indentation.

**Practical implication:** doc-only changes (`.md` files) are not touched by `make lint`. But note: AGENTS.md IS edited by Task 2 above, and `make lint` will still run clean on it (it's ignored).

title: GOTCHA: _runMemoryEmbeddingRegen is NOT exception-safe — resolveModel/toModel raises ValueError (caught by _dtCronJob caller)
content:
In `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py`, the method `_runMemoryEmbeddingRegen` (line 754) has a non-obvious exception contract.

**The chain:** The method calls `self.llmService.resolveModel(ChatSettingsKey.EMBEDDING_MODEL, chatSettings=..., defaultKey=...)` (line 850-852) which is UNGUARDED (not wrapped in try/except inside the method). `resolveModel` calls `chatSettings[modelKey].toModel()`, which raises `ValueError` when the configured `EMBEDDING_MODEL` is empty or not registered in the model manager. This `ValueError` propagates out of `_runMemoryEmbeddingRegen`.

**Why production is safe:** The caller — `_dtCronJob` (line 1008-1015) — wraps the `_runMemoryEmbeddingRegen()` call in `try/except Exception: logger.exception(...)`, so the exception is caught and the refinement pass on the same tick is unaffected (it runs in a separate try/except at 1017-1024).

**Method docstring (now accurate):** The docstring (lines 797-819) documents this as the intentional one unguarded path — `ValueError` propagates to the `_dtCronJob` caller. This is no longer a doc-vs-code discrepancy.

**No supportsEmbedding check:** The code does NOT check `model.supportsEmbedding` before proceeding — this is the current design. Embedding-capability failures are handled inside `LLMService.generateEmbedding`'s internal try/except (returns None), and the re-embed loop's `if memoryEmbedding is not None:` guard skips that memory.

**Testing implication:** When writing tests that call `_runMemoryEmbeddingRegen` directly (not via `_dtCronJob`), ensure `EMBEDDING_MODEL` is registered in the mock model manager, or the method will raise `ValueError` (use `pytest.raises(ValueError)` and assert cleanup/fetch were not reached).

title: dataSource convention: reads only for chat-scoped repos, writes route by chatId
content:
Convention for adding the `dataSource` parameter to repository methods in `internal/database/repositories/*.py`. Discovered 2026-07-09 while mapping the pattern for `UserMemoriesRepository`.

## Core rule: read/write asymmetry for chat-scoped repos

Chat-scoped repositories (tables with `chat_id`, e.g. `chat_messages`, `user_data`, and by extension `user_memories`) follow a deliberate convention:

- **READ methods** get `*, dataSource: Optional[str] = None` added, and call `getProvider(chatId=chatId, dataSource=dataSource, readonly=True)`. This allows reads to cross into archive/explicit sources.
- **WRITE methods** do NOT take `dataSource`. They route purely by `chatId` via `getProvider(chatId=chatId, readonly=False)`. Writes must land where the chat is mapped (`chatMapping`). 

The canonical docstring note on write methods (verbatim, from `user_data.py:96,177,217` and `chat_messages.py:104`):
> "Writes are routed based on chatId mapping. Cannot write to readonly sources."

**Evidence:** `chat_messages.py` — `saveChatMessage`, `updateChatMessageCategory`, `updateChatMessageMetadata` (writes) have no `dataSource`; all 6 read methods have it. `user_data.py` — `addUserData`, `deleteUserData`, `clearUserData` (writes) have no `dataSource`; `getUserData` (read) has it.

## Exception: non-chat-scoped repos DO take dataSource on writes

Repositories whose tables have no `chat_id` concept (`cache.py`, `webhook_updates.py`, `common.py`, `delayed_tasks.py`) use `dataSource` directly on BOTH reads and writes, with NO `chatId`: `getProvider(dataSource=dataSource, readonly=False)`. There's no chat to route by, so the named source is the only routing key.

## Three getProvider call shapes (internal/database/manager.py:103-109)

```python
async def getProvider(self, *, chatId: Optional[int] = None,
                      dataSource: Optional[str] = None, readonly: bool = False)
```

- **(A) chatId only** — chat-scoped reads/writes without dataSource: `getProvider(chatId=chatId, readonly=True/False)`
- **(B) chatId + dataSource** — chat-scoped reads with explicit source: `getProvider(chatId=chatId, dataSource=dataSource, readonly=True)`. dataSource takes priority over chatId mapping (manager.py:130).
- **(C) dataSource only** — non-chat-scoped repos: `getProvider(dataSource=dataSource, readonly=True/False)`, no chatId at all.

## Cross-provider aggregation sub-pattern (chat_users.py, chat_settings.py)

For methods that must union results across ALL databases (e.g. `getUserChats`, `getAllGroupChats`, `listChatsBySetting`), when `dataSource=None` the method loops over every provider:
```python
sourcesList = [dataSource] if dataSource else list(self.manager._providers.keys())
for sourceName in sourcesList:
    sqlProvider = await self.manager.getProvider(dataSource=sourceName, readonly=True)
    ...
```
NOTE (bug, see memory d784610f): `_providers.keys()` only covers lazily-initialized providers, not all configured sources. Used for aggregation queries, not single-chat lookups.

## dataSource routing priority in getProvider (3-tier)

1. Explicit `dataSource` param (highest)
2. `chatMapping[chatId]` lookup
3. `default` source (fallback)

title: dataSource type is Optional[str] deliberately (no StrEnum) — operator-configured provider keys
content:
Decision/convention about the `dataSource` parameter type in the Gromozeka multi-source DB architecture. Discovered 2026-07-09.

## The type: `Optional[str]`, uniformly

Everywhere — `DatabaseManager.getProvider()` (`internal/database/manager.py:107`), every repository method signature, every docstring — `dataSource` is typed `Optional[str]`, default `None`.

**There is deliberately NO enum** (no `StrEnum`, no `Literal[...]`). This is notable because the project's documented convention otherwise mandates `StrEnum` over `Literal[...]` for string-valued params. The `dataSource` value is a free-form string key.

## Why: values are operator-chosen config keys, not a fixed set

`dataSource` values are arbitrary strings matching keys under `[database.providers]` in TOML config. Examples seen in the wild: `"primary"`, `"archive"`, `"default"`, `"source1"`, `"source2"`, `"readonly_source"`, `"llm-stats-data-source"`, `"ds"`, `"other_bot"`. These are defined by operators in config, so a fixed enum would be wrong.

## Validation behavior

`getProvider` does NOT raise on an unknown source name. It logs a warning and silently falls back to the default provider (manager.py:131-135). `None` means "no explicit override → fall through to chatId mapping → default".

## How callers resolve dataSource (orchestration layer only)

`dataSource` is determined at the orchestration/config layer, NEVER inside a repo and NEVER from a `getChatSettings()` lookup. Examples:
- **Resender jobs** (`internal/bot/common/handlers/resender.py:119`): `dataSource` is a field on `ResenderJob`, set when the job is configured, threaded into every read.
- **LLM stats** (`main.py:84-87`): `statsConfig.get("llm-stats-data-source", self.database.manager.default)`.
- **Max webhook receiver** (`internal/max_webhook_receiver/app.py`): from receiver process config.

So when adding `dataSource` support to a repo method, you only need to accept and forward the param — the caller is responsible for sourcing the value.

title: dataSource read/write asymmetry convention for chat-scoped repositories
content:
Established pattern for adding `dataSource` multi-source DB support to chat-scoped repositories. Currently followed by `chat_messages.py` (reference), `user_data.py`, and `user_memories.py`.

## Read methods: add `dataSource`, pass to getProvider

- Signature: `dataSource: Optional[str] = None` as keyword-only param (last kwarg, after `*` or existing kwargs).
- `getProvider` call: `await self.manager.getProvider(chatId=chatId, dataSource=dataSource, readonly=True)`
- Docstring: add `dataSource` to `Args:` section describing it as an optional provider key override.

## Write methods: NO `dataSource`, add Note to docstring

- Write methods do NOT accept `dataSource`. They call `await self.manager.getProvider(chatId=chatId, readonly=False)`.
- Docstring gets a `Note:` section: `"Writes are routed based on chatId mapping. Cannot write to readonly sources."`
- This matches the fact that write routing is determined by chatId-to-provider mapping, not by caller choice — you cannot write to an arbitrary source.

## Exception: private helpers receiving sqlProvider as a param

Some private helpers (e.g. `_upsertVecMemoryEmbedding`) receive `sqlProvider` as a parameter rather than calling `getProvider` themselves. These do NOT get `dataSource` — the calling write method already obtained the provider. Verify the chain when adding `dataSource` to a public method that delegates to such helpers.

## Forwarding through intermediate methods

When a public read method delegates to private helpers that also call `getProvider` (e.g. `searchMemories` → `_filterOnlySearchMemories` + `_semanticSearchMemories`), `dataSource` must be forwarded through ALL methods in the call chain, not just the top-level one.

## When adding to a new repo

Use `chat_messages.py` as the reference implementation. The `dataSource` param is always keyword-only, always `Optional[str] = None`, always last in the kwargs list.

title: internal/bot/constants.py — canonical home for bot-layer constants (handlers + models)
content:
As of 2026-07-09 (with 2026-07-11 updates), `internal/bot/constants.py` is the single canonical home for module-level `UPPER_CASE` constants previously defined inline in bot handler/model files. This mirrors the DB-layer `internal/database/constants.py`.

## What was centralized
- From `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py` (NOTE: file was renamed from `user_data.py` on 2026-07-11): memory refinement thresholds (`MEMORY_COUNT_THRESHOLD`, `MEMORY_TIME_THRESHOLD_SECONDS`, `MEMORY_MIN_MESSAGES_TO_REFINE`, `MEMORY_MAX_MESSAGES_PER_RUN`, `MEMORY_MAX_REFINES_PER_TICK`), dedup thresholds (`MEMORY_DEDUP_DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD`, `MEMORY_DEDUP_SIMILAR_THRESHOLD`), search limits (`MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT`, `MEMORY_SEARCH_MAX_LIMIT`), embedding regen (`MEMORY_BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`, `MEMORY_BACKFILL_INTER_MESSAGE_DELAY_SECS`), wizard (`KNOWLEDGE_CONFIG_PAGE_SIZE`, `KNOWLEDGE_CONFIG_TAG_FILTER_FETCH_LIMIT`).
- From `chat_search.py` (5): `SEARCH_DEFAULT_MAX_RESULTS`, `SEARCH_DEFAULT_DAYS`, `BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`, `SEARCH_TOOL_MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH`, `BACKFILL_INTER_MESSAGE_DELAY_SECS`.
- From `sandbox.py` (2): `MAX_SANDBOX_READ_FILE_BYTES` (64KB), `MAX_SANDBOX_SEND_BYTES` (20MB).

## REMOVED on 2026-07-11 (ChatSettingsKey consolidation refactor)
The constants `MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_MODE_LATEST` ("latest") and `MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_MODE_RELEVANT` ("relevant") were REMOVED from this file AND from the re-export in `internal/bot/models/__init__.py`. Semantic ("relevant") retrieval is now IMPLIED by the derived condition `MEMORY_ENABLED && EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED`; otherwise memory injection uses "latest". The `MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_MODE` ChatSettingsKey enum member was also removed. Do NOT re-add these constants — the consolidation was deliberate.

Constants are organized with section-comment headers + per-constant docstrings (matching the file's style). `internal/bot/models/__init__.py` no longer re-exports the removed retrieval-mode constants; the canonical consumer path is `from internal.bot.constants import ...`.

title: internal/database/constants.py — DB-layer tuning constants (layering rule)
content:
`internal/database/constants.py` exists (created 2026-07-09) to centralize DB-layer tuning constants, superseding inline definitions in `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py`. This is the DB-layer mirror of the bot-layer `internal/bot/constants.py`.

## Contents (5 constants)
- `PERMANENT_INJECTION_CAP: int = 10` — max permanent memories per (chatId, userId) per turn
- `EPHEMERAL_RETRIEVAL_LIMIT: int = 5` — default cap on ephemeral (non-permanent) memories per turn
- `MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT: int = 20` — default result cap for `searchMemories`
- `MEMORY_SEARCH_TOPK_MULTIPLIER: int = 3` — vec0 `k = limit * this` to absorb post-filter trimming
- `BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE: int = 50` — default per-tick batch size for embedding-regen cron

All are typed `int` with per-constant docstrings. The module has ZERO imports (no dependencies).

## Critical layering rule
`internal/database/constants.py` must NOT import from `internal.bot.*`. The DB layer sits BELOW the bot layer; an upward import risks circular imports. This is why the module has no imports. Some constant NAMES (e.g. `MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT`, `BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`) appear in BOTH `internal/database/constants.py` AND `internal/bot/constants.py` — this is INTENTIONAL cross-layer duplication, each layer keeps its own copy. Do NOT merge them.

## What was NOT moved here
- `DEFAULT_THREAD_ID` stays in `internal/database/utils.py` — heavily cross-file, well-established location.
- `*_LIKE_TYPES` converter tuples stay in `utils.py` — internal converter machinery.
- Bot-layer constants live in `internal/bot/constants.py` (centralized separately on 2026-07-09; see that memory), NOT here, per the layering rule.

title: Mirror constants drift risk: MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT & BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE duplicated across bot/db layers with no parity guard
content:
GOTCHA discovered in code review (2026-07-09, branch `user-memory-v2`, reviewer verdict: mergeable with this 🔵 finding).

After the constants-centralization refactor (constants extracted from handler/model files into `internal/bot/constants.py` and `internal/database/constants.py`), two constants are deliberately **mirrored** (defined identically) in BOTH layer-specific constants files:

- `MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20` — `internal/bot/constants.py:184` AND `internal/database/constants.py:15`
- `BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE = 50` — `internal/bot/constants.py:243` AND `internal/database/constants.py:22`

The duplication is **intentional** (layer separation: bot-layer shouldn't depend on db-layer constants and vice versa), and the docstrings cross-reference each other ("Mirrors …"). But parity is enforced **only by human discipline** — there is NO test asserting the two layer-specific copies stay equal.

## Why it matters
The bot-layer value and the db-layer value are meant to track, but if someone changes one without the other, the drift is silent. The existing test at `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_data_memory_regen.py:647` asserts `MEMORY_BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE == 50` (absolute value) but never asserts it equals its db-layer sibling. So a divergence would not be caught.

## Suggested fix (lighter touch)
Add a parity test, e.g.:
```python
assert bot_constants.BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE == db_constants.BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE
assert bot_constants.MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT == db_constants.MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT
```
The alternative — consolidating to a single definition by letting `internal.bot` import `internal.database` — is heavier and may be undesirable for layering. The deliberate mirror pattern is defensible; a guard test closes the drift gap without coupling layers.

## Related
This mirrors the general "stale-after-move" hazard (memory 9ee8199d, test-file-move docstrings) applied to the constants-centralization refactor: two cross-referencing copies of a value are a maintenance liability unless mechanically pinned.

title: Wizard free-text input pattern restored + manual memory creation (memory_config)
content:
The `/memory_config` wizard has a manual memory-creation feature that RESTORED the free-text input path (the `UserActiveActionEnum.UserDataConfig` state).

## Reusable pattern: adding a free-text input step to the wizard
To add a free-text input step (e.g. 'type the memory content'):

1. **Handler sets user state** via `self.cache.setUserState(userId=user.id, stateKey=UserActiveActionEnum.UserDataConfig, value={"data": {...payload...}, "messageId": messageId, "messageChatId": messageChatId})` (in `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py`, class `UserMemoriesHandler` — renamed from UserDataHandler in commit 85aa945).
2. **`newMessageHandler` checks state** AFTER the memory-refinement accounting block (~line 1567-1580), BEFORE `return HandlerResultStatus.NEXT` (~line 1601): `getUserState(userId=..., stateKey=UserActiveActionEnum.UserDataConfig)` (~line 1589). If present, it injects the message text as `ButtonDataKey.Value` (~line 1594) and routes through `_handleUserDataConfiguration` (the dispatcher, ~line 2714), returning `HandlerResultStatus.FINAL` (~line 1599).
3. **Dispatcher clears state at the TOP** (`self.cache.clearUserState(...)`, ~line 2732) BEFORE dispatching to the action handler.

Safe for all messages: `getUserState` returns `None` for users without active wizard state, so non-wizard messages fall through to `NEXT` unchanged.

## Manual memory creation specifics
Enum members in `internal/bot/models/enums.py`: `ButtonUserDataConfigAction.AddMemory = "am"` (line 204), `SetMemoryContent = "sm"` (line 205). Action handlers: `_handleConfigAction_AddMemory` (~line 2470) sets the state for free-text entry; `_handleConfigAction_SetMemoryContent` (~line 2562) consumes the typed text and persists the memory.

Note: the old key-value wizard step handlers (`_handleConfigAction_ClearChatData`, `_handleConfigAction_DeleteKey`, `_handleConfigAction_KeySelected`, `_handleConfigAction_SetValue`) were removed in the refactor and replaced by memory-list/pagination/tagging methods.

title: Command renamed /knowledge_config → /memory_config (constants intentionally kept)
content:
As of 2026-07-09, the bot command was renamed from `/knowledge_config` to `/memory_config`. Method `knowledge_config_command` → `memory_config_command`. No backward-compat alias kept (clean rename).

All references updated across: source (`user_data.py`, `enums.py` docstrings, `constants.py` docstrings, `user_memories.py` repo docstrings), tests (`test_user_data.py`, `test_user_memories.py`), and docs (`docs/llm/handlers.md`, `docs/llm/memories/user-memories.md`, `docs/plans/user-memories-v1.md`).

## Intentionally NOT renamed: KNOWLEDGE_CONFIG_* constants

These are internal identifiers, not user-facing command names — renaming them is out of scope for the command rename. Their docstrings already say `/memory_config`. If a cleanup pass renames these later, search both the constant definitions and all references.

## Test command-metadata inspection pattern

```python
info = getattr(UserDataHandler.memory_config_command, "_commandHandlerInfoV2")
assert "memory_config" in info.commands
```
The `_commandHandlerInfoV2` attribute is attached by the `@commandHandlerV2` decorator (see `internal/bot/models/command_handlers.py`). `info.commands` is the `Sequence[str]` of command strings.

title: Cross-chat message capture: wizard state is userId-scoped, consumes messages from all chats
content:
Identified in the 2026-07-09 Gate 1 review of the memory_config wizard free-text creation flow.

The wizard's active-state (`UserActiveActionEnum.UserDataConfig`) is keyed by `userId` ONLY — not `(userId, chatId)`. Consequence: while a user has the AddMemory prompt open in a PRIVATE chat, `UserMemoriesHandler.newMessageHandler` consumes (`HandlerResultStatus.FINAL`) EVERY message they send in ANY chat — including groups. The message text becomes a memory scoped to the private chat where the wizard was opened (the `chatId` comes from the stored state, not the incoming message), and the message NEVER reaches the LLM in the group.

Verified in `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py` (renamed from user_data.py; class renamed UserDataHandler → UserMemoriesHandler in commit 85aa945):
- Read: `self.cache.getUserState(userId=ensuredMessage.sender.id, stateKey=UserActiveActionEnum.UserDataConfig)` (~line 1589).
- Inject + route: message text injected as `ButtonDataKey.Value`, routed through `_handleUserDataConfiguration`, returns `HandlerResultStatus.FINAL` (~line 1593-1599).
- The cache methods (`getUserState`/`setUserState`/`clearUserState` in CacheService) take only `userId` — no `chatId` parameter.

This is a PRE-EXISTING pattern and is re-introduced by the free-text restoration. Impact is limited because the wizard is private-chats-only, the state is short-lived (cleared on the next message or any callback via `clearUserState` at dispatcher top, ~line 2732), and the user must actively click 'Add memory' to arm it. But it's non-obvious: a user could forget they're mid-wizard, then wonder why their group messages get no response. Worth mitigating if revisited: scope state to `(userId, chatId)`, auto-expire after N messages/time, or show an 'active wizard' hint.

title: Rename-completeness gotcha: user-facing strings (incl. Russian) missed when renaming a command
content:
Recurring pattern, surfaced during the `/knowledge_config` → `/memory_config` rename.

When a bot command is renamed (the `commands=(...)` tuple on `@commandHandlerV2`), three categories of user-facing strings commonly still reference the OLD concept name and get missed:

1. **`helpMessage`** on the decorator — the human-readable help text.
2. **`shortDescription`** on the decorator — easy to miss because it's English and short.
3. **Launch/welcome strings** inside the command method body (e.g., the `messageText` sent when a wizard starts).

Non-English (Russian) strings are the most dangerous gap: they don't share any token with the English command symbol, so a `grep` for the new or old command name won't surface them.

Lesson: after any command rename, grep for the OLD concept word (both English AND the localized equivalents) across the handler file, not just for the command symbol. Check `helpMessage`, `shortDescription`, and any hardcoded launch/welcome strings.

NOTE: The specific instance that surfaced this lesson (the `/memory_config` rename in what is now `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py`) has since been FULLY FIXED — both the helpMessage and launch strings now correctly say 'управления памятью' (memory management), and shortDescription typos were corrected. The method `memory_config_command` now lives in `user_memories.py:2897` (it was previously in `user_data.py` before that handler was split). The lesson remains valid for future renames.

title: handlers.md table rows are single multi-KB lines — grep/read truncate at 2000 chars, use bash/sed
content:
Project-specific gotcha for editing `docs/llm/handlers.md` (discovered 2026-07-09).

The handler-reference table in `docs/llm/handlers.md` has rows that are single very long lines — e.g. the `UserDataHandler` row (line 33) is ~3KB, describing the handler, its LLM tools, config gating, ADR cross-refs, and the `/memory_config` wizard in one markdown table cell.

Trap: both the `grep` tool and the `read` tool truncate each line at 2000 characters. So:
- `grep` will MATCH a long line (returning it) but the output is truncated — you see the start, not the part you searched for.
- `read` shows the same line truncated — the text you need may be past the 2000-char mark.

In this session, the agent initially concluded that a "planned for Phase 5" string did NOT exist in handlers.md, because both tools truncated the row before reaching it. The string was actually there, ~2.5KB into the line. The agent only found it by extracting the full line via bash (`sed -n '33p'` / `awk`).

Workaround: when searching/editing `docs/llm/handlers.md` (or any markdown file with long table rows), use bash to read full long lines:
```bash
sed -n '33p' docs/llm/handlers.md   # full content of line 33
```
Do NOT trust the 2000-char-truncated `read`/`grep` output to conclude a string is absent from a long markdown line.

title: Per-message memory storage is a full content snapshot with significant redundancy
content:
The per-message memory storage design was REFACTORED from a content-snapshot approach to a COMPACT-ID + LAZY-RESOLUTION approach. The 'redundancy problem' described in the original memory no longer applies.

Current design (verified):
1. Injection (message_preprocessor.py:129-132): injectMemories stores ONLY memory IDs into ensuredMessage.metadata['memories'] as {'permanentIds': [...], 'shortTermIds': [...]} — UUID hex strings, not content.
2. Persistence: the compact-ID dict is JSON-serialized into chat_messages.metadata (TEXT column).
3. Load from DB (ensured_message.py:869-872): loaded as-is, no resolution.
4. Render (ensured_message.py:1129-1156): formatForLLM calls cache.getMemoriesByIds(permanentIds + shortTermIds) to resolve IDs to SingleMemoryDict content entries ON-DEMAND at render time.

There is NO setUserMemories method on EnsuredMessage (grep returns zero matches). injectMemories does NOT call convertDBMemoryToSingleMemoryDict (that function is used by CacheService for the by-id cache and at render time, not at injection). Storage is single-path (metadata only), not dual (userMemories + metadata).

Implication: per-message storage cost is ~40 bytes per memory ID (UUID hex), not ~150-170 bytes per content entry. The permanent cohort is stored once in the user_memories table and referenced by ID, eliminating the redundancy.

title: memoryRefinement cursor lives on chat_users.metadata, NOT chat_messages.metadata
content:
Two separate storage surfaces hold 'memory' data on different tables:

1. chat_messages.metadata['memories'] — stores COMPACT MEMORY IDs (CompactMemoryIdsDict = {'permanentIds': [...], 'shortTermIds': [...]}), NOT a content snapshot. Written by injectMemories (message_preprocessor.py:129-132) as UUID hex strings. Content is resolved lazily at render time via cache.getMemoriesByIds. Declared at message_metadata.py:257.

2. chat_users.metadata['memoryRefinement'] — the per-(chat,user,thread) refinement cursor. Schema is UserMemoryThreadDict (user_metadata.py:11-35) with ONLY two fields: lastProcessedMessageId (str) and lastProcessedMessageDate (str). The summary field is LEGACY — no longer written or read (docstring at user_metadata.py:19-23 explicitly notes this). Written by user_memories.py:1356-1365.

Note: the original memory referenced user_data.py:1142-1143, 1279-1288 — user_data.py was renamed to user_memories.py; those line numbers are stale. The cursor persistence logic is now at user_memories.py:1349-1367.

title: FastembedProvider provider-level cache_dir config injection pattern
content:
Added 2026-07-09: FastembedProvider (lib/ai/providers/fastembed_provider.py) now supports a provider-level `cache_dir` config key that flows into every model's fastembed kwargs, with per-model `cache_dir` taking precedence.

**How it works:**
- `FastembedProvider.__init__` reads `config.get("cache_dir")` from the provider config dict (stored on `self.cacheDir: Optional[str]`). The provider config is the TOML table `[models.providers.fastembed]` in configs/00-defaults/providers.toml.
- `FastembedModel.__init__`, after building `_fastembedKwargs` from the model's `extraConfig`, checks: if `cache_dir` is not already in `_fastembedKwargs` AND the provider instance has `cacheDir` set, injects `provider.cacheDir` into `_fastembedKwargs`.
- Per-model `cache_dir` (set via model config / extraConfig) overrides the provider-level default.

**Config example** (providers.toml):
```toml
[models.providers.fastembed]
type = "fastembed"
cache_dir = "/path/to/model/cache"  # optional, applies to all fastembed models
```

**Pre-existing mechanism:** `_CONSUMED_EXTRA_KEYS` in FastembedModel lists config keys that are consumed by the model wrapper itself (not passed to fastembed). Any key NOT in that set (including `cache_dir`, `threads`, `max_length`) passes through to `TextEmbedding(...)` via `_fastembedKwargs`. So per-model `cache_dir` already worked before this change; this addition is purely the provider-level default.

**Reusability:** This provider-level-default-injected-into-model-kwargs pattern (store on provider instance, inject in model constructor with model-level override precedence) is a clean pattern for other provider-level config defaults that should flow to all hosted models.

**Relevant gotcha:** Memory 5d089f06 notes that `_getOrCreateEmbedding` caches TextEmbedding instances keyed by modelId only, silently ignoring differing kwargs on duplicate modelId. Provider-level cache_dir doesn't worsen this (all models under one provider share it), but per-model cache_dir differences on the same modelId would still be silently dropped.

title: Root cause: handleRandomMessage confuses overhearing with direct address
content:
In `internal/bot/common/handlers/llm_messages.py`, `handleRandomMessage` (lines ~790-977) previously produced confusing replies like 'why are you asking me?' because the LLM payload was structurally identical to a direct request. Three structural causes identified 2026-07-09:

1. **Similar system prompt across paths.** Reply, mention, and random paths all use `CHAT_PROMPT + CHAT_PROMPT_SUFFIX`. However, the random path additionally appends `RANDOM_ANSWER_PROMPT` (bot-defaults.toml `random-answer-prompt` key), which instructs the model to use the `<skip>` abstention sentinel.

2. **Triggering message is the last `user`-role turn.** `handleRandomMessage` appends the triggering message via `ensuredMessage.toModelMessageList(...)` (~line 953) with default role `"user"`. From the model's POV the final user turn is a direct utterance.

3. **Abstention exit NOW EXISTS (was the original problem).** Originally there was no abstention mechanism — once the probability roll passed, the bot had to reply. This has since been FIXED: `_sendLLMChatMessage` checks for the `<skip>` sentinel (line 394, gated on `imagePrompt is None`) and returns `LLMReplyOutcome.SKIPPED_BY_MODEL`. `handleRandomMessage` handles `SKIPPED_BY_MODEL` at lines 973-975 by returning `False` (no reply sent). The probability gate (~lines 824-841) is the first-pass filter; model judgement via `<skip>` is the second pass. Reply/mention paths do NOT get abstention (they are explicit addresses).

Related: `_sendLLMChatMessage` returns `LLMReplyOutcome` (not bool); handleReply returns True on send-failure, handleMention and handleRandomMessage return False (asymmetric — memory 81065f25).

title: Plan: random-answer context + model abstention (v1)
content:
Design decision (2026-07-09) to fix confusing `handleRandomMessage` replies. Full plan written to `docs/plans/random-answer-context-v1.md`. Two composable changes:

**1. New `RANDOM_ANSWER_PROMPT` chat setting** — appended to the system prompt ONLY inside `handleRandomMessage` (both assembly paths). Tells the model it's overhearing a chat discussion, not being addressed. Four-site wiring required per `add-chat-setting` skill: enum in `internal/bot/models/chat_settings.py` (~line 324), `_chatSettingsInfo` entry (~line 682), default in `configs/00-defaults/bot-defaults.toml`, consumer in `llm_messages.py`.

**2. Model abstention via `<skip>` sentinel** — chosen over empty-string (some models never return empty) and JSON `{"skip":true}` (format-convention overhead). Detection point: after JSON/media unwrap, before image generation, in `_sendLLMChatMessage`. Requires replacing `_sendLLMChatMessage`'s `bool` return with a tri-state `LLMReplyOutcome` (SENT / SKIPPED_BY_MODEL / ERROR) so `handleRandomMessage` can return without sending. `RANDOM_ANSWER_PROMPT` text encodes the "return `<skip>` if nothing to add" rule.

**Deferred to v2 (§10 of plan):** restructure the conversation payload as a single transcript-wrapped `user` message with explicit instruction turn, instead of natural user/assistant roles — only if v1 framing isn't enough.

**Risks flagged:** `ModelMessage` mutability (verify during impl), `<skip>` leakage into reply/mention (fallback: `allowAbstain` flag on `_sendLLMChatMessage`), streaming edge case, Russian-only default prompt.

Implementation should go to a `software-developer` agent — load `add-chat-setting` skill first, then `run-quality-gates` after. No schema change (setting uses existing chat-settings key/value store). Docs to update: `docs/llm/handlers.md`, `docs/llm/configuration.md`.

title: Empty TRUNCATED_FINAL: text path has no empty-content guard, structured path does
content:
Root-cause finding for the recurring "Message text is empty" BadRequest bug (2026-07-05). The base OpenAI provider (`lib/ai/providers/basic_openai_provider.py`) has an asymmetry between its two generation paths:

**Structured path (`_generateStructured`, ~line 548-551):** has an explicit empty-content guard:
```python
if outcome.status in (ModelResultStatus.FINAL, ModelResultStatus.TRUNCATED_FINAL):
    if not outcome.resText:
        raise ValueError("Structured output: model returned empty content")
```
This converts empty output to an ERROR, which then triggers fallback via `_runWithFallback`.

**Text path (`_generateText`, ~line 424-461):** has NO equivalent guard. When `finish_reason="length"` maps to `TRUNCATED_FINAL` (line 351-352) and `message.content` is empty/None, `resText` becomes `""` (line 362), and the `ModelRunResult` is returned with `status=TRUNCATED_FINAL, resultText=""` unchanged.

The complete downstream chain (all unguarded):
1. `_runWithFallback` (abstract.py:658): `TRUNCATED_FINAL not in ERROR_STATUSES` → treated as success → "succeeded on attempt 1" → returned immediately, no fallback.
2. `LLMService.generateTextViaLLM` (service.py:539-598): only special-cases `FINAL` (regex matchers) and `TOOL_CALLS`. `TRUNCATED_FINAL` falls straight to `break` and returns the empty result.
3. `_sendLLMChatMessage` (llm_messages.py:264,342): `lmRetText = mlRet.resultText.strip()` → `""` → `sendMessage(messageText="")` with no empty check.
4. `_sendTelegramMessage` (bot.py:668-670): guard is `if photoData is None and messageText is None and attachmentList is None` — empty string `""` is NOT `None`, so it passes.
5. `tgBot.send_message(text="")` → raises `telegram.error.BadRequest: Message text is empty`.

The string "Message text is empty" does NOT appear anywhere in the repo — it's python-telegram-bot's exception text.

**Fix implemented (observability only, 2026-07-05):** WARNING-level dump added in `_executeChatCompletion` after the status/text are decided. Trigger: `not resText.strip() and status in (TRUNCATED_FINAL, CONTENT_FILTER, UNKNOWN)`. Dumps: finishReason, status, resText, token counts, `completion_tokens_details` (exposes `reasoning_tokens`), `prompt_tokens_details`, and full `response.model_dump_json()`. All vendor-object serialization wrapped in try/except with str() fallback so the probe can never mask the original outcome. Does NOT change status/resText — the empty output still flows downstream.

**Still unfixed (planned, see `docs/plans/llm-empty-truncated-final-handling-v1.md`):** Option A = provider-side downgrade (treat empty FINAL/TRUNCATED_FINAL as ERROR to trigger fallback), Option B = bot-side guard (reject empty string in _sendTelegramMessage + graceful fallback in _sendLLMChatMessage). Also: `yc_sdk_provider.py` `_generateText` (line 487) has the same gap — returns `result.alternatives[0].text` with no emptiness check.

title: Bot reply path: _sendTelegramMessage guard rejects None but not empty string ""
content:
Safety-gap finding in the bot reply path (2026-07-05). `_sendTelegramMessage` in `internal/bot/common/bot.py` (lines 668-670) has a guard:

```python
if photoData is None and messageText is None and attachmentList is None:
    logger.error("No message text or media data provided")
    raise ValueError("No message text or media data provided")
```

This guard only rejects `None` text. An empty string `messageText=""` passes through, and the code proceeds to `tgBot.send_message(text="")`, which raises `telegram.error.BadRequest: Message text is empty`.

The upstream caller `_sendLLMChatMessage` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/llm_messages.py`, lines 264/342) does `lmRetText = mlRet.resultText.strip()` then `sendMessage(messageText=lmRetText)` with no empty-text check — so any LLM result that produces empty `resultText` (e.g. empty TRUNCATED_FINAL) flows straight to the failing `send_message` call.

The MarkdownV2 retry path (bot.py:829-831) catches the first BadRequest and falls through to a plain-text retry (line 834: `send_message(text=addMessagePrefix + _messageText)`), which also fails if both are empty. The outer except (lines 859-861) then logs "Error while sending message: BadRequest#Message text is empty".

**Planned fix (not yet implemented):** tighten the guard to also reject empty-string `messageText` (e.g. `if not messageText` instead of `if messageText is None`), and/or add an empty-check in `_sendLLMChatMessage` before calling sendMessage. See `docs/plans/llm-empty-truncated-final-handling-v1.md` Option B.

title: Reasoning-token budget hypothesis: empty output + outputTokens=max_tokens means hidden thinking consumed the budget
content:
Debugging insight for empty LLM output on reasoning models (2026-07-05). When an OpenAI-compatible model returns `finish_reason="length"` with empty `message.content` AND `outputTokens` equals the configured `max_tokens` cap (observed: 32768), the likely cause is that the model burned its entire completion-token budget on hidden reasoning/thinking tokens without emitting any visible content.

This is the classic signature of Qwen3-class models in `<think>` mode: the chain-of-thought reasoning consumes the full `max_tokens` budget before any answer text is produced, resulting in `TRUNCATED_FINAL` + empty `resultText`.

**Diagnostic field:** `response.usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` (on OpenAI-compatible APIs that follow the spec). If this value is at or near `outputTokens`, the hypothesis is confirmed. This field is now captured by the observability logging added to `BasicOpenAIModel._executeChatCompletion` (fires on `not resText.strip() and status in (TRUNCATED_FINAL, CONTENT_FILTER, UNKNOWN)`).

**Potential mitigations (not yet implemented):** raise `max_tokens`/`max_completion_tokens`, pass `reasoning_effort="low"`, or for Qwen3 specifically set `enable_thinking=False` via `extra_body`. These are model-specific tuning decisions, documented in `docs/plans/llm-empty-truncated-final-handling-v1.md` Option D.

title: Test-run warning baseline is now 0 (all 151 fixed 2026-07-09)
content:
As of 2026-07-09, a clean `make test` produces **0 warnings** (2926 passed, 11 skipped). This supersedes the old baseline of 151 warnings documented in the deleted memory `145e0109`.

All 151 warnings were fixed in one session:
- **150 aiohttp `NotAppKeyWarning`** → fixed by introducing 7 module-level `web.AppKey[...]` constants in `internal/max_webhook_receiver/app.py` (`DATABASE_KEY`, `WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY`, `GET_UPDATES_SECRET_KEY`, `DATA_SOURCE_KEY`, `ENABLE_CLEANUP_KEY`, `MARK_ON_SUBSEQUENT_POLL_KEY`, `CLEANUP_TASK_KEY`) and replacing all string-key `app[...]` accesses. The test file `tests/max_webhook_receiver/test_app.py` was updated to use the same constants.
- **1 `RuntimeWarning: coroutine never awaited`** → real root cause was `tests/services/proxy/test_lifecycle.py::test_stopTimeout` (NOT `test_restartUsesRestartCommand` as previously documented — GC timing misattribution). Fixed by replacing `side_effect=asyncio.TimeoutError` on patched `wait_for` with a `_consumeAndTimeout(awaitable, *args, **kwargs)` helper that closes the awaitable before raising.
- **3 `ResourceWarning: Unclosed client session`** → real production bug in `lib/sandbox/backends/docker.py::_getClient`. Fixed + regression test added.
- **1 `ResourceWarning: Implicitly cleaning up _TemporaryFileWrapper`** → real production bug in `lib/sandbox/storage.py::atomicWriteJson`. Fixed + regression assertion added.

Triage rule: **any warning in `make test` is now a regression** worth investigating.

title: aiodocker.Docker() opens ClientSession in __init__ — must close on version() failure
content:
**Real production bug fixed 2026-07-09 in `lib/sandbox/backends/docker.py::_getClient`.**

`aiodocker.Docker(url=url)` opens an aiohttp `ClientSession` in its constructor (`__init__`). The old code pattern was:
```python
try:
    self._client = aiodocker.Docker(url=url)  # opens ClientSession
    await self._client.version()               # may FAIL (Docker unreachable)
    ...
except Exception as exc:
    self._client = None  # ← BUG: orphans the partially-constructed Docker object
    raise DockerUnavailable(...) from exc
```

When `version()` fails (e.g., Docker daemon unreachable — exactly the case in CI and any non-Docker dev env), setting `self._client = None` without closing the partially-constructed client leaks the `ClientSession`. On GC, aiohttp emits `ResourceWarning: Unclosed client session`.

**Fix:** hold the client in a local, close both its connector and the client itself in the except branch before raising:
```python
client: aiodocker.Docker | None = None
try:
    client = aiodocker.Docker(url=url)
    await client.version()
    self._client = client
    ...
except Exception as exc:
    if client is not None:
        # close connector then client (mirrors the close() success path)
        if hasattr(client, "session") and client.session is not None and client.session.connector is not None:
            await client.session.connector.close()
        await client.close()
    self._client = None
    raise DockerUnavailable(...) from exc
```

This is distinct from the already-documented close()-ordering gotcha (close connector BEFORE client.close()). The new insight: a **partially-constructed** client (where `__init__` succeeded but the next call failed) also holds an open session that must be explicitly closed.

Regression test: `tests/lib/sandbox/backends/test_docker.py::TestGetClientClientSessionLeak::testFailedGetClientClosesPartiallyConstructedClient` — mocks `aiodocker.Docker` so `version()` raises, asserts both `session.connector.close` and `client.close` are awaited. Verified fail-before/pass-after.

title: atomicWriteJson leaked open file handle on failure path — close before unlink
content:
**Real production bug fixed 2026-07-09 in `lib/sandbox/storage.py::atomicWriteJson`.**

The function writes JSON to a NamedTemporaryFile, fsyncs, then renames to the target path. On the **failure path** (e.g., `json.dump()` raising on a circular reference), the except branch unlinked the temp file from disk but **never closed the open Python file handle**:

```python
try:
    json.dump(payload, tmpFile, ...)  # may raise
    ...
    tmpFile.close()  # only reached on success
    os.rename(tmpFilePath, path)
except BaseException:
    tmpFilePath.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    # BUG: tmpFile (open handle) never closed → ResourceWarning on GC
    raise
```

On GC, Python emits `ResourceWarning: Implicitly cleaning up <_TemporaryFileWrapper ...>`.

**Fix:** close the file handle in the except branch before unlinking:
```python
except BaseException:
    if not tmpFile.closed:
        tmpFile.close()
    tmpFilePath.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    raise
```

Note on triggering the failure in tests: `json.dump` is hard to fail because `atomicWriteJson` passes `default=str` — a custom `__str__`/`__repr__` object is NOT sufficient. Use a circular reference (object that references itself) to trigger `ValueError: Circular reference detected`.

Regression assertion added to the existing `tests/lib/sandbox/test_storage.py::TestAtomicWriteJson::testExceptionCleansUpTempFile`: wraps the call in `warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)`, forces GC, and asserts no `ResourceWarning` with "Implicitly cleaning up" fires. Verified fail-before/pass-after.

title: pytest GC warnings attributed to wrong test — use tracemalloc to find real source
content:
**Debugging gotcha confirmed 2026-07-09.**

`ResourceWarning` and `RuntimeWarning: coroutine never awaited` warnings fire during **garbage collection**, which happens at any later point during the test session. pytest attributes the warning to **whatever test is currently running**, NOT the test that caused it.

This wasted significant time in the 2026-07-09 session: a "coroutine never awaited" warning was attributed to `test_restartUsesRestartCommand`, but the real source was `test_stopTimeout` (whose patched `wait_for` leaked a coroutine). Similarly, 3 "Unclosed client session" warnings were attributed to `testRunCodeWorkDirIsWorkspaceRelative` in `test_manager.py`, but the real source was `test_gc.py`'s `collectGarbage()` exercising `DockerBackend._getClient()`.

**The fix: use tracemalloc to get the real allocation traceback:**
```bash
./venv/bin/python3 -X tracemalloc=10 -m pytest tests/services/proxy/test_lifecycle.py -W error::RuntimeWarning
```
The `-X tracemalloc=10` flag makes the warning include "Object allocated at:" with a full traceback to the actual originating line.

**Takeaway:** when a GC-triggered warning points at a test, do NOT trust the attribution. Reproduce with tracemalloc or bisect by deleting tests to find the real culprit. The warning's nominal location is just "whichever test happened to be running when GC kicked in."

title: Sentinel evolved: empty-string clause + imagePrompt-is-None guard (deviates from plan)
content:
The `<skip>`/abstention sentinel in `_sendLLMChatMessage` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/llm_messages.py`, ~line 372) has EVOLVED beyond what the random-answer-context plan (docs/plans/random-answer-context-v1.md) and memory `d247b3ff` document. The plan specified only `== "<skip>"`. The current code is:

```python
if imagePrompt is None and lmRetText.strip().strip("`").strip() in ("<skip>", ""):
    logger.debug("Model abstained (<skip>) or returned empty, not sending a reply")
    return LLMReplyOutcome.SKIPPED_BY_MODEL
```

**Two user-initiated deviations from the plan (confirmed 2026-07-09):**

1. **`""` (empty-string) clause** — added by the USER, not the plan. Handles reasoning-budget exhaustion: some models (Qwen3-class, see production bug in `lib/ai/providers/basic_openai_provider.py`) return empty `message.content` with `finish_reason="length"` when reasoning tokens consume the entire budget. Without the `""` clause, this empty output would reach `sendMessage` and trigger `telegram.BadRequest: Message text is empty`. Treating it as `SKIPPED_BY_MODEL` gracefully declines instead. The code comment (added 2026-07-09) documents this rationale.

2. **`imagePrompt is None` guard** — added to fix an interaction bug: when the model emits a tag-only image request (`<media-description>foo</media-description>` with no caption), the `<media-description>` extraction sets `lmRetText=""`. The `""` clause would then fire the sentinel BEFORE the image-gen branch, silently dropping the image the model explicitly requested. The `imagePrompt is None` guard ensures image requests proceed to the image-gen branch even when caption text is empty. (Also documented in memory `aedb544c`.)

**Cross-references:**
- Memory `d247b3ff` is STALE on the sentinel form (still says `== "<skip>"`, no `imagePrompt is None` guard, claims "Only reachable from handleRandomMessage" which was also corrected to "detected globally").
- Memory `29c637d3` documents the JSON-format limitation (sentinel only works in TEXT-format chats because the JSON-unwrap block is gated on `llmMessageFormat != JSON`).
- Memory `aedb544c` documents the `imagePrompt is None` fix and the test flip (`testTagOnlyTriggersEmptyTextSentinel` → `testTagOnlyGeneratesImage`).
- The Qwen3 budget-exhaustion production bug is documented at the provider level (memory `8a16ec5c` if readable).

**Tests pinning current behavior:** `TestRandomAnswerPromptAndSkipSentinel` (skip-sentinel tests) and `TestMediaDescriptionExtraction` (9 tests including `testTagOnlyGeneratesImage`) in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_llm_messages.py`. Total: 2925 passed, 11 skipped as of 2026-07-09.

title: Patching wait_for with side_effect=Exception leaks the coroutine argument
content:
**Testing gotcha confirmed 2026-07-09 in `tests/services/proxy/test_lifecycle.py::test_stopTimeout`.**

When patching `asyncio.wait_for` (or any function that takes a coroutine as its first argument) with `side_effect=SomeException`, the coroutine passed as the first positional argument is **never consumed/awaited**. Python emits `RuntimeWarning: coroutine ... was never awaited` when it's GC'd.

The bad pattern:
```python
with patch("...asyncio.wait_for", side_effect=asyncio.TimeoutError):
    # production code does: await asyncio.wait_for(process.communicate(), timeout=30)
    # wait_for raises TimeoutError IMMEDIATELY, process.communicate() coroutine never awaited
```

**Fix:** use a side_effect helper that closes the awaitable before raising, mirroring how the real `asyncio.wait_for` consumes its input even on timeout:
```python
def _consumeAndTimeout(awaitable, *args, **kwargs):
    close = getattr(awaitable, "close", None)
    if close is not None:
        close()
    raise asyncio.TimeoutError

with patch("...asyncio.wait_for", side_effect=_consumeAndTimeout):
    ...
```

This pattern applies to ANY patched async function that receives a coroutine argument — the coroutine must be explicitly closed or awaited in the side_effect to avoid the leak.

title: Pyright narrows class attribute to None after = None assignment — use explicit local annotation
content:
**Pyright gotcha confirmed 2026-07-09 in `tests/lib/sandbox/test_gc.py`.**

When a fixture (or any function) assigns `Foo._instance = None` to a class attribute typed as `Foo | None`, pyright **narrows the attribute's type to `None` for the rest of the function scope**. Reading the attribute back later (even after a `yield`) and narrowing with `if x is not None` produces type `Never`, causing confusing errors like `"Never" is not awaitable`.

The problematic pattern:
```python
@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
async def _resetSingleton():
    SandboxManager._instance = None      # ← narrows _instance to None
    yield
    instance = SandboxManager._instance  # pyright thinks this is None
    if instance is not None:             # narrows None → Never
        await instance._backend.close()  # ERROR: "Never" is not awaitable
```

This was extremely confusing because: (1) minimal repros in standalone files did NOT reproduce it, (2) running pyright CLI on a copy didn't either — only the full file triggered it, (3) the real `SandboxBackend.close()` returns `Coroutine[...None]`, not `Never`.

**Fix:** add an explicit type annotation on the local variable:
```python
instance: "SandboxManager | None" = SandboxManager._instance
if instance is not None:
    await instance._backend.close()  # now correctly typed
```

The explicit annotation overrides pyright's flow-based narrowing from the earlier assignment.

title: media-description regex must use trimmedText (same subject as gate check), not lmRetText
content:
**Bug fix 2026-07-09 in `internal/bot/common/handlers/llm_messages.py` (~line 348), additional to memory `78af24ee`.**

The `<media-description>` extraction has TWO distinct subjects that must stay in sync:
1. **Gate check** uses `trimmedText` (= `lmRetText.strip().strip("\`").strip()`) to decide whether extraction applies.
2. **Regex extraction** must ALSO use `trimmedText` — NOT the raw `lmRetText`.

The bug: the regex `re.search(r"^(.*?)<media-description>(.*?)</media-description>(.*?)$", lmRetText, re.DOTALL)` searched against `lmRetText` (which still carried the surrounding backtick/whitespace wrapper). So `group(3)` captured the trailing backticks/whitespace verbatim. For input `` `  <media-description>foo</media-description>bar  ` ``, `group(3)` = `` `bar  ` `` instead of `bar`.

**General lesson (applies to any gate-then-process pattern):** if a gate check operates on a normalized/trimmed subject, the downstream processing (regex, parsing) MUST operate on the same normalized subject. Diverging the subjects means the gate passes but the processing captures un-normalized artifacts.

Test `testBacktickAndWhitespaceWrappedExtracts` is the regression guard (it failed before, passes after).

Related: memory `78af24ee` documents the EARLIER fix to the same code area (non-greedy trailing group without `$` anchor). This is a separate, later-discovered bug in the same block.

title: Guard side-channel logger calls at the call site when args require computation
content:
Convention (derived from a Gate 1 code-review finding, 2026-07-06, on the user-memory-refinement JSONL logger in `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py`, class `UserMemoriesHandler` — file/class renamed from `user_data.py`/`UserDataHandler`):

When a best-effort side-channel logger method (e.g. `_writeRefinementJsonLog`) is gated internally by an enable flag (`if not self._refineLogEnabled: return`), that internal guard is NOT sufficient if the method's ARGUMENTS require computation. Guard the entire call at the call site too. Current code in `_runSingleRefinement`:

```python
if self._refineLogEnabled:
    toolCounts = self._countRefinementToolCalls(result)   # walks result.toolUsageHistory / result.toolCalls
    self._writeRefinementJsonLog(
        chatId=chatId, userId=userId, threadId=threadId,
        login=messages[0]["username"], messagesCount=len(messages),
        firstMessageId=messages[-1]["message_id"].asStr(),
        lastMessageId=messages[0]["message_id"].asStr(),
        summary=(result.resultText or "").strip(),
        addCount=toolCounts.get(ToolName.ADD_MEMORY.value, 0),
        deleteCount=toolCounts.get(ToolName.DELETE_MEMORY.value, 0),
        searchCount=toolCounts.get(ToolName.SEARCH_MEMORIES.value, 0),
    )
```

Why: without the call-site guard, `_countRefinementToolCalls(result)` is evaluated eagerly on EVERY refinement run — including the common case where logging is disabled (the default). The internal guard only prevents the write, not the wasted argument computation. Refinement runs on a 60s cron tick, so skipping that work when logging is off is a worthwhile microopt.

NOTE: an earlier revision of this logger resolved the model id via a `_resolveRefineModel(chatSettings, result)` helper and passed `model=` / `elapsedTime=` kwargs. That helper and those kwargs were REMOVED in the Phase 4a rewrite (the LLM now emits tool calls instead of a dossier; per-tool counts replaced model/elapsed-time logging). The call-site guard convention still applies — it now guards `_countRefinementToolCalls`.

Precedent: `AbstractModel.printJSONLog` (`lib/ai/abstract.py`, the first JSONL logger) does NOT use a call-site guard because all its arguments (`messages`, `result`, `consumerId`) are already-in-scope locals with zero computation cost — only the dict literal is built inside the guarded method. So the pattern only matters when the logger's args are themselves expensive to compute. When replicating the JSONL-logging pattern for NEW features, audit the call-site arguments: if any require non-trivial work (lookups, formatting, counting, model resolution), add the `if self.<enabled>:` call-site guard in addition to the internal one. The internal `if not self._refineLogEnabled: return` guard is kept as defense-in-depth (protects against direct calls from elsewhere) — do not remove either guard.

title: Language convention: English for code/docs, Russian for bot-facing text
content:
General project convention (not stated in AGENTS.md, inferred from consistent practice): code, comments, docstrings, and developer-facing documentation (docs/, AGENTS.md) are in English. Bot user-facing text — prompt templates in TOML configs (bot-defaults.toml), chat settings `short`/`long` descriptions in `_chatSettingsInfo`, and any text the LLM sees as instructions — is in Russian, because the bot is a Russian-language bot.

This explains several otherwise-puzzling patterns:
- `_chatSettingsInfo` entries use Russian for `short`/`long` fields (memory 4a44472f flagged an English `REGENERATE_EMBEDDINGS` short field as an inconsistency/bug).
- Prompt templates like `chat-prompt-suffix`, `memory-refine-system-prompt`, `divination-discovery-system-prompt` are in Russian.
- Exception: image-generation prompts stay English for model quality (memory 8d614813).

When writing new chat settings, prompts, or any bot-facing config text, use Russian. When writing code, comments, docstrings, or docs, use English.

title: SUPERSEDED banner convention for in-place docs/llm/memories/ files
content:
When a doc in `docs/llm/memories/` describes behavior that has been replaced by a newer feature, do NOT delete the file and do NOT move it to `docs/archive/`. Instead, keep it in place and apply the SUPERSEDED banner pattern:

1. **Prominent banner at top** (right after the H1 title): a block starting with `⚠ SUPERSEDED` that points to the successor doc (relative path link), and briefly enumerates what's superseded vs. what's still relevant/adapted.
2. **Targeted inline `[SUPERSEDED]` notes** at the most misleading spots in the body — sections that describe the removed behavior as if it were live. Don't annotate every line; focus on the 2-3 places a skimming reader would most likely be misled.
3. **Update `docs/llm/memories/index.md`** to flag the entry as SUPERSEDED with a one-line note on what's still relevant.
4. Keep the file: it retains useful historical context (e.g., the cursor/accounting/cron mechanism that was adapted for the new system).

This is DISTINCT from the `(HISTORICAL)` title-suffix convention (memory 673b3260) used for plan docs that are MOVED to `docs/archive/plans/`. The SUPERSEDED banner is for memory docs that STAY IN PLACE in `docs/llm/memories/`.

Applied to `docs/llm/memories/user-memory-refinement.md` in Phase 4c-1 (2026-07-09) when the user-memories feature replaced the old rolling-bio system. The successor doc is `docs/llm/memories/user-memories.md`.

title: getProvider(chatId=None) falls back to default source — for methods without chatId routing
content:
`DatabaseManager.getProvider()` (internal/database/manager.py:103-108) has the signature:

```python
async def getProvider(self, *, chatId: Optional[int] = None, dataSource: Optional[str] = None, readonly: bool = False) -> BaseSQLProvider
```

Provider selection priority: `dataSource > chatId mapping > default source`.

When called with `chatId=None` and `dataSource=None`, it falls back to `self.default` (the default data source, confirmed at manager.py:162-168). This is the correct routing for repository methods that don't have a chatId — e.g., `getMemoriesByIds(memoryIds)` in the memory compaction plan, which fetches by globally-unique UUID and has no chat/user context.

Usage: `sqlProvider = await self.manager.getProvider(chatId=None, readonly=True)` for read-only access to the default DB.

Note: this was previously a point of confusion — an earlier memory (b3fcb13d, now deleted/corrected) falsely claimed getProvider couldn't be called without arguments. It CAN be called with all-None kwargs; it routes to the default source.

title: Variable-length IN clause pattern — :mid0, :mid1 named-placeholder expansion
content:
The `user_memories` repository (and likely others) handles variable-length `IN (...)` SQL clauses by building named placeholders dynamically. Precedent: `_semanticSearchMemories` in `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py:940-943`.

Pattern: instead of using `?` positional placeholders or raw string interpolation, build `:mid0, :mid1, :mid2, ...` named placeholders and pass a dict `{"mid0": val0, "mid1": val1, ...}` as parameters. This works with the `:named` parameter style that all providers translate (SQLite/MySQL natively, PostgreSQL via `$N` positional translation).

This is the correct portable approach for variable-length IN clauses — do NOT use f-string interpolation of values into SQL, and do NOT use `?` positional placeholders (which break the PostgreSQL provider's named→positional translation).

title: fromDBChatMessage is synchronous — cannot do async DB/cache resolution
content:
`EnsuredMessage.fromDBChatMessage()` (internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:784) is a SYNCHRONOUS classmethod (`@classmethod`, not `async`)... 

WAIT — actually it IS async (`async def fromDBChatMessage`). Correction: it's declared `async def` but performs only synchronous deserialization of the already-fetched `ChatMessageDict` data — it does NOT make any DB or cache calls of its own. The `db: Database` parameter is used only for lazy media fetching (when `forceGetAllMedia=True`).

The key constraint: even though it's `async def`, it should NOT make new async DB/cache calls for memory resolution because:
1. It's a deserialization factory — its job is to reconstruct an EnsuredMessage from a DB row dict.
2. Adding async cache resolution here would couple deserialization with the cache service, and would require every call site to await the resolution even when memories aren't needed.

This is why the memory compaction plan introduces a SEPARATE `async def resolveMemories(self, cache: CacheService)` method on EnsuredMessage — called by read-path consumers AFTER the message list is built, not inside fromDBChatMessage. The factory stores raw memory IDs in metadata; resolution happens later as an explicit step.
