title: Module rename gotcha: mock.patch target strings break at runtime, not at import/lint time
content:
When a Python module is renamed (e.g. `user_data.py` → `user_memories.py`), string-based `mock.patch` targets that reference the old dotted module path will break at RUNTIME — not at import time, not at lint/typecheck time. This happened in the `UserDataHandler` → `UserMemoriesHandler` rename (July 2026).

Specific failure: `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_memories_memory_regen.py:664` had:
```python
mock.patch("internal.bot.common.handlers.user_data.asyncio.sleep", ...)
```
After the production module was renamed to `user_memories`, this patch target caused:
```
AttributeError: module 'internal.bot.common.handlers' has no attribute 'user_data'
```
raised from `pkgutil.py` (getattr-based module walking inside the patch resolver).

These string targets are invisible to ALL static checks:
- NOT caught by `import main` circular-import check (they're strings, not imports)
- NOT caught by `grep UserDataHandler` (the patch target references the module path, not the class name)
- NOT caught by `make format lint` / `pyright` / `flake8`

**Checklist for any future module rename in this project:**
1. `grep -rn "old_module_name" tests/ --include="*.py"` — catch string-based `mock.patch` targets, `importlib.import_module()` calls, `getattr(module, ...)` patterns
2. Also check for hardcoded production file path strings in test assertions (see separate memory about `test_memory_resolution_coverage.py`)
3. Clear stale `__pycache__/*.pyc` files from pre-rename filenames — they survive `git mv` and will create false-positive `grep` matches (use `--include="*.py"` to filter them out)

title: Handler rename: UserDataHandler → UserMemoriesHandler (class + module)
content:
The user-memories handler was renamed to align with the "memories" domain concept:

- **Class**: `UserDataHandler` → `UserMemoriesHandler` (at `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py:132`)
- **Module**: `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py` → `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py`

All production-code references were updated.

**Naming distinction gotcha — now FULLY MOOT:** The memory originally noted that `UserDataRepository` (in `internal/database/repositories/user_data.py`) was a SEPARATE v1 repository that was intentionally NOT renamed. As of migration_022 (`migration_022_drop_user_data.py`), the `user_data` TABLE is DROPPED entirely and `internal/database/repositories/user_data.py` no longer exists. So there is no longer any name-collision risk between `UserMemoriesHandler` and `UserDataRepository`.

**Stale references in older memories:** Several existing memories still reference the old class name `UserDataHandler` and old file path `user_data.py`. When these say `UserDataHandler` or `user_data.py`, they mean the current `UserMemoriesHandler` / `user_memories.py`.

title: Frozen/historical docs scope for bulk renames — beyond docs/archive/
content:
When performing bulk find-and-replace across documentation (e.g., class/file renames), the following docs are frozen/historical and must NOT be edited:

1. **`docs/archive/*`** — all archived files (covered by existing archive policy memory `561b6201`)
2. **`docs/plans/*`** — ALL plan files are frozen historical records. This includes `user-memories-v1.md`, `memory-refine-plan-v1.md`, `memory-refine-plan-v0.md`, `user-info-cache-plan-v1.md`, etc. Plan bodies are historical snapshots, not living docs.
3. **`docs/llm/memories/user-memory-refinement.md`** — explicitly marked SUPERSEDED. Describes the v1 rolling-bio system. Kept as historical context only.
4. **`docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md`** — maintained separately by the teamlead agent. Do not edit from other agents' sessions.

Remaining grep matches for old/renamed tokens in these files are expected and intentional. After a bulk rename, verify with:
- `grep -rn "OldName" docs/` — remaining hits should ONLY be in the frozen files above.
- `grep -rn "old/path.py" docs/` — same.

This was applied during the 2026-07-10 `UserDataHandler → UserMemoriesHandler` doc rename.

title: Handler table rows in docs/llm/handlers.md are multi-KB single lines (tool truncation gotcha)
content:
The handler table in `docs/llm/handlers.md` consists of VERY LONG single lines — multi-KB, well over 2000 characters. The `read` and `grep` tools truncate lines at 2000 characters, so you will NOT see the full content of these rows and may miss tokens that appear later in the line.

**Current long lines (verified 2026-07-14):**
- **Line 29** (~2027 chars) — the `MessagePreprocessorHandler` row.
- **Line 33** (~5167 chars) — the `UserMemoriesHandler` row (link label + link target + handler class name + extensive description, all on one line).

**Workaround:** Use `sed` to read the full line before editing:
```bash
sed -n '29p' docs/llm/handlers.md
sed -n '33p' docs/llm/handlers.md
```

**Note:** Line numbers for these rows shift as handlers are added/removed — relocate by grepping for the handler class name (e.g. `grep -n 'UserMemoriesHandler' docs/llm/handlers.md`) rather than trusting the line numbers above. (An earlier version of this memory cited line 447 as a multi-KB line; that line is now a short ~55-char ordered-list item — the long content moved. Always re-verify which lines exceed 2000 chars before relying on truncation workarounds.)

title: When renaming a module, bare filename references also need updating (not just full paths)
content:
During bulk doc renames (e.g., a class/file rename), THREE forms of reference must be updated — the third is easy to miss:

1. **Full path references** — `path/to/old_name.py` → `path/to/new_name.py` (including relative markdown link targets like `../../internal/...`).
2. **Class name references** — `OldClass` → `NewClass`.
3. **Bare filename references** — these slip past path-grep:
   - Markdown link LABELS: `` [`old_name.py`](...) `` → `` [`new_name.py`](...) ``
   - Directory tree entries: `` ├── old_name.py  # handler comment ``
   - Brace expansion paths: `` `path/{a,b,old_name}.py` ``
   - Inline code references: `` (`old_name.py` `_method`) ``

title: Gotcha: grep self-sabotage — don't reintroduce the pattern in your fix note
content:
When the acceptance criteria for a cleanup task is grep-based (e.g., "grep -rn UserDataRepository docs/ returns zero in live docs"), the explanatory note you add during the fix can ACCIDENTALLY REINTRODUCE the exact pattern being removed.

**Observed (2026-07-10):** When removing `UserDataRepository` from `docs/suggestions/refactoring.md`, the agent wrote a parenthetical note: "(the legacy `UserDataRepository` was later removed...)" — which itself contains the grep target string `UserDataRepository` and would have failed the acceptance criteria.

**Fix:** Rephrased to "(the legacy user-data repository was later removed...)" — lowercase, no camelCase — avoiding the exact pattern.

**Lesson:** When adding explanatory notes during a grep-driven cleanup, use natural-language rephrasing (lowercase, different casing, descriptive name) rather than the exact identifier being removed. Run the grep check AFTER all edits, including the notes you added.

title: Dropping a table requires updating expected-tables lists in schema tests
content:
When dropping a database table via a new migration, TWO additional schema-introspection tests will fail unless the table name is removed from their hardcoded expected/required tables lists:

1. `tests/integration/test_database_operations.py::testSchemaCreation` — has an `expectedTables` list that enumerates all tables that should exist after migrations run.

**Checklist when dropping a table:** grep for the table name across `tests/database/` and `tests/integration/` to find any hardcoded lists that include it. Also check migration-specific tests that roll back to pre-state (see memory ad02a28e for the rollback steps gotcha).

title: Drop-table migration convention: down() must recreate the FINAL accumulated table shape, not migration_001's original
content:
Convention established by `migration_022_drop_user_data.py` — the FIRST migration in this codebase whose `up()` drops an existing table. This sets the pattern for future table-retirement migrations.

**The pattern:**
- `up()`: `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS <table>` via `provider.batchExecute([ParametrizedQuery("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ...")])` — matches the shape used in migration_020's down() and migration_001's down().
- `down()`: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS <table>` with the table's FINAL accumulated schema shape — i.e., the state the table was in JUST BEFORE this migration ran, after all prior migrations have been applied.

**THE TRAP (non-obvious):** The `down()` DDL must reflect the POST-all-prior-migrations shape, NOT the original shape from migration_001. If you naively copy the CREATE TABLE from migration_001, you'll reintroduce `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` on timestamp columns that migration_013 explicitly removed. You MUST cross-check the `down()` DDL against BOTH the original migration (e.g. migration_001) AND any intervening schema-modifying migrations (e.g. migration_013 which recreated all tables to strip timestamp defaults).

**Concrete verification:** migration_022's down() recreates `user_data` with `created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL` / `updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL` (no DEFAULT) — matching migration_013's `user_data_new` shape, NOT migration_001's which had `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`.

**Other rules that apply (from AGENTS.md SQL portability):**
- No `AUTOINCREMENT`, no `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`
- Portable types only: TEXT, INTEGER, REAL, TIMESTAMP, BOOLEAN
- Composite natural PK (e.g. `PRIMARY KEY (user_id, chat_id, key)`)
- No indexes to recreate unless prior migrations created them on the table (user_data never had any)

Structural reversibility only — data is unrecoverable after drop. This is acceptable for retiring dead tables.

title: Code review action items for _trackedChats rewrite: discard() fix, test breakage, refinement coupling
content:
Code review output for the uncommitted `_trackedChats` embedding-regen discovery rewrite (branch `user-memory-v2`, reviewed 2026-07-10). Complements memory `492649e3` (which documents WHAT changed) with what needs FIXING before merge.

## Fix: `set.remove()` → `set.discard()` (important)

Both `self._trackedChats.remove(chatId)` calls — `chat_search.py:343` and `user_memories.py:840` — can raise `KeyError` if two CRON ticks overlap. The `.remove()` happens AFTER `await getChatSettings()`, which yields control; `_dtCronJob`/`_runMemoryEmbeddingRegen` have NO re-entrancy guard (unlike `_runMemoryRefinement` which bails on `_refineLock.locked()`). The `.remove()` sits outside any try/except. Fix: use `self._trackedChats.discard(chatId)` — same semantics, never raises.

## Test breakage: 4 test files reference deleted `listChatsBySetting` (critical, `make test` red)

- `tests/database/repositories/test_chat_settings.py` — 7 call sites (lines 64, 94, 119, 134, 148, 191, 197) → `AttributeError` (method deleted).
- `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search.py` — mocks `db.chatSettings.listChatsBySetting` and asserts `assert_awaited_once_with(...)` → assertions fail. Cron-discovery tests must seed `handler._trackedChats` instead.
- `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_memories_memory_regen.py` — lines 231, 310, 322, 335, 740. `test_listChatsBySettingErrorReturnsEarly` (:732) tests a code path that no longer exists.
- `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search_cleanup.py` — lines 109, 123.

Additionally: no NEW tests exist for `_trackedChats` population/eviction logic or the `dimensions` filter. These need coverage.

## Refinement↔embeddings coupling: CRITICAL regression (needs explicit decision)

`_runMemoryRefinement` gate (`user_memories.py:1051-1054`) now requires `MEMORY_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED` in addition to `MEMORY_REFINEMENT_ENABLED`. Previously refinement was independent of embeddings — docstring at :993-999 explicitly states regen and refinement "do not contend" and run independently. The coupling silently disables refinement for any chat with `MEMORY_REFINEMENT_ENABLED=true` but `MEMORY_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=false` (candidates are permanently popped from `_accounting`/`_lastRefinedTS`).

Possible defensible rationale: refinement's `search_memories` LLM tool is semantic and may return nothing without embeddings. If this IS intentional, it must be (a) documented in the gate's docstring, (b) reflected in `MEMORY_REFINEMENT_ENABLED` setting docs. If not, revert the added condition. Either way, needs a decision before merge.

## No-eviction on model misconfiguration (minor)

`chat_search.py:347-352`: a chat whose `EMBEDDING_MODEL` is empty/unknown returns WITHOUT evicting from `_trackedChats`. Such a chat is re-picked every Nth tick and re-fails forever. Should evict on permanent misconfiguration (but NOT on transient model-resolution errors).

## ChatSearchHandler.newMessageHandler per-message cost (minor)

`ChatSearchHandler` previously had NO `newMessageHandler` override (inherited base class returning `SKIPPED`). Now overrides with a version calling `getChatSettings()` — a new per-message cost on every inbound message when search-history is enabled. Cached after first message per chat (dict lookup), so acceptable, but it IS a new handler-chain cost.

## Documentation sync (6 doc files reference deleted `listChatsBySetting`)

Must update in the same change: `docs/llm/database.md:55`, `docs/llm/architecture.md:566`, `docs/llm/configuration.md:822`, `docs/llm/memories/user-memories.md:238`, `docs/llm/memories/chat-history-search.md:85,118,203`.

title: Bugfix: set.remove() → set.discard() on _trackedChats (KeyError risk)
content:
During the regen-discovery rewrite review-fixes session (2026-07-10, branch `user-memory-v2`), a KeyError bug was found and fixed in BOTH crons that evict chats from the in-memory `_trackedChats: MutableSet[int]`:

**Sites (2):**
1. `ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py`) — after the per-chat gate fails (`REGENERATE_EMBEDDINGS` or `EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED` now false)
2. `UserMemoriesHandler._runMemoryEmbeddingRegen` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py`) — after the per-chat gate fails

**Root cause:** The eviction used `self._trackedChats.remove(chatId)`, which raises `KeyError` if the element is not present. A chat could be evicted from `_trackedChats` between ticks (e.g. another code path, or a race) before the cron's per-chat gate re-checks and tries to evict it again. `set.discard()` is the correct method — it's a no-op if the element is absent.

**Fix:** Changed `.remove(chatId)` → `.discard(chatId)` at both sites. This was the ONLY behavioral change in the 13-edit doc-fix changeset; the other 11 edits were purely docstrings/comments.

Note: Memory `492649e3` (the architecture description of this rewrite) documents the eviction as `.remove()` — that is now stale; it's `.discard()`.

title: _d_tCronJob rewrite: in-memory _trackedChats replaces listChatsBySetting DB-scan
content:
A "regen-discovery rewrite" changed how `ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob` discovers which chats to process. The old approach did a DB scan via `ChatSettingsRepository.listChatsBySetting` (querying for chats with `EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=true`). That repository method was **DELETED** entirely.

The new design uses an in-memory set `self._trackedChats: MutableSet[int]` (initialized to `set()` in `__init__`):

- **Population**: `newMessageHandler` adds chat IDs to `_trackedChats` as messages arrive.
- **Round-robin**: The cron processes ONE chat per tick via `chatList = sorted(self._trackedChats); chatId = chatList[self._backfillIndex % len(chatList)]`. (Same round-robin cursor concept as before, but the source set changed.)
- **Gate checks**: Settings check (`REGENERATE_EMBEDDINGS` + `EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED`) then model resolution, same as before.
- **Self-eviction**: On gate failure, the chat is evicted via `self._trackedChats.discard(chatId)`.

New `_dtCronJob` flow:
1. Gate 1: `if not self._trackedChats: return` — early return if empty.
2. Round-robin pick: `chatId = chatList[self._backfillIndex % len(chatList)]`.
3. Gate 2: `getChatSettings()`, check `REGENERATE_EMBEDDINGS` + `EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED`; on fail, `.discard(chatId)` and return.
4. Gate 3: resolve model — bail if missing or no embedding support.
5. Cleanup: `deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings` (gated by `_embeddingModelTracker`).
6. Gate 4: `getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings` batch fetch.

This supersedes the previous DB-scan discovery pattern. The `listChatsBySetting` method no longer exists in `ChatSettingsRepository`.

title: Test pattern: seed handler._trackedChats in tests driving _dtCronJob
content:
After the "regen-discovery rewrite" that replaced `listChatsBySetting` DB-scan with in-memory `self._trackedChats`, tests that drive `ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob` MUST seed `handler._trackedChats` after construction — otherwise the cron's first gate (`if not self._trackedChats: return`) causes an immediate early return and no chat is processed.

In `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search_cleanup.py`, the `_makeHandler` helper was updated to set a default `handler._trackedChats = {100}` right after construction. This makes most tests inherit chat 100 automatically. Tests needing a different set (e.g., `{999}` or `{100, 200}` or `{}`) override `handler._trackedChats` explicitly after calling `_makeHandler`.

The `_makeChatSettings` helper already includes `EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED: "true"` and `REGENERATE_EMBEDDINGS: "true"` — no change needed there.

The old `enabledChats` parameter on `_makeHandler` (which mocked `db.chatSettings.listChatsBySetting`) was removed entirely as dead code.

title: Doc-sync convention: deleted identifiers must have ZERO literal matches in live docs
content:
When a method/identifier is deleted from the codebase and docs are synced, the acceptance criterion is ZERO literal string matches of the identifier in live (non-archive/plans/superseded) docs — not merely removing references that imply the identifier still exists.

Discovered 2026-07-10 during the `listChatsBySetting` deletion doc-sync: the documenting agent initially wrote removal-context mentions like "the previous `listChatsBySetting(MEMORY_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED)` discovery ... was removed" in 8 places across 6 doc files. These are legitimate documentation (they explain the migration), but the strict `rg -n "listChatsBySetting" docs/` acceptance criterion required zero matches. All 8 had to be reworded to describe the deletion without using the literal token (e.g., "the deleted `ChatSettingsRepository` DB-scan discovery method" or "the old DB-scan discovery (now removed)").

Practical guidance: when documenting a deletion, describe the mechanism without naming the deleted identifier. Use phrases like "the old DB-scan discovery method (now removed)" rather than backtick-quoting the exact deleted name.

Note: frozen docs (`docs/archive/`, `docs/plans/`, superseded banner files) are exempt — they retain historical references unchanged per the established archive policy.

title: Gate 2 review: regen-discovery rewrite integration-clean (no behavioral bugs)
content:
A whole-changeset (Gate 2) code review was performed on 2026-07-10 for the complete regen-discovery rewrite (branch `user-memory-v2`, 16 files, ~+513/−480 LOC). The review covered integration/cross-cutting concerns after per-phase reviews handled local correctness.

## Verdict: NO critical or important behavioral bugs found

All integration invariants verified clean:
- **Round-robin `% len(chatList)` math is safe** — `if not self._trackedChats: return` guard precedes every modulo, so no zero-division. Traced for shrink ({100,200}→{100}) and grow ({100}→{100,300}): modulo is recomputed against current `len` each tick, no skip/duplicate.
- **`.discard()` eviction is idempotent** — no KeyError path even on double-eviction.
- **Refinement cannot run with embeddings off** — `_runMemoryRefinement` gate re-checks both `MEMORY_REFINEMENT_ENABLED` AND `MEMORY_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED` per candidate and drops survivors from `_accounting` + `_lastRefinedTS`. `_runSingleRefinement` is only reachable after the gate.
- **Both `newMessageHandler` overrides return `HandlerResultStatus.NEXT`** — don't break the handler chain. `ChatSearchHandler` is registered `PARALLEL`, `LLMMessageHandler` still last/`SEQUENTIAL`.
- **6 new regression tests are meaningful** — they exercise real add/skip/evict paths via `newMessageHandler`, not seed-and-assert-mocks.
- **`ChatSettingsValue` import removal is safe** — no remaining runtime use in either handler (only a docstring reference in user_memories.py:799).
- **`getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings` `dimensions` kwarg** is keyword-only with `None` default — all existing positional callers unaffected.
- **`getChatSettings` always returns all keys** (merged with defaults) — so `chatSettings[key]` subscript won't KeyError even on empty cache.

The `_runRefinement` → `_runSingleRefinement` rename (done IN this changeset) was NOT propagated to docs. `rg "_runRefinement\b"` returns ~20 live-doc references + 1 production docstring. title: Schema docs convention: inline numeric defaults, not constant names
content:
When documenting method signatures in schema docs (`docs/database-schema.md`, `docs/database-schema-llm.md`, `docs/llm/database.md`), use inline numeric values for defaults (e.g., `limit=50`) rather than the Python constant name (e.g., `limit=BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`).

This matches the convention of every adjacent method signature in those files — they all use raw numbers like `limit=10`, `limit=5`, `limit=20`, `limit=100`. Using the constant name would break visual consistency and make the doc less scannable.

If a default is a named constant, look up its value and inline it. Example: `BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE = 50` → write `limit=50` in the doc signature.

title: Correction: getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings already had dimensions param — prior review's "intentional asymmetry" was wrong (checked wrong file)
content:

Actual signatures (verified 2026-07-10):
- `getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings(self, chatId, *, limit=BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE(=50), modelName=None, dimensions=None, dataSource=None) -> List[UserMemoryDict]` — in `user_memories.py:1291`
- `getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings(self, chatId, *, limit=100, modelName=None, dimensions=None, dataSource=None) -> List[ChatMessageDict]` — in `chat_embeddings.py:466`

Both are SYMMETRIC in capability (both filter on dimensions). They differ structurally (see separate architecture memory), not in param availability.

This resolves the `status=open-phase3-must-reconcile` deviation #2 from memory a5e6c6a3 (which flagged `dimensions` as dropped from `getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings`). Deviations #1 (dropped userId) and #3 (tags LIKE vs Python set-intersection) from that memory may still be open.

Also note: memory 92acdbce says "the regen cron's stale-detection is model-only" — this is now IMPRECISE. The method keys off BOTH `embedding_model` AND `embedding_dimensions` via an OR(...) clause. The core point of 92acdbce (content edits must manually invalidate embeddings because the cron doesn't detect content drift) remains valid.

title: Architecture: structural contrast between the two get*WithoutEmbeddings methods (single-table OR vs NOT-EXISTS)
content:
Both `get*WithoutEmbeddings` repo methods have `dimensions: Optional[int] = None` (keyword-only) and are called by their respective regen crons with `dimensions=currentDims`. But they are structurally different:

**`getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings`** (`internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py:1291`):
- Single-table query on `user_memories` (no JOIN, no vec0).
- Stale predicate: `(embedding_model IS NULL OR (:modelName IS NOT NULL AND embedding_model != :modelName)) OR (embedding_dimensions IS NULL OR (:dimensions IS NOT NULL AND embedding_dimensions != :dimensions))` — an OR(...) on provenance columns.
- Filters `deleted_at IS NULL`.
- Default limit = `BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE` (= 50, defined in `internal/database/constants.py:22`).

**`getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings`** (`internal/database/repositories/chat_embeddings.py:466`):
- Uses a `NOT EXISTS` subquery against the `message_embeddings` table (the embedding table is only a filter, not selected from).
- Joins with `chat_users` for `username`/`full_name`.
- Default limit = 100.

**Production callers forward `dimensions`:**
- Memory path: `UserMemoriesHandler._runMemoryEmbeddingRegen` at `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py:887-892` — forwards `modelName=modelName, dimensions=currentDims`.
- Chat path: `ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob` at `internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py:393-398` — forwards `modelName, dimensions=currentDims`.

**Belt-and-suspenders pattern (verified):** `getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings` is complementary to `deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings`. Even if `deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings` swallows a failure (doesn't NULL the provenance columns), the independent `embedding_dimensions != :dimensions` clause re-surfaces stale-dimension rows. This is exercised in production (caller forwards `dimensions`), not just theoretical.

title: Test pattern: dimension-filter regression test design (isolate the variable under test)
content:
The regression test `test_getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings_filtersByDimensions` (`tests/database/repositories/test_user_memories.py:769`) demonstrates a clean pattern for testing filter logic with no false-confidence risk:

**Setup:** Two rows that share the SAME `embedding_model` (matching the `modelName` param) but DIFFER only in `embedding_dimensions` (384 vs 1024). Both are manually UPDATE'd via `sqlProvider.execute` with named placeholders (mirrors the existing test's non-vec0 branch pattern).

**Assertion 1** (`dimensions=1024`): The 384-dim row MUST surface; the 1024-dim row MUST NOT. This can ONLY pass via the `embedding_dimensions != :dimensions` clause — both rows have a non-NULL, matching `embedding_model`, so the model clause is FALSE for both. If the dimensions filter were absent/broken, the 384-dim row would not surface and the assertion fails. No false-confidence path.

**Assertion 2** (`dimensions=None`): NEITHER row surfaces. The `:dimensions IS NOT NULL` guard collapses the dims clause; matching-model rows don't surface. Pins behavior-preservation (the new param didn't change default behavior).

**Key design principle:** both rows share the matching `embedding_model` so the ONLY path to surfacing is the dimensions clause. A common mistake would be to also mismatch the model — then the row could surface via EITHER clause, making the test pass even if the dimensions filter were broken.

**Vec0 vs non-vec0 branches:** In the vec0 branch, `saveMemoryEmbedding` sets both provenance columns. In the non-vec0 branch, a manual `UPDATE user_memories SET embedding_model=:m, embedding_dimensions=:d` is used. Both correctly set up the provenance for the single-table query (which doesn't touch vec0 tables).

title: Condense-path memory fate: condensed messages' memory blocks dropped entirely from structured form
content:
Definitive confirmation (2026-07-11) tracing the condense code path in `getThreadByMessageForLLM` (base.py:786-898). Hypothesis was "memories are dropped in condense path" — CONFIRMED.

**Condense-replay path (previously-cached condensation, base.py:786-817):**
- The first `keepFirstN` messages (default 1) ARE individually formatted via `fromDBChatMessage` + `toModelMessageList` (lines 789-800) — their memories ARE rendered (if `resolveMemories` ran via `cache=self.cache`).
- Each condensed entry becomes `ModelMessage(role="user", content=condensedMessage["text"])` at :808 — a plain text string from persisted `condenseCache`. NO `EnsuredMessage` involved, NO `metadata["memories"]` read.
- The summarized messages are sliced off `dbMessageList` at :817 and NEVER built into `EnsuredMessage` objects. Their `metadata["memories"]` is never read, their memory blocks are never resolved or rendered.
- Remaining messages after condensation boundary (main loop :819-830) ARE individually formatted — memories rendered.

**Fresh condensing path (base.py:836-900):**
- The already-formatted `ret` list (all messages as `ModelMessage`s with JSON content including `userMemories`) is passed to `self.llmService.condenseContext(ret, ...)` at :844-853.
- The LLM produces a condensed text. Whether memory content survives into the summary depends entirely on the LLM's summarization — it's not structurally preserved.
- The condensed output `ModelMessage` has plain text `content`, NO structured `userMemories` field.
- New `condenseCache` entries built at :883-890 and persisted to `eRootMessage.metadata["condensedThread"]` at :893-898.

**Net result:** Only individually-formatted messages (keepFirstN + remaining tail) have memory blocks rendered. Condensed/summarized messages contribute nothing structured — their memories exist only in whatever the LLM chose to include in its summary text.

title: Dedup refactor blast radius: userMemories field removal + getThreadByMessageForLLM insertion points
content:
Complete reference for the user-memories context-deduplication refactor (2026-07-11, line numbers current). Supersedes/refines earlier getThreadByMessageForLLM analysis (5bf7c84a, 2026-07-09).

**Q: Blast radius of removing `EnsuredMessage.userMemories` field:**

Production code — 6 hits, ALL in `internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py`:
- :460 WRITE — `__init__` init: `self.userMemories: Optional[UserMemoriesDict] = None`
- :917 WRITE — `setUserMemories`: `self.userMemories = deepcopy(...)` (strips `id`)
- :960 READ — `resolveMemories`: `if self.userMemories is not None: return` (early-return guard)
- :981 WRITE — `resolveMemories`: `self.userMemories = deepcopy({...})` (from cache resolution)
- :1202 READ — `formatForLLM` JSON branch: `"userMemories": self.userMemories,` (emitted to LLM)
- :1359 READ — `__str__`: debug representation

Test code — ~40 hits across 3 files: `tests/bot/models/test_ensured_message.py` (lines 181-584), `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_llm_messages.py` (lines 1402-1406), `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_message_preprocessor.py` (lines 911-1020). All READs except test_ensured_message.py:306 (mutation test for deepcopy).

`lib/` has ZERO hits. `__slots__` entry to remove is `"userMemories"` at line 374 (the only memory-related slots are `"userMemories"` and `"metadata"`).

**getThreadByMessageForLLM dedup insertion points (base.py:710-900):**
Messages are built+formatted INLINE — each `fromDBChatMessage` is immediately followed by `toModelMessageList` in the same iteration (NOT a build-then-format two-phase). Ordering is OLDEST-FIRST. `toModelMessageList` is called at 3 sites:
1. **Branch A** (standalone, root_message_id is None): between :759-761 (build) and :762 (format) — single message, `excludeMemoryIds=None`.
2. **Condense-replay keepFirstN loop**: between :790-792 (build) and :793-800 (format).
3. **Main loop**: between :820-822 (build) and :823-830 (format).

A dedup loop (computing per-message `excludeMemoryIds`, then formatting) must slot BETWEEN build and format at each site. Since the list is oldest-first but dedup is newest→oldest, the loop must either pre-scan `dbMessageList` in reverse to build a cumulative `seenMemoryIds` set, or process in reverse.

**eRootMessage** (base.py:783) is built via `fromDBChatMessage` but NEVER formatted via `toModelMessageList` — it only exists to read/persist `condenseCache`. No dedup needed there. NO `fromERootMessage` factory method exists (common misconception — `eRootMessage` is a local variable, not a factory).

**EnsuredMessage factory methods:** `__init__` (:383), `fromMaxMessage` (:470), `fromTelegramMessage` (:567), `fromDBChatMessage` (:789 — the ONLY one with `injectMemories`/`cache` params), `_awaitMedia` (:1095, private helper).

title: metadata["memories"] content form NEVER written at runtime — only compact ID form
content:
Confirmed: The content form (`UserMemoriesDict` — `{permanent: [...], shortTerm: [...]}` with full content dicts) is NEVER written to `metadata["memories"]` at runtime. Only the compact ID form (`CompactMemoryIdsDict` — `{permanentIds: [...], shortTermIds: [...]}`) is written.

**Write sites to `metadata["memories"]`** (post-Phase-4):
1. `MessagePreprocessorHandler.injectMemories` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/message_preprocessor.py:129-132`) — writes `{permanentIds: [...], shortTermIds: [...]}` directly into metadata. Sole production write site.
2. `handleMention` text-reply bypass (`internal/bot/common/handlers/llm_messages.py:~726-733`) — whole-dict REPLACEMENT from DB JSON (`ensuredReply.metadata = metadata`). Brings in whatever was persisted, not a new shape.

**Read path:** `EnsuredMessage.formatForLLM` (`internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:~1130-1156`) reads `self.metadata.get("memories")`, checks for `permanentIds`/`shortTermIds` keys, and resolves them via `cache.getMemoriesByIds` into a LOCAL dict. It never mutates `self.metadata`. Legacy content-form rows are silently skipped (no `permanentIds`/`shortTermIds` keys → no resolution → `userMemories` key omitted).

`MetadataDict.memories` is typed as `CompactMemoryIdsDict` only (`internal/bot/models/message_metadata.py:257`) — NOT a union. The `scripts/clear_old_format_memories.py` script removes old-format `memories` keys from legacy DB rows.

title: Condense-replay entries MUST NOT participate in dedup seen-set
content:
Architect-review finding (2026-07-11) for memory-context-dedup plan v2. In `getThreadByMessageForLLM` (`base.py:710-900`), condensed/summarized messages (dropped at `:805-817`, plain-text `ModelMessage`s) MUST NOT contribute their memory IDs to the `seen` set in `computeMemoryExcludes`.

Why: condensed entries are in the MIDDLE (between keepFirstN at oldest and tail at newest). In newest→oldest processing, they'd be processed between tail and keepFirstN. If a memory M appears in both a condensed entry and a keepFirstN entry, including the condensed entry's ID in `seen` would cause the keepFirstN entry (older) to suppress M. But the condensed entry never RENDERS M (it's dropped). So M vanishes entirely from the context — a silent data loss bug.

The BUILD-then-DEDUP-then-FORMAT approach handles this correctly: the build phase constructs EnsuredMessages only for rendered rows (keepFirstN + sliced tail), skipping condensed middle entries. The condensed entries never enter the `computeMemoryExcludes` input list.

Additional condense-replay detail confirmed by the review: the keepFirstN loop (`:789-800`) and the summary loop (`:805-817`) are SEQUENTIAL in the current code (not interleaved). keepFirstN messages are ALL formatted first, THEN condensed summaries appended. This makes the restructure a clean 3-way split: keepFirstN → summaries → tail. The slicing logic (`dbMessageList = dbMessageList[skippedMessages:]` at `:817`) must be extracted into the build phase to determine which rows are tail.

title: Phase ordering: additive-first, removals-last for codebase-green-each-phase
content:
Architect-review finding (2026-07-11) for memory-context-dedup plan v2. The original plan's Phase 1 removed the required `injectMemories` param from `fromDBChatMessage`, breaking 14 callers immediately and leaving the codebase non-compiling until Phase 5. This violates the project's mandatory `make test` after every change rule.

Corrected phase ordering (6 phases, each independently green):
- Phase 1: ADDITIVE ONLY — new params with defaults (`cache=None`, `excludeMemoryIds=None`), new methods (`getMemoryIds`, `computeMemoryExcludes`, `warmMemoriesByIds`), new formatForLLM render algorithm. No removals. Codebase stays green.
- Phase 2: Wire dedup into `getThreadByMessageForLLM` (BUILD→DEDUP→FORMAT) + cache-warm in injectMemories. Add `injectMemories=False` default to `fromDBChatMessage` for transitional compatibility. Green.
- Phase 3: Wire remaining handler paths (handleMention, handleReply fallback, handleRandomMessage, media) with `cache=self.cache`. Green.
- Phase 4: REMOVE dead code atomically — `fromDBChatMessage` signature change + all remaining caller updates + remove `resolveMemories`/`userMemories` field/slot + repurpose `setUserMemories`. One atomic phase. Green at boundary.
- Phase 5: Test updates (blast radius: test_ensured_message.py, test_message_preprocessor.py, test_llm_messages.py).
- Phase 6: Doc sync.

This is a general principle: when removing a required parameter used by many callers, make it optional first (additive), wire new paths, THEN remove in a single atomic phase with all caller updates. Never leave the codebase non-compiling between phases.

title: Lint tooling: pyflakes does NOT flag unused function args, pyright-basic does NOT enable reportUnusedParameter
content:
Project-specific tooling fact confirmed during code review (2026-07-11).

**flake8/pyflakes does NOT report unused function/method parameters.** Only unused local variables and unused imports. So a method like `def foo(self, x: int) -> None:` where `x` is never referenced in the body will pass `make lint` cleanly.

**pyright (basic mode, as configured in this repo) does NOT enable `reportUnusedParameter`.** That check exists in pyright but is off by default and not turned on in this project's config. So unused params also pass `pyright` cleanly.

**Contrast with exception bindings:** pyflakes DOES flag unused exception bindings via F841 (`except Exception as e:` where `e` is never used) — see memory 56b62389. But regular function args are exempt.

**Practical implication:** It is safe in this repo to add a method parameter for API symmetry even when it's unused in the method body (e.g., `warmMemoriesByIds(entries, chatId)` where `chatId` exists only for signature parallelism with `getMemoriesByIds`). The docstring should explain why the param exists. This will NOT trigger any lint failure.

Note: If the project ever switches to ruff, `ARG001` (unused-function-argument) would flag these — but that rule is not active today.

title: getMemoryIds None-valued compact keys bug — or [] coalescing convention
content:
Bug fixed 2026-07-11 in `EnsuredMessage.getMemoryIds` (`internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py`):

**The bug:** `getMemoryIds` used `in`-checks to guard against missing compact keys, then called `set(memories["permanentIds"])`. But `in`-checks only verify key *presence*, not truthiness. When `metadata["memories"]` had a key present-but-`None` (e.g. `{"permanentIds": None, "shortTermIds": ["id1"]}`), both `in`-checks passed (both keys exist), then `set(None)` raised `TypeError`. This violated the method's documented "never raises on unexpected shape" contract.

**The fix:** Replace `in`-checks + direct indexing with `.get(key) or []` coalescing:
```python
memories = self.metadata.get("memories")
if not isinstance(memories, dict):
    return set()
return set(memories.get("permanentIds") or []) | set(memories.get("shortTermIds") or [])
```

**Convention takeaway (broadly applicable):** When reading optional dict values that may be present-but-`None`, prefer `dict.get(key) or []` over `key in dict` guards. The `or []` coalesces `None`/missing/non-truthy uniformly in one expression, whereas `in`-checks only detect key presence and silently pass through `None` values. The sibling method `resolveMemories` (same file) already used `or []` — this fix brings `getMemoryIds` in line.

**Minor behavioral note:** The old code returned `set()` when EITHER compact key was missing. The new code returns the union of whatever non-None values ARE present (e.g. `{"permanentIds": ["a"]}` → `{"a"}`). For the legacy content form `{"permanent": [...], "shortTerm": [...]}` (neither compact key), both old and new return `set()` — so the docstring example still holds.

Test: `test_getMemoryIds_noneValuedCompactKeys` in `tests/bot/models/test_ensured_message.py` (new `TestGetMemoryIds` class). Test count went 3109 → 3110.

title: Behavioral delta: stale-ID messages now omit userMemories key entirely (was empty-cohort dict)
content:
Code review finding (2026-07-11, code-reviewer/glm-5.2) for Phase 2 lazy resolution.

**The delta:** When `metadata["memories"]` carries compact IDs but NONE resolve from cache/DB (e.g., memories soft-deleted, negative-cached as `None`), the new `formatForLLM` code uses `if permanentEntries or shortTermEntries:` before building the output dict — so `resolvedMemories` stays `None` → the `userMemories` key is OMITTED entirely from JSON output.

OLD behavior (pre-Phase 2): `resolveMemories` would set `self.userMemories = deepcopy({"permanent": [], "shortTerm": []})` (truthy dict with empty lists), and old `formatForLLM` would EMIT `{"permanent": [], "shortTerm": []}` in the JSON.

**This is distinct from memory 60816181** (which documents the general `if v` truthiness filter in `formatForLLM`). That covers the `userMemories=None` case. This specifically covers the UNDOCUMENTED behavioral change for the "IDs exist but none resolve" case — which includes both zero-memory messages AND stale-reference messages (deleted memories).

**Impact:** Arguably an improvement (empty cohort block is LLM noise), but it's an undocumented behavioral delta. Worth a one-line note in the `formatForLLM` docstring or the plan's known-limitations section.

**Suggestion:** Add: "When all referenced IDs fail to resolve, the `userMemories` key is omitted entirely (previously emitted an empty-cohort dict)."

title: Behavior change: thread messages now RENDER memories (was cache=None/omitted) — increases token count, may trigger condenseContext more often
content:
Second-order consequence of the Phase 1–3 dedup refactor, flagged by code-review on 2026-07-11 (not previously documented).

Before the refactor: the keepFirstN formatting loop and the tail formatting loop in `getThreadByMessageForLLM` (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py) called `toModelMessageList` WITHOUT a `cache` argument. This meant `formatForLLM` received `cache=None`, and memories (`userMemories`) were OMITTED entirely from those thread messages.

After the refactor: both loops now pass `cache=self.cache` (forced — `cache` became a required keyword-only param in Phase 1/2). So thread messages now RENDER memories, filtered by `excludeMemoryIds`. This is the intended design (the whole point of memory-injection dedup), but it has a measurable side effect:

- The token count of `ret` (the rendered thread) INCREASES because memory blocks are now present in keepFirstN and tail messages.
- Higher token counts can trigger the fresh-condensing path (`condenseContext` on `ret`, base.py ~:908) MORE OFTEN than before — i.e., the condensing threshold is reached with fewer user messages.
- This is expected behavior, not a bug, but operators/devs should be aware that condensing frequency may change after this refactor deploys, purely from memory content being present in the thread.

Note: Branch A (single message, `root_message_id is None`) also passes `excludeMemoryIds=set()` and now passes `cache=self.cache` too — so even single-message LLM calls now include rendered memories (no dedup, but memories ARE injected). Verify this is intended for the single-message path.

title: Pyright gotcha: invalid/removed kwargs make pyright infer return type as Unknown — causes cascade type-narrowing failures
content:
When a function call passes a parameter that no longer exists on the callee (e.g., after a signature change removes a kwarg), pyright infers the call's return type as `Unknown` rather than the declared return type. This causes cascade failures at the call site.

**Observed during Phase 4 memory-compaction cleanup (2026-07-11):**
After `EnsuredMessage.fromDBChatMessage()` lost its `injectMemories` and `cache` kwargs, callers still passing `injectMemories=False` produced a pyright error at a DIFFERENT line — the `_doSummarization(ensuredMessage=ensuredMessage)` call ~3 lines later:

```
summarization.py:684:28 - error: Argument of type "Unknown | EnsuredMessage | None" cannot be assigned to parameter "ensuredMessage" of type "EnsuredMessage"
```

The variable `ensuredMessage` was declared `Optional[EnsuredMessage] = None`, then reassigned inside `if ensuredMessage is None:` via `fromDBChatMessage(...)`. Since the `fromDBChatMessage` call had an invalid kwarg, pyright couldn't resolve its return type → returned `Unknown` → the narrowing after the `if` block produced `Unknown | EnsuredMessage | None` → type mismatch with the non-optional parameter.

**Lesson:** When chasing pyright errors after a signature change, an error at the CONSUMPTION site (where the variable is used) can be caused by an invalid parameter at the PRODUCTION site (where the variable is assigned), even if pyright also reports the invalid parameter separately. Fix the invalid-parameter error first and the cascade error will resolve automatically.

title: Convention: docs/plans/ and ADRs are immutable historical records — status stamps only, never rewrite bodies
content:
Confirmed convention (2026-07-11, during Phase 6 doc sync of the memory-context-dedup refactor):

## docs/plans/ — historical, status stamps only
Plan documents (`docs/plans/*.md`) are point-in-time planning records. When the plan ships:
- Update ONLY the status line (e.g. `PLANNED` → `IMPLEMENTED`) + add a brief completion note.
- Do NOT rewrite the plan body to remove references to symbols/patterns that were later changed or removed. The body documents the as-designed state at planning time.
- Example: `docs/plans/memory-compaction-v1.md` references `setUserMemories`/`resolveMemories` throughout (both later removed). These were left as-is because the plan is a historical record. Only the dedup plans (v1, v2) got status → IMPLEMENTED stamps.

## ADRs (docs/llm/architecture.md) — immutable decision records
Architecture Decision Records are immutable once written:
- To supersede an ADR's decisions, ADD a new ADR (incrementing the number) with a "Relationship to ADR-NNN" paragraph explicitly stating what changed.
- Do NOT rewrite the old ADR's body. It remains a snapshot of the decision as it was made.
- The old ADR's "Follow-up refactor" notes and "Consequences" bullets may reference superseded patterns — this is acceptable because they're explicitly framed as historical snapshots and the newer ADR's supersession paragraph makes the transition clear.

## teamlead-memory.md — [SUPERSEDED date] markers
Durable memory entries in `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` use `[SUPERSEDED YYYY-MM-DD — reason]` markers to flag superseded content rather than rewriting. This preserves the historical chain of decisions.

This convention generalizes the existing `docs/archive/` policy (memory 561b6201) to the plans and ADR layers.

title: Memory resolution kwargs enforced by pyright, NOT an AST guard
content:
The enforcement mechanism for the `formatForLLM`/`toModelMessage`/`toModelMessageList` memory kwargs is **pyright on the `cache` parameter's required keyword-only signature** (no default — verified at ensured_message.py:1072, :1202, :1275). Every render call MUST pass `cache=`, and pyright errors on any caller that omits it. **`excludeMemoryIds` carries a default of `= None`** (ensured_message.py:1073), so pyright does NOT flag its omission — only `cache` is truly required. There is NO AST value-checking guard (it can't robustly distinguish chat-context paths where `cache=self.cache` from non-chat/TEXT paths where `cache=None`).

Value-correctness (`cache=self.cache` on chat-context paths, `cache=None` on non-chat/TEXT paths) is upheld by the call-site audit and the test suite, NOT by a structural value-checking guard.

`tests/test_memory_resolution_coverage.py` retains only **Check-2** (the `setUserMemories`/metadata-bypass ban), now a vacuous regression guard — `setUserMemories` was removed in Phase 4, so Check-2 passes trivially on the current tree (2 sanity tests, not 9). Check-1 (which checked the `fromDBChatMessage cache=` invariant) was REMOVED entirely in Phase 4.

Docs in `docs/llm/architecture.md` ADR-018 (~line 688) describe the real mechanism. NOTE: ADR-018 slightly overstates it by claiming both `cache` and `excludeMemoryIds` have no defaults — only `cache` is truly required; `excludeMemoryIds` defaults to `None`.

title: ADR-017 follow-up note (architecture.md ~651-654) still stale — describes deleted Check-1 invariant
content:
`docs/llm/architecture.md` ~lines 651-654 (ADR-017's follow-up note) still describes Check-1 of `tests/test_memory_resolution_coverage.py` as verifying that each `fromDBChatMessage(injectMemories=<truthy>)` render site passes a non-None `cache=` keyword. 

**This is FALSE:** Check-1 was deleted entirely in Phase 4 of the memory-compaction refactor. The bullet is stale doc drift.

This was noticed during the Gate-2 fix batch (2026-07-11) but left untouched because it is a DIFFERENT claim from the render-method-scanning AST guard false-claim that was fixed (ADR-018 ~line 679 + handlers.md ~line 29). The ADR-017 bullet describes the old `fromDBChatMessage` invariant, not the render-method scan.

**STATUS: UNFIXED.** Should be corrected in a future doc pass to state that Check-1 was removed (not repurposed).

title: BLOCKER: getThreadByMessageForLLM maintainability rewrite regressed keepFirstN dedup (set() instead of excludes)
content:
Code-review finding (2026-07-11, review-only, verdict: Needs fixes). A "maintainability rewrite" of `getThreadByMessageForLLM` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py`) replaced the `computeMemoryExcludes`-based BUILD→DEDUP→FORMAT structure with inline tail-loop accumulation. This introduced a BLOCKER dedup regression.

**The bug:** The keepFirstN (root) message formatting changed from `excludeMemoryIds=excludes[idx]` (computed via `computeMemoryExcludes([*keepFirstN, *tail])`) to `excludeMemoryIds=set()` (base.py:835). The comment `# Keep memories for root message` was added as justification, but it contradicts the established dedup contract (each memory appears EXACTLY ONCE at its latest occurrence) and was NOT reflected in ADR-018, architecture.md, or TestDedupIndexAlignment.

**Impact:** Scoped to the condense-replay path (`condenseCache` non-empty). When a persistent memory ID appears in BOTH the root message (oldest, keepFirstN) and a newer tail message, it now renders TWICE — once fully at the root (via set()) and once at the newer message (newest occurrence in tail). The non-condense path is unaffected (all messages go through the reversed tail loop).

**Root cause lesson:** Hand-rolling inline dedup in the tail loop structurally CANNOT dedup keepFirstN against tail without a pre-build step. The `computeMemoryExcludes` helper was designed precisely to compute cross-boundary excludes. Replacing it with inline accumulation is how the boundary dedup gets silently lost.

**Test suite does NOT catch this:** `getThreadByMessageForLLM` is mocked away in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_llm_messages.py:600,629`. `TestDedupIndexAlignment` (tests/bot/common/handlers/test_base.py) reproduces the consumption-indexing arithmetic IN-TEST rather than calling production. So `make test` is green (~3088) even with the regression. This PROVES the test-gap flagged in memory 9f0075dc is live and exploitable.

**Additional finding from same rewrite:** `computeMemoryExcludes` (base.py:111) now has ZERO production callers (orphaned/dead). The dedup algorithm is hand-rolled inline in TWO places (getThreadByMessageForLLM tail + handleRandomMessage loop). Docs (architecture.md:672, handlers.md, user-memories.md, ADR-018) still describe it as the live mechanism.

**Behavior change (likely intentional, consistency improvement):** keepFirstN/tail render calls changed from `cache=self.cache` (unconditional) to `cache=self.cache if needMemories else None`, making them consistent with Branch A (base.py:800). Edge case: messages with stale memory IDs (injection enabled at save, disabled later) now omit memories where they previously rendered them.

**Recommended fix:** Revert getThreadByMessageForLLM to the committed `computeMemoryExcludes`-based BUILD→DEDUP→FORMAT (fixes the BLOCKER, restores DRY, makes docs true again). If a flatter shape is desired, keepFirstN exclude must be ∪(tail message IDs), not set().

title: handleRandomMessage non-reply dedup NOW IMPLEMENTED and correct (supersedes deferred status)
content:
State change (2026-07-11, verified by code review): `handleRandomMessage` non-reply path (`internal/bot/common/handlers/llm_messages.py`) now HAS memory deduplication, implemented correctly. This supersedes earlier memory `b68d6075` which documented this path as having dedup "previously deferred."

**Implementation (verified correct):**
- `excludedMemoryIds: MutableSet[str] = ensuredMessage.getMemoryIds()` — seeds `seen` with the CURRENT message's IDs. The current message is treated as the newest (renders all its memories). (llm_messages.py:887)
- The context loop iterates `getChatMessagesSince` results which return `ORDER BY c.date DESC` = newest→oldest. So the loop walks newest→oldest. (llm_messages.py:889-917)
- For each context message: `excludeMemoryIds=excludedMemoryIds` is applied BEFORE `excludedMemoryIds.update(eMsg.getMemoryIds())`. This is the correct `excludes[i]=ids∩seen; seen|=ids` contract. (llm_messages.py:910, 914)
- Current-message skip (`storedMsg["message_id"] == ensuredMessage.messageId`) works — `MessageId.__eq__` handles int (TG) and str (Max). `getMemoryIds()` returns a fresh set, so seeding can't alias/corrupt metadata. (llm_messages.py:894)
- Current message appended LAST with `excludeMemoryIds=set()` → renders all its memories. (llm_messages.py:956)
- Assembly: `extendleft(reversed(...))` over newest→oldest input yields oldest→newest; current appended last. (llm_messages.py:907-913)
- `cache=self.cache if injectMemories else None` on all render calls. (llm_messages.py:909, 955)
- Probability gating and abstention logic untouched — dedup changes only memory content, not WHEN the handler answers.

**NIT:** When `injectMemories=False`, the `excludedMemoryIds` seed/updates compute nothing rendered (cache=None → formatForLLM omits userMemories). Harmless wasted work.

**Consistency note:** This path uses inline accumulation (not `computeMemoryExcludes`) because of the `randomContext` early-break logic making pre-building awkward. The inline approach is correct here.

title: RESOLVED: computeMemoryExcludes DELETED — inline dedup is final design, root exemption ACCEPTED (supersedes blocker 62f59e19)
content:

The code-review blocker in memory `62f59e19` — which flagged the inline-dedup rewrite of `getThreadByMessageForLLM` as a BLOCKER regression (keepFirstN root getting `excludeMemoryIds=set()` instead of computed excludes) and recommended REVERTING to the `computeMemoryExcludes`-based BUILD→DEDUP→FORMAT approach — has been RESOLVED by the user choosing the OPPOSITE path.

Consequence: a memory in BOTH the root and a newer tail message may appear twice. The user deliberately accepted this to keep the assembly code simple.
