title: Docs-sync convention: sync existing surfaces, don't create new docs, flag gaps
content:
Convention confirmed during the `condensing_prompt` feature docs-sync (2026-07-17) using the `update-project-docs` skill.

**The boundary of a docs-sync pass:**
- A docs-sync pass (the `update-project-docs` skill) updates EXISTING documentation surfaces to match current behavior — it syncs what's already written to reality.
- It does NOT create NEW documentation for previously-undocumented features. Creating new docs for previously-undocumented features is a separate, deliberate doc-writing task (the implementer's/architect's job), not something to do during a sync.
- When checking staleness: if a surface does NOT document the changed area, leave it alone — no false update, no new creation. Only update surfaces that already document the touched area and are now stale.
- Pre-existing documentation gaps should be FLAGGED in the sync report (for routing to a dedicated docs task), not silently filled during the sync.

This prevents scope creep during docs-sync tasks. Applied correctly, a feature that adds params to tools whose params were never documented results in zero doc edits — just a gap flag in the report.

Source: docs-writer agent reasoning during `condensing_prompt` sync, consistent with the skill's staleness principle ("if a surface does not mention the touched area, no update is needed").

title: Test files carry stale line-number citations — cite by symbol name
content:
Extension of the line-number-drift family (memories 49b5f7d3 = skill docs use ~prefix + grep anchor; dbec997e = AGENTS.md/tasks.md prefer plain file paths): **test files** are a third vector. Tests that pin "production uses EXACTLY this conversion at line N" embed non-executable line-number citations in comments/docstrings that rot silently when production code shifts — and because they're non-executable, no test fails to alert you.

Concrete instance (2026-07-17): `tests/dependencies/test_html_to_markdown.py` had 3 citations (`yandex_search.py:410-426`, `:412-415`, `:417`) pointing at the HTML-to-Markdown conversion block. After the `condensing_prompt` feature added ~90 lines above, the block moved to ~489-507.

**Resolution (the correct approach, validated):** rather than re-pinning to new line numbers (which just re-stales on the next nearby edit), convert each citation to a durable **symbol reference** — e.g. "the `html_to_markdown.convert(...)` block in `_llmToolGetUrlContent`, `internal/bot/common/handlers/yandex_search.py`". Symbol names are stable anchors; line numbers are not. All 3 were converted and `make test` stayed green (3381 passed, 11 skipped).

**One wrinkle when converting:** a symbol name + file path is often longer than a short `:NNN`, which can push a docstring/comment line past the 120-char flake8 E501 limit. black does NOT reflow docstrings (see memory 32a5456e), so wrap the prose manually across lines. The `::` RST literal-block marker stays valid at the end of the wrapped paragraph.

General lesson: when auditing for line-number rot, grep test files (`tests/`) too, not just docs. `make check-docs` only validates local markdown LINKS resolve — it does NOT verify cited line numbers, so this drift is undetected by tooling.

title: condensing_prompt feature (implemented)
content:
**YandexSearchHandler + condensing_prompt feature (IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-17)**

Handler: `internal/bot/common/handlers/yandex_search.py` (`YandexSearchHandler`, registered `internal/bot/common/handlers/manager.py:88`). Two LLM tools:
- `web_search` (`ToolName.WEB_SEARCH`) → `_llmToolWebSearch`. Params: query, return_page_content, enable_content_filter, max_results, **condensing_prompt** (NEW), **max_size** (NEW, forwarded per-page).
- `get_url_content` (`ToolName.GET_URL_CONTENT`) → `_llmToolGetUrlContent`. Params: url, parse_to_markdown, max_size, **condensing_prompt** (NEW).
- Tool-param names are snake_case (documented exception to camelCase rule — matches sibling params). All other identifiers camelCase.

**condensing_prompt feature:** optional STRING param; None/""/whitespace-only → falls back to per-chat `ChatSettingsKey.DOCUMENT_CONDENSING_PROMPT` default. Normalized via `_normalizeCondensingPrompt` static method (`.strip()`, empty→None) computed ONCE before cache lookup. `effectivePrompt = normalizedCustom or chatSettings[DOCUMENT_CONDENSING_PROMPT].toStr()` used as the condensing system message. `web_search` forwards both `max_size` + `condensing_prompt` raw to per-page `_llmToolGetUrlContent` (this also CLOSED a pre-existing gap where web_search never forwarded max_size — always used default 10240). Condensing triggers when `len(content) >= max_size` (len=CHARS, not bytes).

**Cache (changed):** `URL_CONTENT_CONDENSED` ctor switched `JsonKeyGenerator[Dict](hash=False)`→`hash=True`. Key dict now `{"url":url, "max_size":max_size, "condensing_prompt": normalizedCustomPrompt}` — condensing_prompt holds the CUSTOM prompt or None (NOT the resolved per-chat default, to keep lazy chatSettings fetch). Switch to hash mode = **SHA-512 hexdigest** (128 chars, `lib/cache/key_generator.py:207`, `hashlib.sha512(jsonStr.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()`, sort_keys=True default, deterministic). Invalidates all existing condensed entries (1h TTL + 7-day aggressive cleanup → acceptable). Accepted tradeoff: changing a chat's default prompt won't invalidate default cache till 1h TTL (same as pre-change).

**Design doc:** `docs/plans/condensing-prompt-tool-param.md` (authoritative spec, §5 detailed design matched impl item-by-item per Gate 2 review).

**Tests:** `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_yandex_search.py` (NEW, 15 tests): `TestNormalizeCondensingPrompt`×5, `TestCondensingPrompt`×8 (incl. negative no-condense case + cache .set write assertion), `TestWebSearchForwarding`×2. Patterns: module-level helpers `_makeHandler`/`_makeConfigManager` (MUST stub `getYandexSearchConfig()`→`{"enabled":True,...}` else `__init__` raises RuntimeError)/`_makeDatabase`/`_makeEnsuredMessage` (MUST be real EnsuredMessage — production does isinstance check)/`_makeChatSettings` (complete dict incl. DOCUMENT_CONDENSING_PROMPT/CHAT_MODEL/CONDENSING_MODEL — production subscripts directly). Capture `generateText` (NOT generateTextViaLLM) via `kwargs["prompt"]`, `prompt[0].content`=effective prompt. Mock `_downloadUrl`→`{"done":True,"content":"x"*20000,"contentType":"text/plain"}` (text/plain bypasses html_to_markdown branch; content must be ≥max_size to trigger condense). Post-construction override caches/llmService. Relies on autouse `resetLlmServiceSingleton`+`resetProxyServiceSingleton`.

**Verification:** `make format lint` clean; `make test` 3381 passed/0 failed (3366 baseline + 15 new); `make check-docs` 1556 links/0 broken. Gate 1 (handler) + Gate 1 (tests, 3 MINOR+1 NIT all fixed) + Gate 2 whole-work all passed, merge-ready. CHANGELOG `### Added` entry under `## [Unreleased]` (line 14). No doc surface documents tool params or cache key format, so no .md/.txt sync was needed (verified). `tests/dependencies/test_html_to_markdown.py` stale `yandex_search.py:NNN` refs converted to durable symbol refs.

**KNOWN PRE-EXISTING FOLLOW-UPS (out of scope, candidates for separate fixes):**
- `yandex_search.py:434` `max_size` docstring says "bytes" but gate uses `len()`=chars.
- `yandex_search.py:173` `max_results` description "Default: 3" but code default is `5`.
- `yandex_search.py:371` `doc["url"]` referenced inside `except` block — potential NameError if iterator empty (pre-existing bug, NOT introduced here).
- `DOCUMENT_CONDENSING_PROMPT` chat setting is undocumented in `docs/llm/configuration.md` chat-settings reference + no param-level docs for the yandex tools anywhere in `docs/llm/` (pre-existing doc gap).

title: doc["url"] wrong-variable bug in _llmToolWebSearch except block (stale NameError)
content:
PRE-EXISTING latent bug in `internal/bot/common/handlers/yandex_search.py:370-371`, inside `_llmToolWebSearch`'s `return_page_content` path. Surfaced during the Gate 2 review of the `condensing_prompt` feature (2026-07-17) but NOT introduced by it — excluded from that review's scope as pre-existing.

## The bug
The page-fetch loop iterates `for i, contentDict in enumerate(urlContentList):` (line 361). Each `contentDict` has keys `url`, `description`, `fetcher`. The `try` block and the correct fallback lines (366, 373) reference `contentDict["url"]`. But the `except` block at line 371 references `doc["url"]`:

```python
except Exception as e:
    logger.error(f"Error during fetching content of {doc["url"]}: {e}")  # BUG: wrong variable
```

`doc` is a STALE loop variable from the outer `for doc in group` build-loop (line ~350) that constructs `urlContentList`. It is NOT the doc corresponding to the page that failed.

## Two consequences
1. **Wrong URL in error log**: always logs the URL of the LAST doc from the last group, never the page that actually failed.
2. **NameError on empty search results**: if `searchResult["groups"]` is empty or all groups are empty lists, the `doc` variable is never bound, so `doc["url"]` raises `NameError` — masking the original exception and crashing the tool call.

## Fix
Line 371 should use `contentDict["url"]` (matching lines 366 and 373): `logger.error(f"Error during fetching content of {contentDict['url']}: {e}")`.

title: /refine-memory slashcommand automates teamlead-memory.md archival
content:
The opencode slashcommand at `.opencode/commands/refine-memory.md` (added 2026-07-18) automates the established `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` → `docs/llm/memories/<slug>.md` archival workflow (previously manual; see memory 5252a21d).

**Invocation:** Routed to the `teamlead` agent with `subtask: true` (non-interactive, best-effort, mirrors `/changelog`'s posture). teamlead reads the command body as a prompt and delegates the mechanical extraction to `docs-writer` (per teamlead's pure-delegator role).

**What it does:** Scans `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md`, classifies each section as EXTRACT / KEEP / JUDGMENT-CALL, then for each EXTRACT section:
- Creates `docs/llm/memories/<slug>.md` (kebab-case slug; reuse existing slug if topic already covered, else new file)
- New file header: `# <Original Section Heading>` + a one-line context note: `Archived durable notes from [`teamlead-memory.md`](../teamlead-memory.md) (extracted <YYYY-MM-DD>). See the live compact memory there for cross-cutting rules and workflow lessons.`
- Pastes section body verbatim, fixing relative link depth (one extra `../` — e.g. `../../internal/foo.py` from teamlead-memory.md becomes `../../../internal/foo.py` from memories/<slug>.md)
- In teamlead-memory.md: keeps the heading, replaces body with stub `See [`memories/<slug>.md`](memories/<slug>.md) — <one-line summary>.`
- Adds alphabetical bullet to `docs/llm/memories/index.md` "Available Files" list
- Updates the "Task-Specific Memory Files" paragraph (~line 24) of teamlead-memory.md

**Extraction signals:** dated headings (e.g. "verified 2026-07-15"), file-path-scoped headings, post-mortem/implementation-log tone. KEEP signals: cross-cutting rules, repo-wide conventions, workflow lessons, user preferences.

**Verification gate:** `make check-docs` (NOT `make test` — no source changed). The command's own file is excluded from the checker (see separate gotcha memory about `.opencode/` exclusion).

**Hard rules encoded:** NEVER touch `.opencode/memory.jsonl`; never fabricate links; short/cross-cutting sections stay in main file.

title: /review-large slashcommand: routed to teamlead, stops at §6 Step 1 (no auto-remediation)
content:
As of 2026-07-18, `.opencode/commands/review-large.md` exists. This CORRECTS the stale claim in memory 8ee532cc (surveyed 2026-07-15) that ".opencode/commands/ does NOT exist yet" — the dir now contains at least `changelog.md` and `review-large.md`.

**`/review-large` design (the non-obvious decisions, not restating the file body):**
- **Routed to `teamlead`** — the explicit audience named in the methodology doc `docs/llm/reviewing-large-changes.md` header. teamlead orchestrates the per-batch `code-reviewer` dispatches (and `explore` for git invocations, since teamlead has no bash tool — see memories 1e6bd9fb / 8e83d6f7).
- **Deliberately OMITS `subtask: true`** in frontmatter. This is the first concrete application of the omit-subtask-for-interactive rule (memory 58e5934f): the command is long-running and surfaces consolidated findings to the user at the end, so it must run interactively at the top level, NOT as a non-interactive subtask. `/changelog` (which produces a subtask result) keeps `subtask: true`; `/review-large` (interactive) drops it.
- **Stops at §6 Step 1** of the methodology (consolidated findings table) and does NOT auto-remediate. §6 Steps 2-4 (fix Critical/Important, process user-approved rec/nit, final integration pass) require explicit user direction. This reflects a stated user preference: the review surfaces findings; the user decides what to fix (typically via follow-up work or `/changelog` for any resulting entries).
- **Thin wrapper** — `docs/llm/reviewing-large-changes.md` is the authoritative methodology (423 lines). The command fixes scope and stopping point; section numbers in the command body (§1.1, §2, §2.2, §3, §3.3, §4, §4.4, §5, §5.1, §6, §6.1) must match that doc exactly.

**Slashcommand authoring conventions confirmed by building this command:**
- Mirror `.opencode/commands/changelog.md` as the structural template (frontmatter shape, arg handling via `$ARGUMENTS`, explicit posture statements, no filler).
- For doc-only / markdown-only command files, the verification gate is `make check-docs` (read-only markdown link checker → `scripts/check_docs.py`), NOT `make test` — consistent with the docs-only gate convention in memory dd5a9470.
- Verification result baseline for reference: `make check-docs` reports "Checked 107 markdown files, 1556 links; 0 broken." as of this date.

title: check_docs.py excludes .opencode/ entirely — slashcommand/agent files not link-validated
content:
`scripts/check_docs.py` (the `make check-docs` checker) excludes the entire `.opencode/` directory from scanning via `_EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES` (line 70, `scripts/check_docs.py`). Comment on line 69: "`.opencode/` holds agent working state, not authored docs."

**Consequence:** Any markdown file under `.opencode/` — including `.opencode/commands/*.md` slashcommand files, `.opencode/agents/*.md` agent definitions, `.opencode/skills/*` — is NOT validated by `make check-docs`. Broken links in those files will pass the checker silently. This is intentional: those files are agent working state, not authored user-facing docs.

This complements the two known non-obvious behaviors already documented in memory 7db5883b (archive source/target asymmetry, no `:line` verification): the full set of check_docs scan exclusions is:
- `_EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES` (name-based, any depth): `.git`, `.venv`, `venv`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache`, `htmlcov`, `__pycache__`, `node_modules`, `.tox`, `build`, `dist`, `.opencode`
- `_EXCLUDED_PATH_PREFIXES` (position-based, `(root, child)` pairs): `("docs", "archive")`, `("docs", "templates")`, `("lib", "ext_modules")`

**Practical impact:** When adding a new slashcommand file under `.opencode/commands/`, manually verify any markdown links it contains against the repo — do not rely on `make check-docs` to catch them. The `/refine-memory` command file (added 2026-07-18) deliberately uses template-style links (e.g. `memories/<slug>.md`) that would be flagged if scanned, so the exclusion is load-bearing for it.

title: Authoring gotcha: fabricated filesystem refs in .opencode/ evade all checkers
content:
When authoring or reviewing `.opencode/commands/*.md` or `.opencode/agents/*.md`, `make check-docs` provides ZERO validation because the entire `.opencode/` directory is excluded from `scripts/check_docs.py` (see memory dd77405d). This means EVERY internal reference — markdown links, inline-code paths, prose file counts, slug names, section numbers — must be manually verified against the actual filesystem and source docs.

**Concrete failure mode (discovered 2026-07-18 reviewing `/refine-memory`):** The command body claimed "24 task-specific memory files currently live under `docs/llm/memories/`" (actual: 23) and listed "Existing slugs to mirror: `llm-tool-call-healing`, `test-speedup`, `dependency-usage-tests`, `db-cache-cleanup`" — ALL FOUR fabricated; none exist. Root cause: the author confused the *post-extraction target state* (slugs that WILL be created when sections are archived) with the *current state* (files that exist now). The four fabricated slugs correspond to sections still living un-archived in `teamlead-memory.md`. This violated the command's OWN hard rule ("NEVER fabricate links, paths, or counts").

**Review technique that caught it:** glob/grep the actual filesystem for every cited slug/path/count; read the target doc and verify every section name and number exists. For `/refine-memory`, this meant `ls docs/llm/memories/` (count), `grep -r <slug> docs/llm/memories/` (existence), and cross-checking every section name in the KEEP/JUDGMENT CALLS lists against `grep '^## ' docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md`.

**Prevention rule for authors:** before committing a slashcommand body that names files/counts/sections, run the glob/grep yourself and confirm each reference resolves. Do not describe a workflow's *output* as if it already exists.

title: explore and general are built-in agents with NO local .opencode/agents/*.md file
content:
The `.opencode/agents/` directory contains exactly 7 locally-configured agent files: `architect.md`, `code-analyst.md`, `code-reviewer.md`, `debugger.md`, `docs-writer.md`, `software-developer.md`, `teamlead.md`.

`explore` and `general` are NOT among them — they are built-in/global opencode agents with no local config file. They are referenced in `teamlead.md`'s task permissions (`"explore": allow`, `"general": allow`) and in slashcommand bodies (e.g. `/review-large` says "delegate to `explore` or `general`"), but attempting to read `.opencode/agents/explore.md` returns file-not-found.

**Practical consequences:**
- You cannot customize `explore` or `general` behavior, permissions, or model by editing a local file.
- To understand what `explore` can do (e.g. whether it has bash access for `git rev-parse`), you must rely on opencode's built-in defaults, not a local config you can inspect.
- When a command or agent delegates git/read work to `explore`, trust that opencode's built-in explore supports read-only bash (git diff, git rev-parse, etc.) — this is the established pattern per teamlead-memory.md ("The `explore` subagent ... reliable for read-only work").
- Do NOT waste cycles searching for `.opencode/agents/explore.md` or `.opencode/agents/general.md` — they do not exist.

title: /refine-memory: canonical verified slugs for style references (replaces fabricated list)
content:
The original `/refine-memory` command body (`.opencode/commands/refine-memory.md`) fabricated four slug names — `llm-tool-call-healing`, `test-speedup`, `dependency-usage-tests`, `db-cache-cleanup` — as "existing slugs to mirror". NONE existed in `docs/llm/memories/`. This was a concrete instance of the broader gotcha that `.opencode/` files evade `make check-docs` (see memory dd77405d), so fabricated refs survive undetected.

**Corrected (2026-07-18 code-review pass):** the command now cites four REAL, verified slugs as style references (each confirmed present in `docs/llm/memories/index.md`):
- `chat-history-search`
- `proxy-lifecycle`
- `use-tools-filtering`
- `db-maintenance-scripts`

The bullet now also makes the prospective-vs-existing distinction explicit: "Mirror the naming style of existing slugs like … (verify the current inventory against `docs/llm/memories/index.md`). For sections being newly extracted, pick a new descriptive kebab-case slug that does not collide with an existing one."

**Lesson for agents editing slashcommand files:** every slug/path/section-name cited in a `.opencode/` file MUST be manually verified against the live source — `make check-docs` provides zero coverage there. The full inventory of `docs/llm/memories/*.md` (as of 2026-07-18, 23 task-specific files + `index.md`) is the source of truth; do not trust prior prose, always re-glob.

title: Slashcommand header style: named headers, no numbering (and update in-body step refs)
content:
Established convention for `.opencode/commands/*.md` files: use **named section headers** (`## Goal`, `## Argument handling`, `## Pipeline`), NOT numbered headers (`## 1.`, `## 2.`). Verified consistent across `/changelog.md` and `/review-large.md`. `/refine-memory.md` was converted to match on 2026-07-18 (its `## 1.`–`## 6.` became `## Extraction Rule`, `## Extraction Mechanism`, etc., and its previously-unheaded 3-paragraph intro was split into `## Goal` / `## Non-Interactive Posture` / `## Mechanism Context`).

**Load-bearing corollary:** when converting numbered → named headers, also update every in-body cross-reference that pointed at a numbered step. Otherwise the reference dangles. In `/refine-memory.md`, two such references had to be rewritten: "the path-depth fix in step 2" → "the path-depth fix described in 'Extraction Mechanism'", and "this is what step 4 enforces" → "this is what 'Post-Condition / Verification' enforces". Refer to sections by their heading text, never by a positional step number.

title: /refine-memory edit split: teamlead edits teamlead-memory.md in place, docs-writer creates memories/
content:
**Corrects** the `/refine-memory` architecture description in memory 601a32d6, which said teamlead "delegates the mechanical extraction to `docs-writer` (per teamlead's pure-delegator role)" — that framing was incomplete and the original command body's claim that teamlead "does not perform the edits itself" was factually wrong.

**Actual edit split** (made explicit in the command body on 2026-07-18, verified against agent permission scopes):
- **teamlead edits `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` in place directly** — it has scoped `edit`/`write` allow for exactly that file in `.opencode/agents/teamlead.md`. It stubs out extracted sections and updates the "Task-Specific Memory Files" pointer paragraph. It does NOT write to `memories/` (no scope there).
- **docs-writer creates the new files** under `docs/llm/memories/`, updates `memories/index.md`, and runs `make check-docs` — it has `edit`/`write` allow for `*.md`/`*.txt` and `bash` allow for `make check-docs*` / `make lint*`. teamlead has `bash: deny`, so it cannot run `make check-docs` itself.

**Executor note:** the command's Post-Condition / Verification section now explicitly states "`make check-docs` is run by `docs-writer` (teamlead has `bash: deny`). Teamlead coordinates the dispatch — it does not invoke `make` itself." When writing or reviewing teamlead-routed commands, always name which subagent actually executes any `bash`-gated step.

title: opencode slash-command mechanism: discovery, format, and repo state (3 repo-local commands)
content:
Corrected 2026-07-18 (supersedes the 2026-07-15 survey which claimed `.opencode/commands/` did not yet exist — it now exists with 3 commands). The opencode-tooling knowledge below is NOT documented in the Gromozeka repo; the per-command descriptions ARE now in `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` ("Opencode Slash-Command Mechanism" section), so don't duplicate them here.

**Discovery rule:** Slash commands are discovered from a `commands/` directory by filename — NOT registered in `opencode.json`/`opencode.jsonc`. Neither `.opencode/opencode.json` nor `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` has a `command`/`commands` key. Adding a `<name>.md` file is sufficient; no config edit needed.

**Locations (current as of 2026-07-18):**
- Global: `~/.config/opencode/commands/` — 2 commands: `caveman-compress.md`, `caveman-review.md`.
- Repo-local: `.opencode/commands/` — 3 commands: `changelog.md`, `refine-memory.md`, `review-large.md`.

**Command file format:** Filename `<name>.md` → slash command `/<name>`. YAML frontmatter between `---` fences (optional fields: `description`, `agent` (name of a defined agent), `subtask` (bool)), then a free-form prompt body. `$ARGUMENTS` is the placeholder for args passed at invocation. Example (`caveman-review.md`):
```
---
description: Caveman-style code review — one-line findings with severity
agent: cavecrew-reviewer
subtask: true
---
Review the current diff (or files: $ARGUMENTS).
...
```

**Routing convention (observed across the 3 repo-local commands):**
- `changelog` → `agent: software-developer`, `subtask: true`. Drafts a CHANGELOG.md entry from the current diff; format/rules in `docs/llm/changelog.md`.
- `refine-memory` → `agent: teamlead`, `subtask: true`. Extracts task-specific deep-dive sections from `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` into `docs/llm/memories/` to keep the main memory file compact.
- `review-large` → `agent: teamlead`, NO `subtask`. Wraps the methodology in `docs/llm/reviewing-large-changes.md` for diffs >24 files (characterize → batch → per-batch review → integration → consolidated findings; stops before remediation).

Note the asymmetry: `review-large` is NOT a subtask (runs as a top-level teamlead invocation), while `changelog` and `refine-memory` are subtasks. This is intentional per each command's frontmatter.

**Config files note:** Repo config is at `.opencode/opencode.json` (inside `.opencode/`, not at repo root). Global config is `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (there is NO `opencode.json` at `~/.config/opencode/`, only `.jsonc`). Both define `default_agent`, per-subagent model tiers, and MCP servers, but contain no command registration.

**Doc-sync rule when adding a command:** Update the "Opencode Slash-Command Mechanism" bullet in `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` to list the new command, and add an `### Added` entry to `CHANGELOG.md` under `## [Unreleased]`. Verify internal links resolve with `make check-docs` (read-only; runs `./venv/bin/python scripts/check_docs.py`).

title: Convention: teamlead-memory.md command bullets link to context docs, not command files
content:
In `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md`'s "Opencode Slash-Command Mechanism" section, each command bullet links to the most useful RELATED context document — NEVER to the command file itself (which is the bullet's own subject). This is a deliberate, consistent pattern across all three repo-local commands:

- `/changelog` bullet → links to `docs/llm/changelog.md` (the process spec), not `.opencode/commands/changelog.md`
- `/refine-memory` bullet → links to `memories/index.md` (the extraction destination), not `.opencode/commands/refine-memory.md`
- `/review-large` bullet → links to `reviewing-large-changes.md` (the methodology), not `.opencode/commands/review-large.md`

Rationale: the command file IS the bullet's subject; the link adds value by pointing to deeper context (process rules, destination layout, methodology) that helps the reader understand what the command operates on or wraps. Linking to the command file would be self-referential and add no information.

When adding a 4th (or Nth) command bullet, follow this pattern: identify the single most useful companion doc the command wraps/operates-on/produces, and link to THAT.

title: Path-fix transformation recipe for teamlead-memory.md → memories/ extraction
content:
When extracting a section from `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` into a new `docs/llm/memories/<slug>.md` file, every relative markdown link `[label](path)` in the pasted body must be rewritten because the new file is ONE directory deeper. Three transformation rules (verified 2026-07-18 across a 13-file batch extraction):

1. **Repo-root paths** `../../<x>` → `../../../<x>` (prepend one extra `../`).
   - Example: `` [`bayes_storage.py`](../../internal/database/bayes_storage.py) `` → `` [`bayes_storage.py`](../../../internal/database/bayes_storage.py) ``
   - Example: `` [`scripts/delete_stopwords.py`](../../scripts/delete_stopwords.py) `` → `` [`scripts/delete_stopwords.py`](../../../scripts/delete_stopwords.py) ``

2. **Sibling docs/llm/ files** `<filename>.md` → `../<filename>.md` (prepend `../`).
   - Example: `` [`changelog.md`](changelog.md) `` → `` [`changelog.md`](../changelog.md) ``
   - Example: `` [`reviewing-large-changes.md`](reviewing-large-changes.md) `` → `` [`reviewing-large-changes.md`](../reviewing-large-changes.md) ``

3. **Other memory files** `memories/<slug>.md` → `<slug>.md` (DROP the `memories/` prefix, because the new file is itself inside `memories/`).
   - Example: `` [`memories/db-maintenance-scripts.md`](memories/db-maintenance-scripts.md) `` → `` [`memories/db-maintenance-scripts.md`](db-maintenance-scripts.md) ``

**Gotchas:**
- The extraction preamble's link `` [`teamlead-memory.md`](../teamlead-memory.md) `` is ALREADY correct — do NOT "fix" it again to `../../teamlead-memory.md`. It is a sibling-relative link from the source file, and the new file lives one dir deeper, so `../teamlead-memory.md` happens to remain correct only because the preamble is written fresh for the new location. Only rewrite links INSIDE the pasted body.
- **Code spans (backtick-wrapped, no parens) are NOT links** — leave them alone. Only touch `[label](path)` markdown-link forms. This matters because pasted bodies frequently contain inline-code path references like `` `docs/llm/memories/chat-history-search.md` `` that look link-ish but must not be touched.
- Many section bodies have ZERO `](...)` markdown links and need no fixes at all — verify by scanning rather than assuming.

**Post-extraction verification sweep** (catches stale patterns):
- `rg "\]\(\.\./\.\./|memories/" docs/llm/memories/<new-file>.md` should return nothing. The `](../../` alternative catches under-rewritten repo-root links; the `memories/` alternative catches un-dropped prefixes (note: this also matches legitimate code spans, so eyeball the hits).

This recipe is more specific than the general docs/llm/ link-path rules (see memory 8defc824) — it covers only the extraction transformation, which is a recurring operation now that `/refine-memory` (memory 601a32d6) automates archival.

title: Memory file preamble template + MERGE pattern for multi-section extraction
content:
Structural conventions for `docs/llm/memories/<slug>.md` files created by extracting sections out of `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md`. Established/confirmed during the 2026-07-18 13-file batch extraction.

**SINGLETON file structure** (one source section → one file):
```
# <Original Section Heading verbatim, minus the leading "## ">

Archived durable notes from [`teamlead-memory.md`](../teamlead-memory.md) (extracted YYYY-MM-DD). See the live compact memory there for cross-cutting rules and workflow lessons.

<blank line>
<section body verbatim, with path-fixes applied>
```
- The H1 IS the original H2 heading text verbatim — only the `## ` prefix is dropped (promoted to `# `).
- Preserve backticks in headings verbatim, e.g. `# LLM maxRounds round-limit (`generateTextViaLLM`) — added 2026-07-16`.
- Preserve parens in headings verbatim, e.g. `# LLM Tool-Call Healing (internal/services/llm/service.py) — implemented 2026-07-15`.

**MERGE file structure** (two source sections → one file). Use when two sections cover the SAME topic from different phases (e.g. pre-review planning + post-review outcomes) OR have near-duplicate headings that differ only in capitalisation/formatting (e.g. `## User Memory V2 Pre-Merge Review` vs `## user-memory-v2 Pre-Merge Review`):
```
# <Synthesized descriptive title>

Archived durable notes from [`teamlead-memory.md`](../teamlead-memory.md) (extracted YYYY-MM-DD). See the live compact memory there for cross-cutting rules and workflow lessons.

<blank line>
## <Original section 1 heading verbatim>

<section 1 body verbatim, path-fixed>

---

## <Original section 2 heading verbatim>

<section 2 body verbatim, path-fixed>
```
- The H1 is a SYNTHESIZED descriptive title (NOT one of the originals).
- Each H2 sub-section heading is one original section heading VERBATIM (including original capitalisation/hyphenation — do not normalise).
- A single `---` horizontal rule separates the two H2 sub-sections.
- Both bodies get path-fixed per the extraction recipe (memory on path-fix transformation rules).

**Rationale** for the MERGE pattern: preserves the audit trail of both phases/variants while consolidating the topic into one file. Deleting either variant loses signal; keeping them as separate files pollutes the index with near-duplicate slugs.

**index.md update convention** (`docs/llm/memories/index.md` "Available Files" list):
- Format: `- [`<slug>.md`](<slug>.md) — <one-line description>.` (em-dash separator, trailing period).
- Insert in ALPHABETICAL position by slug. The list is the canonical inventory.
- Verification after batch edits: `rg -c "^- \[" docs/llm/memories/index.md` (bullet count) and `ls docs/llm/memories/*.md | wc -l` (file count = bullets + 1 for index.md itself).

Note: the older convention for existing memory files (pre-2026-07-18, e.g. `chat-users-cache.md`) does NOT use this two-line preamble — they open with a free-form H1 + body. The preamble template above is the NEW convention going forward; do not retro-fit existing files unless explicitly asked.

title: Duplicate User Memory V2 sections in teamlead-memory.md RESOLVED (merged into user-memory-v2-review.md)
content:
RESOLUTION of the open issue tracked in memory 10514655 (which was marked `status: pending-refine-memory`).

**Background:** `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` contained TWO near-duplicate "User Memory V2 Pre-Merge Review" sections differing only in capitalisation/formatting:
- `## User Memory V2 Pre-Merge Review (2026-07-14, in progress)` (capital U, space, "in progress" suffix) — pre-review state/planning
- `## user-memory-v2 Pre-Merge Review (2026-07-14)` (lowercase u, hyphenated) — post-review outcomes/invariants

**Resolution (2026-07-18):** Both sections were extracted and MERGED into a single new file `docs/llm/memories/user-memory-v2-review.md` using the MERGE pattern:
- H1: `# user-memory-v2 Pre-Merge Review (2026-07-14)` (synthesised)
- H2 sub-section 1: the original capital-U heading verbatim + its body
- `---` separator
- H2 sub-section 2: the original lowercase-u heading verbatim + its body

Both original headings are preserved verbatim as H2 sub-sections (audit trail intact); the merge consolidates the topic into one slug. The bodies were pasted verbatim with no path-fixes needed (neither body contained `](...)` markdown links — only code-span references like `` `docs/llm/memories/chat-history-search.md` ``, which were left alone).

**Implication for `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md`:** Once the teamlead's own edits land, both original sections should be REMOVED from `teamlead-memory.md` (the canonical content now lives in the archived file). This removal is the teamlead's responsibility — the docs-writer task that created the archive file was explicitly instructed NOT to edit `teamlead-memory.md`. Until that removal happens, the near-duplicate headings still physically exist in the source file but are considered superseded.

Future agents searching for "user-memory-v2 review" or "User Memory V2" content should read `docs/llm/memories/user-memory-v2-review.md`, not expect to find it in `teamlead-memory.md`.

title: make check-docs accepts both leading-slash and relative link paths (style not enforced)
content:
`scripts/check_docs.py` (the `make check-docs` checker) validates only that a link's TARGET RESOLVES to an existing file — it does NOT enforce link path-STYLE. Both forms pass cleanly:

- **Leading-slash / repo-root-relative**: `/internal/services/cache/service.py`, `/tests/...`
- **Deep relative**: `../../../internal/services/cache/service.py` (from `docs/llm/memories/<slug>.md`)

Evidence: A 2026-07-18 memory-extraction created 13 new files under `docs/llm/memories/` using the RELATIVE form (`../../../internal/...`) for repo-root paths, plus updated the index with 13 bullets and stubbed 15 sections in `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` with pointer lines like `See [\`memories/<slug>.md\`](memories/<slug>.md) — ...`. `make check-docs` reported "Checked 120 markdown files, 1600 links; 0 broken." and `make lint` passed (flake8/isort/import-main/pyright all clean).

CONSEQUENCE / GOTCHA: Memory c7a76036 frames leading-slash (`/internal/...`) as a "Locked repo convention" for `docs/llm/memories/*.md`, but this is a STYLE PREFERENCE, not a tooling-enforced rule. Convention drift between leading-slash and relative forms WILL NOT be caught by `make check-docs` — it must be caught at review time. Do NOT "fix" relative paths to leading-slash (or vice versa) under the assumption that the checker requires one form; both resolve identically.

The checker does enforce: (a) the target file must exist at the resolved path, (b) `.opencode/` and `docs/archive`, `docs/templates`, `lib/ext_modules` are excluded (see memory dd77405d). It strips `#anchor`, `?query`, and `:lineNumber` suffixes before resolving (see memory 1a464bba).

title: /refine-memory execution: sibling path-collapse, merge convention, edit-split sequencing
content:
Operational details for executing the `/refine-memory` extraction workflow (companion to memory 601a32d6, which covers the high-level command). Learned from the 2026-07-18 run that extracted 15 sections into 13 files (422→230 lines).

## 1. Sibling `memories/` path-collapse rule (NOT covered by memory 8defc824)

When a section being extracted from `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` contains a link to ANOTHER memory file written as `memories/X.md`, that link must COLLAPSE to bare `X.md` in the new file — because the new file lives in `memories/` itself, so `memories/X.md` would resolve to `memories/memories/X.md` (broken).

Rule set when moving a body from `teamlead-memory.md` → `memories/<slug>.md`:
- Repo-root paths: `../../internal/foo.py` → `../../../internal/foo.py` (gain one `../`)
- Sibling `docs/llm/` paths: `changelog.md` → `../changelog.md` (gain one `../`)
- Sibling `memories/X.md` references: `memories/X.md` → `X.md` (DROP the `memories/` prefix — the new file is already inside `memories/`)

Real examples from the 2026-07-18 run: `memories/db-maintenance-scripts.md` → `db-maintenance-scripts.md`; `memories/condensed-context-retrieval.md` → `condensed-context-retrieval.md`; `memories/doc-link-fix-campaign.md` → `doc-link-fix-campaign.md` (2 occurrences). Forgetting this collapse is the #1 cause of post-extraction `make check-docs` breakage.

## 2. Merge convention for related sections

When two source sections cover the SAME topic from different phases (e.g. a pre-review plan + post-review outcomes, or a performance profile + the speedup fix), merge them into ONE archived file. The prompt's JUDGMENT CALLS list hints at this ("likely: merge into one archived file").

Merged-file format:
- **H1**: synthesized descriptive title (not a verbatim copy of either source heading).
- Context-note line (standard header).
- **H2**: verbatim first source heading, followed by its body verbatim.
- `---` horizontal rule separator.
- **H2**: verbatim second source heading, followed by its body verbatim.

Main-file handling for merges: BOTH source sections get stubs (each at its original location) pointing to the SAME merged file. Two stubs to one file is intentional — preserves the audit trail that two near-duplicate headings existed and were deliberately merged.

Real merges from 2026-07-18 run:
- `user-memory-v2-review.md` ← "User Memory V2 Pre-Merge Review (2026-07-14, in progress)" + "user-memory-v2 Pre-Merge Review (2026-07-14)" (capital-U/spaced vs lowercase-u/hyphenated near-duplicates).
- `test-suite-speedup.md` ← "Test Suite Performance Profile (2026-07-12, measured)" + "Test Speedup IMPLEMENTED (2026-07-12)" (profile → fix → outcome phases of one effort).

Decision rule for merge vs keep-separate: MERGE when the two sections are sequential phases of one effort or near-duplicate headings; KEEP SEPARATE when they cover genuinely different topics (e.g. "Large Review Campaign Lessons" = parallel-review-at-scale mechanics vs "Review-Fix Round Lessons" = applying fixes — distinct, kept as `large-review-campaign.md` + `review-fix-lessons.md`).

## 3. Edit-split sequencing (prevents content loss)

The `/refine-memory` edit split is: teamlead edits `teamlead-memory.md` in place; docs-writer creates new files under `memories/`, updates `index.md`, runs `make check-docs`.

Correct execution order:
1. **docs-writer creates new files FIRST** (reading verbatim bodies from the still-intact `teamlead-memory.md`) + updates `index.md`.
2. **teamlead stubs extracted sections in `teamlead-memory.md` AFTER** docs-writer confirms creation.
3. **docs-writer runs `make check-docs` LAST** (after both file sets are in final state).

If teamlead stubs first, docs-writer loses access to the verbatim source bodies (would need git history to recover them). Sequencing matters because docs-writer creates files by copying bodies from the live main file.

## 4. Stub format reminder

Each extracted section in `teamlead-memory.md` becomes:
```
## <Original Heading verbatim>

See [`memories/<slug>.md`](memories/<slug>.md) — <one-line summary of what is archived>.
```
The original heading is PRESERVED (audit trail), only the body is replaced. For merged sections, the one-line summary should note both phases.

## 5. Verification baseline (2026-07-18 run)

`make check-docs` on a clean tree after this extraction: 120 markdown files, 1600 links, 0 broken. `make lint` clean. `make test` intentionally NOT run (docs-only change). Use these counts as a sanity baseline for future runs — a wildly different file/link count suggests something unexpected happened.

title: CacheType GM_* prefix = Geocode Maps, NOT Google Maps
content:
Terminology gotcha confirmed 2026-07-15 during the DB cache cleanup work.

The `CacheType` StrEnum (`internal/database/models.py`) has three members with the `GM_` prefix:
- `GM_SEARCH = "geocode_maps_search"`
- `GM_REVERSE = "geocode_maps_reverse"`
- `GM_LOOKUP = "geocode_maps_lookup"`

**GM = Geocode Maps** (the geocode.maps.co service, implemented in `lib/geocode_maps/`), NOT Google Maps. The enum *values* are self-documenting (`geocode_maps_*`), but the `GM_` *member-name prefix* is ambiguous and was misread as "Google Maps" during this session — the user had to correct the teamlead explicitly ("BTW, GM is geocode maps, not google maps").

When documenting or referencing these cache namespaces, spell out "Geocode Maps" rather than "Google Maps". The implementation is backed by `GeocodeMapsClient` (`lib/geocode_maps/client.py`), and the API reference lives at `docs/other/geocode-maps/Geocode-Maps-API.md`. Note: of the three client methods (search/reverse/lookup), only `search()` is actually consumed by handlers today (see memory daa23b59).

Related: the aggressive 7-day cache cleanup TTL (`AGGRESSIVE_CLEANUP_CACHE_TYPES` in `internal/bot/common/handlers/manager.py`) deliberately EXCLUDES the GM_* namespaces — they are kept at the 365-day default floor, since geocode lookups are stable/slow-changing.

title: Correction: markdown-link false-positive fires ONLY at begin-of-message, NOT trailing
content:
Supersedes/corrects the "trailing with no following text" claim in memory dc6d25d5 ("Broken-known-tool matcher false-positives on edge markdown links with tool-name text"). That memory states the markdown-link false positive occurs when the link is "the entire message OR trailing with no following text". The "trailing" half is WRONG.

## Definitive analysis (confirmed 2026-07-15 via regex trace, prompted by user)

The `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` matcher (internal/services/llm/service.py) uses the begin/end-edge guard: a bracket block is rejected only when BOTH prefix and suffix are non-empty (`if prefixStr.strip() and suffixStr.strip(): return False`).

For a real markdown link `[text](url)`:
- The `(url)` ALWAYS lands in the suffix (group 4), because it follows the `]`.
- Therefore the suffix is NEVER empty for a real link.
- Therefore the END-of-message condition (suffix empty) can NEVER be satisfied by a markdown link.

Consequences:
- `[generate_and_send_image](url)` as the WHOLE message → prefix="" (empty), suffix="(url)" (non-empty) → one edge empty → ACCEPTED (matches). This is the begin-of-message case (prefix empty). resultText becomes "(url)".
- `Some preamble [generate_and_send_image](url)` (trailing link WITH preceding text) → prefix="Some preamble " (non-empty), suffix="(url)" (non-empty) → BOTH non-empty → REJECTED. NOT a false positive.
- A bare `[name]` at the END with no `(url)` → suffix empty → matches. But that's the intended bracket-at-end detection, not a markdown link.

So the false-positive surface is NARROWER than dc6d25d5 implies: it fires ONLY when the bracket sits at the very BEGINNING of the message (prefix empty). Trailing-with-preamble links are correctly rejected. dc6d25d5's "trailing with no following text" phrasing is self-contradictory for a markdown link (the `(url)` is always "following text").

## Optional safe refinement identified
Reject when `]` is immediately followed by `(` (markdown-link syntax). This is SAFE because the real broken-call formats are `[Вызов функции \`name\` …]` (Russian pseudo-call) and `[name]{json}` — never `[name](url)`. This would eliminate even the narrow begin-of-message false positive. Offered to user 2026-07-15; not yet applied.

## Why this matters
Prevents future readers from (a) worrying about trailing markdown links that are actually safe, or (b) building unnecessary guards for a non-problem. The actual residual risk is: a message that BEGINS with `[<registeredToolName>](<url>)` — rare in practice.

title: Dependency testability classification: PURE / EXTERNAL / MIXED framework
content:
Framework for deciding whether a third-party dependency can get a "pure" regression test (no external service needed) vs. needs a live endpoint / golden-replay workflow. Established 2026-07-15 when scoping the `tests/dependencies/` suite. This is the testability axis (distinct from the coverage map in memory 1a4fcca8, which tracks what IS currently tested).

**PURE (6 — no I/O, testable in isolation, primary dep-usage-test targets):** python-dateutil, numpy, html-to-markdown, packaging, python-magic, tomli. All six now have `tests/dependencies/test_<lib>.py`.

**EXTERNAL (7 — need a live endpoint / Docker / model download; cannot be pure-tested):** aiodocker (Docker daemon), boto3 (S3/MinIO), fastembed (downloads ONNX models from HF), httpx-socks (proxy/socket), openai (LLM provider — covered by golden tests), yandex-ai-studio-sdk (Yandex gRPC endpoint), sqlink (hosted DB). These need the golden-test record-once/replay workflow (see openai golden infra) or are inherently un-pure-testable.

**MIXED (5 — have a pure/in-process core worth testing):** aiosqlite (in-memory `:memory:` works — already exercised via testDatabase fixture), aiohttp (ships test_utils/TestClient for in-process HTTP), httpx (AsyncClient mockable; real calls need network — only client deserialization worth locking, covered via golden), python-telegram-bot (constants/MessageEntity/parse-mode helpers are pure-ish; ExtBot always mocked), sqlite-vec (loadable native extension — testable in-process into a sqlite3 conn; NO external service needed, so it WAS included in the dep-usage suite despite being "mixed").

**DEV/test-only (9 — formatters, linters, pytest stack, PyYAML debug-scripts-only):** out of scope for app regression tests.

Key decision rule that fell out of this: a lib is a candidate for `tests/dependencies/` iff it is PURE or has a MIXED in-process core that doesn't need a live service. sqlite-vec was the one MIXED lib included because its only "external" need is the bundled binary extension, loaded in-process. fastembed and yandex-ai-studio-sdk were EXCLUDED because their core behavior (ONNX inference / gRPC generation) fundamentally requires the external artifact.

Version pins as of 2026-07-15 (see requirements.direct.txt for current): dateutil 2.9.0.post0, numpy 2.5.1, html-to-markdown 3.8.3, packaging 26.2, python-magic 0.4.27, tomli 2.4.1, sqlite-vec 0.1.9.

title: Deferred: yandex-ai-studio-sdk + fastembed need golden-test follow-up (not pure-testable)
content:
Explicit decision (2026-07-15, user-approved) during the dependency-usage regression-test task: the two largest coverage gaps — `yandex-ai-studio-sdk` (entire `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py` untested) and `fastembed` (real ONNX inference never exercised) — are DEFERRED to a separate golden-test follow-up round. They were excluded from the `tests/dependencies/` suite because they are EXTERNAL (need a live Yandex gRPC endpoint / ONNX model download respectively) and cannot be pure-tested.

Why they can't be pure-tested:
- yandex-ai-studio-sdk: generation is gRPC-backed (AsyncAIStudio / AsyncGPTModel.generate / AsyncImageGenerationModel). No way to exercise result deserialization or tool-call parsing without a real or recorded response.
- fastembed: TextEmbedding downloads ONNX models from HuggingFace on first use and runs onnxruntime. The embedding contract (dim, normalization, values) is the untested surface.

Chosen path forward: extend the existing golden-test infrastructure (the `OpenAIReplayerPatcher` / `GoldenDataReplayer` pattern in `tests/lib/ai/golden/` and `tests/lib/aurumentation/`) to these providers — record real responses once, replay. This is the SAME mechanism already used to cover the openai SDK's deserialization.

Scope guard for future sessions: do NOT attempt to add these as `tests/dependencies/test_<lib>.py` direct-lib tests — they will fail by design. They belong in a new `tests/lib/ai/golden/`-style suite. The coverage-gap ranking (Tier 1 #1 = yandex-ai-studio-sdk, Tier 2 #4 = fastembed) lives in memory 1a4fcca8.

title: CORRECTION: _llmToolSearchMessages None-degradation was REVERSED — None now raises→error
content:
Memory `ecdad0a9` claims that in `ChatSearchHandler._llmToolSearchMessages` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py`), when `LLMService.generateEmbedding` returns `None`, the tool "degrades to filter-only search (`done: True`)". **This is STALE as of 2026-07-16 — that degradation never shipped to production (or was reverted same-session).**

**Actual current behavior (verified 2026-07-16, user-directed):** `None` is treated as a FAILURE, restoring the pre-migration error-on-failure behavior. The code (chat_search.py ~lines 710-714) does:

```python
queryEmbedding = await self.llmService.generateEmbedding(query, chatId=..., chatSettings=...)
if queryEmbedding is None:
    raise Exception("Embedding generation failed")
```

The raise is caught by the surrounding defensive `try/except Exception` → returns `{"done": False, "error": "Unable to generate query embedding"}` and the repo is NOT reached.

**Why:** the user explicitly wanted to preserve the previous behavior (error on embedding failure) rather than silently degrade. The `raise Exception(...)` + immediate-catch pattern funnels the None case through the single error-handling block (shared with the `side_effect` raise path) for consistent logging via `logger.exception`.

**Test impact (locked in):** `test_search_messages_embedding_returns_none_errors` stubs `generateEmbedding=AsyncMock(return_value=None)`, asserts `{"done": False, "error": "Unable to generate query embedding"}`, AND asserts `searchChatMessages.assert_not_called()` (repo not reached). `test_search_messages_embedding_failure` (side_effect=RuntimeError → same error) is the sibling covering the boundary-raise path.

The rest of memory `ecdad0a9` (return shape `Optional[Tuple[str, List[float]]]`, wrapper owns model resolution, plural-vs-singular distinction) remains accurate — only the `_llmToolSearchMessages` degradation claim is wrong.

title: MessageId(str) accepts ANY string — except-fallback branches only reachable for non-str/non-int
content:
Testing gotcha that caused a wrong test premise in 2026-07-16 work (teamlead assumed `MessageId("not-a-number")` would raise and trigger a fallback; it does NOT).

**The fact:** `MessageId.__init__` (`internal/models/types.py`) accepts `int` (Telegram) or `str` (Max). Because Max message IDs are ARBITRARY STRINGS, **every** string is a valid `MessageId` — `MessageId("not-a-number")`, `MessageId("")`, `MessageId("anything")` all succeed without raising. The only explicit rejection is `bool` (memory `ba6a78ae`: `ValueError("Invalid message ID type: bool")` because bool is an int subclass).

**Consequence:** any `except (ValueError, TypeError): pass` (or similar) fallback branch that wraps `MessageId(x)` is ONLY reachable when `x` is a non-str/non-int type (float, list, dict, None, etc.). A string input will always construct successfully and never hit the fallback.

**Concrete instance:** `ChatSearchHandler._llmToolSearchMessages` resolves `thread_message_id` via `threadMessageId = MessageId(thread_message_id)` inside `try/except (ValueError, TypeError): pass`. A test intended to exercise the fallback (`threadMessageId is None` → fall back to `current_thread_only` scoping) MUST pass a non-str/non-int value (e.g. `3.14` float, which `MessageId` rejects with `ValueError`) — NOT a junk string like `"not-a-number"`, which would silently succeed and override `current_thread_only`.

**General rule for tests:** when testing a `MessageId(...)` exception/fallback path, use a float or list as the invalid input, never a string.

Related: memory `ba6a78ae` (bool rejection), memory `b9334f69` (MessageId type unification).

title: LLM-tool BOOLEAN params need string-aware coercion — bool("false") is True
.opencode/memory.jsonl IS normally committed — hands-off rule, NOT exclude-from-git
content:
AUTHORITATIVE RULE, set by direct user correction on 2026-07-18: `.opencode/memory.jsonl` (OpenCode's auto-managed session memory store) IS git-tracked and IS normally committed as part of regular git flow. **Do NOT exclude it from commits, and do NOT `git restore` / revert it before staging feature work.** OpenCode auto-appends/modifies it on every session that uses memory tools, and those additions are expected to land in history.

The ONLY constraint is **hands-off for the agent team**: never `cat`/read it, never edit it, never manually stage/unstage it, never flag it as a stray or unrelated change in review, and never quote/paste its contents into reports, diffs, or summaries. It is generated by OpenCode; the team should simply ignore it.

SUPersedes and corrects two prior WRONG memories:
- `6230764b` (2026-07-04) claimed the file "MUST be reverted before committing feature work" with `git restore .opencode/memory.jsonl` — this is the OPPOSITE of correct and is destructive: following it discards legitimate (uncommitted) memory entries. Do NOT run `git restore` on this file.
- The even earlier guidance "never read, touch, flag, or commit it" (c90e28aa) was also wrong on the "commit" half.

User's exact words (2026-07-18): "It usually is commited. Just you and your team shouldn't look at it and touch it (as it is generated by opencode)."

Note: this session's teamlead agent had wrongly told the user to "exclude `.opencode/memory.jsonl` from the commit" — that advice was incorrect and the user corrected it. The file commits normally; agents stay hands-off.

title: maxRounds Gate-2 refinement: roundLimitHit flag + error-status propagation + user_memories cap-hit surfacing
content:
**Third hardening pass of the `maxRounds` feature (2026-07-18). Complements ad411546 (the two-tier loop bound) and RESOLVES the open concern in f15f35a7. ad411546 was written before this pass and does not mention `roundLimitHit`.**

## Resolution of the user_memories caller concern (overrides f15f35a7's recommendation)
f15f35a7 flagged (status=open) that `user_memories._runSingleRefinement` (the autonomous memory-curation loop) silently inherits `maxRounds=32` and recommended passing `maxRounds=None`. **User decision: KEEP 32** (intended per TODO "memory refinement: hard limit on steps, constant 32") but **surface the cap-hit** instead of letting incomplete curation look like success. The other 4 callers (chat path `llm_messages.py`, `divination.py` which degrades gracefully on non-FINAL, `dev_commands.py`) use the default unchanged.

## `ModelRunResult.roundLimitHit: bool` (lib/ai/models.py)
New `__slots__` field, default `False`, omitted from `__str__` (via the existing `if value is False: continue` rule → logs stay clean until True). Set to `True` inside `generateTextViaLLM`'s `else: break` block whenever `budgetExhausted` — i.e. on ANY post-budget termination regardless of resulting status (empty/non-empty FINAL, post-budget TOOL_CALLS, ERROR, CONTENT_FILTER, UNKNOWN all set it). Lets callers detect an incomplete result programmatically (no brittle string-matching on the fallback text). Backward-compatible (defaulted; ~100 existing `ModelRunResult(...)` construction sites unaffected). A service-level `logger.warning("generateTextViaLLM hit maxRounds cap ({maxRounds}) for callId #{callId}; forcing termination")` also fires (exactly once — the `break` is unconditional).

## user_memories.py cap-hit detection
`user_memories._runSingleRefinement` (after the result debug-log, inside the try, before the except): `if result.roundLimitHit: logger.warning("Memory refinement hit the maxRounds cap; curation may be incomplete for this batch")`. Detection + warning only; the curation logic itself is unchanged. Fires at most once per refinement call.

## Post-budget fallback synthesis TIGHTENED (refines ad411546 §"Post-budget fallback synthesis")
ad411546 described the guard as `if budgetExhausted and not ret.resultText:`. **That was too broad** — it fired for ANY non-TOOL_CALLS empty-text status, masking ERROR/CONTENT_FILTER/UNKNOWN as FINAL+fallback (hiding real error telemetry). **Tightened to:** `if budgetExhausted and not ret.resultText and ret.status in (ModelResultStatus.FINAL, ModelResultStatus.TOOL_CALLS):` — synthesize the fallback ONLY for empty FINAL and post-budget TOOL_CALLS (a glitching model that ignored empty `tools=[]`); genuine error statuses propagate with their original status + empty `resultText` so callers detect the failure. The `ret.toolCalls = []` reset (NIT 1 from ad411546) still applies inside this tightened branch.

**Open edge (deferred 2026-07-18):** empty `TRUNCATED_FINAL` / `PARTIAL` / `UNSPECIFIED` also propagate (not in the `(FINAL, TOOL_CALLS)` set). All callers degrade gracefully (divination returns None on non-FINAL; chat handler treats empty text appropriately). Could fold `TRUNCATED_FINAL` into the set later if an empty truncated-final surfaces as an empty chat message — left as-is pending user decision since it's consistent with the comment/CHANGELOG and safe.

## Tests grew: 8 → 13 in test_max_rounds.py + 1 in test_user_memories.py
Added: `testMaxRounds_setsRoundLimitHitOnExhaustion` (asserts flag True + caplog warning substring "hit maxRounds cap (2)"), `testMaxRounds_noRoundLimitHitWhenWithinBudget` (flag False), parametrized `testMaxRounds_propagatesErrorStatusPostBudget[ERROR/CONTENT_FILTER/UNKNOWN]` (asserts status preserved + empty resultText + no fallback + roundLimitHit True). The existing `TerminatesWhenModelKeepsReturningToolCallsPostBudget` extended with `assert result.roundLimitHit is True` + `assert result.toolCalls == []`. The error-propagation regression was proven to fail on revert (all 3 parametrized cases failed with `status == FINAL` and synthesized fallback — exactly the masking the tightening prevents). New `test_runSingleRefinementWarnsWhenRoundLimitHit` in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_memories.py` (builds a real ModelRunResult with roundLimitHit=True, asserts the warning via caplog).

## Reusable test technique
To regression-test an infinite-loop bug without hanging the suite: give the mock a FINITE `side_effect` list. An unbounded loop exhausts it and raises `StopAsyncIteration` → test fails loud (not hang). Used in `testMaxRoundsTerminatesWhenModelKeepsReturningToolCallsPostBudget` (8-element list; bounded loop makes 3 calls, unbounded would hit StopAsyncIteration at call 9).

## CHANGELOG
Two entries under `## [Unreleased] → ### Changed`: (1) the maxRounds bound itself (5 exhaustion actions + roundLimitHit + warning + FINAL/TOOL_CALLS-only fallback + error propagation + None/0/negative semantics); (2) the user_memories caller's roundLimitHit detection + warning.

title: Teamlead direct memory-maintenance edits are EXEMPT from Gate 1/Gate 2 reviews
content:
Refines memory 23657f10 (the mandatory two-level code review gates). The gates apply to "code-change subtasks" — defined as any subtask that produced `edit`, `write`, or `bash` output modifying source files. Teamlead's direct edits to `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` are NOT in that category.

**The exemption:** Teamlead may edit `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` directly (it has a scoped `edit`/`write` allow for that one file — see `.opencode/agents/teamlead.md`). Per the teamlead role definition, this is "memory maintenance, part of orchestration, not substantive project work." Such edits do NOT trigger another Gate 1 or Gate 2 code-reviewer pass.

**Operational consequence (observed 2026-07-18):** After Gate 2 passed clean on a 4-file change, teamlead added two durable bullets + fixed a stale `TODO.md:7` reference directly in `teamlead-memory.md`'s "Opencode Slash-Command Mechanism" section, then proceeded to synthesis WITHOUT re-dispatching code-reviewer. This is correct: the edit was within the memory-maintenance exception, introduced no new internal links (so no `make check-docs` breakage risk), and teamlead has `bash: deny` anyway (cannot run `make check-docs` itself — that would require dispatching `docs-writer`).

**Boundary:** The exemption is narrow — it covers ONLY `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` (teamlead's scoped allow). Edits to `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/llm/memories/*`, or any other file still go through the normal delegation + gate flow. If a memory-maintenance edit introduces new internal links, sanity-check them by hand (or delegate `make check-docs` to `docs-writer`) since `scripts/check_docs.py:70` excludes `.opencode/` but DOES scan `docs/llm/`.

title: Two distinct CRON_JOB interval-gating patterns — ProxyService vs SandboxHandler, do not conflate
content:
The codebase has TWO different mechanisms for gating work inside `_dtCronJob` (the QueueService CRON_JOB handler that fires ~every 60s). They are easy to conflate in documentation — a 2026-07-18 audit found `docs/llm/memories/proxy-lifecycle.md` had wrongly attributed SandboxHandler's flags to ProxyService.

**Pattern A — ProxyService (`internal/services/proxy/service.py` + `lifecycle.py`):**
- `_dtCronJob` runs on EVERY tick. It iterates `_activeLifecycles`, starts any not-yet-started ones (checks `lifecycle.started` boolean each tick — NO one-time flag), then calls `lifecycle.onCronTick()` on each.
- Interval gating lives inside `ProxyLifecycle.onCronTick()`: uses `_tickCounter += 1` then `if self._tickCounter % healthCheckInterval != 0: return`. Pure modulo on tick count.
- `ProxyLifecycle` also has a `_starting` re-entrancy guard (distinct from `_started`).
- NO `_recoveryDone`, NO `_lastCronRun`, NO `time.time()` delta anywhere in the proxy code.

**Pattern B — SandboxHandler (`internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py`):**
- Uses `self._recoveryDone = False` (one-time startup recovery flag, set True after first recovery run).
- Uses `self._lastCronRun = time.time()` + `if now - self._lastCronRun < 1800: return` (wall-clock delta gating, 1800s = 30min).
- This is the time.time()-delta pattern, NOT the modulo-counter pattern.

**Why it matters:** When documenting or reviewing either handler's cron logic, do not assume they share a mechanism. If a doc claims ProxyService uses `_recoveryDone` or `_lastCronRun`, it is describing SandboxHandler by mistake. The two patterns are intentionally different designs.

title: Durable memory drift categories beyond line numbers: dep versions and tool counts
content:
Complements memories dbec997e (line numbers rot) and 79fdc932 (file paths drift). A July 18, 2026 audit of `docs/llm/memories/chat-history-search.md` surfaced two ADDITIONAL drift-prone claim categories that the existing "avoid brittle references" memories do not name:

1. **Dependency version pins in prose** — the file claimed `numpy==2.4.6`; actual is `numpy==2.5.1` (requirements.direct.txt). Also `fastembed==0.8.0` was correct but only by luck. Dependency versions in durable memory rot on every bump. When auditing, re-verify ALL version pins against requirements.direct.txt; when writing, prefer omitting the pin and pointing at the requirements file instead.

2. **Registered-tool / registration counts** — the file claimed "3 LLM tools registered (search_messages, list_users, get_thread)" but a 4th (`get_messages_by_ids`, added for ADR-019 condensed-context) existed. Tool/registration counts go stale whenever a new tool is added to a handler. When auditing, grep `registerTool(` and count actual calls rather than trusting a stored number; when writing, avoid hardcoding tool counts — list tool names if needed but omit the cardinality.

Also confirmed again: full method signatures rot (the file claimed `embedAndSaveMessage(ensuredMessage, modelName, db) -> bool`; actual is `(self, ensuredMessage: EnsuredMessage) -> bool`). Prefer referencing the symbol + file path over transcribing the signature.

Audit verdict pattern that worked here: when a durable file is mostly accurate (anti-patterns, gotchas, test-mocking rules still valid) but has drifted on 5+ concrete claims, FIX-IN-PLACE with targeted edits rather than ARCHIVE — archiving loses the still-valid durable lessons. Do NOT update meta indexes when fixing a single file.

title: UserMemoriesHandler dual-lock concurrency: _refineLock + _accountingLock
content:
The user-memory refinement concurrency model in `UserMemoriesHandler` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py`) uses TWO locks, not one. Existing memories (`59e37f96`, `93c64c1c`) and the docs (`docs/llm/memories/user-memories.md` lines 624-629, `docs/llm/memories/user-memory-refinement.md` "Concurrency model") all describe only `_refineLock` and call it the "single global lock" — this is NOW STALE.

**Current truth (verified 2026-07-18):**
- `_refineLock` (`asyncio.Lock`): serializes the whole scan+dispatch in `_runSingleRefinement` / `_runMemoryRefinement`. A bail-fast check (`if self._refineLock.locked(): return`) skips a cron tick if a previous batch (a single LLM call can exceed the 60s cadence) is still running, so the provider is never flooded with concurrent refinement calls.
- `_accountingLock` (`asyncio.Lock`): serializes ALL mutations of the in-memory `_accounting` (per-(chatId, userId, threadId) new-message counter) and `_lastRefinedTS` (per-key last-refined timestamp) dicts. Acquired from BOTH `newMessageHandler` (which increments `_accounting`) and `_dtCronJob`/`_runSingleRefinement` (which reads and resets them). This prevents the read-modify-write race between the message-ingress path and the cron path.

**Why the drift matters:** `user-memories.md` actively defers to `user-memory-refinement.md`'s "Concurrency model" section as "still accurate", so the stale "no per-entry locks" / "single global lock" claim propagates. The `user-memory-refinement.md` file was corrected on 2026-07-18 to describe both locks; `user-memories.md` lines 624-629 still need the same correction (see separate memory).

Class/method renames carried over from the rolling-bio → user-memories rewrite: `UserDataHandler` → `UserMemoriesHandler` (file `user_data.py` → `user_memories.py`), `_runRefinement` → `_runSingleRefinement`. The locks and counters themselves are unchanged in purpose.
