If you instead grep for refactor-induced stale method/repo references in migration docstrings (the 35ed0592 class), those are NOT actionable. The two drift classes are treated differently. If this distinction is ever challenged, surface it to the user rather than silently picking one rule.

The brief's exact framing was: "Migration files are historical records — only their DOCSTRINGS/COMMENTS should be updated, never the SQL or `down()` logic."

## Lesson for future audits
Audit notes can mislocate drift within a package/module. When a flagged file doesn't contain the claimed text:
1. Do NOT fabricate an edit to match the audit description.
2. Grep the surrounding directory / package for the actual offending string.
3. Fix the real location and flag the audit's path error in the change summary.

This also reaffirms: "type-safe responses" is an accurate description of TypedDict-based models and should NOT be treated as a Pydantic implication. The no-pydantic rule (AGENTS.md) is about not USING pydantic, not about banning the phrase "type-safe".

title: Convention: Resolution-sync doc set when closing a previously-documented open issue
content:
When an issue that was documented as OPEN/dormant/did-not-land across multiple docs gets RESOLVED, you must do a coordinated pass updating EVERY doc that described it as open — not just the primary reference. This is a distinct doc-maintenance pattern from "adding a new config key" (see memory a92b25e7 for that one) and involves a DIFFERENT doc set.

## The pattern (established 2026-07-18, webhook unregister-webhook mismatch)
The motivating example: `unregister-webhook` had a divergent code default (`True` at `internal/bot/max/application.py:127`) vs config default (`false` in `configs/00-defaults/webhook-receiver.toml:23`). The mismatch was flagged as "open"/"dormant"/"did not land" in 4 docs. After the code default was flipped to `False`, all 4 needed updating to avoid being stale in the OPPOSITE direction (describing a problem that no longer exists).

## Doc set for resolution-sync (distinct from the new-key-addition set)
1. **`docs/llm/configuration.md`** — rename the open-issue callout header (e.g. "Dormant default mismatch (code ↔ config)" → "Default alignment (resolved YYYY-MM-DD)") and rewrite body to past tense. Preserve historical context under an explicit "Historical context:" sentence.
2. **`docs/llm/memories/<feature>.md`** (e.g. `max-webhook-support.md`) — move the item OUT of the "Known limitations" section into a NEW `## Resolved (YYYY-MM-DD):` subsection. Do NOT delete; preserve the historical divergence explanation. (Distinct from the whole-file SUPERSEDED banner convention in memory 909dc68a — this is an in-file item-level move.)
3. **`docs/llm/memories/review-fix-lessons.md`** (or analogous lessons file) — rewrite present-tense "did not land" / "open nit" framings to past-tense "landed YYYY-MM-DD" / "resolved".
4. **`docs/llm/architecture.md`** — VERIFY only. Often already correct (states the default accurately without describing a mismatch). No edit needed if it never described the issue as open.

## Key distinctions from related conventions
- vs. memory a92b25e7 (new-config-key sync): that covers `configuration.md` + `architecture.md` + `developer-guide.md` + `teamlead-memory.md`. Resolution-sync instead centres on the `docs/llm/memories/*.md` files that tracked the open issue, plus `configuration.md` callouts. The sets overlap but are not identical.
- vs. memory 909dc68a (SUPERSEDED banner): that's for a WHOLE file becoming obsolete. Resolution-sync handles individual bullets/items within a still-live file.
- vs. memory 71b4f7f4 (plans/ADRs immutable): plans/ADRs get status stamps only, never body rewrites. The memories/ and configuration.md files ARE edited in-place for resolution-sync.

## Ownership boundary observed
`docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` is maintained by the teamlead role separately. A software-developer doing a resolution-sync was explicitly instructed NOT to touch it ("teamlead handles that separately"). So the dev-owned resolution-sync set is the 3-4 docs above; teamlead-memory.md sync happens independently via the teamlead.

## Per-file framing guide
- Callout (configuration.md): header rename to "resolved YYYY-MM-DD" + past-tense body + preserved historical context.
- Memories feature file: bullet moves to "## Resolved (date):" subsection, keeps the historical divergence note.
- Lessons file: "did not land" → "landed YYYY-MM-DD", "open nit" → "resolved".
- Architecture: verify; usually no-op.

Acceptance check for any resolution-sync: no doc in the set still describes the issue as currently open; historical context preserved so a reader can tell it was previously a problem.

title: Single-shot empty FINAL: handler guard is sole defense (synthesizer gated on budgetExhausted)
content:
Architectural gotcha verified 2026-07-18 while writing regression tests for the empty-LLM-response guard. Clarifies the defense-in-depth layering between the service-layer synthesizer and the handler-level guard.

## The layering
Two mitigations exist for empty LLM output:
1. **Service-layer post-budget synthesizer** at `internal/services/llm/service.py:941` — fires a fallback LLM call to regenerate a non-empty reply.
2. **Handler-level guard** at `internal/bot/common/handlers/llm_messages.py:394` — returns `LLMReplyOutcome.SKIPPED_BY_MODEL` when text collapses to "".

## The non-obvious point
The synthesizer is gated on `budgetExhausted = maxRounds is not None and roundN >= maxRounds` (service.py:788) AND `status in (FINAL, TOOL_CALLS)` (TRUNCATED_FINAL is excluded — see memory 69a9d11f). The gating has a critical implication:

**A single-shot empty FINAL (no tool-use rounds, the COMMON case — model returns empty content with finish_reason="stop") does NOT set `budgetExhausted`, so the synthesizer NEVER fires.** The handler-level guard at L394 is the SOLE defense for this case.

Memory 69a9d11f documents that TRUNCATED_FINAL is excluded from the synthesizer (so empty TRUNCATED_FINAL also relies solely on the handler guard). This memory adds the symmetric insight: empty FINAL in the single-shot (non-round-capped) path ALSO relies solely on the handler guard, for a different reason (budgetExhausted=False).

## Why this matters
If someone removes or weakens the L394 guard thinking the synthesizer is a backstop, they would reintroduce the empty-message bug (`BadRequest: Message text is empty`) for the most common single-shot path. The synthesizer is NOT a general backstop — it only covers the round-budget-exhaustion corner case.

The handler guard predicate is: `lmRetText.strip().strip("`").strip() in ("<skip>", "")` — it catches both model abstention (`<skip>`) and genuinely empty output (after stripping whitespace and backticks).

## Test pinning
`TestLLMEmptyResponseGuard::testFinalStatusWithEmptyTextReturnsSkippedByModel` locks this in: a mocked single-shot empty FINAL returns SKIPPED_BY_MODEL via the handler guard, with the docstring explicitly recording that the synthesizer does not apply here.

title: Test convention: _sendLLMChatMessage direct-call pattern + ModelRunResult helpers
content:
Test convention confirmed 2026-07-18 for testing the LLM reply path in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_llm_messages.py`. Use when adding tests that exercise empty/edge-case LLM outputs or the abstention guard.

## Direct-call pattern (preferred over public handler methods)
Tests that need to assert on `_sendLLMChatMessage` outcomes call it DIRECTLY rather than going through the public `handleReply`/`handleMention`/`handleRandomMessage` entry points. This is how `TestRandomAnswerPromptAndSkipSentinel`, `TestMediaDescriptionExtraction`, and `TestLLMEmptyResponseGuard` are all structured. Pattern:

```python
liveHandler.llmService.generateTextViaLLM = AsyncMock(  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    return_value=_modelRunResultWithStatus(ModelResultStatus.FINAL, "some text")
)
em = _liveEnsuredMessage()
messagesHistory = [ModelMessage(role="system", content="sys")]
typingManager = AsyncMock()

outcome = await liveHandler._sendLLMChatMessage(em, messagesHistory, typingManager=typingManager)

assert outcome == LLMReplyOutcome.SKIPPED_BY_MODEL  # or .SENT
liveHandler.sendMessage.assert_not_awaited()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
liveHandler.llmService.generateImage.assert_not_awaited()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
```

Only `llmService.generateTextViaLLM` is mocked — the synthesizer logic (inside the real `generateTextViaLLM`) does NOT run, so tests isolate the handler-level guard cleanly.

## Fixtures and helpers
- `liveHandler` fixture (file-local): live `LLMMessageHandler` with `sendMessage` mocked as `AsyncMock(return_value=[Mock()])`. Uses `_fullChatSettings()` which defaults `llmMessageFormat="text"` (NOT JSON).
- `_liveEnsuredMessage()`: builds a realistic `EnsuredMessage` for the live handler.
- `_modelRunResult(resultText)`: builds `ModelRunResult(rawResult={}, status=ModelResultStatus.FINAL, resultText=resultText)`. Hardcodes FINAL — do NOT modify it (used by many existing tests).
- `_modelRunResultWithStatus(status, resultText="")` (line 471, added 2026-07-18): the status-flexible variant. Use this when you need TRUNCATED_FINAL, TOOL_CALLS, or other non-FINAL statuses.

## ModelRunResult construction notes
`ModelRunResult(rawResult={}, status=..., resultText=...)` — `resultText` defaults to `""` (never None); `isFallback`/`isToolsUsed` default False; `toolUsageHistory` empty. These are the values the handler paths under test exercise.

## LLMReplyOutcome members (llm_messages.py:68)
`SENT`, `ERROR`, `SKIPPED_BY_MODEL`. Import as `from internal.bot.common.handlers.llm_messages import LLMMessageHandler, LLMReplyOutcome`.

## When sendMessage is reached
For the SENT path: `sendMessage` returns `[Mock()]` (a list), and `sendSucceeded = (... is not None)` evaluates True → returns `SENT`. So asserting `SENT` requires `sendMessage.assert_awaited_once()`.

title: Convention: "formerly <OldName>" historical-pointer framing for renamed code symbols
content:
Project convention for docstrings/comments that reference a renamed or removed code symbol (method, function, class): use the historical-pointer form ``formerly ``_OldName`` `` rather than (a) the bare old name in backticks (which reads as if it's still current) or (b) silently updating to only the new name (which loses the breadcrumb for readers grepping the old name).

Established and applied consistently across 8+ non-archive sites during the 2026-07-18 Phase 8 docstring/comment fix pass, anchored on the `_persistMemoryEntry` → inlined-into-`_runSingleRefinement` rename:

- `internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:1175` — "inlined cursor-persist block, formerly the standalone ``_persistMemoryEntry``"
- `internal/services/cache/service.py:1137-1139` — "formerly ``_persistMemoryEntry``"
- `tests/services/cache/test_user_info.py:449` — "formerly _persistMemoryEntry"
- `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_memories.py:819-820, 857`
- `docs/llm/architecture.md:513, 532, 542, 544`
- `docs/llm/memories/user-memory-refinement.md:65, 84`
- `docs/llm/memories/chat-users-cache.md:55`
- `docs/llm/tasks.md:493`

The verification rule: when a symbol is renamed/removed, grep the old name across non-archive files. Every surviving reference should carry a "formerly" pointer. Present-tense-as-current references (e.g. "calls ``_persistMemoryEntry``") are drift and must be fixed. Archive files (`docs/archive/**`) are exempt — they're frozen historical snapshots.

This RESOLVES the "open-3-locations" status in memory 295b24d0: as of 2026-07-18 Phase 8, all three flagged sites use the historical-pointer convention correctly. No `_persistMemoryEntry` references remain in present-tense-as-current form outside `docs/archive/`.

Related: memory 0f9495aa covers the analogous forward-pointer convention for plan files superseded by a refactor. This convention is the inline-docstring/comment counterpart.

title: Gotcha: teamlead-memory.md "open follow-up" lists go stale when the follow-up batch lands
content:
Recurring documentation-drift failure mode, surfaced as the one medium-severity finding of the 2026-07-18 Phase 7-11 Gate 2 review.

**The pattern:** An audit or task creates a tracking section in `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` listing follow-up items as "open" / "deferred" / "flagged for separate code passes". When a subsequent batch of work (e.g. Phase 8/9/10/11) actually completes those items, the code and target docs get fixed BUT the tracking section in teamlead-memory.md is NOT reconciled. The result: a canonical memory file describes completed work as still-open, misleading every future agent that reads it for context.

**Concrete instance (as of 2026-07-18, needs reconciliation):**
- `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md:258-273` ("Cross-cutting code-side follow-ups") — enumerates ~12 code-side drifts (_persistMemoryEntry docstrings, application.py:127 default, constants.py stale path, mergeCondensingDicts docstring, chat_search.py schema comment, no regression test for llm_messages.py:394 empty-guard, etc.) that Phase 8/9 have since FIXED. The section still reads as a pending list.
- `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md:275-280` ("Open documentation decisions (deferred)") — lists "FREEZE-and-link for database-README.md" (resolved by Phase 11) and "AGENTS.md L124-127 needs the lib/ext_modules carve-out" (resolved by Phase 10). Still framed as deferred.
- `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md:287` — states "docs/archive/design/ = 24 archived + 1 README = 25 total" but Phase 7's restoration of custom-modules-design.md decremented the count to "23 archived + 1 README = 24 total" (confirmed by `docs/archive/README.md` and `docs/archive/design/README.md`).

**The fix when landing a follow-up batch:** Re-read the tracking sections of teamlead-memory.md that enumerate the work you just did. Either strike items through with "RESOLVED <date>" annotations, rewrite the section as a completed-retrospective, or delete the now-resolved section per the post-task memory-hygiene workflow (memory 5252a21d). Also re-verify any aggregate counts (archive totals, test totals) the section cites.

**Why it matters:** A future agent reading "Open documentation decisions: AGENTS.md L124-127 needs the carve-out" will either re-do the work or conclude the codebase is in a worse state than it is. This wastes session time and can cause incorrect reverts.

Complements memory 5252a21d (post-task memory hygiene — move completed task-specific sections out). This is the distinct failure mode that 5252a21d's workflow is meant to prevent but didn't catch here because the follow-up batch was tracked as a separate phase from the audit that created the list.

content:
Result of the 2026-07-18 systematic re-capture of `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/chat-openai-compat.md`. This NARROWS the scope of memory `7635bdd9` (which says the whole yc-ai-sdk bundle is unverified against the pinned 0.22.0 SDK). Sibling narrowing memory: `92f29e88` (image-generation.md).

Banner upgraded from "Version drift" to "Mostly verified against pinned SDK v0.22.0" (Option B). H1 updated to drop stale `(v0.20.2)` framing.

**Two concrete doc errors found and FIXED:**
1. `ChatModelResult` dataclass fields were wrong — copied from `GPTModelResult`. Actual v0.22.0 fields: `choices: tuple[ChatChoice, ...]`, `usage: ChatUsage | None`, `created: datetime`, `model: str`, `id: str`. The "Same structure as GPTModelResult" claim was false (GPTModelResult has `alternatives / usage / model_version`). See dedicated memory for full shape.
2. `model.list()` had wrong receiver — `list()` is on the domain/function class (`sdk.chat.completions.list(...)`), not on a model instance. Returns `tuple[AsyncChatModel, ...]`. This resolves the "should be" note in memory `647a8ec3` — now actually fixed in the doc.

**Endpoint discrepancy surfaced (not a doc bug):** production (`yc_openai_provider.py _getBaseUrl`) uses `https://ai.api.cloud.yandex.net/v1`; SDK internally (`_utils/http.py`) resolves `http_completions` to `https://llm.api.cloud.yandex.net/v1/`. Both are YC aliases. See dedicated memory.

**Verified correct (sample):** AsyncAIStudio constructor; `sdk.chat.completions(name, *, model_version='latest')`; `.configure(temperature, max_tokens, reasoning_mode, response_format, tools, parallel_tool_calls, tool_choice, extra_query)`; ChatReasoningMode enum LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH; `reasoning_mode` → `reasoning_effort` JSON mapping; `extra_query` top-level dict.update merge; `model.run/run_stream` signatures; `{"role":..., "content":...}` message shape + `TextMessage(role=, text=)`; `sdk.chat.text_embeddings("doc")` + `.run(input, *, timeout=)`; `gpt://`/`emb://` URI prefixes; comparison tables (gRPC has run_deferred/tokenize/tune, chat does not).

**Constraint noted:** SDK uses snake_case for its own API (Python convention) — match SDK naming in code examples, don't impose project camelCase on SDK calls. Project camelCase applies only to project-internal identifiers.

title: SDK v0.22.0 internally uses llm.api.cloud.yandex.net (explains production ai. override)
content:
Refines memories `743be180` (production URL changed llm. → ai.) and `6a158012` (production uses ai.api.cloud.yandex.net). Both recorded production's URL but neither explained the WHY.

**Finding (2026-07-18, SDK v0.22.0):** The `yandex_ai_studio_sdk` package itself STILL uses `llm.api.cloud.yandex.net` internally. In `venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/yandex_ai_studio_sdk/_utils/http.py`, the `CLOUD_ENDPOINTS` dict maps `http_completions` → `'https://llm.api.cloud.yandex.net/v1/'`. The SDK's `BaseChatFunction._fetch_raw_models` (the `sdk.chat.completions.list()` path) and any direct `sdk.chat.*` HTTP calls go through this.

**So the divergence is intentional on production's side:** `lib/ai/providers/yc_openai_provider.py:290` (`_getBaseUrl()`) hardcodes `https://ai.api.cloud.yandex.net/v1`, overriding what the SDK would use if production consumed `sdk.chat.*` directly. But production does NOT use `sdk.chat.*` — it uses the raw `openai` Python SDK (`openai.AsyncOpenAI`) against YC's OpenAI-compat endpoint, so the SDK's internal endpoint never comes into play at runtime.

**Practical implication:** Both `ai.api.cloud.yandex.net` and `llm.api.cloud.yandex.net` are YC aliases for the same service. If debugging at the HTTP level or refactoring to use `sdk.chat.*` directly, expect the SDK to spell the URL differently from production. Don't "fix" one to match the other without confirming YC still honours both.

title: YC SDK v0.22.0 ChatModelResult shape + reasoning_effort wire mapping
content:
Durable SDK-shape knowledge verified 2026-07-18 from `venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/yandex_ai_studio_sdk/_chat/completions/result.py` (v0.22.0). Not previously captured; complements the chat-openai-compat.md doc fix.

**`ChatModelResult` actual fields (NOT same as `GPTModelResult`):**
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ChatModelResult(
    TupleSequence[ChatChoice],
    BaseJsonResult,
    HaveToolCalls[ToolCallTypeT],
):
    choices: tuple[ChatChoice[ToolCallTypeT], ...]
    usage: ChatUsage | None       # NOT CompletionUsage; ChatUsage extends Usage
    created: datetime.datetime
    model: str
    id: str
    # NO model_version field (that's GPTModelResult-only)
```

For comparison, `GPTModelResult` (gRPC side, `_models/completions/result.py`) has `alternatives: tuple[Alternative, ...]`, `usage: CompletionUsage`, `model_version: str`. They are structurally DIFFERENT — do not copy one's shape when documenting the other.

**`ChatModelResult` convenience properties (beyond tuple-indexing via TupleSequence):**
- `.text` — shortcut to first choice's content
- `.content` — alias-ish for first choice content
- `.role` — first choice's role
- `.status` — first choice's status
- `.finish_reason` — first choice's finish_reason
- `.tool_calls` — first choice's tool calls (HaveToolCells mixin)
- `.reasoning_text` / `.reasoning_content` — reasoning fields (chat-specific)
- `.alternatives` — PROPERTY (not field) returning `.choices`; exists for gRPC-API familiarity, do not mistake for a dataclass field

**Other v0.22.0 chat-domain facts worth remembering:**
- `ChatReasoningMode(str, Enum)`: `LOW='low'`, `MEDIUM='medium'`, `HIGH='high'`. Coerces input via `.lower()`. Accepted as `ChatReasoningModeType = Union[Literal['low','medium','high'], Literal['LOW','MEDIUM','HIGH'], ChatReasoningMode]`.
- Wire-format translation: `reasoning_mode` (Python param) → `reasoning_effort` (JSON body key). Implemented in `_chat/completions/model.py:106-107`.
- gRPC side uses a DIFFERENT enum: `ReasoningMode` with `DISABLED`/`ENABLED_HIDDEN` (not low/medium/high).
- `extra_query` merge: top-level `result.update(c.extra_query)` in the request body (`model.py:118-119`).
- URI prefixes: `gpt://` for `sdk.chat.completions`, `emb://` for `sdk.chat.text_embeddings`.

title: "Verified against pinned SDK" banner + ⚠ marker — post-re-capture banner variant
content:
NEW banner variant introduced 2026-07-18 during the full re-capture of `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/image-generation.md` (software-developer agent, glm-5.1). Distinct from and SUCCESSOR TO the drift-banner conventions in `39c3e386` (bundle-level drift), `e2e64de9` (file-scoped drift cross-reference), and `c581510d` (per-fix "Drift correction" body callout).

**The lifecycle:** a version-pinned reference doc transitions through three banner states:
1. **Drift banner** (`39c3e386`/`e2e64de9`) — installed SDK version has moved on from the doc's pinned version; drift suspected or confirmed.
2. **Per-fix drift-correction callouts** (`c581510d`) — spot-fixes applied inline to specific wrong claims, each marked `> **Drift correction (VERSION).** ...`.
3. **"Verified against" banner** (THIS memory) — a FULL re-capture against the installed wheel has been completed; the drift banner is REMOVED and REPLACED with a positive verification assertion.

**The "Verified against" banner shape** (applied to image-generation.md):
```
> **Verified against pinned SDK v0.22.0** (re-captured 2026-07-18 from
> `venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/yandex_ai_studio_sdk/`). Production
> consumers: `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py::_generateImage` (YC SDK
> direct, `yandex-art`); `lib/ai/providers/basic_openai_provider.py::_generateImageViaImagesApi`
> (OpenAI-compat Images API, `aliceai-image-art`). Claims marked with ⚠ are
> server-side facts not checkable from the SDK source.
```

**Three required elements of this banner variant:**
1. The pinned SDK version + re-capture date + wheel source path.
2. Production consumer citations (with method names + model identifiers) — see `ca61665e` for why BOTH consumers must be named for image-gen.
3. The ⚠ marker semantics definition: "Claims marked with ⚠ are server-side facts not checkable from the SDK source."

**The ⚠ inline marker convention** (new, defined by this banner): any concrete claim in the doc body that cannot be verified from the installed wheel source (server-side facts: model-name availability/roster, IAM scopes, server-side limits like character counts, endpoint availability) is marked with an inline `⚠`. Client-side/wheel-verifiable claims carry NO marker. This lets a reader distinguish "verified from source" from "asserted but server-dependent" at a glance, and lets a future re-auditor `grep ⚠` to find everything that needs re-checking against server docs.

**Observed ⚠ instances in image-generation.md (2026-07-18):** (1) "YandexART model family" roster grouping, (2) `yandex-art` server availability, (3) `yandex-art-2.0` server availability, (4) 500-char context limit, (5) `yc.ai.imageGeneration.execute` scope, (6) "server-side availability" caveat on the Complete Example.

**When to use this banner variant:** only after a COMPLETE walk-through of every concrete claim in the file against the installed wheel (not after spot-fixes — those use `c581510d` callouts and keep the drift banner). The H1 is also typically updated to include `(verified against pinned vX.Y.Z, DATE)`.

**Complements/supersedes:** for image-generation.md specifically, this REPLACES the file-scoped drift banner documented in `e2e64de9`. The drift-banner conventions remain valid for files that have NOT yet been fully re-captured.

title: YC AI Studio SDK wheel layout — per-domain file roles for audit navigation
content:
Navigation aid for auditing/re-capturing `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/*.md` against the installed SDK wheel at `venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/yandex_ai_studio_sdk/`. Confirmed 2026-07-18 during the image-generation.md full re-capture (software-developer agent, glm-5.1). SDK pinned at `yandex-ai-studio-sdk==0.22.0` (per `requirements.direct.txt`).

**Per-domain package structure** under `_models/<domain>/` (e.g. `_models/image_generation/`, `_models/completions/`, `_models/text_embeddings/`, `_models/text_classifiers/`):
- `__init__.py` — empty (no re-exports).
- `function.py` — the `Base<Domain>` factory class + `Async<Domain>` / `<Domain>` (sync) subclasses. This is what `sdk.models.<domain>(...)` actually invokes. Defines `__call__(model_name, *, model_version="latest")` and constructs the model URI via `BaseSDK._get_model_uri(prefix, ...)`. For image_generation the prefix is `"art"` → URI `art://<folder_id>/<model_name>/<model_version>`; completions uses `"gpt"`.
- `model.py` — `Async<Model>` / `<Model>` (sync) classes. Contains `configure(...)`, `run_deferred(...)`, `_run_deferred(...)`, and the internal `_to_proto` / wire-coercion logic. For image_generation: `AsyncImageGenerationModel`.
- `config.py` — `@dataclass(frozen=True) class <Domain>ModelConfig(BaseModelConfig)`. Fields default to `None` at the dataclass level; the corresponding `configure()` params default to `UNDEFINED` (UndefinedOr sentinel) — these are TWO DIFFERENT defaults and conflation is a common drift (see drift-checklist memory).
- `result.py` — `<Domain>ModelResult` dataclass, typically `@dataclass(frozen=True, repr=False)`, inheriting from `BaseProtoResult[<ProtoResponse>]`. Snippets in docs often OMIT the base class — verify and add it.
- `message.py` (where applicable) — message TypedDict(s) + the `messages_to_proto` coercion. TypedDict fields often use `NotRequired[...]` for optional fields; field types here are authoritative (e.g. `weight: NotRequired[float]`, NOT int).

**Supporting type files** under `_types/`:
- `model.py` — `BaseModel`, `ModelAsyncAttachMixin` (provides `attach_deferred(operation_id, *, timeout=60)`), `ModelTypeT`. The attach mixin is where `attach_deferred` lives, NOT on the domain model class itself.
- `operation.py` — `AsyncOperation[ResultT]` returned by `run_deferred`. Has `id`, `__await__` (delegates to `wait()`), `wait(*, timeout=60, poll_timeout=None→default 3600, poll_interval=None→default 10)`, `get_status`, `get_result`, `cancel`. All `wait()` args after `*` are keyword-only.
- `function.py` — `BaseModelFunction` base for the factory classes.
- `misc.py` — `Undefined` sentinel class, `UNDEFINED` singleton, `UndefinedOr[T]` type alias. `UNDEFINED` means "leave the existing config value unchanged" at the `configure()` parameter level.
- `model_config.py` — `BaseModelConfig` base.

**Top-level entry points:**
- `__init__.py` — exports `AIStudio`, `AsyncAIStudio`.
- `_sdk.py` — `BaseSDK`, `AsyncAIStudio` (line ~265), `AIStudio`. Has `.models` property returning `AsyncModels` / `Models`. Contains `_get_model_uri(prefix, model_name, model_version)` — if `'://' in model_name`, returns model_name verbatim; else `f"{prefix}://{folder_id}/{model_name}/{model_version}"`.
- `_models/__init__.py` — `AsyncModels` / `Models` (subclass of `DomainWithFunctions`); one factory property per domain (`image_generation`, `completions`, `text_embeddings`, `text_classifiers`).
- `exceptions.py` + `_exceptions.py` — `AioRpcError` (subclass of `grpc.aio.AioRpcError`), `AIStudioError`, `AsyncOperationError`, `RunError`, etc. `AioRpcError.details()` is the method to read error detail strings (used in ETHIC_DETAILS content-filter detection).

**Method availability per domain model:** NOT every domain model has `run()` / `run_stream()`. Image generation has ONLY `run_deferred()` + `attach_deferred()` (image gen is async-only server-side). Always check which methods exist on the specific `<Domain>Model` class before claiming them in docs.

title: Drift-checklist for YC SDK doc re-captures — 8 recurring drift categories
content:
Reusable audit checklist of drift categories found during the 2026-07-18 full re-capture of `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/image-generation.md` against `yandex-ai-studio-sdk==0.22.0` (software-developer agent, glm-5.1). These categories are generalizable to sibling docs in the bundle (`completions.md`, `speech.md`, `text-embeddings.md`, etc.) — check each one when re-capturing.

**1. Config-table conflation (configure param vs dataclass field).** Doc tables mix the `configure()` parameter default (`UndefinedOr[T] = UNDEFINED`) with the config dataclass field default (`T | None = None`). These describe two different layers. Fix: split into two columns or add a clarifying footnote. Recurs in EVERY domain that has a config (all of them).

**2. Missing base class on result/model dataclass snippets.** Doc shows `@dataclass class FooResult:` as standalone; actually inherits from `BaseProtoResult[<ProtoResponse>]` (or analogous base). Always check the `class FooResult(...):` parens. Also check the `@dataclass(...)` decorator args — image-gen uses `frozen=True, repr=False` (because a custom `__repr__` is defined).

**3. TypedDict field types (float vs int, NotRequired).** Doc examples pass `weight: 5` (int) but the TypedDict declares `NotRequired[float]`. The runtime accepts it; the static type is wrong. Always cross-check example literals against the TypedDict field types in `message.py`.

**4. Undocumented related APIs.** The doc shows `await operation` and `operation.wait(poll_interval=..., poll_timeout=...)` but never documents the full `AsyncOperation` API (`id`, `get_status`, `get_result`, `cancel`, default `poll_timeout=3600` / `poll_interval=10`). When a return type has its own rich API, document it as a subsection, not just the await shape.

**5. Wire-level None coercion.** `_run_deferred` / `_run` often does `self.config.seed or 0`, `self.config.mime_type or ""`, etc. A `None` config value reaches the server as `0` / `""`, NOT omitted. This is non-obvious and worth documenting (affects what "default" means server-side).

**6. Internal method signature precision.** Doc prose references production helper calls like `toDict("text", skipRole=True)` without naming the first positional parameter. Verify against the real signature (`lib/ai/models.py:696` → `toDict(content_key=None, ..., skipRole=False, ...)`). Name the parameters explicitly.

**7. TOML key vs actual model_id mismatch.** The config TOML key (e.g. `"aliceai-image-art"`) is often different from the `model_id` value sent to the API (e.g. `aliceai-image-art-3.0`). When citing "the model", show BOTH the TOML key and the `model_id` value to avoid confusion. Check `configs/00-defaults/yc-*-models.toml`.

**8. Server-side vs client-side claim confusion.** Doc presents server-side facts (model-name availability, IAM scopes, character limits, endpoint URLs) as if they were client-side verifiable. Mark these with inline ⚠ (see the "Verified against" banner memory). Specifically: model roster grouping ("YandexART family"), individual model availability (`yandex-art`, `yandex-art-2.0`), context/character limits, IAM scopes like `yc.ai.imageGeneration.execute`.

**Audit workflow that surfaces these:** walk every concrete claim in the doc; for each, open the corresponding wheel file under `venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/yandex_ai_studio_sdk/_models/<domain>/{model,config,result,message,function}.py` (see wheel-layout memory) and the production consumer under `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py`; mark unverifiable server-side claims with ⚠. The two-production-consumers gotcha (`ca61665e`) applies when deciding which consumer to cite.

title: Verified YC SDK 0.22.0 tools & structured-output API facts (tools-and-structured-output.md Wave 12 audit)
content:
Concrete SDK 0.22.0 API facts verified at the source during the 2026-07-18 Wave 12 re-verification of `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/tools-and-structured-output.md`. All file:line citations are against `venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/yandex_ai_studio_sdk/`. Useful when auditing the still-unaudited bundle files (`index.md`, `gap-analysis.md`, `embeddings-and-other.md`) or when modifying production tool-handling code.

**`sdk.tools.function(parameters, *, name, description, strict)`** signature — `_tools/function.py:22-29`. All three kwargs are `UndefinedOr[T] = UNDEFINED` (NOT `None` — passing `None` explicitly sets the proto field to None, which differs from leaving it unset). Returns `FunctionTool`.

**`FunctionTool` frozen dataclass** — `_tools/tool.py:83-103` (fields at 96-103): `name: str`, `description: str | None`, `parameters: JsonSchemaType`, `strict: bool | None`.

**`sdk.tools.search_index(indexes, *, max_num_results, rephraser, call_strategy)`** — `_tools/domain.py:83-90`.
**`sdk.tools.generative_search(*, description, site, host, url, enable_nrfm_docs, search_filters)`** — `_tools/domain.py:122-131`.
**`site`/`host`/`url` mutually exclusive** — enforced BOTH in docstring (`_tools/domain.py:143`) AND at runtime via assertion (`_tools/generative_search.py:73`).
**Delegation** — generative_search internally calls `sdk.search_api.generative(...).as_tool(description=...)` (`_tools/domain.py:163-170`). `as_tool()` lives on `BaseGenerativeSearch` at `_search_api/generative/generative.py:155-174`.

**`tool_choice` accepted forms** — `_types/tools/tool_choice.py`:
- String: `ToolChoiceStringType = Literal['none', 'None', 'NONE', 'auto', 'Auto', 'AUTO', 'required', 'Required', 'REQUIRED']` — any casing accepted (lines 16-22).
- Dict: `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "<name>"}}` — shape `FunctionDictType` at `_types/tools/function.py:13-15`.
- `FunctionTool` instance directly.

**`GPTModelConfig` 7 fields** — `_models/completions/config.py:39-59`: `temperature`, `max_tokens`, `reasoning_mode`, `response_format`, `tools`, `parallel_tool_calls`, `tool_choice`. SDK docstring says `parallel_tool_calls` defaults to 'true' server-side.

**`ChatModelConfig(GPTModelConfig)`** — `_chat/completions/config.py:46-61`. Inherits all GPTModelConfig fields, but OVERRIDES `reasoning_mode` and `tools` (tools narrowed to `tuple[CompletionTool, ...] | None`) and ADDS `extra_query`. Docs that imply identical field sets are slightly imprecise.

**`result.tool_calls`** — `_models/completions/result.py:148-149` returns `ToolCallList | None`; iterable via `TupleSequence`. Each item has `.id: str | None` (proto path sets `id=None` in completions domain — see `_tools/tool_call.py:42-45, 60-64`), `.function.name: str`, `.function.arguments: JsonObject` (parsed dict, NOT JSON string — see separate memory `9b4e19b8`). Production `yc_sdk_provider.py:478` falls back to `uuid.uuid4()` when `call.id is None`.

**`response_format` accepts FOUR input shapes** — `_types/schemas.py:38` (`ResponseType = Union[StrResponseType, JsonSchemaResponseType, type]`):
1. Literal `"json"` (`LITERAL_RESPONSE_FORMATS = ('json',)`) — SDK sets `json_object=True`; "you must mention JSON in the prompt" is SERVER-SIDE guidance, not SDK-enforced.
2. Schema dict `{"json_schema": {...}, "name": ..., "strict": ...}`.
3. Pydantic `BaseModel` subclass.
4. **Pydantic dataclass** — `_types/schemas.py:124-152`. UNDOCUMENTED in the pre-Wave-12 doc; Wave 12 added a one-line note. Easy to miss.

**Strict mode** — `_tools/function.py:46` docstring claims "strict parameter validation"; actual enforcement is SERVER-SIDE — the SDK only forwards the boolean flag to the proto. The flag is **completions-only at the wire level** (`_tools/tool.py:136-147` raises `ValueError` for `sdk.assistants` because the assistants proto `FunctionTool` has no `strict` field). Mark with ⚠ in any doc that claims strict-validation behavior.

**Production consumer code locations (verified 2026-07-18):**
- Tool-call extraction: `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py:480` — `parameters=call.function.arguments` (dict assigned directly; no `json.loads`).
- `_convertMessages` (feed-back shape conversion): `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py:330-370` — emits bundled `{role, tool_results: [{name, content}]}` (matches `FunctionResultMessageDict` at `_models/completions/message.py:27-33`).
- `_tryHealToolCall` orchestrator-side healing loop: `internal/services/llm/service.py:624` (NOT in yc_sdk_provider.py — easy to misattribute). See `docs/llm/memories/llm-tool-call-healing.md`.

**`FunctionResultMessageDict` gRPC shape** — `_models/completions/message.py:27-33`: `{role?: str, tool_results: Iterable[{name: str, content: str, type?: str}]}`. `ToolResultDictType = FunctionResultDict` at `_tools/tool_result.py:38-48`. (Cross-references existing memory `dafc1c74`.)

**Chat-domain tool-result wire format** (different from completions domain): `{"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "<id>", "content": "<str>"}` — one message per result, NOT bundled. Verified at `_chat/completions/message.py:119-126`.

No code-level drifts found beyond Wave 11's 5 fixes; only the undocumented pydantic-dataclass capability was added. Server-side-only claims (auto RAG routing, AI-summarized citations, "must mention JSON", strict-mode enforcement) were marked ⚠ in the doc.

title: YC SDK _get_model_uri only does "://" passthrough — short-form URIs with slashes get mangled
content:
Non-obvious gotcha in `yandex-ai-studio-sdk` (verified against pinned v0.22.0, 2026-07-18) that affects how fine-tuned model URIs must be constructed.

**The behavior** — `BaseSDK._get_model_uri(prefix, model_name, model_version)` in `_sdk.py`:
```python
def _get_model_uri(self, prefix, model_name, model_version, well_known_names=None):
    if '://' in model_name:
        return model_name                      # passthrough branch
    well_known_names = well_known_names or {}
    model_name = well_known_names.get(model_name, model_name)
    return f'{prefix}://{self._folder_id}/{model_name}/{model_version}'
```

The passthrough branch fires ONLY when the literal substring `://` appears in `model_name`. Otherwise the SDK blindly interpolates `model_name` into `f'{prefix}://{folder_id}/{model_name}/{model_version}'` — it does NOT validate that `model_name` is a single path segment.

**Consequence for fine-tuned models** — `sdk.models.completions("yandexgpt-lite/latest@<tuning-suffix>")` (short form, as some docs/examples show) is SILENTLY BROKEN:
- No `://` in the input → falls into the construct branch.
- Result: `gpt://<fid>/yandexgpt-lite/latest@<tuning-suffix>/latest` — `/latest` (the default `model_version`) gets appended AFTER the `@<tuning-suffix>`, producing a malformed URI.

**Correct usage** — always pass the FULL URI so the `://` passthrough branch fires:
```python
model = sdk.models.completions("gpt://<folder_id>/yandexgpt-lite/latest@<tuning-suffix>")
```

`parse_uri` in `_utils/parse_uri.py` uses regex `r'^\w+://(?P<folder_id>[^/]+)/(?P<name>[^/]+)/(?P<version>[^@/]+)(@(?P<fine_tune>[^/]+))?'` — so the `@<fine_tune>` suffix IS supported, but only when the input already contains `://`.

**Production impact** — `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py` (gRPC completions path, `YcAIModel` class) is the consumer. If it ever needs to construct a fine-tuned model handle, it MUST pass the full `gpt://...@suffix` URI, not a short form.

Related: memory 23dccbe6 (SDK has no well_known_names registry — the dict defaults to empty for completions, so there is no short-form rescue there either).

Docs reference: `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/completions.md` § "Fine-Tuned Models" was corrected on 2026-07-18 to use the full-URI form for exactly this reason.

title: YC SDK GPTModel.configure() is immutable and has exactly 7 params (no frequency_penalty, no extra_query)
content:
Non-obvious behavioral facts about `AsyncGPTModel.configure()` / `GPTModel.configure()` in `yandex-ai-studio-sdk` (verified against pinned v0.22.0, 2026-07-18).

**1. Immutability — `.configure()` returns a NEW instance, does NOT mutate the receiver.**

Source (`_types/model.py::BaseModel.configure`):
```python
def configure(self, **kwargs) -> Self:
    kwargs = {k: v for k, v in kwargs.items() if not isinstance(v, Undefined)}
    new_config = self._config._replace(**kwargs)   # frozen dataclass _replace
    return self.__class__(                          # NEW instance, not self
        sdk=self._sdk,
        uri=self._uri,
        config=new_config,
    )
```

Implication: `model.configure(temperature=0.5)` discards its return value → silent no-op, original `model` keeps its old config. Must capture the return: `model = model.configure(temperature=0.5)`. The return type annotation `-> Self` is the class type, NOT instance identity, which is easy to misread as "mutate-and-return-self".

**2. Exact parameter list — 7 keyword-only params, NOT the OpenAI-compat set.**

From `_models/completions/model.py::BaseGPTModel.configure`:
```python
def configure(
    self, *,
    temperature: UndefinedOr[float] = UNDEFINED,
    max_tokens: UndefinedOr[int] = UNDEFINED,
    reasoning_mode: UndefinedOr[ReasoningModeType] = UNDEFINED,
    response_format: UndefinedOr[ResponseType] = UNDEFINED,
    tools: UndefinedOr[Sequence[CompletionTool] | CompletionTool] = UNDEFINED,
    parallel_tool_calls: UndefinedOr[bool] = UNDEFINED,
    tool_choice: UndefinedOr[ToolChoiceType] = UNDEFINED,
) -> Self:
```

Params that DO NOT EXIST on `.configure()` (common wrong assumptions from OpenAI-compat):
- `frequency_penalty` — not a param
- `presence_penalty` — not a param
- `top_p` — not a param
- `stop` — not a param
- `seed` — not a param (only on `ImageGenerationModelConfig` and tuning params)
- `n` — not a param (response schema `tuple[Alternative, ...]` can still hold multiple, but count is server-determined)
- `logprobs` — not a param
- `user` — not a param
- `extra_query` / `extra_body` — not a param

**3. `UNDEFINED` sentinel filtering.** Any kwarg whose value is the `UNDEFINED` singleton (from `yandex_ai_studio_sdk._types.misc`) is stripped before `_replace`. This is how "leave as-is" is expressed — `None` is a real value (e.g. `parallel_tool_calls=None` means "auto/default behavior"), distinct from "didn't pass it".

**Production impact** — `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py` (`YcAIModel._getModel` ~line 244) calls `.configure()` per-request. Any caller assuming mutation or passing OpenAI-style params will silently get wrong behavior.

Docs reference: `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/completions.md` § ".configure() Parameters" + immutability note verified 2026-07-18.

title: YC SDK run_stream is an async generator — never await it (TypeError)
content:
Reusable gotcha verified against pinned `yandex-ai-studio-sdk==0.22.0` during the 2026-07-18 `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/speech.md` re-verification. Applies to any future audit of the remaining unaudited bundle files (`index.md`, `gap-analysis.md`, `embeddings-and-other.md`) and is a general Python trap worth remembering.

**The trap.** `run_stream` on BOTH `TextToSpeech` and `SpeechToText` (and their async/sync variants) is an **async generator function**, not a coroutine. Source: `_speechkit/text_to_speech/tts.py:250` and `_speechkit/speech_to_text/stt.py:374` — both are `async def ... :` with a `yield chunk` body. Per PEP 525, calling an async generator function returns an async generator object that is **async-iterable but NOT awaitable**.

- WRONG: `async for chunk in await tts.run_stream(...):` → raises `TypeError: object async_generator can't be used in 'await' expression`
- RIGHT: `async for chunk in tts.run_stream(...):` (no `await`)

`run_stream` yields `TextToSpeechResult` (TTS) / `SpeechToTextStreamingEvent` (STT), one per chunk.

**Contrast — these ARE awaitable (don't conflate):**
- `run(...)`, `run_deferred(...)`, `attach_deferred(...)`, `get_recognition_result(...)` — all `async def` returning a value (coroutines). MUST be awaited.
- `AsyncOperation` — has `__await__` (`_types/operation.py:410`), so `result = await operation` is valid. (Also has `.wait(poll_interval, poll_timeout)`, `.get_status()`, `.get_result()`, `.cancel()`.)
- `attach_deferred` specifically (`_types/model.py:163`): `async def attach_deferred(self, operation_id: str, timeout: float = 60)`. A common doc bug is awaiting `run_deferred` correctly but forgetting to await `attach_deferred`.

**Decision rule for distinguishing in docs/code review:**
1. `async def` with `yield` in body → async generator → `async for`, NEVER `await`.
2. `async def` without `yield` → coroutine → MUST `await`.
3. Object with `__await__` (e.g. `AsyncOperation`) → awaitable → `await` works.

When auditing SDK examples, grep for `await .*\.run_stream` and `await .*\.run_stream\(` as a drift signal — every match is a bug unless the method has been changed to a coroutine-returning shape (re-verify the source first).

title: speech.md re-verification (Wave 12): 3 more drifts fixed, ⚠ convention established
content:
Result of the 2026-07-18 follow-up re-verification of `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/speech.md` (residual claims Phase 3d Wave 11 did not touch). Complements the prior Wave 11 speech.md memory (6 drifts) and the completions facts memory `dafc1c74`. All 17 claim groups in the task brief were verified against pinned SDK 0.22.0 source at `venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/yandex_ai_studio_sdk/_speechkit/`; 3 NEW drifts beyond Wave 11's 6 were found and fixed.

**Newly-found drifts (fixed):**
1. **`await tts/stt.run_stream(...)`** (4 sites) — `run_stream` is an async generator; `await` raises TypeError. Removed the spurious `await` at all 4 sites. See the dedicated async-generator gotcha memory for the full rule.
2. **`stt.attach_deferred(...)` missing `await`** — `attach_deferred` is `async def` (`_types/model.py:163`). Doc awaited `run_deferred` correctly but not `attach_deferred`. Added `await`.
3. **`Utterance.final_refinement_text` typed `str`** — actually `str | None` (`_speechkit/speech_to_text/result/top_containers.py:65`; returns None when no `final_refinement` events arrived). Clarified that `.text` is always `str` (it falls back to `final_text`).

**⚠ documentation convention (now canonical for the bundle):** the banner reads `Claims marked with ⚠ are server-side facts not checkable from the SDK source.` Refined interpretation established this session: facts that appear **inside SDK source** (field types, signatures, AND docstrings — e.g. speed default 1.0, MAX_PEAK volume range (0,1] default 0.7, LUFS range [-145,0) default -19, pitch_shift range [-1000,1000], PCM16 server default 22050Hz WAV) ARE checkable → no ⚠. The only genuine ⚠ in speech.md is the **TTS `voice` name examples** ("oksana", "alice", "ermil") — the available-voice roster is server-side data, not enumerated anywhere in the SDK. Apply the same rule when auditing other bundle files.

**Verified SDK 0.22.0 speech facts (for cross-doc reuse — likely to recur in index.md / gap-analysis.md / embeddings-and-other.md):**
- Factories + aliases: `sdk.speechkit.text_to_speech(...)` / `.tts(...)` / `.speech_to_text(...)` / `.stt(...)` (`domain.py:20-27,32-36,41-45`). Factory-level `sdk.speechkit.speech_to_text.get_recognition_result(operation_id, timeout=60)` is async.
- `TextToSpeechConfig`: 12 fields (`config.py:14-47`); `single_chunk_mode: bool = False` is the only non-None default.
- `SpeechToTextConfig`: 9 fields (`config.py:21-67`); `audio_format` is REQUIRED (no default). The factory/configure accept `recognition_classifiers: ... | bool` for True/False shortcuts even though the dataclass stores `RecognitionClassifiersInputType | None`.
- `AudioFormat` enum (`enums.py:71-93`): members `MP3`, `WAV`, `OGG_OPUS`, `PCM16`. There is NO `RAW_OPUS` or `WAV_PCM` member. `PCM16(sample_rate_hertz, channels=1)` is a classmethod where `sample_rate_hertz` is REQUIRED (no default) — only `channels` defaults to 1.
- `LanguageCode` enum (`enums.py:163-199`): 17 values (`auto` + 16 locale-specific); matches doc exactly.
- `LoudnessNormalization` (`enums.py:152-160`): `MAX_PEAK`, `LUFS` only.
- Default timeouts: `run`/`run_stream`/`run_deferred`/`attach_deferred` = 60s; `create_bistream` = `10*60`=600s (both TTS at `tts.py:220` and STT at `stt.py:337`). Note these are HALF the completions defaults (180s run / 60s deferred) — speech and completions use different timeout scales.
- `SpeechToTextResult` is a `Sequence` over `ChannelResult` (iterating yields channels, NOT utterances). `ChannelResult.tag: str`, `.utterances: tuple[Utterance, ...]`. Single-channel proxies: `result.text`, `result.final_text`, `result.final_refinement_text`.
- `Utterance` (`top_containers.py:33-74`): fields `events`, `classifiers`, `speaker_analysis`, `timespan`, `finals`, `final_refinements`, `final_classifiers` + properties `.final_text` (str), `.final_refinement_text` (str | None), `.text` (str).
- TTS and STT are entirely unused in production (no callers in `lib/`, `internal/`, `main.py` — see `gap-analysis.md`).

**SDK layout navigation note:** the task brief's reference path `_speechkit/top_containers.py` does NOT exist. The real location is `_speechkit/speech_to_text/result/top_containers.py` (the STT result module is a subpackage with 16 files: `alternatives.py`, `audio_cursors.py`, `base.py`, `classifier*.py`, `context.py`, `conversation_analysis.py`, `descriptive_statistics.py`, `event.py`, `llm_post_process_result.py`, `speaker_analysis.py`, `status_code.py`, `top_containers.py`, `utils.py`). TTS result is a single module `_speechkit/text_to_speech/result.py`.

title: YC SDK v0.22.0 structural facts for the 6 unwired domains (embeddings/classifiers/search/tuning/datasets/batch)
content:
Verified API shapes for the 6 SDK domains that are NOT wired in production (production embeddings use `lib/ai/providers/fastembed_provider.py`). Captured 2026-07-18 from `venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/yandex_ai_studio_sdk/` (pinned `yandex-ai-studio-sdk==0.22.0`). These are the facts most likely to bite future doc edits or any attempt to wire these domains:

**Auth import gotcha:** `APIKeyAuth` (and the other 6 auth classes) are NOT exported from the top-level `yandex_ai_studio_sdk` package. Import via `from yandex_ai_studio_sdk.auth import APIKeyAuth` (the `auth.py` submodule re-exports them). Using `APIKeyAuth(...)` after only `from yandex_ai_studio_sdk import AsyncAIStudio` raises `NameError`.

**Search API has 5 subdomains, not 4:** `sdk.search_api.generative(...)`, `.web(...)`, `.image(...)`, `.by_image(...)`, AND `.wordstat()`. The `wordstat` subdomain (keyword statistics: `get_top`/`get_dynamics`/`get_regions_distribution`/`get_regions_tree`) is commonly missed — it has no `run()` method and doesn't fit the model-style method-availability table.

**SearchType valid values:** `RU | TR | COM | KK | BE | UZ`. The SDK alias dict is `{'BY': 'BE', 'KK': 'KZ'}` — meaning `"BY"` is accepted as an alias for `BE` (NOT for KK, as one doc erroneously claimed). `KK` resolves directly as a member; the `'KK': 'KZ'` alias entry is effectively unreachable.

**Search Indexes `index_type` MUST be a class instance, not a string:** it must be a `BaseSearchIndexType` subclass instance — `TextSearchIndexType(...)`, `VectorSearchIndexType(...)`, or `HybridSearchIndexType(...)`. Passing `index_type="BM25"` (as one doc did) raises `TypeError`; there is NO "BM25" type. `create_deferred` returns `AsyncOperation[AsyncSearchIndex]`. The `SearchIndex` object has `update`/`delete`/`get_file`/`list_files`/`add_files_deferred` — there is NO `.query()` method (querying is done via the Assistant API).

**Batch access pattern:** there is NO `as_batch()`/`batch_run()`/`batch_run_deferred()` on models. The correct pattern is `model.batch.run_deferred(dataset, *, timeout=60)` where `.batch` is a `cached_property` returning a `BatchSubdomain`. ONLY `GPTModel` (completions) mixes in `BaseModelBatchMixin` — embeddings/classifiers/search models do NOT have batch support.

**KnownTaskType enum has no "TextGeneration":** the valid value is `TextToTextGeneration`. Other members: `TextClassificationMultilabel`, `TextClassificationMulticlass`, `SpeechToTextGeneration`, `TextToSpeechGeneration`, `TextToImageGeneration`, `TextEmbeddingsPair`, `TextEmbeddingsTriplet`. The enum is explicitly non-exhaustive (server may accept more). SDK typo to be aware of: `sdk.datasets.text_classifiers_binary` is bound to `TextClassificationMultilabel` (likely should be a binary type).

**Tuning/Datasets/Batch are DOMAINS, not callables:** there is no `sdk.tuning(...)`/`sdk.datasets(...)`/`sdk.batch(...)` factory. Reach them via `.get()`/`.list()`/`.draft_from_path()` (datasets) etc. Tuning itself is initiated from a model instance via `model.tune(...)` / `model.tune_deferred(...)`.

**list() yield-type field-name gotchas (these caused real doc bugs):**
- `sdk.tuning.list()` yields `AsyncTuningTask` — has `.id` but NOT `.task_id`/`.status` directly; must call `await task.get_task_info()` to get a `TuningTaskInfo` (which has `.task_id`, `.status`, etc.).
- `sdk.batch.list_info()` yields `BatchTaskInfo` — has `.task_id` (NOT `.id`) and `.status`.
- `sdk.batch.list_operations()` yields `BatchTaskOperation` — has `.id`/`.task_id` but `.status` requires `await op.get_status()`.

**Chat Embeddings vs gRPC Text Embeddings results DIFFER:** `sdk.chat.text_embeddings(...).run(...)` returns `ChatEmbeddingsModelResult` with fields `embedding`/`model`/`usage` (NO `num_tokens`/`model_version`). Default timeout is 180 (not 60). Config is `ChatEmbeddingsModelConfig` (adds `encoding_format`/`extra_query`). The chat factory does NOT resolve well-known name aliases (e.g. `"doc"`→`text-search-doc`), unlike `sdk.models.text_embeddings(...)`.

**Text Classifiers few-shot routing:** if ANY of `task_description`/`labels`/`samples` config fields is non-None, the `FewShotClassify` RPC is used (else zero-shot `Classify`). In the few-shot path BOTH `labels` AND `task_description` must be non-None (else `ValueError`); `samples` is optional.

**Tuning status enum:** `STATUS_UNSPECIFIED(0)`, `CREATED(1)`, `PENDING(2)`, `IN_PROGRESS(3)`, `COMPLETED(4)`, `FAILED(5)`.

title: YC SDK run_stream is an async generator in ALL domains (completions, chat, speech) — never await
content:
EXTENDS memory `c4ddc735` (which verified the speech-domain case). Verified 2026-07-19 during the Gate 2 integration review of `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/` against pinned `yandex-ai-studio-sdk==0.22.0`.

**The rule generalizes to every SDK domain, not just speech.** `run_stream` is an async generator function (`async def` + `yield` body) in ALL domains checked:
- `_models/completions/model.py:346-364` — `async def run_stream(...) -> AsyncIterator[GPTModelResult[...]]`, body does `async for result in self._run_stream(...): yield result`. gRPC completions domain.
- `_chat/completions/model.py:275` — `async def run_stream(...)`. HTTP/OpenAI-compat chat domain.
- `_speechkit/text_to_speech/tts.py:250-257` — async generator (covered by `c4ddc735`).
- `_speechkit/speech_to_text/stt.py:374` — async generator (covered by `c4ddc735`).

In EVERY domain, `await model.run_stream(...)` raises `TypeError: object async_generator can't be used in 'await' expression`. Correct shape is `async for chunk in model.run_stream(...)` (no await).

**Do NOT conflate with these awaitable shapes** (also general across domains):
- `run(...)`, `run_deferred(...)`, `attach_deferred(...)`, `tokenize(...)` — coroutines, MUST await.
- `AsyncOperation` — has `__await__`, so `result = await operation` is valid.

**Gate 2 finding (the reason this matters operationally):** the speech.md re-capture agent fixed `await run_stream()` and documented the trap, but the SAME bug persisted in `completions.md:173` and `chat-openai-compat.md:123,309` — two files that were ALSO marked "Verified against pinned v0.22.0". Per-file verification agents do not cross-check sibling files. Detection grep for any future audit: `await .*(\w+\.)?run_stream\(` — every match is a bug (re-verify the source first in case the SDK changes the shape).

title: YC SDK chat-domain text_embeddings does NOT resolve doc/query well-known aliases
content:
Non-obvious SDK behavior verified 2026-07-19 during the Gate 2 review of `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/` against pinned v0.22.0.

`sdk.chat.text_embeddings(name)` (the HTTP/OpenAI-compat chat embeddings factory, `_chat/text_embeddings/function.py`) does **NOT** apply the `doc` / `query` well-known aliases. It builds the model URI `emb://<folder>/<name>/latest` directly from the literal `name` string. So `sdk.chat.text_embeddings("doc")` produces `emb://<folder>/doc/latest` — NOT resolved to `text-search-doc`. To target the search-doc/search-query models via the chat factory you must pass the full name, e.g. `sdk.chat.text_embeddings("text-search-doc")`.

Contrast: the gRPC embeddings domain (`sdk.models.embeddings`) DOES resolve well-known aliases.

**Cross-file doc inconsistency found at Gate 2:** `chat-openai-compat.md:193` shows the example `sdk.chat.text_embeddings("doc")` — exactly the discouraged usage — while `embeddings-and-other.md:157-160` explicitly warns the chat factory skips alias resolution and recommends the full `text-search-doc` name. The chat-domain example must use the full model name.

title: yc-ai-sdk docs convention: ⚠ marks ONLY server-side facts; "Verified" vs "Mostly verified" banner rule
content:
Documentation conventions established during the 2026-07-18/19 `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/` re-capture. Enforce these in any future audit of the bundle.

**⚠ marker discipline.** The ⚠ marker is reserved EXCLUSIVELY for server-side facts that cannot be checked from the SDK source: model catalogue names, context sizes, required scopes, server-side routing/behavior. SDK-source-verifiable claims — method signatures, `TypeError` behavior, object attribute shape (`.id` vs `.task_id` vs `.status`), enum values, mutual-exclusion validation — must NOT carry ⚠. When auditing, grep for ⚠ and verify each instance marks a genuinely server-side fact.

**Banner terminology.** Each file's blockquote banner says either "Verified" or "Mostly verified against pinned SDK v0.22.0":
- "Verified" = every SDK-source-checkable claim was checked; the file's ⚠ items are all genuine server-side facts (inherently unverifiable from source).
- "Mostly verified" = the file ALSO has non-server-side unchecked claims (e.g. `chat-openai-compat.md`'s third-party-tool compatibility table — external runtime facts) OR covers domains entirely unwired in production (e.g. `embeddings-and-other.md`'s 6 domains, lower verification priority).
The distinction is defensible but is NOT self-documented anywhere a reader can see; consider adding a one-line gloss to `index.md`'s banner.

**H1 title pattern (all 7 re-captured files).** `# Yandex Cloud AI Studio SDK Reference [— Subtitle] (verified against pinned v0.22.0, 2026-07-18)`. Must stay identical across the bundle.

**Gate 2 ⚠-discipline violations found (2026-07-19):** `embeddings-and-other.md` had 3 misplaced ⚠ on SDK-verifiable claims — `:503` (SearchIndex `index_type` TypeError + concrete types), `:588` (`AsyncTuningTask` exposes `.id` but not `.task_id`/`.status`), `:718` (`BatchTaskOperation` exposes `.id`/`.task_id` but not `.status`). All three are readable in SDK source and should not carry ⚠.

title: Gate 2 integration review: per-file fixes don't propagate — grep sibling files for each fix pattern
content:
Operational lesson from the 2026-07-19 Gate 2 whole-work review of the 7-file `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/` parallel re-capture. Complements the parallel-dispatch workflow described in memory `d949e4cf` (which covers the dispatch shape, not the cross-file propagation check).

**The failure mode.** When N parallel `software-developer` agents each re-verify/rewrite ONE file in a bundle, each agent catches and fixes bugs in its own file, but the SAME bug class routinely persists in sibling files that cover the same SDK surface — because each agent only looks at its own file and does not know a sibling already fixed the pattern elsewhere. Per-file "Verified" banners do not catch this; only a whole-work integration review does.

**The Gate 2 technique.** For EVERY fix applied in any one file, grep ALL sibling files for the same anti-pattern. Concrete patterns from this review (all caught only at Gate 2):
- `await .*(\w+\.)?run_stream\(` — speech.md fixed `await run_stream()` (async-generator trap, see `c4ddc735`); the identical bug survived in `completions.md:173` and `chat-openai-compat.md:123,309`.
- `configure\(\).*mutat` / "mutates.*in place" — completions.md corrected `.configure()` to immutable (see `a23a676e`); `tools-and-structured-output.md:343` and `chat-openai-compat.md:329` still claimed it mutates in place, directly contradicting the corrected file.

**Also verify cross-file production-consumer references by grep.** Doc banners cite production code paths/methods (e.g. "consumer: `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py` at `_tryHealToolCall`"). These must be grepped against the actual tree: the tools-and-structured-output.md banner misattributed `_tryHealToolCall` to `yc_sdk_provider.py`, but the method lives only in `internal/services/llm/service.py` (see `9cce1e2fe`). And line-number citations drift (e.g. `_getBaseUrl` cited at `:290`, actually `:280`) — prefer method-name citations without line numbers, or re-grep before publishing.

**Artifact-level checks that were clean here (replicate):** `make check-docs` for link integrity (107 files / 1613 links green); code-fence balance (count ``` per file, expect even); H1-title and banner-terminology uniformity across the bundle; Method Availability Summary table cross-checked against each companion file's per-method claims.
