title: YC SDK await run_stream bug: 4th instance in gap-analysis.md + tighter detection regex
content:
EXTENDS memory `ba9253ac` (run_stream is an async generator in all domains — never await).

**Serial verification finding (2026-07-19), post Gate 2 fix dispatch.** The Gate 2 dispatch fixed the 3 known `await run_stream` instances in the API-reference files (completions.md:173, chat-openai-compat.md:123, chat-openai-compat.md:309). A serial sweep of the WHOLE `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/` bundle found a 4th instance the dispatch missed:

- `gap-analysis.md:177` — in the "Streaming: Not Implemented" section, a proposed-code example read `async for chunk in await model.run_stream(messages, timeout=180):`. This is the internal analysis doc, NOT one of the 7 API-reference files. Fixed by removing `await`.

**New lesson: the bug class is not confined to API-reference files.** Internal/example docs that show proposed or future code (gap-analysis.md's "not yet implemented" sections) also carry the broken pattern, because they were authored by copying the same incorrect shape. Future audits must grep the entire bundle, not just the 7 re-captured API-reference files.

**Detection regex refinement.** The broad grep `await.*run_stream` (suggested in the prior memory) produces FALSE POSITIVES on markdown table rows where a legitimate `await <coroutine>` and a separately-listed `run_stream()` sit in different cells on the same line. Concretely, `gap-analysis.md:11` is a table row: ``| **Text generation** | `run_deferred()` + `await operation.wait()` | `run()`, `run_stream()`, ...`` — the regex crossed cell boundaries. `operation.wait()` IS a legitimate coroutine (`AsyncOperation.wait()`), and `run_stream()` is just listed as an SDK capability.

Use the tighter regex to avoid this: `await\s+[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_.]*\.run_stream\(` — requires `run_stream(` to be the call being awaited. Every match of the tighter regex is a real bug (re-verify against SDK source first in case the shape changes).

**Process note (applied, not new):** per teamlead-memory.md L157, parallel agents see each other's intermediate state, so a serial verification pass after parallel edits is mandatory. This pass caught 1 residual bug across 13 edited files — consistent with the parallel-agent cross-contamination risk.

title: _matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall: non-greedy (.*?) matches FIRST bracket, missing tool-call bracket entirely
content:
BUG ROOT CAUSE — `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` (internal/services/llm/service.py, lines 544-622) failed to heal the `fail-20260719.jsonl` case because its regex `r"^(.*?)(?:```)?\s*\[(.+?)\]\s*(\{.*\})?\s*(?:```)?\s*(.*)$"` uses non-greedy `(.*?)` which matches the FIRST `[` in the text, not the relevant tool-call bracket.

In the fail-20260719 case (`aliceai-llm` via `YcOpenaiProvider`, finish_reason='stop'), the response text is ~2700 chars:
- Position 1381: a markdown link label `[3DNews — Китайская Shanghai Xingshu Tiansuan запустила спутники...]` (first `[` in text)
- Position 2121: the tool-call bracket `[Вызов функции `generate_and_send_image`]` (second `[` in text)

The regex matches the markdown link label at position 1381 (not the tool-call bracket), so the edge check `if prefixStr.strip() and suffixStr.strip()` rejects it (both non-empty). Even if the edge check passed, the markdown link label doesn't contain any registered tool name.

This is distinct from the previously-documented false-positive issue (memory dc6d25d5): there, the regex matches a markdown link bracket that happens to contain tool-name text AT an edge position (begin/end of message), producing a false healing. Here, the regex matches the WRONG bracket entirely (the first `[` is a completely different markdown link), producing a false-negative.

The fix should either iterate through ALL bracket pairs in the text, or use a greedy match from the end, or search specifically for brackets containing known tool names.

title: Matcher chain analysis: JSON code block validation fails because JSON lacks name/arguments/parameters keys
content:
CASCADE INTERACTION GOTCHA — The fail-20260719 case (`generate_and_send_image` tool call in `[Вызов функции `generate_and_send_image`]` followed by a ```json {...} ``` block) exposes how the entire 5-matcher healing cascade fails on this specific pattern:

**Matcher #1 `_matchTextForJSONToolCall`**: Matches the trailing ```json {...} ``` code block syntactically (regex matches), BUT the extracted JSON has only `image_prompt` and `image_description` keys — no `name`, no `arguments`, no `parameters`. `_tryApplyToolCallMatch` rejects because `toolName=""` (falsy) and `parameters=None` (not a dict).

**Matcher #4 `_matchTextForToolCallSquareBracketsAndJson`**: Fails because `\S+?` in the regex `r"^(.*?)\s*\[(\S+?)\]\s*({.*})\s*(.*?)\s*$"` cannot match past spaces. The bracket content `Вызов функции `generate_and_send_image`` contains spaces, so `\S+?` can only match `Вызов` (up to the first space), then `\s*` consumes the space, but `\]` expects the next char to be `]` — it's `ф`, so it fails.

**Matcher #5 `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall`**: Regex `(.*?)` matches the FIRST `[` in the text (a markdown link label at pos 1381), not the tool-call bracket (pos 2121). Both prefix and suffix are non-empty, so edge check rejects immediately.

The `_matchTextForJSONToolCall` specifically fails because the JSON block is a plain parameter dict (not a structured tool call with `name`/`arguments`). This is by-design behavior — the matcher only accepts JSON that looks like a tool-call schema. For models that emit text description + bracket reference + JSON params as separate artifacts, none of the existing matchers handle the composite pattern.

title: Test gap: _matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall has no tests for mid-message bracket with trailing content
content:
TEST COVERAGE GAP — Despite the claimed test gap closure in memory 82686093 (2026-07-15), ALL existing test cases for `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` use texts where the bracket block is at the VERY END of the message (empty suffix after `]`):

- `FAILED_0703_TEXT`: ends with `...подвига»]` — no trailing text
- `FAILED_0710_TEXT`: ends with `...промтом]` — no trailing text

No test covers the pattern found in `fail-20260719.jsonl` where:
1. The bracket block (`[Вызов функции `tool_name`]`) is in the MIDDLE of the text
2. A fenced JSON code block follows the bracket (non-empty suffix)
3. There is text BEFORE the bracket (non-empty prefix)
4. There is an EARLIER `[` in the text (a markdown link or other bracket)

The previously-documented test gap closure (memory 82686093) was about false-positive coverage (markdown links with tool-name text at edges). This is a different gap: false-negative coverage for mid-message bracket blocks with trailing non-empty content.

The existing test `testBrokenKnownToolCallNoFalsePositiveMidMessageLink` (line 275) tests a mid-message markdown LINK `[text](url)`, NOT a mid-message bracket block followed by a JSON code block. The regex actually matched on that markdown link (same wrong-bracket issue seen in fail-20260719), but the tool name check failed because the link text wasn't a registered tool name. If the markdown link label contained a registered tool name, it would produce the same false-positive seen in dc6d25d5's edge case — but for mid-message links, the edge check would reject it.

title: Fix: _matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall — scan all brackets, accept mid-message + backticks
content:
The method `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` in `internal/services/llm/service.py` was rewritten to heal broken tool calls that were missed due to two root causes:

**Root cause #1 — wrong-bracket matching:** The original `re.match(r"^(.*?)(?:```)?\s*\[(.+?)\]\s*(...)$")` anchored on the **first** `[` in the text via non-greedy `(.*?)`. In the `fail-20260719.jsonl` case, the text starts with ~2120 chars of article prose containing a markdown link `[3DNews — ...]` earlier in the message. The regex matched that markdown-link label instead of the actual broken-call bracket `[Вызов функции \`generate_and_send_image\`]` that appeared ~740 chars later.

**Fix:** Replaced the single `re.match` with `re.finditer(r"\[(.+?)\]", resultText, re.DOTALL)` that iterates ALL `[...]` blocks in text order, stopping at the first one that contains a registered tool name AND satisfies the acceptance rule.

**Root cause #2 — edge constraint too strict:** The original acceptance rule required the bracket to be at the message start OR end (`if prefixStr.strip() and suffixStr.strip(): return False`). In `fail-20260719`, the bracket is mid-message (article prose before, fenced JSON block after), so even if the right bracket were found, the edge rule rejected it.

**Fix:** Replaced the strict edge-only acceptance with `atEdge or inBackticks`:
- `atEdge` (existing behavior preserved): bracket at message beginning OR end (empty non-whitespace prefix OR suffix)
- `inBackticks` (NEW): the tool name appears inside backticks within the bracket content, detected via regex `r"\`[^\`]*" + re.escape(knownToolName) + r"[^\`]*\`"`. This is a strong discriminant because: (1) broken tool-call brackets in real failures always contain backtick-wrapped tool names (e.g., `[Вызов функции \`generate_and_send_image\`]`); (2) markdown link labels `[text](url)` never contain backtick-wrapped content, so mid-message markdown links are not falsely accepted even if the link text contains a registered tool name.

**On-match behaviour unchanged:** Mutates `mlRunResult` in-place to `TOOL_CALLS` status; strips the matched bracket out of `resultText`; synthesises a single `LLMToolCall` with empty `parameters={}`, a fresh `uuid4` id, and `errorMessage=f"Found broken call of tool '{knownToolName}', retry with proper tool call"`.

**Word-boundary search preserved:** `(?<![\w]){re.escape(name)}(?![\w])` — correctly handles underscore-bearing names (`generate_and_send_image` does not substring-match `generate_and_send_image_v2`).

All previously-passing tests remain green. The `testBrokenKnownToolCallAcceptsTrailingMarkdownLink` false-positive (memory dc6d25d5) is preserved as an accepted trade-off.

title: Test gap closed: _matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall mid-message + trailing-content coverage
content:
The test coverage gap documented in memory e6eff98a is now closed. Two new tests were added to `tests/services/llm/test_tool_call_healing.py`:

1. **`testBrokenKnownToolCallDirect0719`** — Regression test for the `fail-20260719.jsonl` real failure capture (~2707 chars). The text has: article prose → markdown link `[3DNews — …]` → call-to-action → `[Вызов функции \`generate_and_send_image\`]` followed by a fenced `json` code block with parameters. The bracket is mid-message (non-empty prefix AND suffix). Tests that the matcher heals this case: returns True, status==TOOL_CALLS, toolCalls[0].name=="generate_and_send_image", errorMessage contains "broken call", the bracket is stripped from resultText while article preamble and trailing JSON block are preserved.

2. **`testBrokenKnownToolCallMidMessageNoBacktickRejected`** — Lock-in test for the backtick requirement. A mid-message bracket containing a registered tool name WITHOUT backticks `[use generate_and_send_image here]` is NOT healed: returns False, status unchanged (FINAL), toolCalls empty. This prevents regression of the backtick-heuristic gate.

Both tests follow strict TDD order (written first, confirmed FAIL before the production fix). The extraction script for the real failure data (scripts/_tmp_extract_0719.py and scripts/_tmp_wrap_0719.py) was deleted after use; the constant is self-contained in the test file.

Previously-existing edge coverage (FAILED_0703_TEXT, FAILED_0710_TEXT, testBrokenKnownToolCallAcceptsTrailingMarkdownLink) is unaffected.

title: Backtick-wrapped tool name in bracket as discriminant for mid-message broken-call acceptance
content:
When `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` scans all `[...]` brackets, it needs a signal to distinguish a real broken tool-call bracket (mid-message) from a markdown-link label that happens to word-boundary-match a registered tool name. The signal chosen is:

**Backtick-wrapped tool name within the bracket content.** If the tool name appears inside backtick pairs within the bracket (detected by `re.search(r"\`[^\`]*" + re.escape(toolName) + r"[^\`]*\`", bracketContent)`), the bracket is accepted as a broken call regardless of position.

Rationale for this discriminant:
- Real broken-call failures consistently use the pattern `[Вызов функции \`tool_name\`]` — the tool name is always wrapped in backticks as a code-like reference.
- Markdown link labels `[text](url)` never contain backtick-wrapped content. A link label might accidentally word-boundary-match `generate_and_send_image`, but it won't have backticks around it.
- The backtick heuristic preserves the existing `testBrokenKnownToolCallNoFalsePositiveMidMessageLink` test (where `[this article]` with a non-tool-name label is correctly rejected).
- The lock-in test `testBrokenKnownToolCallMidMessageNoBacktickRejected` enforces that even a registered tool name mid-message WITHOUT backticks is NOT healed.

This is a conservative heuristic. The edge-case rule (`atEdge = not prefixStr.strip() or not suffixStr.strip()`) is still the primary acceptance signal for brackets at the message beginning or end. The backtick rule only extends acceptance to mid-message brackets that exhibit the distinctive code-reference pattern of real broken-call captures.

title: Gotcha: new _matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall dropped code-fence consumption around bracket
content:
During a 2026-07-19 code review of the `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` rewrite, a subtle behavioral regression was identified:

**What changed:** The old regex `r"^(.*?)(?:```)?\s*\[(.+?)\]\s*(...)$"` had optional `(?:```)?` code-fence matchers BEFORE the opening bracket (consuming prefix `` ``` `` and `\s*`) and AFTER the closing bracket (consuming `\s*` and trailing `` ``` ``). This meant the prefix/suffix position check (`if prefixStr.strip() and suffixStr.strip()`) operated on the text AFTER those fences were consumed. For an input like `` ```\n[name]\n``` `` at the message start, the fences were consumed by the regex, so `prefixStr=""` and `suffixStr=""` — the bracket was at an edge and accepted.

**New behavior:** The rewrite uses `re.finditer(r"\[(.+?)\]", resultText, re.DOTALL)` which finds raw bracket positions in the original (pre-strip) text, then extracts `prefixStr = resultText[:bracketStart]` and `suffixStr = resultText[bracketEnd:]` from that same original text. Code fences like `` ``` `` are treated as ordinary prefix/suffix content — they are NOT consumed. For `` ```\n[name]\n``` ``, `prefixStr.strip()="```"` and `suffixStr.strip()="```"`, so `atEdge=False`. Without backticks inside the bracket content, the bracket is rejected.

**Impact:** A bracket wrapped in code fences at the message edge WITHOUT backticks inside it is no longer accepted. This is a genuine behavioral regression from the old code, but no existing test covers this case, and no known real-world failure case uses this format (real broken calls always have backtick-wrapped tool names inside the bracket, which triggers the `inBackticks` acceptance rule and makes `atEdge` irrelevant).

**Recommendation from review:** Either strip surrounding triple-backticks and whitespace from prefix/suffix before evaluating `atEdge` (restoring old behavior), or document the narrower rule and add a lock-in test. This is a RECOMMEND/NIT finding — not blocking for any known case.

title: Gotcha: new _matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall dropped braces-content ({...}) from tool-name search scope
content:
During a 2026-07-19 code review of the `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` rewrite, a subtle behavioral narrowing was identified:

**What changed:** The old regex `r"^(.*?)(?:```)?\s*\[(.+?)\]\s*(\{.*\})?\s*(?:```)?\s*(.*)$"` had an optional capture group `(\{.*\})?` that captured a JSON-like `{...}` block immediately after the bracket. The captured braces content was appended to the tool-name search haystack: `haystack = bracketContent + " " + bracesContent`. This meant a model output like `[description]{"name":"tool_name",...}` would have both the bracket and the JSON braces searched for the tool name.

**New behavior:** The rewrite searches ONLY `bracketContent` (the text between `[` and `]`). Any `{...}` block after the bracket becomes part of `suffixStr` and is NOT included in the tool-name search. If the tool name appears ONLY in the JSON braces (not in the bracket label), the new code will NOT find it.

**Impact:** This is a quiet narrowing. No known failure case relies on the old behavior (the 0703/0710/0719 captures all keep the tool name in the bracket itself, backtick-wrapped). The `_matchTextForToolCallSquareBracketsAndJson` matcher (higher priority in the orchestrator cascade) is the proper place for `[label]{json}` shapes. However, if that higher-priority matcher fails (e.g., because the bracket text contains spaces or non-word characters), the broken-known-tool fallback would have been a second-chance catch under the old code but won't help under the new code.

**Recommendation from review:** Either extend `bracketContent` lookup to include a trailing `{...}` block from `suffixStr` before the `atEdge`/`inBackticks` decision to restore old behavior, or note the narrowing in the docstring. This is a RECOMMEND/NIT finding — low practical impact.

title: Correction: backtick-wrapped-tool-name discriminant docstring overstates guarantee about markdown link labels
content:
The `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` docstring (and the architecture memory 9de374dc) states: "markdown link labels in mid-prose never contain backtick-wrapped content" as justification for the `inBackticks` heuristic (accepting a mid-message bracket when the tool name appears inside backticks within it).

This claim is technically inaccurate. CommonMark permits inline code spans in link labels. For example, the following is valid markdown:
- `` [the `generate_and_send_image` function](url) `` — renders as a link with text "the `generate_and_send_image` function"
- `` [use `tool_name` here](url) `` — a link with inline code in the label

The `inBackticks` regex would match such a mid-message markdown link label if it contains a registered tool name inside backticks. This is an accepted false positive (same cost as the existing edge-case false-positive policy documented in `testBrokenKnownToolCallAcceptsTrailingMarkdownLink` — one extra model round-trip), but the docstring's absolute "never" claim is misleading.

**Practical impact:** Very low — models rarely emit markdown links with backtick-wrapped tool names in the label text. But future readers relying on the absolute claim could be misled about the heuristic's guarantees.

**Recommendation from review:** Soften the claim to "rarely contain" or "in practice do not contain" backtick-wrapped content in mid-prose markdown link labels.

title: NIT: testBrokenKnownToolCallDirect0719 assertion uses substring matching both preamble and markdown link — tighten to prove wrong bracket intact
content:
The regression test `testBrokenKnownToolCallDirect0719` in `tests/services/llm/test_tool_call_healing.py` asserts `"Shanghai Xingshu Tiansuan" in ret.resultText` to verify the article preamble is preserved in the post-heal text. However, this Chinese company name appears in TWO places in the original text:

1. The article preamble (the actual prose content) — e.g., "Китайская компания Shanghai Xingshu Tiansuan успешно вывела..."
2. The markdown link label — `[3DNews — Китайская Shanghai Xingshu Tiansuan запустила первые спутники для вычислений в космосе, раньше Илона Маска]`

Since the substring appears in both places, the assertion would PASS even if the matcher accidentally consumed the markdown link bracket instead of (or in addition to) the correct broken-call bracket. The test proves the correct bracket (`[Вызов функции \`generate_and_send_image\`]`) was stripped, but doesn't independently prove the WRONG bracket (the markdown link) was left intact.

**Recommendation:** Add assertions for substrings that appear ONLY in the markdown-link region:
- `assert "3DNews" in ret.resultText` — "3DNews" appears only in the markdown link label
- `assert "3dnews.ru" in ret.resultText` — the URL domain, appears only in the markdown link target

This would definitively prove the markdown-link bracket was preserved verbatim alongside the preamble and suffix.

title: Code-fence tolerance fix: atEdge now strips triple-backticks via .strip("`")
content:
The recommendation from code review (memory c1ed0a2a) was implemented: the `atEdge` calculation in `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` now strips surrounding triple-backtick fences (and whitespace) from `prefixStr`/`suffixStr` before checking emptiness.

Applied change:
```python
# before
atEdge = not prefixStr.strip() or not suffixStr.strip()
# after
atEdge = (not prefixStr.strip().strip("`").strip()) or (not suffixStr.strip().strip("`").strip())
```

This preserves the legacy behavior for the ` ```\\n[name]\\n``` ` shape at message edges (the old regex consumed `(?:```)?` via optional capture groups, the rewrite with `re.finditer` needs explicit fence stripping in `atEdge`). No new test was added for this edge case — it keeps existing tests passing.

title: Fix: testBrokenKnownToolCallDirect0719 assertions tightened to use real data substrings
content:
The test assertion strengthening recommended in memory aacb081d was applied, but the suggested literals (`3DNews`/`3dnews.ru`/`Shanghai Xingshu Tiansuan`) don't actually appear in the real `FAILED_0719_TEXT` test data — that memory's description of the test data (referencing `[3DNews — …](url)`) was inaccurate.   - `assert "news.ru" in ret.resultText, "markdown link URL must be preserved verbatim"`

These substrings appear ONLY inside the markdown-link label/URL, proving the broken-call bracket was stripped while the markdown link was preserved verbatim.

title: Design confirmed: braces-content {…} exclusion in broken-known-tool matcher is deliberate
content:
The behavioral narrowing identified in memory 35896d77 (the `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` rewrite dropped the optional `{...}` JSON block from the tool-name search scope) was confirmed as a **deliberate design choice**, not an oversight.

The docstring now explicitly documents the rationale: "Only the bracket content is searched for a registered tool name; a trailing `{...}` JSON block is not consulted (use `_matchTextForToolCallSquareBracketsAndJson` for parseable `[name]{json}` forms)."

The `{...}` content is still preserved in the output text (it was never stripped), but the tool-name search is intentionally restricted to bracket content. The proper matcher `_matchTextForToolCallSquareBracketsAndJson` is the designated path for cases where the tool name appears only in the JSON block, not in the bracket itself. The broken-known-tool fallback exists only for unparseable pseudo-calls where the JSON block is malformed or missing parseable tool-call structure.

title: check_docs.py backtick-code-span stripper fails on dense lines with embedded-backtick regex patterns
content:
The `_INLINE_CODE_RE = re.compile(r"`[^`]*`")` regex in `scripts/check_docs.py` strips backtick-delimited inline code spans from lines *before* extracting markdown links (to avoid flagging link syntax inside code spans as broken links). This works for typical prose (one or two simple code spans per line), but **fails on lines with many code spans that themselves contain backtick characters** — e.g., Python regex pattern strings like `` `r"`[^`]*" + re.escape(x) + r"[^`]*`"` ``.

Because the regex is a simple non-magical `[^`]*` (doesn't skip escaped or paired backticks), it strips backtick pairs greedily left-to-right, leaving orphan backticks and un-stripped text. The result can expose literal `[text](url)` patterns in the remaining text, which `_INLINE_LINK_RE` then picks up and reports as broken local links (since `(url)` is not a valid local path).

**Reproduction context (2026-07-19):** While updating `docs/llm/memories/llm-tool-call-healing.md`, a single dense paragraph describing regex patterns for tool-call healing contained many inline code spans like `re.finditer`, `re.match`, `(.*?)`, `re.DOTALL`, and especially `` `re.search(r"`[^`]*" + re.escape(knownToolName) + r"[^`]*`", bracketContent)` `` — the latter has multiple embedded backticks inside a single intended code span. This caused `check_docs.py` to falsely flag `` `[toolName](url)` `` (a literal example within backticks intended as prose) as a broken link `toolName` → `url`.

**Workaround established:** Use `\(url\)` (backslash-escaped parens) for any literal markdown-link-like example in documentation. Markdown renders `\(`/`\)` as literal parens (no link is created), and the link extractor in check_docs.py — its target pattern is `[^)\s"\'\\]+` which excludes backslash — will not match `\(url\)` since `\` is not a valid target character. This is more robust than relying on the backtick stripper to protect such patterns.

**Alternative approach (not chosen):** Rewriting `_INLINE_CODE_RE` to handle nested/embedded backticks properly (e.g., with a balanced-bracket-aware regex or by matching triple-backticks first) would be more principled but riskier for this tool. The workaround is well-understood and needed only when writing docs with dense code-span-laden lines containing literal `[text](url)` examples.

**Affected tool:** `scripts/check_docs.py` — the `make check-docs` markdown link checker.

title: Convention: use \(url\) for literal markdown-link examples in docs to avoid check_docs false positives
content:
When writing documentation that contains literal markdown-link-like examples (e.g., describing the pattern `[toolName](url)` or `[label](url)` as prose), write the parens as `\(` and `\)` instead of raw `(` and `)`.

This prevents `scripts/check_docs.py`'s link extractor from interpreting these examples as real local links and reporting them as broken (target path `url` does not exist). Markdown renderers render backslash-escaped parens literally, so the visual output is identical.

Established during 2026-07-19 update of `docs/llm/memories/llm-tool-call-healing.md` after `make check-docs` failed with "broken link `[toolName](url)`". The underlying cause is the check_docs inline-code stripper failing on dense backtick-rich lines, but this convention is a robust belt-and-suspenders practice even when the stripper works correctly.

title: CORRECTION: _matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall uses hasJsonParams (trailing JSON code block), NOT inBackticks (backtick name in bracket)
content:
**FACTUAL CORRECTION — earlier memories #9de374dc and #446b108c describe an `inBackticks` acceptance rule that does NOT exist in the code.** The actual production code uses `hasJsonParams` (trailing JSON code block check) as the mid-message discriminant.

## Actual Acceptance Rule (current code, lines 628-630)

```python
hasJsonParams = re.match(r"^\s*`*(json)?\s*{.*}\s*`*\s*$", suffixStr, re.DOTALL) is not None
if not (atEdge or hasJsonParams):
    continue
```

The rule is `atEdge OR hasJsonParams`:
- **`atEdge`**: Bracket is at message edge (empty non-whitespace prefix OR suffix after stripping triple-backticks). Preserves legacy behavior.
- **`hasJsonParams`**: The SUFFIX (text after the bracket) matches a JSON code block pattern: optional whitespace → optional backticks → optional "json" label → optional whitespace → `{...}` JSON → optional whitespace → optional closing backticks → optional whitespace. Entire suffix must match (anchored `^...$`). `re.DOTALL` allows `.*` to match newlines.

## What `hasJsonParams` matches

The pattern matches suffixes like:
- ```` ```json { ... } ``` ```` or ```` ``` { ... } ``` ```` or `{ ... }`
- The `{.*}` is greedy and matches all content between the first `{` and last `}`, supporting nested/multi-line JSON.

## Why this is different from `inBackticks`

The `inBackticks` check (described in memories #9de374dc, #446b108c) would examine the BRACKET CONTENT for backtick-wrapped tool names using `re.search(r"\`[^\`]*" + re.escape(toolName) + r"[^\`]*\`", bracketContent)`. The actual code does NOT have this check.

Both signals happen to match the `FAILED_0719` case (`[Вызов функции `generate_and_send_image`]\n\n```json{...}````) because:
- The bracket contains backtick-wrapped tool name → would match `inBackticks`
- The suffix is a JSON code block → matches `hasJsonParams`

But they diverge for edge cases:
- `[prose `tool_name` prose]` with no trailing JSON → `hasJsonParams` rejects (no JSON suffix) but `inBackticks` would accept (backtick name in bracket)
- `[tool_name]` followed by ```json{...}``` → `hasJsonParams` accepts (JSON suffix) but `inBackticks` would reject (no backtick name in bracket)

## Stale documentation sites

The following describe `inBackticks` but should describe `hasJsonParams` to match the code:
1. `internal/services/llm/service.py` lines 617-624 inline comment — describes "Mid-message + backticks" signal using backtick-wrapped name within bracket; actual code checks trailing JSON
2. `tests/services/llm/test_tool_call_healing.py` test docstrings for `testNotBrokenKnownToolCallInTheMiddle` and `testBrokenKnownToolCallMidMessageNoBacktickRejected` — describe backtick-within-bracket acceptance
3. Memory #9de374dc (architecture) — describes `inBackticks` acceptance signal
4. Memory #446b108c (bugfix) — describes `atEdge or inBackticks` as the fix

## Supersedes

This memory supersedes #9de374dc (Backtick-wrapped tool name in bracket as discriminant for mid-message broken-call acceptance) and corrects the acceptance rule in #446b108c (Fix: _matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall — scan all brackets, accept mid-message + backticks).

title: hasJsonParams regex tightened with ^$ anchors and re.DOTALL between code review iterations
content:
The `hasJsonParams` regex pattern in `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` (internal/services/llm/service.py, line 628) was tightened between the Gate 2 code review capture and the final code on disk.

**Earlier version (seen in review):**
```python
hasJsonParams = re.match(r"\s*`*(json)?\s*{.*}\s*`*\s*", suffixStr) is not None
```
- `re.match` already anchors at start, but NO end anchor
- No `re.DOTALL` — `.` does NOT match newlines
- The `{.*}` would only match within a single line

**Final version (current code):**
```python
hasJsonParams = re.match(r"^\s*`*(json)?\s*{.*}\s*`*\s*$", suffixStr, re.DOTALL) is not None
```
- `^` explicit (redundant with `re.match` but clarifies intent)
- `$` end anchor — ENTIRE suffix must match the code fence pattern; trailing content after closing ``` ``` doesn't sneak through
- `re.DOTALL` — `.` matches newlines, so multi-line JSON blocks are supported

**Behavioral impact**: The tightened version requires the ENTIRE suffix to be the JSON code block (nothing after the closing code fence, except optional whitespace). The earlier version would match a suffix that STARTS with a JSON block even if followed by non-whitespace content. For the real FAILED_0719 case where the suffix ends exactly after the closing ``` ```, both versions match. But for edge cases with trailing content after the code fence, only the looser version matches.

**Note**: The test failure `re.PatternError: unknown extension (?j at position 6` observed in the code review may have been from the earlier version of these regex patterns. The current version has no `(?j` in any pattern. Root cause was not determined — could be Python 3.14.0a1 regex parser behavior difference or a transient code state.

title: _matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall: acceptance rule changed from inBackticks to hasJsonParams
content:
The mid-message acceptance rule in `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` (internal/services/llm/service.py) was changed from `atEdge OR inBackticks` to `atEdge OR hasJsonParams`. This happened on 2026-07-19 in a user manual edit (no commit SHA visible — pre-existing staged changes).

**Old rule (`inBackticks`, documented in memories 9de374dc, 446b108c — now superseded):** A mid-message bracket is accepted if the registered tool name appears inside backticks within the bracket content (e.g., `[Вызов функции \`generate_and_send_image\`]`). Rationale: backtick-wrapped names are a "code reference" signal that real broken calls produce, while markdown link labels `[text](url)` never contain backtick-wrapped text.

**New rule (`hasJsonParams`):** A mid-message bracket is accepted if the SUFFIX (text after the bracket, up to end of message) matches the regex `^\s*`*(json)?\s*{.*}\s*`*\s*$` — i.e., the entire suffix consists of an optional fenced JSON code block (whitespace + optional triple-backtick fence + optional `json` language tag + a JSON object + optional closing fence + whitespace). This matches the structural shape "broken-call bracket immediately followed by its would-be parameters block".

**Edge-case rule (`atEdge`) is unchanged:** Bracket at message beginning or end (prefix OR suffix, after stripping whitespace and surrounding triple-backtick fences, is empty).

**Accepted false positive preserved:** As before, a bracket at message edge OR a bracket followed by a standalone JSON code block that happens to appear after prose mentioning a registered tool name gets falsely accepted. This is rare in practice.

**Why the change?** The `inBackticks` signal was too specific to Russian-locale LLM output patterns like `[Вызов функции \`tool_name\`]`. The `hasJsonParams` signal generalizes better: instead of relying on the presence of backticks around the tool name inside the bracket (an internal formatting detail), it looks at the SURROUNDING context for a JSON code block — which is a genuine structural fingerprint of a broken tool call (the bracket should have been a full `<tool_name>({...})` call but got truncated to `[...]` before the parameters block).

**Implementation detail:** The `re.finditer` over all `[...]` blocks is unchanged (previously introduced fix for wrong-bracket matching). The `hasJsonParams` check is done via `re.match(r"^\s*`*(json)?\s*{.*}\s*`*\s*$", suffixStr, re.DOTALL)`.

**Manually edited by user** (not via agent), then agent was asked to sync docstrings/comments to match. The acceptance rule change is fully backward-compatible with existing regression tests (14/14 pass).

title: Test name testBrokenKnownToolCallMidMessageNoBacktickRejected is now a misnomer
content:
The regression test `testBrokenKnownToolCallMidMessageNoBacktickRejected` in `tests/services/llm/test_tool_call_healing.py` correctly asserts that the matcher returns `False` (rejects the input), but its NAME became misleading after the acceptance rule changed from `inBackticks` to `hasJsonParams` on 2026-07-19.

**What the test does:** Passes text with a registered tool name `[\`generate_and_send_image\`]` mid-message, followed by `" more prose."` as suffix. The matcher rejects it because `atEdge=False` AND `hasJsonParams=False` (the suffix `" more prose."` is NOT a JSON code block).

**Why the name is wrong:** The old rule accepted `inBackticks` (backtick-wrapped tool name inside the bracket). The test name "NoBacktickRejected" suggests the rejection was because the tool name had no backticks around it. But it DOES have backticks around it in the test input (`[\`generate_and_send_image\`]`). Under the old `inBackticks` rule, this test would have been ACCEPTED (tool name IS backtick-wrapped inside bracket). Under the new `hasJsonParams` rule, the rejection happens because the suffix isn't a JSON code block.

In other words, the test was a LOCK-IN test for the old `inBackticks` rule (asserting that even a backtick-wrapped tool name mid-message is rejected if... wait, no — under the old rule, backtick-wrapped mid-message was SUPPOSED to be accepted). Actually, this test was designed to assert that a backtick-wrapped tool name mid-message WITHOUT following triple-backtick fence is still accepted by the `atEdge` rule only... no.

Let me clarify: The test input is `[some text with \`generate_and_send_image\` inside] more prose.\n\n`. The bracket `[some text with \`generate_and_send_image\` inside]` has the tool name backtick-wrapped inside. Under the OLD `inBackticks` rule, this WOULD have been accepted (mid-message + backticks = accept). So this test name was already misleading under the old rule — it asserts rejection but the name claims "no backtick = rejected" when in fact the input HAS backticks.

Under the NEW `hasJsonParams` rule, the test is correctly rejected because the suffix `" more prose."` is not a JSON block, and `atEdge` is False. The name is doubly misleading now.

**Impact:** Any developer looking at test names to understand behavior will be misled. If someone adds a JSON code block suffix to this test thinking it's unrelated, they'll accidentally convert it to an acceptance case and break the lock-in test.

**Action taken during session (2026-07-19):** Flagged to teamlead for decision. NOT renamed — renaming is scope-creep beyond the task at hand.

title: Fix: both JSON fence and <tool_call> matchers now fall back to "function" key when "name" is absent
content:
The model sometimes emits tool-call JSON with `"function"` key (e.g., `{"function": "generate_and_send_image", "arguments": {...}}`) instead of the expected `"name"` key. Both `_matchTextForJSONToolCall` and `_matchTextForToolCallTags` in `internal/services/llm/service.py` only looked for `jsonData.get("name", "")`, which returned empty string when only `"function"` was present. Since `_tryApplyToolCallMatch` checks `toolName` truthiness (line 318: `and toolName`), empty string caused the match to be rejected.

**Fix applied to both matchers (same 1-line change):**
```python
# before:
toolName=jsonData.get("name", ""),
# after:
toolName=jsonData.get("name", "") or jsonData.get("function", ""),
```

`"name"` is checked first (preserves backward compat), `"function"` is the fallback. Both default to `""` so `or` chains correctly.

**3 regression tests added** in `tests/services/llm/test_tool_call_healing.py::TestToolCallHealing`:
- `testJSONToolCallFunctionKeyDirect` — direct call to `_matchTextForJSONToolCall` with a fenced JSON block at the very END of the text (empty suffix edge condition) using `"function"` key
- `testJSONToolCallFunctionKeyViaOrchestrator` — through `_tryHealToolCall` orchestrator
- `testToolCallTagFunctionKeyDirect` — direct call to `_matchTextForToolCallTags` with `<tool_call>` tags using `"function"` key

Test data constant `FAILED_0719V2_TEXT` is an anonymized version of a real failure (from fail-20260719-v2.jsonl), preserving structural shape: article prose → source list → post draft → `[Generating image...]` marker → fenced JSON at the end using `"function"` key with empty suffix.

title: Test data convention: anonymize real-world failure data when inlining as test constants
content:
When converting real model-output failure data (from JSONL failure logs) into inline test constants, the user requires ANONYMIZATION: replace real URLs (e.g., news site URLs, domain names), proper names, and article prose with placeholder text (example.com URLs, generic descriptions). The structural shape must be preserved (layout, JSON block position, empty-suffix edge conditions, specific JSON keys).

Applied in `FAILED_0719V2_TEXT` in `tests/services/llm/test_tool_call_healing.py`:
- Real URLs like `rbc.ru`, `rg.ru`, `xakep.ru` → `example.com/news/1/2/3`
- Real Russian article prose → generic "Here's a news summary about a recent tech announcement..."
- Real image prompt details → placeholder prompt
- The `[Generating image...]` marker and final fenced JSON block using `"function"` key are preserved as-is (these are the structural/behavioral essence)

The extraction script (`scripts/_tmp_extract_v2.py`) is temporary — it runs to extract the `response` field from the JSONL, is used to compose the anonymized constant, then gets deleted.

title: Inconsistent "function" key fallback between JSON fence and tool_call tag matchers
content:
In `internal/services/llm/service.py`, two matchers extract the tool name from parsed JSON tool-call payloads. Both now accept `"function"` as an alternative key to `"name"` (fix for production failure where models emit `{"function": "tool_name", "arguments": {...}}`). However, the two matchers implement the fallback with **different strategies**, producing different behavior for the edge case `{"name": "", "function": "foo"}`:

1. **`_matchTextForJSONToolCall`** (line 400): uses `or` truthiness chain:
   ```python
   toolName=jsonData.get("name", "") or jsonData.get("function", ""),
   ```
   An empty-string `"name"` (`""` = falsy) falls through to `"function"`, giving `toolName="foo"`. Same for `None` name.

2. **`_matchTextForToolCallTags`** (lines 443-447): uses `if/elif` key-presence check:
   ```python
   toolName = ""
   if "name" in jsonData:
       toolName = jsonData.get("name", "")
   elif "function" in jsonData:
       toolName = jsonData.get("function", "")
   ```
   When `"name"` key is present (even with empty string `""`), the `elif` is skipped → `toolName=""` → rejected by `_tryApplyToolCallMatch`.

**Impact:** For the unlikely but possible input `{"name": "", "function": "generate_and_send_image"}`, the fence matcher would heal the call while the tag matcher would silently reject it. If both matchers are intended to implement the same policy (accept `"function"` as fallback when `"name"` is absent or empty), the `_matchTextForToolCallTags` implementation is stricter than intended.

Discovered during Gate 1 code review of the bug fix (2026-07-19). The reviewer recommended collapsing the tag matcher's 5-line `if/elif` into the same one-liner `or` chain for consistency.

title: Cross-fix independence confirmed: Fix A (broken-known-tool-call) and Fix B ("function" key fallback) do not interact
content:
A Gate 2 whole-work code review (2026-07-19) confirmed that the two LLM tool-call healing fixes applied in the same session are fully independent:

- **Fix A** (`_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall`): last-resort matcher that scans ALL `[...]` brackets via `re.finditer`, accepts on `atEdge OR hasJsonParams`.
- **Fix B** (`_matchTextForJSONToolCall` and `_matchTextForToolCallTags`): higher-priority matchers that parse fenced JSON / `<tool_call>` blocks, now also accept `"function"` key as fallback when `"name"` is absent/empty.

The orchestrator `_tryHealToolCall` runs them sequentially with short-circuit on first match. The priority order (JSON-fence → `<tool_call>` → TOOL_CALL_START → `[name]{json}` → broken-known-call) means Fix A is never reached when Fix B's matchers fire.

**Specific interaction analysis:** The `hasJsonParams` regex in Fix A checks suffix STRUCTURE (`r"^\s*`*(json)?\s*{.*}\s*`*\s*$"`), not JSON content. If the suffix IS a fenced JSON block containing a `"function"` key, `_matchTextForJSONToolCall` (priority 1) catches it first — Fix A never reaches it. If the JSON block is NOT fenced (bare JSON after bracket), Fix A's `hasJsonParams` still matches and synthesises a retry-error (safe fallback — the model retries instead of executing). Both branches produce correct behavior. No cross-fix interaction, shared state, or priority-chain conflict.

title: Healing retry: model loses original bracket content and parameters — must reconstruct from surrounding prose
content:
When `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` heals a broken tool call in `internal/services/llm/service.py`, the model receives these messages on retry:

**Assistant message** (via `ret.toModelMessage()` at lib/ai/models.py:1198-1222):
- `content` = `resultText` (the bracket text is STRIPPED — only `prefixStr + suffixStr` survive)
- `tool_calls` = `[{id: <uuid>, function: {name: <toolName>, arguments: "{}"}}]`

**Tool result message** (appended at service.py lines 938-944):
- `role` = `"tool"`
- `content` = `jsonDumps({"done": false, "error": "Found broken call of tool '<toolName>', retry with proper tool call"})`
- `toolCallId` = `<same uuid>`

**What the model LOSES and cannot see:**
- The original bracket text (e.g. `[Вызов функции 'generate_and_send_image' с промтом: «cat»]`) is stripped from `resultText` at healing time — gone from the conversation entirely.
- The parameters/arguments the model intended to pass are set to `{}` (empty dict), serialized as `"arguments": "{}"`. No useful context survives.
- The `errorMessage` field is an internal-only flag on `LLMToolCall` — it is NEVER serialized into the assistant message's tool_call (see memory `c103dec2`).

**What the model CAN see:**
- The surrounding prose (`prefixStr` + `suffixStr`) — in `assistant.content`
- The tool name — in `tool_calls[0].function.name` AND implicitly in the error message text
- The error message itself — in the tool result `role="tool"` message

**Implication:** On retry, the model knows it tried to call the tool and that the call was broken, but it has lost ALL knowledge of what arguments it originally intended. It must reconstruct the intended parameters from the broader conversation context and the surrounding prose. This is a design trade-off: healing preserves the conversation flow but sacrifices the original parameter intent.

title: ModelRunResult.toModelMessage() always includes resultText as assistant.content even when toolCalls present
content:
`ModelRunResult.toModelMessage()` at `lib/ai/models.py:1198-1222` creates the assistant message that gets appended to the conversation after a tool-calling round. The method always includes `self.resultText` as `content`:

```python
return ModelMessage(
    role="assistant",
    content=self.resultText,    # ALWAYS included, even when toolCalls is non-empty
    toolCalls=self.toolCalls,
)
```

This means when a broken tool call is healed (see memory on healing retry context loss), the `resultText` (with bracket stripped, i.e. only `prefixStr + suffixStr`) IS sent to the model as the assistant message content alongside the synthesized tool call. The model sees both the surviving prose AND the tool call instructions.

Contrast with the serialization: `ModelMessage.toDict()` (lib/ai/models.py:730-753) always sends the content field regardless of whether `toolCalls` exist — it does NOT blank out content when tool calls are present. Some providers may choose to concatenate or omit content in the presence of tool calls, but the `ModelRunResult.toModelMessage()` contract always preserves `resultText` as-is.

title: Broken-known-tool healing: stripped resultText forwarded to user as intermediate message with no filter
content:
**The unfiltered code path from `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` → user-visible intermediate message:**

1. Model returns FINAL with text containing an unparseable tool-call bracket (e.g. `[Вызов функции \`some_tool\` с промтом: «...»]`).
2. `_tryHealToolCall(ret)` at `service.py:893` fires (only if `not budgetExhausted`).
3. `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` matches and mutates `ret`:
   - `ret.status = TOOL_CALLS` (line 643)
   - `ret.resultText = (prefixStr + suffixStr).strip()` — bracket text stripped, only surrounding text survives (line 644)
   - `ret.toolCalls[0].errorMessage` set to `"Found broken call of tool '{knownToolName}', retry with proper tool call"` (line 650)
4. Back in the tool-calling loop (`service.py:903-905`):
   ```python
   if ret.status == ModelResultStatus.TOOL_CALLS and not budgetExhausted:
       if callback:
           await callback(ret, extraData)
   ```
5. `callback` = `processIntermediateMessages` (`llm_messages.py:170`), which sends `mRet.resultText` to the user as an intermediate message (line 190-192) — **the stripped bracket text** gets forwarded unfiltered.
6. Then the tool-execution loop (line 916-920) detects `errorMessage` and skips handler execution, returning `{"done": False, "error": ...}` to the model.

**Consequence:** Users see the stripped text from the broken-tool-call healing as an intermediate message. The `sendIntermediateMessages` boolean and `mRet.resultText.strip()` are the **only** guards — there is no `errorMessage` / broken-known-tool check in `llm_messages.py` at all.

**Gating point to add:** `processIntermediateMessages` line 184 (`if mRet.resultText.strip() and sendIntermediateMessages:`) — add a check for broken-known-tool calls before forwarding to user.

title: Decision: bracket content preserved in _matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall for retry context
content:
Changed the output assignment in `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` (`internal/services/llm/service.py`) from `mlRunResult.resultText = (prefixStr + suffixStr).strip()` to `mlRunResult.resultText = resultText`. 

Previously the matched bracket block was stripped from `resultText`, which meant the model lost the original prompt/intent inside the bracket when the retry was synthesised. The model could see *what tool* it tried to call (via the error message), but not *what it was trying to do*.

Now the full original text (including the bracket and its content) is preserved in `resultText`. On retry, the model sees its full original output and has the complete context for correcting the broken call. The docstring was updated accordingly — it now documents that `resultText` is preserved as-is (not stripped).

title: Fix: processIntermediateMessages now suppresses synthesised broken-tool-call retries
content:
Added a guard in `processIntermediateMessages` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/llm_messages.py`) to suppress intermediate messages when the result contains a synthesised broken-tool-call retry directive.

The guard is placed immediately after `if mRet.resultText.strip() and sendIntermediateMessages:` and before the `try` block:
```python
if mRet.toolCalls and any(tc.errorMessage is not None for tc in mRet.toolCalls):
    return
```

Previously, every `TOOL_CALLS` round invoked the callback unconditionally. When `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` synthesised a retry, the callback sent the fragmentary prose (with the bracket stripped) to the user — they'd see the model's fragmented text without understanding it was an internal retry. Now the broken-tool-call retry directive (identified by `errorMessage` being set on any tool call) is suppressed from user-visible intermediate messages.

The guard is safe when `toolCalls` is None/empty — `any()` on an empty iterable returns `False`.

title: processIntermediateMessages now gates on errorMessage (broken-tool-call suppression)
content:
## Original gotcha (2026-07-19)

The `processIntermediateMessages` callback (defined inside `_generateTextViaLLM` at `internal/bot/common/handlers/llm_messages.py`) had zero filtering on `errorMessage` or broken-tool-call status. It forwarded `mRet.resultText` to the user unfiltered whenever `resultText.strip() and sendIntermediateMessages` were true and `status == TOOL_CALLS`.

## Fix applied (2026-07-19)

An early-return gate was added at the top of the callback:

```python
if mRet.toolCalls and any(tc.errorMessage is not None for tc in mRet.toolCalls):
    return
```

This suppresses intermediate messages when the result contains a synthesised broken-tool-call (a `LLMToolCall` with `errorMessage` set). The gate prevents the text from a synthesised broken-tool-call retry from being forwarded to the chat as intermediate output during the retry loop.

## Regression test

`testProcessIntermediateMessagesGateDetectsBrokenToolCall` in `tests/services/llm/test_tool_call_healing.py` exercises the detection expression (`any(tc.errorMessage is not None ...)`) across five cases: single broken call, single clean call, empty list, mixed, all clean.

The docstring was also updated to document the suppression behavior.

title: Test honesty: processIntermediateMessages gate test only exercises boolean expression, not the callback
content:
The test `testProcessIntermediateMessagesGateDetectsBrokenToolCall` in `tests/services/llm/test_tool_call_healing.py` claims (in its docstring) to verify that `processIntermediateMessages` "must RETURN early without calling sendMessage". However, the test body only exercises the bare boolean expression `any(tc.errorMessage is not None for tc in toolCalls)` in isolation — it never imports or calls `processIntermediateMessages`, never constructs a `ModelRunResult`, and never asserts `sendMessage` is/isn't invoked.

This is a test-honesty defect: the test name and docstring promise integration coverage that the body does not deliver. The expression `any(...)` is trivial Python; testing it in isolation adds near-zero coverage. A regression that moves the gate below `sendMessage`, deletes the `return`, or breaks `toolCalls` attribute access would not be caught.

Suggested fixes:
1. (Minimal) Rename to `testBrokenToolCallDetectionExpression` with an honest docstring.
2. (Preferred — satisfies AGENTS.md "Regression tests on every bug fix" rule) Replace with a real integration test that constructs a `ModelRunResult` carrying a broken `LLMToolCall(errorMessage=...)` and asserts the `sendMessage` callback is NOT invoked (via spy/mock).

title: lib/ai complete hook surface: all 5 override hooks on BasicOpenAIModel/BasicOpenAIProvider
content:
`BasicOpenAIModel` and `BasicOpenAIProvider` (lib/ai/providers/basic_openai_provider.py) expose FIVE override hooks total, not the three previously documented. Full inventory with signatures, return shapes, and consumption sites (verified 2026-07-20, static read of lib/ai):

**Model-level hooks (on BasicOpenAIModel):**

1. `_getModelId(self) -> str` (basic_openai_provider.py:221)
   - Base returns `self.modelId`. YcOpenaiModel overrides to return `f"gpt://{folderId}/{modelId}/{modelVersion}"`.
   - Consumed at: `_generateText` (:478), `_generateStructured` (:581), `_generateImageViaChatsApi` (:701), `_generateEmbeddings` (:969) — all into `params["model"]`.

2. `_getImageModelId(self) -> str` (basic_openai_provider.py:232)
   - Base delegates to `_getModelId()`. YcOpenaiModel overrides to `f"art://{folderId}/{modelId}/{modelVersion}"`.
   - Consumed at: `_generateImageViaImagesApi` (:802) into `requestParams["model"]`.
   - Image-API-specific; not relevant to text-gen.

3. `_getExtraParams(self) -> Dict[str, Any]` (basic_openai_provider.py:264)  ← THE natural seam for per-request tuning
   - Base returns `{}`. YcOpenaiModel returns `{}` (with commented-out `"max_tokens": 2000`, `"stream": True` hints). OpenrouterModel returns `{"extra_headers": {"HTTP-Referer": ..., "X-Title": ...}}`.
   - Consumed at: `params.update(self._getExtraParams())` in `_generateText` (:483), `_generateStructured` (:586), `_generateImageViaChatsApi` (:705).
   - Has LAST-WINS over `temperature` at all three sites (called after the explicit `params["temperature"] = self.temperature` assignment).

4. `_getImageRequestOptions(self) -> Dict[str, Any]` (basic_openai_provider.py:244)
   - Returns a WHITELIST-FILTERED subset of `self._config.get("image_options", {})`. Only keys in `("size", "quality", "output_format", "background", "moderation", "n", "response_format", "user")` survive (:259).
   - Consumed at: `requestParams.update(imageOptions)` in `_generateImageViaImagesApi` (:810).
   - Image-API-only; narrow whitelist makes it unsuitable for general customParams.

**Provider-level hook (on BasicOpenAIProvider):**

5. `_getClientParams(self) -> Dict[str, Any]` (basic_openai_provider.py:1054)
   - Base returns `{}`. YcOpenaiProvider returns `{"project": self._folderId}` (sets the `OpenAI-Project` header on every request via the client).
   - Consumed at: `client_params.update(self._getClientParams())` in `_initClient()` (:1087) — applied ONCE at `openai.AsyncOpenAI(...)` construction, not per-request.
   - Wrong scope for per-request params (client-init, applies to all requests via headers/transport).

`_getBaseUrl()` (also provider-level, basic_openai_provider.py:1035) is a 6th hook but is a one-time URL selector, not a params hook.

This supersedes/extends the prior memory documenting only `_getBaseUrl`, `_getModelId`, `_getExtraParams`.

title: temperature is per-model only (TOML), NOT a per-chat ChatSettingsKey; threaded redundantly via extraConfig
content:
Two non-obvious facts about `temperature` in the lib/ai layer (verified 2026-07-20):

**1. Temperature is server-wide/per-model only — there is NO per-chat temperature.**
- There is no `ChatSettingsKey.TEMPERATURE` in the enum (internal/bot/models/chat_settings.py:281-457). The chat-settings system has model selectors (CHAT_MODEL, FALLBACK_MODEL, etc.) but no temperature key.
- The bare string `"temperature"` in tests/integration/test_database_operations.py:738 is arbitrary key material testing the generic setChatSetting mechanism — NOT wired to anything.
- `LLMService.generateText/Structured/Image` (internal/services/llm/service.py:1237, 1330, 1378) forward only messages, tools, schema, fallback models — they NEVER pass temperature. Temperature is set once at model construction (TOML) and immutable for the life of the instance.
- `dev_commands.py:194` has `"temperature": "Температура"` — a Russian i18n label for displaying `getInfo()` output, not a flow site.

Implication: any refactor of temperature threading does NOT need to touch ChatSettingsKey, chat_settings.py, or the chat-settings infrastructure.

**2. Temperature is threaded in TWO redundant ways due to `extraConfig=modelConfig`.**
- `LLMManager._initModels` (lib/ai/manager.py:164-189) reads `temperature: float = modelConfig.get("temperature", 0.5)` (:173) AND passes it explicitly to `provider.addModel(temperature=temperature, ...)` (:185).
- But it ALSO passes the WHOLE `modelConfig` dict verbatim as `extraConfig=modelConfig` (:188).
- So `self._config["temperature"]` already exists inside every model today. `FastembedModel._CONSUMED_EXTRA_KEYS` (fastembed_provider.py:343-363) explicitly strips `temperature` (and provider, model_id, model_version, context, enabled) before forwarding the remainder — confirming this redundancy is real and visible.

Implication for refactor: models can read temperature from `self._config` today; the explicit `temperature=` plumbing through every ctor/addModel/_createModelInstance is largely redundant. A refactor moving temperature into a customParams dict could either (a) add a new ctor arg, or (b) read a `customParams` sub-key from the existing `self._config` (parallel to how `image_options` works) — option (b) is a smaller diff.

title: no-Any rule: Dict[str, Any] is the established pattern for heterogeneous passthrough in lib/ai
content:
AGENTS.md forbids `Any` except when "a method genuinely accepts any type (e.g., a generic container, a passthrough decorator)." The lib/ai layer is SATURATED with `Dict[str, Any]` in exactly this passthrough position — establishing clear precedent that heterogeneous provider/request config dicts SHOULD be typed `Dict[str, Any]`, not forced into a single cross-provider TypedDict (verified 2026-07-20):

Established `Dict[str, Any]` passthrough sites:
- `AbstractModel.__init__(extraConfig: Optional[Dict[str, Any]])` — lib/ai/abstract.py:87
- `AbstractModel._config: Dict[str, Any]` — lib/ai/abstract.py:105
- `BasicOpenAIModel._getExtraParams() -> Dict[str, Any]` — basic_openai_provider.py:264
- `BasicOpenAIModel._getImageRequestOptions() -> Dict[str, Any]` — basic_openai_provider.py:244
- `BasicOpenAIProvider._getClientParams() -> Dict[str, Any]` — basic_openai_provider.py:1054
- `BasicOpenAIModel._executeChatCompletion(params: Dict[str, Any])` — basic_openai_provider.py:276
- `LLMManager(config: Dict[str, Any])` — lib/ai/manager.py:70
- `AbstractLLMProvider.__init__(config: Dict[str, Any])` — lib/ai/abstract.py:947
- `AbstractModel.generateStructured(..., schema: Dict[str, Any])` — lib/ai/abstract.py:364

Rationale for NOT using a single cross-provider TypedDict (e.g. `LLMRequestParams(TypedDict, total=False)`): providers take genuinely different keys — YC SDK's `.configure()` accepts `reasoning_mode`, OpenAI doesn't; OpenRouter takes `route_scale_parameters`; the Images API takes `size`/`quality`/etc. Forcing one TypedDict would either under-type (omit provider-specific keys) or over-type (claim keys every provider must accept).

Guidance: the cross-provider CONTRACT should stay `Dict[str, Any]`. A concrete TypedDict is appropriate ONLY inside a single provider for its own consumed subset (private, internal). This matches how `_getExtraParams` already works and the `ProxyKwargs`/`ProxyLifecycleConfigDict` pattern in lib/proxy/.

title: customParams refactor (Phase 1 of 5) — design, status, and what it supersedes
content:
A 5-phase refactor is replacing `AbstractModel`'s explicit `temperature: float` ctor arg with `customParams: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None`. Phase 1 (source edits in lib/ai, 2026-07-20) is committed in design but source edits were NOT yet verified via `make format lint` / `make test` (step budget hit before gates ran). Tests are EXPECTED to fail in Phase 1 and get fixed in Phase 3 — this is intentional.

**Design (LOCKED — do not redesign):**
- `AbstractModel.__init__` (lib/ai/abstract.py): dropped `temperature`, added `customParams: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None`. Stored as `self._customParams: Dict[str, Any] = dict(customParams) if customParams is not None else {}` (defensive copy). The `self.temperature` attribute is REMOVED with NO `@property` shim.
- Module constant `DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE = 0.5` added in lib/ai/abstract.py after imports, for sites that previously fell back to the ctor default.
- `getInfo()` (abstract.py:744): `"temperature": self.temperature` → `"customParams": dict(self._customParams)`.
- `LLMManager._initModels` (manager.py:~173-185): dropped `temperature=temperature`; now passes `customParams=modelConfig.get("customParams", {})`. The `extraConfig=modelConfig` line is KEPT (self._config still carries full modelConfig: capability flags + provider wiring).
- The 3 OpenAI-compatible `params = {... "temperature": self.temperature ...}` literals in basic_openai_provider.py (`_generateText`, `_generateStructured`, `_generateImageViaChatsApi`) LOST the temperature entry. Temperature now flows via `params.update(self._getExtraParams())` which returns customParams.
- `BasicOpenAIModel._getImageRequestOptions()`: whitelist (`size, quality, output_format, background, moderation, n, response_format, user`) REMOVED; now `return dict(self._customParams)` — "send everything, no whitelist."
- YC SDK `_generateStructured` override (yc_sdk_provider.py:~574-577): `temperature=min(self._customParams.get("temperature", DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE), 0.3)` — imports DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE from lib.ai.abstract.
- YC SDK `_getModel` text path: `kwargs = dict(self._customParams)` (was `{"temperature": self.temperature}`).
- All 6 provider files updated ctor signatures on `__init__`, `addModel`, and `_createModelInstance` — no `temperature: float` kwarg anywhere.

**YC SDK image-path DECISION (flagged for review):** `_getModel` image path now seeds `imageKwargs = dict(self._customParams)` then layers YC-specific reads (`mime_type`, `width_ratio`, `height_ratio`, `seed` from self._config) on top, then `configOverrides` win last. Rationale: consistency with "send everything" for OpenAI Images API, while preserving YC-SDK-specific image params. Opinionated interpretation — review before Phase 2.

**SUPERSEDES memory 171ada91** ("model.temperature must be preserved as @property"): the locked decision is the OPPOSITE — remove the attribute entirely, no shim, tests fixed in Phase 3. The test-file enumeration in 171ada91 (tests that reference `model.temperature` and `temperature=`) is STILL VALID and is exactly the Phase 3 scope list: tests/services/llm/test_llm_service.py, tests/services/llm/test_tool_call_healing.py, tests/integration/test_llm_integration.py, tests/lib/ai/providers/test_basic_openai_provider.py, tests/lib/ai/providers/test_openrouter_provider.py, tests/lib/ai/test_manager.py, tests/lib/ai/golden/test_golden.py, tests/utils.py, tests/fixtures/database_fixtures.py.

**SUPERSEDES memory 94dd8f50** ("temperature reaches LLM API at exactly 4 sites"): the 3 OpenAI sites no longer emit `"temperature": self.temperature` — it now comes from `_getExtraParams()` (customParams). The "last-wins via params.update(_getExtraParams())" observation is WHY this works.

**Phases remaining:** Phase 2 = TOML config migration (move temperature etc. into customParams in configs/). Phase 3 = fix the test files enumerated in 171ada91. Phase 4/5 = TBD.

title: _getExtraParams() override merge-ordering rule — user customParams must win over provider defaults
content:
Subtle convention established in the customParams refactor (Phase 1, 2026-07-20): provider subclasses that override `BasicOpenAIModel._getExtraParams()` must MERGE provider-specific defaults WITH the base (customParams), such that USER customParams takes precedence over provider defaults when the same key is set.

**Base impl** (BasicOpenAIModel._getExtraParams, basic_openai_provider.py): `return dict(self._customParams)`.

**Correct override shape** — provider defaults FIRST, then `super()._getExtraParams()` so customParams wins:
```python
def _getExtraParams(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {"extra_headers": {...provider defaults...}, **super()._getExtraParams()}
```
i.e. `{**providerDefaults, **super()._getExtraParams()}` — NOT the reverse.

**Why this ordering:** the call site `params.update(self._getExtraParams())` is already last-wins within `_generateText` etc. So within `_getExtraParams()` itself we want user customParams (from super, which returns customParams) to take precedence over provider defaults. Putting `super()._getExtraParams()` second (last) makes it win.

**Gotcha — easy to get backwards:** OpenRouter's override is `return {"extra_headers": {"HTTP-Referer": "https://notacompany.org/products/gromozeka", "X-Title": "Gromozeka AI Bot"}, **super()._getExtraParams()}`. If reversed to `{**super()._getExtraParams(), "extra_headers": {...}}`, a user setting nothing would still get the provider default, but a user who wanted to OVERRIDE extra_headers via customParams would lose. The locked intent: user customParams wins.

**YC OpenAI** (yc_openai_provider.py): override is `return {**super()._getExtraParams()}` — no YC-specific defaults today (the old commented-out `# "max_tokens": 2000` / `# "stream": True` hints were deleted; users now set those via customParams in TOML).

title: Fastembed _CONSUMED_EXTRA_KEYS filter removed — forwards customParams directly; Phase 2 TOML migration list
content:
Fastembed refactor (Phase 1 of customParams refactor, 2026-07-20). The `FastembedModel._CONSUMED_EXTRA_KEYS` constant and its filtering logic were REMOVED from lib/ai/providers/fastembed_provider.py. Previously, FastembedModel filtered `extraConfig` to strip known-consumed keys before forwarding the rest to the embedding library.

**New behavior:** `FastembedModel._fastembedKwargs = dict(self._customParams)` (was a filtered view of extraConfig). The provider-wide `cache_dir` fallback is PRESERVED: if `"cache_dir" not in self._fastembedKwargs and provider.cacheDir is not None`, the provider default is applied. (See memory 222e5612 for the provider-level cache_dir injection pattern — that behavior is unchanged.)

**Embedding-library call site (unchanged):** `TextEmbedding(model_name=modelId, **fastembedKwargs)` inside `_getOrCreateEmbedding` (~fastembed_provider.py:264). Cache keyed by modelId only (see memory 5d089f06 — kwargs silently ignored if duplicate modelId registered).

**What `_CONSUMED_EXTRA_KEYS` previously filtered OUT** (these never reached TextEmbedding before; they're consumed by AbstractModel/FastembedModel from self._config):
- Capability flags: `support_text`, `support_tools`, `support_images`, `support_structured_output`, `support_embeddings`
- FastembedModel-consumed: `embedding_dimensions`, `tier`
- Standard routing keys from LLMManager: `provider`, `model_id`, `model_version`, `temperature`, `context`, `enabled`

**What previously SURVIVED the filter** (reached TextEmbedding): anything NOT above — typically `cache_dir`, `threads`, `max_length`, and any other `TextEmbedding.__init__` kwargs the user placed at the TOP LEVEL of the model config.

**PHASE 2 TOML MIGRATION LIST (critical brief):** Users who had fastembed-specific kwargs at the top level of the model config (alongside capability flags) must now move them INSIDE the `customParams` dict. Specifically:
- `cache_dir` (only if set at the MODEL level — provider-level cacheDir still applies as fallback)
- `threads`
- `max_length`
- Any other `TextEmbedding.__init__` kwargs the user supplied

The capability flags and routing keys (`support_embeddings`, `embedding_dimensions`, `tier`, `provider`, `model_id`, etc.) STAY at the top level of modelConfig — they are NOT customParams; they're consumed from self._config (extraConfig). Only keys intended for the TextEmbedding constructor go into customParams.

title: Signature refactors COUPLE make lint and make test — pyright type-checks tests/* and flags stale call sites
content:
REFINES memory 7ac68e4d ("make lint vs make test orthogonality is permanent"). The orthogonality holds for runtime/config bugs (json.load key mismatches, golden data) but BREAKS for signature/interface refactors.

**The coupling:** `make lint` runs pyright, and pyright type-checks `tests/*` (only `ext/` is excluded per pyproject.toml). When a public constructor/method signature changes — e.g. removing a `temperature` kwarg — pyright emits `reportCallIssue` on every test call site still passing `temperature=`, and `reportAttributeAccessIssue` on every test reading/writing the removed attribute. The SAME stale call sites then fail at runtime with `TypeError`/`AttributeError` in `make test`. So for signature changes, lint and test are COUPLED by a shared root cause — a clean `make lint` is impossible while test fixes are deferred.

**Verified 2026-07-20 during the lib/ai customParams refactor:** `pyright lib/ai/` returned 0 errors (production clean), but `make lint` showed 66 pyright errors — ALL in `tests/*` (18 in test_basic_openai_provider.py, 18 in test_yc_openai_provider.py, 15 in test_openrouter_provider.py, etc.). flake8, isort, and the `import main` check all passed independently.

**Task-design implication (agent lesson):** A task with contradictory criteria like "make format lint passes clean" + "DO NOT try to fix tests (deferred to next phase)" is UNSATISFIABLE for a signature refactor. The correct response is: verify production code is pyright-clean in isolation (`pyright lib/<dir>/`), surface the contradiction explicitly, and do NOT hack test files to satisfy lint. Note that `import main` only catches module-level instantiation errors during import — it does NOT catch call-site signature mismatches inside function/method bodies (pyright is the gate that catches those).

**How to verify production-only cleanliness:** Run pyright directly on the source subtree, e.g. `./venv/bin/pyright lib/ai/` — this excludes tests/ and gives the true production-code verdict.

title: customParams refactor behavior change — chat-completion params now leak into OpenAI Images API calls
content:
NEW behavior-change gotcha introduced by the customParams refactor (Phase 1, 2026-07-20), flagged at RECOMMEND severity in source review:

**Before refactor:** `BasicOpenAIModel._getImageRequestOptions()` applied a whitelist of Images-API-compatible keys (`size`, `quality`, `output_format`, `background`, `moderation`, `n`, `response_format`, `user`). Chat-completion-only keys (`temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `stop`) were implicitly stripped.

**After refactor:** `_getImageRequestOptions()` returns `dict(self._customParams)` verbatim — no whitelist. Because the SAME `_customParams` dict feeds BOTH `_getExtraParams()` (chat completions / `_generateText` / `_generateStructured` / `_generateImageViaChatsApi`) AND `_getImageRequestOptions()` (the `openai-images` transport in `_generateImageViaImagesApi`), any chat-completion param a user puts in customParams will now be forwarded verbatim to `images.generate(...)`.

**Failure mode:** A dual-purpose model configured with a single `customParams={"temperature": 0.7, "max_tokens": 4096}` (sensible for text) will see image-generation calls via the `openai-images` transport fail with `BadRequestError` from OpenAI rejecting the unknown keys. No in-code warning points back to the cause.

**Mitigation in code:** The `_getImageRequestOptions()` docstring (basic_openai_provider.py:248-262) lists Images-API-compatible keys and ends with "The caller is responsible for providing provider-compatible keys" — technically correct but understates the risk. Review RECOMMENDS appending an explicit warning naming the chat-only keys that will leak.

**Operational guidance:** Either keep image-generation models on a separate model entry (separate customParams), or ensure customParams for a dual-purpose model only carries keys valid for both transports.

Note: the YcAIModel SDK image path is NOT affected — it seeds `imageKwargs = dict(self._customParams)` then layers YC-specific mime_type/width_ratio/height_ratio/seed from self._config ON TOP, so YC-specifics win. The leak risk is specific to the OpenAI Images API path.

title: customParams is shared by chat-completions AND Images API — chat-only keys leak to image generation
content:
Architectural gotcha in lib/ai (customParams refactor Phase 1, 2026-07-20): `BasicOpenAIModel._customParams` is a SINGLE dict that backs BOTH transport paths:

1. `_getExtraParams()` → forwards customParams into chat-completion API calls.
2. `_getImageRequestOptions()` → now returns `dict(self._customParams)` verbatim (no whitelist — the old image_options-key whitelist was REMOVED in this refactor) and merges into the OpenAI Images API request.

Consequence: chat-only keys (`temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `stop`) will ALSO be forwarded to the Images API if present in customParams. The Images API ignores or rejects unknown keys depending on provider.

Design guidance (now documented in the `_getImageRequestOptions` docstring Note): either keep image-generation models on a SEPARATE model config entry from chat models, or ensure customParams only carries keys valid for both transports.

Note for future agents: the two stale memories that described the OLD whitelist behavior ("_getImageRequestOptions whitelist excludes style" and "_getImageRequestOptions defensive fallback on image_options config") were DELETED because that code path no longer exists. Do not re-add them. `_getImageRequestOptions` is now a one-liner: `return dict(self._customParams)`.

title: customParams TOML config shape conventions (post Phase-1 migration)
content:
After the customParams refactor (Phase 1, 2026-07-20), all model TOML blocks under `configs/00-defaults/*model*.toml` were migrated to the new shape. Conventions established (apply when adding/editing model config):

**1. `temperature` is no longer a flat top-level key.** Use the dotted-key form:
```toml
[models.models.someModel]
customParams.temperature = 0.3   # dotted-key, single space around =
```
Do NOT use `temperature = X` (flat) — `LLMManager._initModels` no longer reads it. Do NOT use `[models.models.X.customParams]` table headers — the project deliberately uses the lighter dotted-key form. When `customParams.temperature` is absent, `DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE = 0.5` (lib/ai/abstract.py:44) is the fallback.

**2. Image-API params live in `customParams.*`, NOT in an `image_options` sub-table.** `BasicOpenAIModel._getImageRequestOptions()` now reads `self._customParams` (the old `self._config["image_options"]` reader is GONE). So a model like `aliceai-image-art` carries its image params inline:
```toml
[models.models."aliceai-image-art"]
customParams.temperature = 0.2
customParams.size = "1024x1024"
customParams.output_format = "png"
customParams.moderation = "low"
```
No `[model.image_options]` sub-table header should exist. (Supersedes memory c6853702 which documented the now-deleted image_options sub-table shape.)

**3. `customParams` is a SHARED dict backing both chat-completions AND Images API** — see gotcha memory e19e29e9: chat-only keys leak into image generation. Only put keys safe for both paths, or that are explicitly image-only on an image-only model.

Migration applied 2026-07-20 to all 5 files: yc-openai-models.toml (11 temps + 1 image_options flatten), yc-sdk-models.toml (3 + 1 commented), openrouter-models.toml (9), openrouter-models-free.toml (1), fastembed-models.toml (3 vacuous temps DELETED — see Fastembed classification memory).

title: Fastembed TOML key classification: top-level vs customParams
content:
Non-obvious decision made during the customParams config migration (2026-07-20): which keys under a `[models.models.X]` Fastembed block stay at top level vs. move into `customParams.*`. Derived by reading `lib/ai/providers/fastembed_provider.py`.

**STAY at top level** (read from `extraConfig`/`self._config` by capability code, NOT forwarded to `TextEmbedding(...)`):
- `provider`, `model_id`, `model_version`, `context`, `enabled`, `tier` — standard model metadata
- `support_tools`, `support_text`, `support_images`, `support_structured_output` — capability flags
- `support_embeddings` — consumed at `FastembedProvider.addModel` (~L223): `extraConfig.get("support_embeddings", False)`
- `embedding_dimensions` — consumed by `AbstractModel` base class (not referenced in fastembed_provider.py directly)

**MOVE to `customParams.*`** (TextEmbedding-library kwargs, forwarded via `**self._customParams` after Phase 1 removed the `_CONSUMED_EXTRA_KEYS` filter): `cache_dir`, `threads`, `max_length`, `doc_embed_type`, and any other kwarg `fastembed.TextEmbedding(...)` accepts.

**DELETE entirely** (Rule 4): Fastembed's vacuous `temperature = 0.0`. Fastembed is embeddings-only; temperature has no semantic meaning. Do NOT migrate it to `customParams.temperature`.

Current state (2026-07-20): `configs/00-defaults/fastembed-models.toml` has NO `cache_dir`/`threads`/`max_length`/`doc_embed_type` keys present, so its 3 model blocks ended up with NO `customParams` block at all (only the vacuous `temperature = 0.0` lines were deleted). At runtime `LLMManager._initModels` does `modelConfig.get("customParams", {})` → passes `{}` → `FastembedModel._fastembedKwargs = {}` (+ provider-wide `cacheDir` from `providers.toml` applied as default). Correct.

If a future agent adds TextEmbedding-library kwargs to a Fastembed model TOML, they MUST go under `customParams.*`, not flat top-level.
