title: Release cuts are CHANGELOG-only: no version field anywhere, no tag/README policy in spec
content:
Discovered 2026-07-21 during the 1.0.0 release-cut research pass. Extends memory 7f440485 (pyproject.toml has no version) to the whole repo, and documents a doc/reality gap.

## There is NO app-version string anywhere in the repo

Confirmed by grep across `pyproject.toml`, `Makefile`, `.sourcecraft/ci.yaml`, `README.md`, `docs/*.md`, `docs/llm/*.md`, `configs/`, `internal/`. Every `0.x.y`-shaped hit is either:
- a loopback IP (`127.0.0.1`), or
- a third-party dependency pin (`python-magic==0.4.27`, `sqlite-vec==0.1.9`, `aiodocker==0.27.0`, etc.).

There is no root `package.json` with a version. `pyproject.toml` is purely tool config (no `[project]` block — see memory 7f440485). So nothing needs bumping on release.

## Doc/reality gap: docs/llm/changelog.md §142 is unfulfillable here

`docs/llm/changelog.md` line 142 says: "If the project doesn't publish to a registry, version bumps are still useful for tracking — keep `package.json` (or equivalent) version in sync with the changelog heading."

The "(or equivalent)" clause has NO concrete target in this repo. A future agent following this instruction literally will hunt for a version field that does not exist. This is a known doc/process gap — not yet resolved as of 2026-07-21.

## A release cut is a pure CHANGELOG.md file operation

The authoritative cut procedure (`docs/llm/changelog.md` §96-126 + the `/changelog cut` command, Branch 1 — see memory e1d905fa) does exactly two things:
1. Rename `## [Unreleased]` → `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD`.
2. Insert a fresh empty `## [Unreleased]` above it.

The spec does NOT cover (these are policy gaps the teamlead must decide on, not established conventions):
- git tag creation (`git tag -a vX.Y.Z`) or tag pushing — NOT mentioned anywhere in docs/llm/changelog.md
- README version bumps — no version in README to bump
- Any version-field sync — nothing to sync (see gap above)

## Initial baseline section interaction (first release only)

`docs/llm/changelog.md` §128-130 documents the one-time `## Initial State - YYYY-MM-DD` baseline (this repo has `## Initial State - 2026-07-15`). The standard cut does NOT touch it — it stays in place, ending up further down the file beneath the new versioned heading. Post-first-release order: `## [Unreleased]` (empty) → `## [1.0.0] - date` → `## Initial State - 2026-07-15`.

## Practical implication

When cutting any release, an agent should: run `/changelog cut X.Y.Z` (or do the rename+insert manually), then STOP and surface the tag/README/version-sync decisions to the teamlead rather than inventing a tag or hunting for a nonexistent version field. As of 2026-07-21 no git tags existed at all (1.0.0 would be the first).

title: CHANGELOG structural drift: duplicate same-category ### headings under one release
content:
Observed 2026-07-21 during the 1.0.0 release cut on CHANGELOG.md. The `## [Unreleased]` section had accumulated TWO separate `### Changed` subsection headings (a 4-bullet block and a 5-bullet block), with `### Added` / `### Removed` interleaved between them. Keep-a-Changelog requires at most ONE of each category heading per release; duplicates are a structural violation that must be merged.

This is DISTINCT from memory ce8d9c99, which covers per-ENTRY misclassification (fixes under Added, bundled entries, internal refactors that should be dropped). This is a SECTION-level problem: the same category heading appears twice as separate subsections.

## Detection (use during release cut or any changelog review)

Run `rg "^### " CHANGELOG.md` and confirm exactly one of each category (Added / Changed / Removed / Fixed) per release heading. During the 1.0.0 cut this surfaced as `### Added / ### Changed / ### Removed / ### Changed / ### Fixed` — the duplicate `### Changed` was immediately visible.

## Fix

Merge the duplicate blocks into a single subsection under the release heading. Preserve every bullet's text verbatim (do not reword/summarize — per AGENTS.md hard rule). Reorder bullets within the merged block for topical coherence only. Ensure final category order follows Keep-a-Changelog: Added → Changed → Removed → Fixed.

## Why it matters

The release-cut procedure in `docs/llm/changelog.md` §96-126 covers the heading rename + empty-Unreleased insert but does NOT mention a heading-uniqueness audit. Without the `rg "^### "` check, a duplicate-category release would ship. The `/changelog` command and manual edits can both re-introduce this drift, so treat the heading audit as a mandatory release-cut step.

## Post-cut verified state (1.0.0)

`rg "^### " CHANGELOG.md` after the merge yielded: Added / Changed / Removed / Fixed (under [1.0.0]) then a single Added (under Initial State). Exactly one `### Changed` — duplicate resolved.

title: pyproject.toml [project].version is the canonical app version (PEP 621, no build-system)
content:
As of 2026-07-21 (1.0.0 release prep), `pyproject.toml` now has a `[project]` table at the TOP of the file, above all `[tool.*]` sections (PEP 621 convention: `[project]` comes first). Minimal content:

```toml
[project]
name = "gromozeka"
version = "1.0.0"
description = "Multi-platform LLM-powered bot for Telegram and Max Messenger"
```

Key conventions:
- **`[project].version` is the canonical machine-readable version string.** It mirrors the `CHANGELOG.md` release heading (`## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD`). The two MUST stay in lockstep — bump both on every release. The `/generate-release` slash-command automates this.
- **NO `[build-system]` table** (intentional — the repo is NOT a distributable package and uses no build backend). Adding `[project]` without `[build-system]` is valid PEP 621; tools just read the metadata.
- **NO `authors`, `license`, `readme`, `requires-python`, or `dependencies` fields.** The block is deliberately minimal: name + version + description only. Runtime deps live in `requirements.direct.txt` / `requirements.txt` (frozen), NOT in `[project].dependencies`.
- The `description` value is consistent with README's first sentence ("…multi-platform AI bot supporting Telegram and Max Messenger").

This SUPERSEDES the prior state where there was no version string anywhere in the repo (the old "no [project] section" and "no version field anywhere" memories are deleted as obsolete). When cutting a release, the version field MUST be bumped — it is no longer a CHANGELOG-only operation.

title: /generate-release slash-command: 4th repo-local command, routed to teamlead, full release sequence
content:
On 2026-07-21, `.opencode/commands/generate-release.md` was created — the 4th repo-local opencode slash-command. `.opencode/commands/` now holds: `changelog`, `refine-memory`, `review-large`, `generate-release` (corrects memory 2070cde9's "3 commands" count). Invoke as `/generate-release <X.Y.Z>`.

## Frontmatter decisions
- **`agent: teamlead`** — rationale: the release process spans multiple file types requiring sequential coordination (CHANGELOG cut = docs-writer territory; pyproject.toml + commit + tag = software-developer territory) with verification gates between. Teamlead decomposes and dispatches; a single software-developer would have to do it all itself.
- **`subtask: true`** — non-interactive: never blocks on user input, makes best-effort decisions, states assumptions in the final report, NEVER guesses the version.

## Body design (models on /changelog Branch structure)
`$ARGUMENTS` validation follows the branch-ordering convention (memory 137b9edb — reserved/empty branches must precede the generic valid branch):
- **Branch 0a — empty**: abort with exact guidance message ("Re-invoke as `/generate-release <X.Y.Z>` … Semver bump rules: patch=bugfixes, minor=new features, major=breaking changes").
- **Branch 0b — invalid**: non-empty but fails STRICT semver `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`. Rejects pre-release/build metadata variants (`1.0.0-rc1`, `1.2.3+build4`) on purpose — users wanting those run steps manually. Abort with same message.
- **Branch 0c — valid**: proceed.

4 operations in order (per `docs/llm/changelog.md` "Release operations" section):
1. **CHANGELOG cut** — dispatch docs-writer: rename `## [Unreleased]` → `## [<VERSION>] - <TODAY>` (date via `date +%Y-%m-%d`, fallback `date -u +%Y-%m-%d` UTC), insert empty `## [Unreleased]` above.
2. **Version bump** — set `[project].version` in `pyproject.toml` to `<VERSION>`.
3. **Commit** — stage `CHANGELOG.md` + `pyproject.toml` (+ thematically-related dirty files only), message `Release v<VERSION>` (consistent with free-form commit convention, memory 12da30a8).
4. **Tag + push** — annotated tag `v<VERSION>` with message `Release v<VERSION>`, then `git push origin v<VERSION>`.

## Safety rules (best-effort, never block)
- **Tag already exists** (`git rev-parse -q --verify refs/tags/v<VERSION>` succeeds): ABORT before tagging, surface conflict. NEVER force-overwrite an existing tag in subtask mode without explicit user sign-off.
- **`git push` fails** (no remote/auth/network): surface error, leave tag local — user pushes manually.
- **Date unobtainable both ways**: abort, ask user to invoke manually.
- **Dirty tree beyond CHANGELOG + pyproject**: include extra files ONLY if thematically part of release; otherwise commit just CHANGELOG + pyproject and leave rest dirty. State the choice in the final report.

## Link target / anchor
The command links to `docs/llm/changelog.md#release-operations-version-bump-commit-tag-push`. A parallel docs-writer task added the section with heading `## Release operations (version bump, commit, tag, push)`. GitHub-style anchor derivation: lowercase, strip parens/commas/punctuation, spaces → dashes = `release-operations-version-bump-commit-tag-push`.

## Gotcha
`make check-docs` EXCLUDES `.opencode/` (`scripts/check_docs.py` `_EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES`), so internal links inside slash-command files are NOT machine-validated — manually verify any links when authoring/editing commands. (pyproject.toml and `.opencode/` markdown are also outside the black/isort/flake8/pyright graph, so `make format lint` is a no-op on them.)

title: RELEASE PROCESS ESTABLISHED: pyproject.toml [project].version + full release ops documented
content:
SUPERSEDES two now-STALE memories that must be ignored/deleted when the delete tool cooperates:
- `7f440485` ("pyproject.toml has no [project] section") — now FALSE
- `6dd5e741` ("Release cuts are CHANGELOG-only: no version field anywhere, no tag policy") — now FALSE on every claim

## What changed (2026-07-21, parallel software-developer task + docs task)

`pyproject.toml` (repo root) now has a `[project]` table:
```toml

version = "1.0.0"
description = "Multi-platform LLM-powered bot for Telegram and Max Messenger"
```
The `[tool.*]` sections remain. The `name = "gromozeka"` / description are NEW project metadata.

## Canonical version source + sync rule

`[project].version` in `pyproject.toml` is the **canonical machine-readable** version source. The CHANGELOG release heading (`## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD`) is the **human-readable mirror**. The two MUST stay in sync. The old `(or equivalent)` / `package.json` hedge in `docs/llm/changelog.md` §Versioning has been removed and replaced with the concrete `pyproject.toml` reference.

`docs/llm/changelog.md` has a new `## Release operations (version bump, commit, tag, push)` H2 section (between `## The [Unreleased] Section` and `## Versioning`). The complete release = CHANGELOG cut + these three operations:

(a) **Version bump**: set `[project].version` in `pyproject.toml` to match the new dated heading.
(b) **Atomic commit**: stage `CHANGELOG.md` + `pyproject.toml` (and any release-prep files from `git status`) as ONE commit. Convention commit message: `Release v<X.Y.Z>` (e.g. `Release v1.0.0`).
(c) **Tag + push**: ANNOTATED tag (NOT lightweight) — `git tag -a v<X.Y.Z> -m "Release v<X.Y.Z>"` then `git push origin v<X.Y.Z>`. Annotated is the chosen convention per git-semantic norms (records tagger/date/message).

The `/generate-release <version>` slash-command (`.opencode/commands/generate-release.md`) automates the whole sequence end-to-end. `make check-docs` → "Checked 108 markdown files, 1696 links; 0 broken." The inline anchor `#release-operations-version-bump-commit-tag-push` resolves correctly (GitHub anchor rule: lowercase, spaces→hyphens, parens/commas stripped).

## Practical implication for future agents

Do NOT tell a teamlead that the release spec "has no tag/version policy" — that gap is now closed. Do NOT hunt for a nonexistent version field — it's `[project].version` in `pyproject.toml`. When cutting a release, run `/generate-release <version>` for the full automation, or follow `docs/llm/changelog.md` §Release operations manually.

title: Drift risk: /changelog cut and /generate-release Step 1 both describe the CHANGELOG release cut independently
content:
Identified 2026-07-21 during Gate 1+2 review of the `/generate-release` addition. This is a drift-risk gotcha for future edits to either command — NOT yet fixed.

## The overlap
Two repo-local slash-commands both describe the CHANGELOG release cut (rename `## [Unreleased]` → `## [<VERSION>] - <DATE>`, insert empty `## [Unreleased]` above):

- **`/changelog cut <X.Y.Z>`** (`.opencode/commands/changelog.md`, Branch 1) — CHANGELOG cut ONLY. Routed to `agent: software-developer`. This is the canonical/first implementation.
- **`/generate-release <X.Y.Z>`** (`.opencode/commands/generate-release.md`, Step 1) — does the cut as the FIRST of 4 operations (cut → version bump → commit → tag+push). Routed to `agent: teamlead`, which "dispatches docs-writer to perform the cut".

## The problem
`/generate-release` Step 1 re-describes the cut from scratch and dispatches `docs-writer`, instead of reusing `/changelog cut` (which dispatches `software-developer`). The two prose descriptions of the identical cut operation are independent and WILL drift over time — e.g. if the date-source rule, heading-rename format, or empty-section-insertion logic changes in one, the other won't automatically follow.

Neither `docs/llm/changelog.md` §Automation nor the command files currently document this relationship, so a reader can't tell which is authoritative for the cut.

## Reviewer's recommended fix (not yet applied)
Either:
(a) Have `/generate-release` Step 1 dispatch the existing `/changelog cut <VERSION>` slash-command to reuse the single canonical cut implementation; OR
(b) Add a one-line note in BOTH command files AND `docs/llm/changelog.md` §Automation stating that `/changelog cut` does the CHANGELOG heading rename only (subset), while `/generate-release` does the full release sequence (cut + bump + commit + tag + push), and that the cut contract is shared so future edits stay in sync.

## Scope note for `docs/llm/changelog.md` §Automation
That paragraph should clarify the overlap: `/changelog cut` = CHANGELOG-only subset; `/generate-release` = full release. Currently it introduces `/generate-release` without noting `/changelog cut` also exists for the cut sub-operation.

title: /generate-release known robustness gaps: no detached-HEAD guard, no merge-conflict guard
content:
Identified 2026-07-21 during Gate 1+2 review of `/generate-release`. These are KNOWN-INCOMPLETE behaviors of the command — NOT blockers for the 1.0.0 release (repo was on `master` with a clean dirty tree at review time), but should be fixed before relying on the command for many future releases.

## Gap 1: no detached-HEAD guard
`/generate-release` Step 3 (Commit) and Step 4 (Tag+push) have no check for detached HEAD. `git commit` and `git tag -a` BOTH succeed silently in detached HEAD, but the release commit becomes orphaned (no branch advances to it) — reachable only via the tag. `git push origin v<VERSION>` pushes the tag (and its commit) but no branch ref updates, so future `git checkout master` will NOT see the release commit. Dangerous for a release.

**Fix:** Before Step 3, check `git symbolic-ref -q HEAD` (returns non-zero in detached HEAD) and ABORT with a one-liner telling the user to checkout a branch first.

## Gap 2: no merge-conflict / unmerged-paths guard
Step 3's dirty-tree decision rule ("include extra files ONLY if thematically part of the release") silently assumes a clean dirty tree. If `git status` shows `Unmerged paths` (ongoing merge conflict), the rule is meaningless and the teamlead could stage half-resolved files or fail confusingly.

**Fix:** Before Step 3, check `git status` for `Unmerged paths`; if present, ABORT with a message to resolve conflicts and re-invoke.

## Related minor robustness notes from the same review (lower priority)
- **Date determinism:** Step 1 obtains the date via local TZ first (`date +%Y-%m-%d`), UTC only as a fallback (`date -u +%Y-%m-%d`). The same release executed at the same instant from different timezones can yield different CHANGELOG dates. Reviewer suggested UTC-first for determinism.
- **$ARGUMENTS trimming:** strict regex `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` rejects whitespace-padded input (` 1.0.0`); multi-token input is correctly rejected but leading/trailing whitespace from copy-paste hits the unhelpful "invalid semver" branch.

## Durable lesson (applies to ANY future git-automation slash-command in this repo)
Release/commit automation that runs `git commit` / `git tag` must explicitly guard against (1) detached HEAD and (2) unmerged paths, because both states let the underlying git commands succeed while producing dangerous results (orphaned commits, half-resolved merges). Do not rely on `git commit` failing to catch these.

title: /generate-release hardened 2026-07-21: detached-HEAD + unmerged-paths guards, UTC dates, arg trimming
content:
On 2026-07-21, `.opencode/commands/generate-release.md` was hardened with 4 robustness fixes (applied via software-developer, since `.opencode/**` is docs-writer-denied). All four close the previously-open Gate 1+2 findings (supersedes deleted memory adf1fd40).

## Fixes applied
1. **Merge-conflict guard (Step 3 Commit).** Before staging, check `git status` for "Unmerged paths" (equiv. `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` non-empty). If present, ABORT: "Working tree has unmerged paths. Resolve conflicts and re-invoke `/generate-release <VERSION>`." The dirty-tree decision rule previously assumed a clean tree.

2. **Detached-HEAD guard (new Branch 0d, early in Step 0).** Placed as a precondition BEFORE Step 1 so no partial work precedes the abort. Check `git symbolic-ref -q HEAD` (non-zero) or `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` returns "HEAD". If detached, ABORT: "HEAD is detached. Checkout a release branch first (e.g. `git checkout master`) and re-invoke `/generate-release <VERSION>`." Rationale: `git commit` + `git tag -a` succeed in detached HEAD but produce an orphaned commit reachable only via the tag.

3. **`$ARGUMENTS` whitespace strip (Step 0 intro).** Added instruction to strip leading/trailing whitespace from `$ARGUMENTS` before the strict semver regex `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` — otherwise copy-paste padding hits the unhelpful "invalid semver" branch.

4. **UTC-only date (Step 1.1 CHANGELOG cut + best-effort bullet).** Reversed the prior local-TZ-first → UTC-fallback preference. Now uses `date -u +%Y-%m-%d` only (cross-timezone reproducibility). If that fails (vanishingly rare), ABORT and tell the user to invoke manually. No local-TZ path remains.

## Corrections to architecture memory 8355dd01
8355dd01 (the command's architecture record) is now PARTIALLY OUTDATED on two points — the file itself is authoritative:
- It says "Branch 0c — valid: proceed." **Now:** Branch 0c says "Continue to Branch 0d"; Branch 0d is the detached-HEAD check that gates proceeding to Step 1. Step 0 now has FOUR branches (0a empty, 0b invalid, 0c valid, 0d detached HEAD).
- It says date via "`date +%Y-%m-%d`, fallback `date -u +%Y-%m-%d` UTC". **Now:** UTC-only (`date -u +%Y-%m-%d`); the local-TZ fallback was dropped.

## Durable lesson (retained from the original open finding)
ANY future git-automation slash-command in this repo must explicitly guard against (1) detached HEAD and (2) unmerged paths before `git commit`/`git tag` — both states let the underlying git commands succeed while producing dangerous results (orphaned commits, half-resolved merges). Do not rely on git failing. Bake these guards in from the start; the generate-release design now exemplifies the pattern (detached-HEAD check early in Step 0, unmerged-paths check in Step 3 before staging).

## Verification
All 4 fixes confirmed present via targeted `rg` searches; `make format lint` clean (markdown-only change; sanity check).

title: Inline fenced-tool healing can execute prose examples
content: A code review of the inline-code tool-name + fenced-JSON healing path found a false-positive risk: `_matchTextForBrokenKnownToolCall` accepts any complete response shaped like `` `registered_tool` `` followed by a fenced JSON object, with no discriminator that the text is an actual tool request rather than documentation/prose showing an example. `_tryHealToolCall` converts the match into `TOOL_CALLS`, and `generateTextViaLLM` then executes the registered handler; this is especially consequential for side-effecting tools such as media generation. If this representation remains ambiguous, prefer treating ambiguous matches as retry/error rather than executing, or require an additional unambiguous call marker. Add an integration regression test where the model explains or documents the exact syntax and assert the handler is not called.

title: Inline healing needs disabled-tool allowlist coverage
content: The inline healing matcher validates the tool name against the global `toolsHandlers` registry, while actual execution later applies the `filteredToolNames`/`useTools` allowlist. Existing integration coverage enabled all tools, and the disabled-tool test covered only native `TOOL_CALLS`; therefore the new inline route lacked a regression test proving that a registered-but-disabled inline tool is not executed and that the model receives the expected “not available” tool result. Add an end-to-end inline-form test with the tool excluded by `useTools`, asserting the handler is never awaited and the next model turn receives the rejection result.

title: Tool healing must reject trailing JSON remainder
content: Code review of `internal/services/llm/service.py` found that the fenced/inline healing path uses `_tryParseJson()`/`raw_decode()`, which parses only the first JSON value and returns `endPos`. If `_tryApplyToolCallMatch()` does not require `toolArgsStr[endPos:].strip()` to be empty, inputs such as `{"a": 1}\n{"b": 2}` or valid JSON followed by prose can be converted into an executable tool call using only the first object. The matcher should require full argument-string consumption and regression-test multiple objects, trailing prose, and no-mutation on rejection.

title: Healing matcher needs explicit malformed-input coverage
content: For the inline-code tool-name plus fenced-JSON healing route in `tests/services/llm/test_tool_call_healing.py`, successful coverage should include both unlabeled and `json`-labeled Markdown fences; negative coverage should include unknown tools, malformed JSON, and trailing content/multiple JSON objects. These cases exercise the regex language-tag branch and the raw-decoder boundary, rather than only proving the happy path with an unlabeled fence.

title: Durable healing docs must list new matcher
content: When adding a new LLM tool-call healing matcher, update both `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` and `docs/llm/memories/llm-tool-call-healing.md`; stale text claiming the orchestrator has five matchers and omitting `_matchTextForInlineCodeToolNameAndJson` makes the documented recovery cascade inaccurate. Keep durable implementation notes synchronized with the actual matcher count and names.

title: Yandex SpeechKit STT API — integration reference
content:
Comprehensive technical reference for integrating Yandex SpeechKit STT (via AI Studio / Yandex Cloud). Gathered 2026-07 from official docs at aistudio.yandex.ru/docs/en/speechkit (mirrors cloud.yandex.ru/en/docs/speechkit).

## API modalities
- v1 SYNC (REST): POST https://stt.api.cloud.yandex.net/speech/v1/stt:recognize — <=30s, <=1MB, mono.
- v2 ASYNC (REST): POST https://transcribe.api.cloud.yandex.net/speech/stt/v2/longRunningRecognize — Object Storage URI only; result embedded inline when done. Returns per-word confidence scores.
- v3 ASYNC (REST + gRPC) [PREFERRED for transcription]:
  - submit: POST https://stt.api.cloud.yandex.net/stt/v3/recognizeFileAsync
  - poll:   GET  https://operation.api.cloud.yandex.net/operations/{id}
  - result: GET  https://stt.api.cloud.yandex.net/stt/v3/getRecognition?operation_id={id}  (concatenated JSON stream of events)
  - delete: DELETE .../stt/v3/deleteRecognition?operation_id={id}
  - gRPC host: stt.api.cloud.yandex.net:443, AsyncRecognizerStub.RecognizeFile / .GetRecognition
  - Protobuf: github.com/yandex-cloud/cloudapi/tree/master/yandex/cloud/ai/stt/v3
- v2/v3 STREAMING (gRPC): RecognizerStub.RecognizeStreaming — <=5min session, <=10MB, mono.

NO VIDEO SUPPORT anywhere — only audio. Must demux first (ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -ac 1 -ar 16000 -c:a pcm_s16le out.wav).

## Formats (only 3)
- LPCM raw (LINEAR16_PCM, 16-bit signed LE): 8/16/48 kHz for STT.
- OggOpus (OGG+OPUS): no restrictions.
- MP3: no restrictions EXCEPT not supported in v1 sync or v2 streaming.
- Containers in v3: WAV, OGG_OPUS, MP3 via container_audio.container_audio_type.
- Channels: sync/streaming=1; async<=2.

## Timestamps (CRITICAL — both word + utterance level available)
v3 getRecognition returns concatenated JSON objects, each a result.{final|finalRefinement|eouUpdate|...}:
- final.alternatives[].words[]{text, startTimeMs, endTimeMs} — WORD-level, ms from start (as strings).
- final.alternatives[]{text, startTimeMs, endTimeMs} — PHRASE-level.
- eouUpdate.timeMs — end-of-utterance boundary = "replica" delimiter.
- finalRefinement.normalizedText — same timestamps, normalised (punctuation/caps/numbers).
- v3 confidence field is always 0 (placeholder). v2 returns real confidence 0-1.
v2 longRunningRecognize returns response.chunks[].alternatives[].words[]{startTime:"0.160s",endTime,word,confidence} (Go duration strings).

## Speaker labeling (v3 only)
- speakerLabeling.speakerLabeling=SPEAKER_LABELING_ENABLED.
- Constraints: FULL_DATA mode, MONO, MAX 2 SPEAKERS. channel_tag 0/1 per phrase.
- For >2 speakers need external diarisation.

## Auth
- IAM token: Authorization: Bearer <token> — expires ~12h, refresh needed.
- API key: Authorization: Api-Key <key> — SERVICE ACCOUNT only, long-lived. PREFERRED for daemons.
- Folder ID: required for user accounts (v1/v2 in body folderId=; v3 in x-folder-id header). NOT required for service accounts (inferred).
- ASYNC REQUIRES service account — user/federated accounts cannot do async.
- Roles on SA: ai.speechkit-stt.user + storage.uploader (+ KMS roles if bucket encrypted).

## Languages
- ru-RU default + best. 16 total: en-US, de-DE, es-ES, fr-FR, it-IT, pt-PT, pt-BR, kk-KZ, uz-UZ, nl-NL, pl-PL, sv-SE, fi-FI, tr-TR, he-IL.
- auto-detection (v3 only): language_restriction with restriction_type=WHITELIST, language_code=['auto'] or list. Returns per-phrase language_code + probability.
- Model tags: general (stable), general:rc, general:deprecated (2-week overlap after general bump — pin in prod). Async also: deferred-general (cheaper, low-priority queue).

## Limits
- Sync: 30s / 1MB / 1ch.
- Streaming: 5min / 10MB / 1ch.
- Async: 4h / 1GB (Object Storage URI) or 60MB (inline base64 in v3) / 2ch.
- Results retained 3 days then deleted.
- Quotas: streaming 40 rps; sync 20 rps; async 500 req/hour; status poll v2=2500/hour, v3=5/sec; 10000 billable hours/day.

## Pricing (USD ex-VAT)
- Sync/streaming: $0.0013327867 per 15s mono.
- Async standard: $0.0012418035 per 15s of 2-CHANNEL audio (channels rounded UP to even; min 15s per 2ch; per-second after 16s).
- Async deferred: $0.0003122955 per 15s 2ch.
- Empty request = 1 unit (billed). 5xx internal errors NOT billed.
- ~Cost: 1h mono ru-RU async standard ≈ $0.596/hour of audio; deferred ≈ $0.15/hour.

## Python SDK
- PREFERRED: yandex-cloud-ml-sdk (official, multimodal). pip install yandex-cloud-ml-sdk. Python>=3.9. Latest 0.19.x (Jan 2026). Repo github.com/yandex-cloud/yandex-cloud-ml-sdk. Init: YCloudML(folder_id=..., auth=...); auto-reads YC_API_KEY env var.
- LEGACY: yandex-speechkit-lib-python (TikhonP) — community, v2 only, avoid.
- SDK STT method names evolve between minors — verify against pinned version's examples/ + py.typed stubs. readthedocs index currently 404s. Underlying wire contract is v3 gRPC regardless.
- Raw gRPC fallback: clone cloudapi repo, grpcio-tools protoc to generate stt_pb2/stt_service_pb2 stubs.

## Gotchas
- Inline base64 in v3 capped at 60MB — larger files MUST go via Object Storage URI.
- Single global endpoint, no regions.
- Results expire 3 days — persist immediately.
- IAM token ~12h expiry — use API key for long-running services.
- v3 status poll quota is 5/sec (friendlier than v2's 2500/hour).
- Recognition is ~10x realtime (1 min audio -> ~10s).
- general tag silently moves on updates — pin to general:rc or general:deprecated for reproducibility; watch release-notes-stt.
- v3 confidence always 0 — use v2 if confidence scoring needed.
- Speaker labeling: mono, <=2 speakers, FULL_DATA.
- Errors via google.rpc.Status in operation.error when done:true. Retry 5xx (not billed). 4xx may be billed.
- MP3 unsupported in v1 sync and v2 streaming.

## Source URLs (all under aistudio.yandex.ru/docs/en/speechkit, mirror cloud.yandex.ru/en/docs/speechkit)
- /en/speechkit/stt/ (modality matrix)
- /en/speechkit/formats (audio formats)
- /en/speechkit/stt/models (languages, model tags)
- /en/speechkit/stt/transcribation (async concepts, modes)
- /en/speechkit/stt/speaker-labeling
- /en/speechkit/concepts/auth (auth + folder id rules)
- /en/speechkit/concepts/limits (quotas + technical limits)
- /en/speechkit/pricing (billing rules + prices)
- /en/speechkit/stt-v3/api-ref/ (v3 REST service URL)
- /en/speechkit/stt-v3/api-ref/AsyncRecognizer/recognizeFile (full request schema: content vs uri, RecognitionModelOptions, SpeakerLabelingOptions, SummarizationOptions)
- /en/speechkit/quickstart/stt-quickstart-v2 (curl flow + response examples for both v2 and v3)
- /en/speechkit/stt/api/transcribation-api-v3 (gRPC Python example)
- /en/speechkit/stt/api/streaming-examples-v3 (v3 streaming gRPC example)
- /en/speechkit/stt/api/request-examples (v1 sync example)
- github.com/yandex-cloud/cloudapi (protobuf interface definitions)
- pypi.org/project/yandex-cloud-ml-sdk

title: STT integration gap: voice/audio downloaded but never transcribed
content:
Comprehensive map of the bot-side gap that motivates STT integration, gathered 2026-07-27. Complements the Yandex SpeechKit STT API research (memory 17b7097b, the vendor/API side). The bot has NO speech-to-text code anywhere — voice/audio messages are downloaded and stored but their audio content is never converted to text. The LLM never sees audio content.

## What exists today (download + store, but no transcription)
- `MessageType.AUDIO` and `MessageType.VOICE` are defined in `internal/models/shared_enums.py` (lines 74, 77).
- Telegram voice/audio detection: `EnsuredMessage.fromMessage` (`internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:646-660`) sets `messageType = MessageType.AUDIO`/`VOICE` when `message.audio`/`message.voice` present.
- Download path: `TheBot.downloadAttachment(mediaId, fileId)` (`internal/bot/common/bot.py:1018-1040`) → Telegram uses `tgBot.get_file(fileId).download_as_bytearray()`, Max uses `maxBot.downloadAttachmentPayload(fileId)` (HTTP GET).
- Storage: `BaseBotHandler.storeAttachment(data, prefix, mediaType)` (`base.py:1932-1967`) — content-addressed (SHA512), key format `{prefix}{mediaType}-{sha512}.{mimeType}`, backed by `StorageService`.

## The image-only parsing pipeline (THE gap)
`BaseBotHandler._processMediaV2` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:1726-1929`) is the central media-processing pipeline. It downloads and stores ALL media types, but parsing/analysis is IMAGE-ONLY:
- Lines 1834-1837 and 1892-1901: only `MessageType.IMAGE` and `MessageType.STICKER` are marked `MediaStatus.PENDING` for parsing.
- Non-image media (including voice/audio) hits the else branch: `logger.warning(f"{ret.type}#{ret.id} is not an image, skipping parsing")`, marks `MediaStatus.NEW`, and returns with an empty task.
- This is where STT transcription would hook in — extend the condition to include `MessageType.VOICE`/`MessageType.AUDIO`.

## Telegram routing
`processTelegramMedia` (`base.py:1507-1602`) routes by `ensuredMessage.messageType`: IMAGE→`processTelegramImage`, STICKER→`processTelegramSticker`, ANIMATION/VIDEO/VIDEO_NOTE/AUDIO/VOICE/DOCUMENT→`_processTelegramMedia` (lines 1542-1597). Voice and audio ARE downloaded/stored via this path (lines 1568-1587).

## Max routing
`processMaxMedia` (`base.py:1604-1724`) iterates `baseMessage.body.attachments`, dispatches by type. Audio attachments (lines 1693-1707) ARE processed/stored.

## Max AudioAttachment.transcription field — UNUSED OPPORTUNITY
`lib/max_bot/models/attachment.py:340-386`: `AudioAttachment` has a `transcription: Optional[str]` field (line 370, 384) populated from `data.get("transcription")` from the Max API. The bot reads this attachment type in `processMaxMedia` but NEVER reads or sets the `transcription` field. Max may provide server-side transcription — worth checking if this field is populated for voice messages before building a custom STT path.

## Integration points for a new STT service
1. **Config**: new `[stt]` or `[yandex-stt]` TOML section + `ConfigManager.getSTTConfig()` accessor. Follow the Yandex Search pattern: `[yandex-search]` section in `configs/00-defaults/00-config.toml:146-178`, accessor at `internal/config/manager.py:429-443`. Standard keys: `enabled`, `use-proxy`, `api-key`/`folder-id` (via `${VAR}` env substitution), `request-timeout`, `ratelimiter-queue`.
2. **Client**: standalone client class following `lib/yandex_search/client.py` — ephemeral `httpx.AsyncClient(**proxyConfig.toKwargs(), timeout=...)` per request, never-raise-to-caller (catch all exceptions, return None), `ProxyConfig.fromServiceConfig()` for proxy. See memory 4d6c5139 for the Yandex Search HTTP client pattern. Handler proxy wiring uses `ProxyService.getInstance().resolveProxy(serviceConfig, serviceLabel)` (memory f72e0361).
3. **Pipeline hook**: extend `_processMediaV2` (`base.py:1726-1929`) to transcribe non-image audio. Currently voice/audio are stored and skipped — the STT call would go here, producing text that feeds into the message text for LLM processing.
4. **Auth**: for Yandex SpeechKit, follow the YC SDK auth pattern — API key preferred for daemons (memory 306505be: `auth-type` config key, `YC_API_KEY`/`YC_IAM_TOKEN` env fallbacks). The Yandex SpeechKit STT research (memory 17b7097b) details auth: API key = `Authorization: Api-Key <key>` (service account, long-lived, PREFERRED), IAM token = `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (expires ~12h).

## Constraints for STT design
- **No temp-file convention in bot/AI code.** Media bytes stay in-memory (`bytes`/`bytearray`) throughout the pipeline. No `tmp/` dir, no `tempfile` usage in `internal/`. Tempfile usage exists only in `lib/sandbox/` (Docker workspace) and tests. If the STT API needs file uploads or chunking, there's no existing temp-file pattern — either keep bytes in-memory or introduce one.
- **No ffmpeg anywhere in the repo** (grep for `ffmpeg` in `*.py` returns nothing). Telegram voice messages are OGG/Opus format. Yandex SpeechKit accepts OggOpus directly (memory 17b7097b), so ffmpeg may not be needed for Telegram voice. Video notes would need demuxing.
- **No centralized web-fetch utility** (memory b15834c3): every subsystem creates ad-hoc httpx clients. An STT client would follow the same standalone pattern.
- **No file-size limit guard** in the download path. Telegram `get_file` only works for files <20MB (Telegram API limit). Max downloads are raw HTTP. No size guard before download.
- **Voice/audio already downloaded**: the bytes are already available in-memory via the existing download+store pipeline, so an STT integration can reuse `downloadAttachment` + the stored bytes rather than re-downloading.

## Yandex integration context
Yandex is already integrated in two places (but NOT for STT):
- LLM providers: `yc-openai` (OpenAI-compatible endpoint, `lib/ai/providers/yc_openai_provider.py`), `yc-sdk` (native SDK, `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py`). Config: `configs/00-defaults/providers.toml`.
- Yandex Search API: standalone client `lib/yandex_search/client.py` + handler `internal/bot/common/handlers/yandex_search.py`.
- Env vars: `YC_FOLDER_ID`, `YC_API_KEY`, `YC_IAM_TOKEN`, `YANDEX_SEARCH_API_KEY`, `YANDEX_FOLDER_ID`.
- No `speechkit`, no `stt`, no `recognize` references in the codebase.

title: SpeechKit SDK correction: project uses yandex-ai-studio-sdk, NOT yandex-cloud-ml-sdk
content:
Cross-references and corrects the SDK recommendation (§9) in research memory `17b7097b` (Yandex SpeechKit STT API — integration reference). The research was accurate at the REST/gRPC API level (endpoints, formats, timestamps, auth, limits, pricing — all package-independent and stand). ONLY the SDK-recommendation section is corrected here.

## The discrepancy
The research recommends `yandex-cloud-ml-sdk` (import `yandex_cloud_ml_sdk`, class `YCloudML(folder_id=..., auth=...)`, PyPI "official, current"). This is a REAL but DIFFERENT and OLDER package. **This project does NOT use it and must not add it.**

This project pins and actively uses **`yandex-ai-studio-sdk==0.22.0`** (import `yandex_ai_studio_sdk`, class `AsyncAIStudio(folder_id=..., auth=APIKeyAuth(...))`):
- `requirements.direct.txt:18` → `yandex-ai-studio-sdk==0.22.0`
- `requirements.txt:94` → same pin
- Actively imported in `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py` (lines 53-68) for completions, image generation, function-calling/tools. Uses `AsyncAIStudio`, `AsyncGPTModel`, `AsyncImageGenerationModel`, `AsyncFunctionCall`, `APIKeyAuth`/`IAMTokenAuth`/`YandexCloudCLIAuth` from `yandex_ai_studio_sdk.auth`.

These two packages are NOT the same SDK renamed — they are separate distributions with incompatible APIs (`YCloudML` vs `AsyncAIStudio`). Introducing `yandex-cloud-ml-sdk` would duplicate the Yandex SDK dependency.

## The installed SDK already has full SpeechKit STT support
The `yandex-ai-studio-sdk` ships a `_speechkit/` module exposing both TTS and STT. The STT API surface (audited 2026-07-18 against the installed wheel at `venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/yandex_ai_studio_sdk/_speechkit/`, fully documented in `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/speech.md`):

```python
from yandex_ai_studio_sdk import AsyncAIStudio
from yandex_ai_studio_sdk.auth import APIKeyAuth
from yandex_ai_studio_sdk._speechkit.enums import AudioFormat

sdk = AsyncAIStudio(folder_id="b1g...", auth=APIKeyAuth("..."))
stt = sdk.speechkit.stt(                      # or .speech_to_text(...)
    audio_format=AudioFormat.WAV,             # WAV | MP3 | OGG_OPUS | PCM16(sample_rate_hertz=16000, channels=1)
    language_codes="auto",                    # NOTE underscore codes: ru_RU, en_US, not ru-RU
    speaker_labeling=True,                    # bool, not an enum
)
result = await stt.run(audio_bytes, timeout=60)        # real-time, returns SpeechToTextResult (Sequence over ChannelResult)
async for event in stt.run_stream(audio_bytes): ...    # async GENERATOR (never await — see memories c4ddc735, ba9253ac)
operation = await stt.run_deferred(audio_bytes_or_s3url)  # long audio; await operation for DeferredSpeechToTextResult
await stt.attach_deferred(operation_id="...")
stream = stt.create_bistream(timeout=600)              # bidirectional streaming
# factory-level (NOT model-level): sdk.speechkit.stt.get_recognition_result(operation_id="...")
```

Key SDK facts for the architecture proposal:
- **Execution methods on the model**: `run`, `run_stream`, `run_deferred`, `attach_deferred`, `create_bistream`. `get_recognition_result` is on the speechkit FACTORY (`sdk.speechkit.stt`), NOT the model instance — calling it on a model raises AttributeError.
- **`SpeechToTextConfig` fields** (audio_format REQUIRED): model, language_codes, text_normalization, eou_classifier, recognition_classifiers, speech_analysis, speaker_labeling (bool), llm_post_process.
- **`SpeechToTextResult`** is a `Sequence` over `ChannelResult`; each `ChannelResult.utterances` is a tuple of `Utterance`. For single-channel audio, `result.text` returns joined text. Iterate `for channel in result: for utt in channel.utterances:`.
- **`Utterance`**: `.final_text`, `.final_refinement_text` (None if no refinement events), `.text` (refinement or final). Also `.events`, `.finals`, `.final_refinements`, `.timespan`, `.speaker_analysis`, `.classifiers`.
- **`SpeechToTextStreamingEvent`**: `event_type` (str-enum: partial/final/final_refinement/eou_update/...), fields `partial`/`final` are `Alternatives | None` (NOT bool). Convenience props: `.partial_text`, `.final_text`, `.final_refinement_text`, `.text`.
- **`run_stream` is an async generator in ALL domains** — never `await` it (TypeError). General rule per memory `ba9253ac`.
- **Language codes use UNDERSCORES** in the SDK (`ru_RU`, `en_US`, `auto`) — the REST API uses hyphens (`ru-RU`). Easy to get wrong.

## Current wiring status
SpeechKit (TTS + STT) is **entirely UNWIRED in production** — grep for `speechkit|text_to_speech|speech_to_text|\btts\b|\bstt\b` across `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py` returns ZERO matches. `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/gap-analysis.md` lists both TTS and STT as "Not used / Low priority". So the SDK package is installed but the SpeechKit domain is not yet exercised by any production code path — the architecture proposal would be the first integration.

## Net guidance for the proposal
1. Use the EXISTING `yandex-ai-studio-sdk==0.22.0` and its `sdk.speechkit.stt(...)` API. Do NOT add `yandex-cloud-ml-sdk`.
2. The REST/gRPC-level reference in memory `17b7097b` (endpoints, formats, timestamps, auth, limits, pricing) remains valid and authoritative — that's the wire contract the SDK implements under the hood.
3. For long-audio transcription specifically, `stt.run_deferred(s3_url_or_bytes)` is the SDK entry point (wraps v3 async `recognizeFileAsync`). For per-word timestamps and replica boundaries, the SDK surfaces them via `Utterance.timespan` / `SpeechToTextStreamingEvent.eou_update_ms` and the `final`/`final_refinement` `Alternatives` (which carry the word-level `startTimeMs`/`endTimeMs` from the underlying v3 API).
4. Auth reuses the project's existing `APIKeyAuth`/`IAMTokenAuth` pattern already in `yc_sdk_provider.py` — same credential model as completions.

title: STT feature — design decisions locked-in
content:
Video/voice/audio transcription feature for Gromozeka. Locked-in design decisions from planning session (m0001-m0007):

SCOPE: Video + voice + audio (VIDEO, VIDEO_NOTE, VOICE, AUDIO). Unified pipeline, one chat setting, one provider.

TRIGGER: Chat-setting auto, mirroring PARSE_ATTACHMENTS image-parsing path. New TRANSCRIBE_MEDIA chat setting (BOOL, page=FRIEND, default=false). Runs in _processMediaV2 message preprocessor.

PROVIDER: Yandex SpeechKit v3 async (recognizeFileAsync). Word-level timestamps available (startTimeMs/endTimeMs per word), utterance/replica boundaries via eouUpdate.timeMs.

AUDIO EXTRACTION: PyAV (Python wheel bundling ffmpeg libs, no system install). CPU-bound decode via asyncio.to_thread. Optional-dep guard pattern (_AV_AVAILABLE flag).

DELIVERY: Transcript stored as media_attachments.description column (REUSED — zero schema migration). Auto-injects into LLM message via existing updateMediaContent → formatForLLM path as <media-description>…</media-description>. Format: [HH:MM:SS] utterance per line.

ABSTRACTION: Build lib/stt/ provider registry now (mirrors lib/ai/ shape). AbstractSTTProvider + STTManager + YandexSpeechKitProvider. Reversible — can swap providers later.

HTTP: Raw httpx for Yandex SpeechKit provider (NOT yandex-cloud-ml-sdk). Research flagged SDK STT method surface as underdocumented. Mirrors lib/yandex_search/ pattern (Api-Key header, ProxyConfig.fromServiceConfig, never-raise contract). SDK can be added as alternative provider later.

DEFERRED: Object Storage (>60MB files), speaker diarization, auto-language detection, word confidence scores. v1 is inline-only (≤60MB), ru-RU only, single-speaker.

KEY FILES TO MIRROR:
- lib/yandex_search/client.py (raw httpx + never-raise pattern)
- lib/ai/ + internal/services/llm/ (layering template)
- internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:1316-1367 (_parseImage — template for _transcribeMedia)

content:
Canonical STT feature plan persisted to disk at `docs/plans/media-transcription-stt-v1.md` (1135+ lines, matches the `docs/plans/` convention — header block with Status/Date/Owner/Companion docs, numbered sections, file:line references, Mermaid sequence diagram, decision table, phased implementation, risks).

Memory `db79f4e2` holds the locked-in decisions; the plan doc is the authoritative reference for implementation agents. All design decisions ratified 2026-07-27.

Implementation is NOT started. Awaiting user go-ahead on Phase 1 (Step 1: add `av` dependency; Step 5 research: verify SpeechKit v3 field names against live API). These two can run in parallel — Step 5's research is read-only and informs the provider implementation in Step 5-build.

title: PyAV in-memory STT conversion requires dual flushing
content: For the planned media-to-SpeechKit pipeline, current PyAV supports `av.open(io.BytesIO(...))` for in-memory demuxing and bundled wheels generally avoid a system FFmpeg runtime dependency on supported platforms; source builds still need FFmpeg development libraries. A viable conversion is `AudioResampler(format="s16", layout="mono", rate=16000)`, an output stream `add_stream("pcm_s16le", rate=16000)`, set output layout to `mono`, encode/mux, close the output container, then read `BytesIO.getvalue()`. `AudioResampler.resample()` returns a list of frames. Critical gotcha: flush both stages—call `resampler.resample(None)` after input decoding, then drain encoder packets with `outputStream.encode(None)`—or delayed samples may be truncated. Prefer named layouts (`mono`/`stereo`) rather than numeric channel counts. Wheel behavior is platform/release dependent, so do not claim absolute host determinism.

title: SpeechKit v3 result retrieval is separate streaming response
content: For `recognizeFileAsync`, the operation poll endpoint only reports operation state; after `done=true`, fetch the transcript separately with `GET https://stt.api.cloud.yandex.net/stt/v3/getRecognition?operation_id=...`. Parse recognition event envelopes (`result.final`, optionally `result.finalRefinement.normalizedText`) rather than expecting `operation.response` or a flat `alternatives` array. Timestamp fields are integer millisecond fields: `final.alternatives[].startTimeMs/endTimeMs` and `words[].startTimeMs/endTimeMs`. Do not emit both final and normalized-final text as separate transcript messages. The endpoint is server-streaming and the exact REST framing (NDJSON, concatenated JSON, or another representation) should be verified with a live request before choosing `response.json()`.

title: SpeechKit v3 uses protobuf JSON recognition_model schema
content: The v3 async REST submit contract is camelCase `POST https://stt.api.cloud.yandex.net/stt/v3/recognizeFileAsync`, not the v2-style `:recognize_file_async` path. The JSON body is based on `RecognizeFileRequest`: inline audio is `content` (protobuf bytes represented as base64) or `uri`, with recognition options under `recognition_model` such as `model`, `audio_format.container_audio.container_audio_type`, and `language_restriction` (`WHITELIST`/`BLACKLIST` plus language codes). Do not send v2-like top-level `folderId`, `audioFormat`, `recognizeSpec`, `languageCode`, or `autoLanguage`. Include `x-folder-id` consistently according to the v3 examples, alongside `Authorization: Api-Key ...` or `Bearer ...`.

title: STT pipeline needs bounded admission before media work
content: Validation of docs/plans/media-transcription-stt-v1.md found a resource-safety flaw: the proposed semaphore/rate limiter is acquired only inside STTService.transcribe(), after _processMediaV2 has downloaded the complete source and _transcribeMedia has already run PyAV extraction. Concurrent large videos can therefore cause unbounded download memory, decode CPU, and native-thread pressure before the intended guard. The implementation must enforce source-size limits before/while download, and acquire a bounded global/per-chat admission guard before download/extraction (or place all expensive work inside the bounded unit). Also define decode wall-clock/resource limits; asyncio cancellation does not stop a worker thread/native decoder. Do not rely solely on extracted WAV size limits.

title: STT duplicate delivery requires atomic claim
content: The existing _processMediaV2 flow checks for a media_attachments row and later inserts it; addMediaAttachment() can return False on duplicate but callers do not use that result. For a first-seen duplicate file_unique_id delivered concurrently, both handlers can schedule transcription and incur duplicate SpeechKit billing. A PENDING shortcut only helps after one insert commits. STT integration must add an atomic insert-or-return-existing/status-claim operation, or a keyed lock plus a database claim, and regression-test concurrent first delivery and duplicate-while-PENDING behavior.

title: STT plan state and integration contracts need correction
content: The STT plan validation found several contract mismatches that must be resolved before implementation: RateLimiterManager.applyLimit() blocks and has no rejection result, so a test expecting 'rate-limit hit -> ERROR' is invalid unless a timeout/rejection policy is added; an stt queue mapping must be explicitly configured rather than silently falling back to default. Current media status behavior is PARSE_ATTACHMENTS=false -> DONE, while parsing-enabled non-image rejection can become NEW; tests must not assume all disabled transcription cases become NEW. Persist FAILED on every exception after PENDING, including download/MIME/task-creation failures, or EnsuredMessage._awaitMedia() can poll PENDING for five minutes. The proposed 300-second STT timeout also equals the entire EnsuredMessage media-await budget and leaves no time for download, extraction, queueing, DB updates, or polling; make the operation budget materially smaller or revise the await contract.

title: STT plan has stale ADR and dependency workflow references
content: The media-transcription plan's documentation steps need live-source checks: ADR-014 is already assigned and architecture ADRs extend through ADR-019, so the next new ADR should be allocated at implementation time (currently ADR-020, if no intervening change). The singleton table already lists seven singleton-style services (including Proxy and Sandbox), so adding STT makes eight rather than six. Dependency workflow must distinguish make install (frozen requirements.txt) from make install-direct, regenerate the frozen lock after pinning av in requirements.direct.txt, and avoid python -c because repository rules prohibit it.

title: STT admission must receive declared media size
content: A review of docs/plans/media-transcription-stt-v1.md found a contract gap distinct from merely placing bounded admission before media work: the plan requires rejecting oversized media before limiters/semaphore, but its loader interface exposes only maxBytes and the actual size after loading. The implementation must carry the platform-declared size (or an equivalent pre-load size signal) into the admission check before limiter/semaphore acquisition; otherwise the required pre-admission rejection cannot be implemented and oversized downloads may still consume resources.

title: Media attachment updates do not verify row existence
content: The current media attachment repository's updateMediaAttachment() executes the UPDATE but does not check the affected-row count, so it can report success even when fileUniqueId matches no row. Any STT/media state machine that relies on update success must either make the repository return failure for zero matches or explicitly verify the row/claim before treating a transition as persisted; otherwise missing or concurrently changed records can be silently misclassified.

title: Max attachment downloads are currently unbounded
content: lib/max_bot/client.py's downloadAttachmentPayload() performs an HTTP GET and returns the full response.content without a byte cap or streaming enforcement. Adding media/STT limits only after this call cannot protect memory or bandwidth; the platform adapter (and corresponding Telegram download path) must enforce the maximum before or while buffering the payload, with regression tests for oversized responses.

title: Max STT dispatch omits voice and video notes
content: Validation of docs/plans/media-transcription-stt-v1.md against current code found the plan's claim that all four STT media types already flow through `_processMediaV2` is too broad. Telegram dispatches VIDEO, VIDEO_NOTE, AUDIO, and VOICE in `internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:1548-1587`, but Max dispatch currently handles only VIDEO and AUDIO at `internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:1678-1707`. A bounded STT implementation must explicitly extend Max routing for VOICE and VIDEO_NOTE (or document the intentional scope), rather than assuming the shared downstream path receives them.

title: TEXT media injection misses Max multi-attachments
content: `EnsuredMessage` has asymmetric media-description injection: JSON formatting falls back to `mediaList`, but TEXT formatting emits the `<media-description>` block only when `self.mediaContent` is set (`internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:1110-1114, 1158-1185`). Max preprocessing deliberately calls `addMediaProcessingInfo(..., setMediaId=False)` for each attachment (`internal/bot/common/handlers/message_preprocessor.py:168-170`), so multi-attachment Max messages can have descriptions in the list while `mediaContent` remains unset and TEXT output omits them. Any STT result injection must populate the field/path consumed by both output formats or add a regression test for Max multi-media TEXT rendering.

title: Media await path is not uniformly bounded
content: `MediaProcessingInfo.awaitResult()` directly awaits its task (`internal/bot/models/media.py:39-51`). The database polling/timeout logic is in `EnsuredMessage.updateMediaContent()` (`internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:984-998, 1025-1061`) and occurs after the task await. Therefore an STT worker must not be attached to the existing `MediaProcessingInfo.task` if the plan relies on the DB timeout to bound work; use a separately managed background task or enforce cancellation/timeout before the direct await contract is reached.

title: STT plan schema docs show stale metadata default
content: During plan validation, `docs/database-schema-llm.md:175-188` was found to document `media_attachments.metadata TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, while the actual post-migration schema in `internal/database/migrations/versions/migration_013_remove_timestamp_defaults.py:268-280` has no default. For STT/media schema work, treat migration code as authoritative and update both schema documentation files together if the schema contract changes.

title: STT lifecycle must register workers with QueueService
content: Source validation for docs/plans/media-transcription-stt-v1.md confirmed a load-bearing shutdown contract: QueueService drains only tasks registered through addBackgroundTask(), and its DO_EXIT handler waits for the tracked backgroundTasks set. Therefore every STT worker must be registered before it can be considered drainable; merely using an internal asyncio task/semaphore does not keep the STT HTTP client alive through shutdown. Recommended lifecycle placement is: start scheduler before ProxyService initialization so DO_EXIT handlers register in order (queue drain first, proxy stop second), initialize STT after RateLimiterManager.loadConfig() (current main.py also initializes LLMManager in between proxy and rate limiters), and close STT after queue/background-task drain but before rate limiters and database are destroyed. Evidence: main.py:60-100,121-155; internal/services/queue_service/service.py:152-179,194-223,224-257,370-393.

title: STT media completion needs a placeholder task
content: The existing media wait path has two distinct mechanisms: MediaProcessingInfo.awaitResult() directly awaits its task with no timeout, while EnsuredMessage._awaitMedia() performs bounded database polling (300 seconds). An STT implementation must attach a short/completed placeholder task to MediaProcessingInfo and let the actual worker update the media row, rather than attaching the long-running STT worker itself; otherwise awaitResult() bypasses the intended bounded polling and can wait indefinitely. Evidence: internal/bot/models/media.py:39-51 and internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:1011-1061.

title: STT source-loader API must evolve for bounded acquisition
content: The current TheBot.downloadAttachment() contract returns only Optional[bytes] after materializing the complete Telegram download, and Max downloadAttachmentPayload() returns full response.content. A safe STT source loader cannot enforce declared size limits merely by passing maxBytes after this call: it needs a compatibility-designed bounded/probing API, such as a keyword-only maxBytes plus a richer result carrying declared/observed size, or a separate metadata/streaming path. This is also where platform-specific size enforcement must happen, before PyAV decode, semaphore admission, or rate limiting. Evidence: internal/bot/common/bot.py:1018-1040; lib/max_bot/client.py:1675-1723.

title: STT tests need local singleton cleanup and new media-state coverage
content: For STT implementation tests, only LLMService, ProxyService, and ProxyHelper are reset by the global autouse fixtures. QueueService, StorageService, and RateLimiterManager retain singleton state unless each test module provides explicit cleanup/reset fixtures. Existing precedents are tests/services/queue_service/test_queue_service.py:25-37 and tests/services/storage/test_integration.py:17-22. Also, current tests cover media repository operations/integration but do not directly exercise _processMediaV2 state transitions, so real-DB media state/race tests proposed by the STT plan are new focused coverage rather than extensions of an existing handler-state suite.

title: Media pipeline lacks dedicated integration coverage
content: The STT plan review found no existing dedicated tests for the core media pipeline: `_processMediaV2`, platform attachment download, or `MediaProcessingInfo` integration. Existing `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_base.py` primarily covers unrelated inherited handler behavior, while `tests/database/test_db_wrapper.py` only exercises basic media CRUD (`media` around lines 847-898). STT integration must therefore add explicit media-handler tests rather than assuming current media coverage protects routing, bounded loaders, state transitions, or async lifecycle.

title: S3 backend is synchronous and has no transport timeouts
content: `S3StorageBackend` uses synchronous boto3 calls, including `put_object()` (`internal/services/storage/backends/s3.py:113-135`), despite being invoked from async media code. Its constructor/client setup (`internal/services/storage/backends/s3.py:57-91`) currently has no connect/read timeout or retry configuration, and `configs/00-defaults/storage.toml:8-28` has no such keys. Media/STT storage work must either move these calls off the event loop and add explicit transport settings, with tests updating both `tests/services/storage/test_s3_backend.py` (exact boto3 kwargs) and `tests/services/storage/test_service.py` (config-to-constructor forwarding).

title: STT shutdown ordering preserves dependencies
content: For STT lifecycle integration, initialize the STT service after RateLimiterManager.loadConfig() (the current main.py sequence has LLM setup between ProxyService and rate-limit loading). On shutdown, close STT only after QueueService has drained tracked background tasks, but before rate limiters and the database are destroyed. QueueService's DO_EXIT drain must remain registered before dependent service stop handlers so STT workers can still use proxy/rate-limit/database resources while draining. STT startup must not require StorageService: storage is initialized later when HandlersManager is constructed, so handler-supplied loaders should access storage only at dispatch time.

title: STT request must carry complete row seed
content: The reviewed STT plan's STTMediaRequest description (media/chat IDs, size, loader) is insufficient if STTService owns the media_attachments race/claim row. The service needs immutable row-seed data such as fileId, mediaType, file metadata/size, and prompt (or must explicitly keep row creation in the handler). Prefer service-owned creation with the complete seed because the service owns deduplication and verified state transitions; otherwise the request contract leaves the service unable to create the required attachment record.

title: Split STT formatter and provider event parser
content: The implementation plan's file tree omitted a formatter despite requiring deterministic bounded transcript formatting, and placing Yandex SpeechKit event parsing directly in the provider would make the high-risk wire parser hard to isolate. Keep a dedicated lib/stt/formatter.py and preferably lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py so formatting and event-envelope parsing can be unit-tested independently and adjusted after live-wire validation without expanding the HTTP provider's responsibilities.

title: Separate STT code-complete from release-ready
content: The STT plan contradicted itself by calling §13.3 manual smoke tests release gates while §16 said implementation is complete only after those gates. Use two milestones: code-complete means automated tests/format/lint/full test pass with STT still default-off (P0–P16); release-ready means live SpeechKit wire/model, Max media, latency/RSS, graceful native-decoder shutdown, and Alpine/clean-install gates pass, with any corrections merged and docs/changelog synchronized. Manual runtime gates block release/enabling STT, not completion of the safely default-off code.

title: lib/stt extraction spec at docs/plans/lib-stt-v1.md
content:
A focused, self-contained, implementation-ready spec for the `lib/stt/` portion of the STT feature was extracted to `docs/plans/lib-stt-v1.md` (2026-07-31). It is a documentation-extraction task only — NO source code, no STT behavior added; a companion to and extracted from the parent plan `docs/plans/media-transcription-stt-v1.md` (which remains authoritative, ratifying D1–D8).

Status: REVIEWED — implementation-ready (inherits parent's status). This doc is meant to be the single focus artifact for implementing `lib/stt` (parent impl steps 2 and 3) — a developer should be able to build all modules from this doc alone.

It pins SIX load-bearing contracts explicitly (these are the "clarification" value beyond the parent plan):
1. Dependency firewall (two seams): (a) proxy is INJECTED into the provider constructor as an already-resolved ProxyConfig — lib/stt never calls ProxyConfig.fromServiceConfig(); (b) the media loader is a typed async callable passed in by STTService; its result type lives in models.py. lib/stt imports NO internal.bot/internal.database/singleton-service. Sibling bot-free libs (lib/ai, lib/rate_limiter, lib/markdown, lib/yandex_search, lib/openweathermap) are precedent.
2. Raise contract: providers' transcribe() returns TranscriptionResult (incl. ERROR) and NEVER raises for expected failures; the ONLY runtime raise-point in lib/stt is audio.extractAudio() raising typed exceptions that map 1:1 to STTErrorCode (caught by downstream service → FAILED); constructors MAY raise on startup config validation when STT enabled.
3. Caps ownership: lib/stt modules RECEIVE caps as params (never read [stt] config). audio.py enforces source-byte recheck + decoded-duration + incremental WAV-output growth DURING decode; yandex_events.py enforces result-body cap; formatter.py applies transcript-char cap. The §8.1 limits table is carried over and annotated row-by-row as "enforced in lib/stt module X" vs "STTService-owned / never reaches lib/stt".
4. Live-wire known-unknown: the getRecognition transport framing/content-type is PROVISIONAL (parent §9.3 + §13.3 gate-1). yandex_events.py is "implemented per the provisional streaming-JSON spec; verified/adjusted by the parent §13.3 gate-1 smoke test before release." Warned against over-committing parser shape in golden tests before that gate.
5. Formatter purity: pure function TranscriptionResult -> str; cap is a PARAMETER; header is a CONSTANT; deterministic head/tail truncation fully specified.
6. PyAV guarded import: exact AGENTS.md pattern (module-level try/except ImportError + private _AVAILABLE flag; NO PEP 695 type alias; NO dummy stub class in except branch). Missing-PyAV-while-STT-enabled = startup error; module imports fine without PyAV when STT disabled.

Module layout = 10 files (the task brief said "9 files" but its enumerated list contained 10, and the acceptance criteria require both isolated modules; the "9" is a miscount): __init__.py, abstract.py, audio.py, exceptions.py, formatter.py, manager.py, models.py, providers/__init__.py, providers/yandex_speechkit.py, providers/yandex_events.py. The last two isolated files (formatter.py, yandex_events.py) come from readiness correction #2 (already in memory 1d4f543b).

Corrections handled: #2 (isolate formatter.py + yandex_events.py) — reflected in layout; #1 (STTService-side immutable row-seed fields; loader-result type carries actual fileSize + detected mimeType so service can update row metadata) — noted as downstream/integration-doc; #3 (TEXT media rendering uses pre-computed multi-attachment content) — downstream/integration-doc.

Clarifying choices made where the parent was ambiguous (flagged in the prose summary): the no-speech sentinel `[No speech detected]` is returned by the formatter with NO untrusted-data header (parent §10 says "store exactly"); the truncation marker embeds N so len(output)==cap exactly requires resolving a small fixed-point (N digit width); corrupt/truncated + decoder/muxer failures map to PROVIDER_ERROR via AudioDecodeError/EncoderError.

Dependency note: PyAV `av==18.0.0` must be added under `# Runtime` in requirements.direct.txt and requirements.txt regenerated via freeze workflow (documented only, not performed).

title: Proxy injection seam: resolve in service, inject into lib client constructor
content:
Two distinct proxy-wiring patterns exist for lib-level HTTP clients, and the choice matters because of per-service proxy lifecycle registration:

PATTERN A — "resolve inside lib" (used by AI providers): the lib calls `ProxyConfig.fromServiceConfig(providerConfig).toKwargs()` itself and spreads the result into a per-request or persistent `httpx.AsyncClient`. Example: `lib/ai/providers/basic_openai_provider.py` (~line 908, and the `_proxyHttpClient` field). See memory 10a28aa1.

PATTERN B — "service resolves, lib receives injected" (REQUIRED for lib/stt; the cleaner pattern for any lib client owned by a singleton internal service): the internal service calls `ProxyService.resolveProxy(serviceConfig, serviceLabel)` which returns a resolved `ProxyConfig` AND registers the per-service proxy lifecycle, then passes that ProxyConfig into the lib client's constructor. The lib stores it (e.g. `self._proxyConfig`) and spreads `self._proxyConfig.toKwargs()` into `httpx.AsyncClient` at request time. It NEVER calls `fromServiceConfig()` itself. Clean existing examples: `lib/yandex_search/client.py` (stores `self._proxyConfig`, line ~182; spreads `toKwargs()` line ~363), `lib/openweathermap/client.py` (line ~473), and `lib/max_bot/client.py._getHttpClient()` (memory 182ba59e).

WHY IT MATTERS: `ProxyConfig.fromServiceConfig()` bypasses per-service proxy lifecycle registration. The lifecycle registration happens inside `ProxyService.resolveProxy()` (`internal/services/proxy/service.py`, the `resolveProxy(serviceConfig, serviceLabel)` method — see memory 24c90899). So a lib that calls `fromServiceConfig()` directly gets a proxy that is not registered for health-check/CRON/shutdown lifecycle management by ProxyService.

RULE OF THUMB: if the lib client is instantiated by and owned by a singleton internal service (like STTService owning YandexSpeechKitProvider), use Pattern B — the service resolves via `ProxyService.resolveProxy(...)` and injects the resolved ProxyConfig into the lib constructor. The lib/stt dependency firewall explicitly forbids `fromServiceConfig()` inside lib/stt (parent plan §9.2, now pinned in lib-stt-v1.md §1 contract 1).

`ProxyConfig.toKwargs()` returns a `ProxyKwargs` TypedDict that spreads safely into `httpx.AsyncClient(**kwargs)` — empty dict when proxy type is NONE (so `toKwargs()` is a no-op and safe to always spread). It also accepts an optional `verify: Optional[ssl.SSLContext]` kwarg for SOCKS5 SSL (memory aa1b8899).

title: Prior STT implementation source removed — only .pyc artifacts remain
content:
As of 2026-07-31, the `lib/stt/` and `internal/services/stt/` directories contain ONLY compiled `.pyc` artifacts under `__pycache__/` (e.g. `lib/stt/__pycache__/models.cpython-314.pyc`, `audio.cpython-314.pyc`, `manager.cpython-314.pyc`, `abstract`, `exceptions`, `__init__`; and `internal/services/stt/__pycache__/__init__`, `types`, `service`) — but NO `.py` source files exist for these modules.

This means the prior STT implementation (the phased P0–P16 build referenced across many existing STT memories — e.g. P2 `lib/stt/audio.py extractAudio()` API in memory 00b8f821, the formatter marker digit-boundary bug in `lib/stt/formatter.py` memory 6ed22f4e, P3 manager tests, P8b registry lifecycle) was REMOVED from the source tree. Those memories describe code, line numbers, and bug fixes that NO LONGER EXIST on disk.

IMPLICATIONS for future agents:
- Do not expect to find `lib/stt/*.py` or `internal/services/stt/*.py` — they are gone. Reading those memories will describe a prior implementation that must be rebuilt.
- The fresh, authoritative spec to rebuild `lib/stt` from is `docs/plans/lib-stt-v1.md` (the extraction doc), NOT the stale .pyc bytecode.
- The .pyc files are cpython-314 (Python 3.14), while the project targets py312 — likely from a different/dev environment; do not treat them as authoritative for either API or Python version.
- The stale .pyc files can be safely deleted (`rm -rf lib/stt/__pycache__ internal/services/stt/__pycache__`); they are build leftovers, not a source of truth.
- Existing STT memories with concrete code/line references are still conceptually valid (the design decisions, bugs, and contracts they capture) but their file/line pointers are stale until the code is rebuilt.
