Authoritative source: docs/design/stt-v1.1.md (supersedes any stale session-analyser memories about service-layer/threshold-in-service/callables).

title: STT v1.1 Object Storage routing — co-located helper design
content: Gate-3 of STT v1.1 uses a co-located Yandex-specific Object Storage helper (`lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py`) that lives in `lib/stt` (not a service-layer client), is constructed by `YandexSpeechKitProvider.__init__` when `object-storage-bucket` is configured, and is used directly by the provider. The boto3 dependency is imported with a module-level guarded try/except ImportError pattern setting `_BOTO3_AVAILABLE`, following AGENTS.md optional-dependency convention (like `_HTTPX_SOCKS_AVAILABLE`). Runtime behavior: when `object-storage-bucket` is set but `_BOTO3_AVAILABLE` is False, the provider raises ValueError at construction (misconfiguration, not silent inline-only fallback). Config keys are flat in `[stt]` section, not nested. Auth uses one SA with both SpeechKit api-key and static access keys for S3 (different credential types). TTL is delegated to Yandex Object Storage native bucket lifecycle (recommended 86400s/24h), no bot sweep.

title: kebabToCamelCase spread in STTService leaks stats-enabled to provider
content: In `internal/services/stt/service.py:201-208`, the `kebabToCamelCase` spread forwards all `[stt]` config keys to the provider constructor EXCEPT for `("enabled", "use-proxy", "proxy-config", "provider")`. The new `stats-enabled` key (added in STT v1.1) is NOT in this exclusion tuple, so it would be forwarded to the provider as an unexpected `statsEnabled` kwarg, causing TypeError. The provider expects `statsStorage` (a StatsStorage object), not `statsEnabled` (the bool). Fix: add `"stats-enabled"` to the exclusion tuple at line 206.

title: STT operation budget drift: config 2400s vs parent docs 180s
content: The actual `configs/00-defaults/stt.toml:16` ships `operation-budget-seconds = 2400`, but parent docs still say 180s: `lib-stt-v1.md` §7.4 (line 714), §10 inherited-limits table (line 923), and `media-transcription-stt-v1.md` §8.1 (line 414). The v1 rationale was "180s preserves part of the 300-second media-poll budget". This is a doc drift: config is authoritative at 2400s, parent docs need reconciliation. When updating docs, check that budget figures align with actual config defaults.

title: STT stats recording must wrap both success and ERROR paths
content: In STT v1.1 gate-4, `YandexSpeechKitProvider._recordStats()` (mirroring lib/ai pattern) must record on BOTH the success TranscriptionResult AND every ERROR result (OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR, SOURCE_TOO_LARGE, etc.). The implementation must build `result` first (success or ERROR), run finally cleanup, then record stats, then return. Early `return ERROR(...)` in except blocks would skip stats. The design doc pseudocode in §4.3 is illustrative (shows early returns) and omits stats for clarity; the contract is clarified in the lifecycle rules bullet and §7 sequence diagram.

title: lib-stt-v1.md has no §8.1; vendor caps are in unnumbered §10 table
content: `docs/design/lib-stt-v1.md` has NO numbered §8.1 section. The vendor ceiling + conservative defaults content is in an unnumbered subsection under §10: "### Inherited limits table (parent §8.1), annotated by cap-ownership" at line 905. Cross-references from other docs to "lib-stt-v1.md §8.1" are broken; point to `media-transcription-stt-v1.md §8.1` (which actually exists at line 399) or to `lib-stt-v1.md §10 inherited-limits table`.

title: Design doc revision notes: trim to one-liners, avoid defensive prose
content: When iterating design docs, trim revision-note blockquotes to at most a one-liner: "Earlier revisions considered X, rejected because Y — see §12 for full analysis." Remove defensive triple-negative prose ("no service-layer client, no injected callables, no firewall tension") and instead state the positive design choice with a pointer to the alternatives section. This reduces residual complexity from iterative revisions. Rejected alternative names (e.g., STTObjectStorage, uploadFn/deleteFn) only belong in the §12 alternatives table, not in the main body.

title: Documentation gate verification workflow for doc-only changes
content:
When architects revise documentation without shell access, the gate verification process requires running two commands from repo root:

1. `make check-docs` — validates markdown links (must report 0 broken links)
2. `make format lint` — ensures code hygiene (must report 0/0/0 on flake8/isort/pyright)

If broken links are found, fix them only in `*.md` files (never source/config/test files), then re-run `make check-docs` until clean. Common failure modes include:
- `[text](path)` referencing a non-existent file
- `:line-range` suffix leaking into href (the `:NN` is a file:line ref convention, not part of the path)

This workflow was used for `docs/design/stt-v1.1.md` revisions where the architect had no shell access and needed an authoritative gate-verification pass.

title: stt-v1.1 design doc link target renamed: lib-stt-v1.md → media-transcription-stt-v1.md
content: The STT v1.1 design doc (`docs/design/stt-v1.1.md`) uses `media-transcription-stt-v1.md` as the link target for the parent v1 plan (e.g., at §4.1), not `lib-stt-v1.md`. The architect noted this as a link-target change from earlier drafts. All references should point to `media-transcription-stt-v1.md`, which is the canonical STT feature plan location in `docs/plans/`.

title: Non-existent provider paths in stt-v1.1 doc must be code spans only
content: In `docs/design/stt-v1.1.md`, the not-yet-existent path `lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py` must appear as a code span (wrapped in backticks like `` `lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py` ``) everywhere in the document, never as a markdown link (`[text](path)`). This convention prevents `make check-docs` from flagging broken links to files that don't exist yet. The document contains 5 occurrences of this path, all correctly formatted as code spans.

title: StrEnum member docstrings are source-only, not accessible at runtime
content:
When using Python's `enum.StrEnum` (or any enum), accessing `member.__doc__` returns the **class** docstring, not the per-member docstring written after the `= "value"` line. The per-member docstrings exist only in source code and are not accessible at runtime through the member object.

For example, with:
```python
class STTErrorCode(StrEnum):
    """Class docstring."""
    PROVIDER_ERROR = "provider-error"
        """This docstring is source-only."""
```

Accessing `STTErrorCode.PROVIDER_ERROR.__doc__` returns `"Class docstring."`, not `"This docstring is source-only."`.

**Testing implication**: To verify per-member documentation, either:
1. Test against the class docstring (which should mention all members and their roles), OR
2. Use `inspect.getsource()` to read the source file and parse per-member docstrings directly.

This was discovered 2026-08-05 during STT v1.1 Phase 1 implementation (adding `OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR` member) when tests tried to assert `STTErrorCode.OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR.__doc__` mentioned "upload" — the assertion failed because `__doc__` returned the class docstring, not the member docstring.

title: Guarded import constants must stay inside the try block
content:
When using the AGENTS.md pattern for optional dependencies — module-level `try/except ImportError` setting an `_AVAILABLE` flag — any **module-level code that references the imported symbols must also be inside the `try` block**.

Example of the WRONG pattern (causes NameError at import time when boto3 is absent):
```python
try:
    import boto3
    from botocore.config import Config as BotocoreConfig
    _BOTO3_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    _BOTO3_AVAILABLE = False

# WRONG: This runs even when the import fails, causing NameError: name 'BotocoreConfig' is not defined
_STT_S3_CONFIG = BotocoreConfig(connect_timeout=5, read_timeout=30, retries={"max_attempts": 3})
```

The CORRECT pattern:
```python
try:
    import boto3
    from botocore.config import Config as BotocoreConfig
    _BOTO3_AVAILABLE = True
    
    # Module constants that use the optional symbols must be inside the try block
    _STT_S3_CONFIG = BotocoreConfig(connect_timeout=5, read_timeout=30, retries={"max_attempts": 3})
except ImportError:
    _BOTO3_AVAILABLE = False
```

This is critical because the whole point of the guarded import is that **the module imports cleanly** when the optional dependency is absent. If `_STT_S3_CONFIG` is defined outside the `try`, the import fails with `NameError` even though the module never actually uses boto3 (e.g., in test environments).

Discovered 2026-08-05 during STT v1.1 Phase 1 when `yandex_object_storage.py` failed to import in the guarded-import test — the test mocked boto3 as unavailable, but `_STT_S3_CONFIG = BotocoreConfig(...)` was still evaluated at module level.

title: Testing guarded imports: mock sys.modules with ImportError stubs
content:
To properly test that a module with guarded optional imports loads cleanly when the dependency is absent, simply removing the dependency from `sys.modules` is insufficient — Python will re-import it from the filesystem.

**The correct approach**: Manipulate `sys.modules` to inject stubs that raise `ImportError` when accessed, so the module's `try/except ImportError` takes the `except` branch.

Example test pattern:
```python
import sys
import types

class _ImportErrorStub(types.ModuleType):
    """Stub module that raises ImportError on any attribute access."""
    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Never:
        raise ImportError(f"Mocked unavailable: {name}")

# Save parent package modules to restore later
savedParentMods: dict[str, ModuleType | None] = {}
for pkg in ("boto3", "botocore", "botocore.config", "botocore.exceptions"):
    if pkg in sys.modules:
        savedParentMods[pkg] = sys.modules.pop(pkg)

# Inject stubs
for pkg in ("boto3", "botocore", "botocore.config", "botocore.exceptions"):
    sys.modules[pkg] = _ImportErrorStub(pkg)

try:
    # Now import the module under test — it should take the except branch
    from lib.stt.providers import yandex_object_storage
    assert not yandex_object_storage._BOTO3_AVAILABLE
finally:
    # Restore original modules
    for pkg, original in savedParentMods.items():
        if original is None:
            sys.modules.pop(pkg, None)
        else:
            sys.modules[pkg] = original
```

Key points:
- Also remove/restore **parent package modules** (`boto3`, `botocore`) — Python's import machinery may find cached parent packages.
- The stub must be a `types.ModuleType` subclass that raises on `__getattr__`, not just `None`.
- Restore original modules in a `finally` block to avoid polluting other tests.

Discovered 2026-08-05 during STT v1.1 Phase 1 when `testModuleImportsCleanlyWhenBoto3Unavailable` initially failed — removing from `sys.modules` didn't work because `importlib.import_module` found boto3 on the filesystem.

title: Yandex Object Storage helper URI scheme is HTTPS-based pending smoke test
content:
The `lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py` helper's `upload()` method returns a URI of the form `https://storage.yandexcloud.net/{bucket}/{key}` for SpeechKit to consume.

This URI scheme choice is documented as **smoke-pending** per design §11 item 1 — the SpeechKit API documentation is unconfirmed on whether it accepts HTTPS URIs or requires `s3://`-scheme URIs. The chosen HTTPS scheme was reasoned as "sensible default" but must be validated in smoke testing (Phase 3+).

Key implementation details:
- Endpoint constant: `_YANDEX_OS_ENDPOINT = "https://storage.yandexcloud.net"`
- Region constant: `_YANDEX_OS_REGION = "ru-central1"`
- `upload()` generates key as `{prefix}{uuid4}` (default prefix `"stt/"`)
- `delete()` recovers key from the URI to perform `delete_object(Bucket=..., Key=...)`
- Both methods raise on infrastructure failure; `delete()` no-ops on `NoSuchKey`/404

The `YandexObjectStorage` helper is a pure library module (under `lib/stt/providers/`) with zero `internal.*` imports, maintaining the dependency firewall. Discovered 2026-08-05 during STT v1.1 Phase 1 implementation.

title: STT Phase 1 async/sync gotcha: boto3 calls must use asyncio.to_thread
content: Blocking sync boto3 calls (put_object, delete_object) inside async def methods block the event loop for up to the configured read_timeout (30s). In async single-process apps like Gromozeka, this stalls every handler/share during upload/delete. The fix: offload via asyncio.to_thread(self._client.put_object, ...) and asyncio.to_thread(self._client.delete_object, ...). This pattern was missing in the initial Phase 1 implementation and flagged as MAJOR in Gate-1 review (lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py). Unlike internal/services/storage/backends/s3.py (which is synchronous and called from sync contexts), the STT helper is called from async transcribe() paths.

title: aclose naming trap in async cleanup chains
content: The `aclose()` method name (with `a` prefix) is Python's async convention for cleanup (PEP 532). When STTService.aclose is `async def` and calls `await self._provider.aclose()`, and the provider's `aclose` is also `async def`, developers naturally mirror this pattern for helper objects like YandexObjectStorage. If the helper's `aclose` is actually `def` (sync), writing `await self._objectStorage.aclose()` will fail: TypeError: object NoneType can't be used in 'await' expression. This is a forward-looking trap that will manifest in Phase 2. Either make helper.aclose truly async (async def aclose: await asyncio.to_thread(self._client.close)) or rename to close() to be honest about its sync nature. Found in lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py Phase 1 review.

title: Guarded import constants must stay inside try block
content: When guarding optional imports with try/except ImportError (AGENTS.md pattern), module-level constants that reference the imported types must be defined INSIDE the try block, not at module level. Example: _STT_S3_CONFIG = BotocoreConfig(...) must be inside try where BotocoreConfig is imported. If placed outside, when the optional dependency is absent, the NameError occurs at import time (BotocoreConfig not defined). This is the correct approach, not a deviation. Verified in lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py Phase 1 review.

title: StrEnum member docstrings are source-only, not accessible at runtime
content: Python's StrEnum (and enums in general) have Member.__doc__ return the CLASS docstring, not per-member docstrings from source. Per-member docstrings are purely documentation in source code and cannot be introspected at runtime. Testing enum member docstrings requires asserting against the CLASS docstring (which IS runtime-accessible), not individual members. This is why the STT Phase 1 enum tests assert against STTErrorCode.__doc__ (the class docstring). Source-level per-member docs like OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR's docstring cannot be tested via runtime introspection. Found in lib/stt/models.py Phase 1 review.

title: Thread offload regression test: prove asyncio.to_thread via threading.current_thread() capture
content:
Testing pattern to prove that blocking third-party I/O is genuinely offloaded to a worker thread via `asyncio.to_thread()` (not run on the event-loop thread). 

**Pattern:**
```python
import threading

async def testUploadOffloadsBoto3ToWorkerThread(self, ...):
    mainThread = threading.current_thread()
    capturedThread = []

    def fakePutObject(**kwargs):
        capturedThread.append(threading.current_thread())
    
    mockS3Client.put_object.side_effect = fakePutObject
    await helper.upload(b"data")
    
    assert capturedThread and capturedThread[0] is not mainThread
```

**Why this matters:**
- Guards against accidental removal of `asyncio.to_thread()` wrapper
- Proves the contract is actually enforced (work runs in a different thread)
- The test MUST FAIL if `to_thread` is removed — this is the litmus test

**Use case:** 
STT Phase 1 Gate-1 fix for YandexObjectStorage, where boto3's synchronous `put_object()`/`delete_object()` must be offloaded to avoid blocking the event loop for up to 30s (`read_timeout`).

**Reference implementation:**
`tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_object_storage.py` — class `TestOffload` with methods `testUploadOffloadsBoto3ToWorkerThread` and `testDeleteOffloadsBoto3ToWorkerThread`.

title: URI validation pattern: explicit ValueError guard for better error messages
content:
Error-handling pattern for methods that recover structured data from URIs/strings: replace opaque `IndexError` from slice access with an explicit `ValueError` containing a clear diagnostic message.

**Before (opaque error):**
```python
key = uri.split(f"/{self._bucket}/", 1)[1]
# If URI is malformed, raises: IndexError: list index out of range
```

**After (clear error):**
```python
parts = uri.split(f"/{self._bucket}/", 1)
if len(parts) != 2:
    raise ValueError(f"Not an upload URI: {uri!r}")
key = parts[1]
```

**Benefits:**
- Self-documenting contract — error message explains what was expected
- Faster debugging — caller knows immediately they passed wrong input
- Consistent with AGENTS.md requirement: docstring must document `Raises: ValueError`

**Use case:**
`YandexObjectStorage.delete()` recovers the key from `upload()`'s output URI (`https://storage.yandexcloud.net/{bucket}/{key}`). The contract is that `delete` is only called with `upload`'s output, but an explicit error is clearer than `IndexError` if violated.

**Implementation:**
`lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py` lines 141-143; docstring updated with `Raises: ValueError`. Test: `testDeleteRaisesValueErrorOnMalformedUri`.

title: Defensive test pattern: assert_not_called to lock in early-out exception ordering
content:
When testing code that raises an exception before making external calls (e.g., `ValueError` on malformed input before boto3 S3 operations), use `mock.assert_not_called()` as a defensive assertion to lock in the early-out ordering. This prevents a future refactor from silently moving the validation after the network call.

Example from `testDeleteRaisesValueErrorOnMalformedUri`:
```python
with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Not an upload URI"):
    await storage.delete("https://example.com/no-bucket-here/key")
# Defensive: ensure no boto3 call was made
mockS3Client.delete_object.assert_not_called()
```

This double-checks that the exception is raised BEFORE any boto3 call, not just that the correct exception type is eventually raised.

title: STT v1.1 Phase 2 scope: provider construction wiring only
content:
STT v1.1 Phase 2 (gate-3 Object Storage routing) implements ONLY provider construction wiring, not the actual routing logic. The scope includes:

**In scope:**
- Add 5 new keyword params to `YandexSpeechKitProvider.__init__` with backward-compatible defaults: `maxInlineBytes`, `objectStorageBucket`, `objectStoragePrefix`, `objectStorageKeyId`, `objectStorageKeySecret`
- Validate Object Storage configuration (all-or-nothing, ${...} placeholder rejection, boto3 presence, maxInlineBytes range)
- Construct `self._objectStorage: Optional[YandexObjectStorage]` when bucket is set
- Store `self._maxInlineBytes: int`
- Extend `aclose()` to close the helper when present

**Out of scope:**
- `transcribe()` body or `_buildSubmitBody` (Phase 3 wires content-vs-uri + lifecycle)
- `_recordStats` / `consumerId` / `statsStorage` (Phase 4)
- `internal/services/stt/service.py` / `configs/00-defaults/stt.toml` / `main.py` (Phase 5)

Reference: `docs/design/stt-v1.1.md` §3.1 (helper + provider construction), §6.1 (config keys), §6.3 (validation rules)

title: STT v1.1 Object Storage all-or-nothing validation rule
content:
YandexSpeechKitProvider enforces all-or-nothing Object Storage configuration in `__init__`:

**Validation rules (design §6.3):**
1. If `objectStorageBucket` is set (non-empty), require BOTH `objectStorageKeyId` AND `objectStorageKeySecret` (both non-empty)
2. If `objectStorageBucket` is unset, Object Storage is disabled (inline-only mode)
3. If either key is present without a bucket → reject as partial config (raise `ValueError`)
4. This mirrors the existing validation pattern for `api-key`/`folder-id` (lines 209-237 in `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py`)

**Rationale:** Prevents misconfiguration where large clips would fail opaquely with SOURCE_TOO_LARGE later because only half the Object Storage credentials are present. Explicit rejection at construction time is better than runtime failures.

**Error message example:** `ValueError("objectStorageKeyId and objectStorageKeySecret must both be non-empty when objectStorageBucket is set")`

title: STT v1.1 boto3 availability validation at provider construction
content:
YandexSpeechKitProvider checks boto3 availability at construction time when Object Storage is configured:

**Rule:** If `objectStorageBucket` is set but `_BOTO3_AVAILABLE is False` → raise `ValueError`

**Rationale:** Object Storage explicitly requested but its dependency is absent. This is a misconfiguration, NOT a silent inline-only fallback. If we silently fell back, large clips would fail later with SOURCE_TOO_LARGE (40 MiB → ~53 MB base64 → vendor inline ceiling is 60 MB base64-expanded, but still close to edge). Explicit rejection at construction time prevents opaque runtime failures.

**Implementation:**
- Import `_BOTO3_AVAILABLE` flag from `yandex_object_storage.py` (module-level guarded import)
- Check after validation passes: `if objectStorageBucket is not None and not _BOTO3_AVAILABLE: raise ValueError("boto3 is required for object-storage-bucket but not available")`

**Error message:** `ValueError("boto3 is required for object-storage-bucket but not available")`

title: Test gotcha: boto3 Config object assertion cannot match real Config from import time
content:
When testing boto3 client construction in `YandexObjectStorage`, asserting on the `config` parameter of `boto3.client()` is fragile and will fail. The real `BotocoreConfig` object is constructed at module import time (before the patch), so the mock cannot match against it.

**Problem code pattern:**
```python
mockBoto3.client.assert_called_once_with(
    "s3",
    endpoint_url="https://storage.yandexcloud.net",
    region_name="ru-central1",
    aws_access_key_id="test-key-id",
    aws_secret_access_key="test-key-secret",
    config=Config(
        connect_timeout=5,
        read_timeout=60,
        retries={"max_attempts": 3},
    ),
)
```

This assertion fails with: `AssertionError: Expected call: client(..., config=Config(...))` because the mock cannot match the `Config` object.

**Solution:** Simplify the assertion to not verify the Config object, just check that the call happened with the right positional/keyword args. Or use `ANY` for the config parameter.

**Working pattern:**
```python
call = mockBoto3.client.call_args_list[0]
assert call[0][0] == "s3"  # positional arg 0
assert call[1]["endpoint_url"] == "https://storage.yandexcloud.net"
assert call[1]["region_name"] == "ru-central1"
assert call[1]["aws_access_key_id"] == "test-key-id"
assert call[1]["aws_secret_access_key"] == "test-key-secret"
# Skip checking config entirely, it's constructed at module import time
```

**Reference:** Fixed in `tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_speechkit.py::testObjectStorageHelperConstructedWhenBucketSet`

title: STT v1.1 provider param names must match kebabToCamelCase config keys
content:
STT provider construction parameter names are CRITICAL: they must match the camelCased config keys that result from `STTService.initialize` applying `kebabToCamelCase` to the TOML `[stt]` section.

**Mechanism:**
- Config file uses kebab-case: `object-storage-bucket`, `object-storage-prefix`, `object-storage-key-id`, `object-storage-key-secret`
- `STTService.initialize` (`internal/services/stt/service.py:201-208`) spreads the `[stt]` section via `kebabToCamelCase`
- Provider receives camelCase params: `objectStorageBucket`, `objectStoragePrefix`, `objectStorageKeyId`, `objectStorageKeySecret`

**Naming constraint:** Provider `__init__` params MUST be named exactly as the camelCased config keys. If the provider param is `objectStorageBucket` but the config key is `object-storage-bucket`, the spread will fail to forward the value.

**Examples:**
- `object-storage-bucket` (TOML) → `objectStorageBucket` (provider param)
- `max-inline-bytes` (TOML) → `maxInlineBytes` (provider param)
- `request-timeout-seconds` (TOML) → `requestTimeoutSeconds` (provider param)

**Reference:** Memory 482d2abf covers the test assertion side (assert on camelCall params, not kebab-case keys), but this memory captures the construction naming requirement.

title: boto3 AsyncMock causes RuntimeWarning with asyncio.to_thread
content:
**Gotcha:** When mocking boto3 S3 clients in tests, using `AsyncMock()` for the client produces a `RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'AsyncMockMixin._execute_mock_call' was never awaited` when the code wraps boto3 calls with `asyncio.to_thread()`.

**Root cause:**
- boto3 S3 clients are **synchronous** (not async)
- The `YandexObjectStorage.aclose()` calls `await asyncio.to_thread(self._client.close)` expecting a sync callable
- `AsyncMock.close()` returns a coroutine when called
- `asyncio.to_thread` invokes `close()` in a worker thread, the coroutine is created and discarded → RuntimeWarning

**Fix:** Use `MagicMock()` for boto3 client mocks, not `AsyncMock()`. This correctly models boto3's sync interface and silences the warning.

**Example:**
```python
# Wrong (produces RuntimeWarning):
mockClient = AsyncMock()
mockBoto3.client.return_value = mockClient

# Correct:
from unittest.mock import MagicMock
mockClient = MagicMock()
mockBoto3.client.return_value = mockClient
```

**Context:** Seen in `tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_speechkit.py::testObjectStorageHelperConstructedWhenBucketSet` during Phase 2 STT v1.1 code review.

title: Test false-confidence pattern: error message substring matching
content:
**Testing gotcha:** Parametrized tests that validate error messages by matching substrings can pass for the WRONG REASON when multiple validation paths produce similar messages.

**Example from STT Phase 2:**
- Test case: `{"objectStorageKeyId": "${YC_S3_KEY_ID}"}` with no bucket/keySecret
- Expected: placeholder rejection on keyId
- Actual: partial-config check fires FIRST (keys without bucket), raising "objectStorageKeyId/objectStorageKeySecret set without objectStorageBucket"
- Test passes because `match="objectStorageKeyId"` matches BOTH error messages
- Result: placeholder-rejection branch never exercised → false confidence

**Validation order that caused this:**
1. All-or-nothing check: `osBucket is None and (osKeyId is not None or osKeySecret is not None)` → raises
2. Placeholder check: `${...}` pattern scan → never reached

**Fix strategy:** When testing a specific validation branch, ensure the test case ONLY triggers that path. For the placeholder test:
```python
# Before (tests wrong branch):
({"objectStorageKeyId": "${YC_S3_KEY_ID}"}, "objectStorageKeyId"),

# After (isolates placeholder branch):
(
    {"objectStorageBucket": "b", "objectStorageKeyId": "${YC_S3_KEY_ID}", "objectStorageKeySecret": "s"},
    "objectStorageKeyId",
),
```

**Lesson:** Error message substring matching is fragile. Use teeth-check verification (memory 7ec2e077) or ensure test cases uniquely exercise the intended branch.

**Context:** STT v1.1 Phase 2 code review finding 🟡-1 in `testUnresolvedPlaceholderInOsCredsRejected` case 1.

title: STT v1.1 validation ordering: partial-config/placeholder before boto3
content:
**Validation ordering requirement:** In STT v1.1 `YandexSpeechKitProvider.__init__`, configuration validation errors must fire BEFORE the boto3 availability check so they're not masked by it.

**Required order (per design §6.3):**
1. Numeric limits (including `maxInlineBytes` range: positive AND <= 60_000_000)
2. All-or-nothing OS config: bucket requires both keys; keys without bucket rejected
3. `${...}` placeholder rejection on OS credentials
4. boto3 presence check: `if osBucket is not None and not _BOTO3_AVAILABLE: raise ValueError`

**Why ordering matters:**
If boto3 check runs first, a misconfiguration (e.g., `${BUCKET}` placeholder) would produce "boto3 not installed" instead of "unresolved placeholder in objectStorageBucket" — masking the real issue and confusing the operator.

**Actual implementation (lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py:262-284):**
- Lines 262-263: `maxInlineBytes` validation
- Lines 270-274: All-or-nothing (both directions)
- Lines 276-282: Placeholder sweep
- Line 284: boto3 availability check

**Nuance:** Placeholder check runs AFTER all-or-nothing, so `bucket="${BUCKET}"` + missing keys reports "keys missing" first. Not a spec violation (design requires partial-config/placeholder errors not be masked by boto3 check, which holds), but suboptimal for operator clarity.

**Context:** Phase 2 Gate-1 review confirmed implementation matches design requirements.

title: Empty string to None normalization in config values
content:
**Normalization pattern:** Optional string config parameters are normalized to `None` via `if value else None`, treating both `None` and empty string `""` as unset.

**Example from STT v1.1:**
```python
osBucket = objectStorageBucket if objectStorageBucket else None
osKeyId = objectStorageKeyId if objectStorageKeyId else None
osKeySecret = objectStorageKeySecret if objectStorageKeySecret else None
```

**Effect:**
- `objectStorageBucket=None` → `osBucket=None`
- `objectStorageBucket=""` → `osBucket=None`
- `objectStorageBucket="my-bucket"` → `osBucket="my-bucket"`

**Why:** Empty string is often a user mistake or a TOML placeholder (e.g., `object-storage-bucket = ""` from missing env var substitution). Normalizing to `None` produces consistent "not configured" behavior.

**Testing implication:** Add explicit test for empty-string input to verify normalization holds. Example case:
```python
{"objectStorageBucket": ""} → assert provider._objectStorage is None
```

**Context:** Documented during STT v1.1 Phase 2 review — normalization exists but was untested.

**See also:** Similar pattern exists in webhook secret validation (memory c5bab93c) where empty strings pass placeholder checks but should be handled.

title: Validation error messages: split for distinct rejection reasons
content:
**Convention:** When validation logic has multiple distinct reasons to reject a value, split the error messages so each branch produces a unique, honest message. This improves debugging and enables precise test matching.

**Example from maxInlineBytes validation (STT v1.1 Phase 2):**

Before (conflated message):
```python
if maxInlineBytes <= 0 or maxInlineBytes > 60_000_000:
    raise ValueError("maxInlineBytes must be positive and <= 60000000")
```

After (split messages):
```python
if maxInlineBytes <= 0:
    raise ValueError("maxInlineBytes must be positive")
if maxInlineBytes > 60_000_000:
    raise ValueError("maxInlineBytes must be <= 60000000 (vendor inline ceiling)")
```

**Benefits:**
- Tests can distinguish which validation branch fired via distinct match patterns
- Error messages accurately report the specific problem, not a generic "wrong" state
- Easier to debug which condition triggered rejection

**Testing implication:** Update parametrized tests to match the specific message for each case:
```python
# Before:
@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [-1, 0, 60_000_001])
def testMaxInlineBytesValidation(value):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="must be positive and <= 60000000"):
        YandexSpeechKitProvider(..., maxInlineBytes=value)

# After:
@pytest.mark.parametrize("value,expected_match", [
    (-1, "must be positive"),
    (0, "must be positive"),
    (60_000_001, "must be <= 60000000"),
])
def testMaxInlineBytesValidation(value, expected_match):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=expected_match):
        YandexSpeechKitProvider(..., maxInlineBytes=value)
```

**Context:** Applied in Phase 2 Gate-1 fixes to `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py::validateConfigParam` lines 262-264, resolving 🟡-3 finding.

**Related:** This complements the false-confidence test pattern (memory e26173f7) — split messages reduce the risk of substring matching across branches.

title: STT v1.1 Phase 3: upload-outside-budget design and lifecycle
content:
STT v1.1 Phase 3 implemented the Object Storage routing lifecycle per docs/design/stt-v1.1.md §4.3. Key architectural decisions:

**Upload happens OUTSIDE the operation budget:**
- The `asyncio.timeout(self._operationBudgetSeconds)` context starts AFTER staging is complete
- Upload is "preparation work," not a SpeechKit operation step
- Upload failures return `OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR` immediately (no operation created)
- Upload timeouts are bounded by the Object Storage client's own botocore timeouts (Phase 1), not the operation budget
- Test 7 proved a 50ms upload survives a 10ms operation budget timeout

**Two-part deletion in finally (order matters):**
```python
finally:
    if operationId is not None:
        await self._bestEffortDeleteOperation(operationId)  # FIRST
    if objectUri is not None:
        await self._bestEffortDeleteObject(objectUri)       # SECOND
```
- Object delete runs AFTER operation delete
- Both are best-effort (never raises) to avoid invalidating successful transcripts
- Object delete triggers even on operation failure to prevent leaks

**Content vs URI branching in _buildSubmitBody:**
- Added `objectUri: Optional[str] = None` parameter
- When `objectUri` is not None: returns `{"uri": objectUri, "recognition_model": {...}}`
- When None: returns `{"content": <base64>, "recognition_model": {...}}`
- The `recognition_model` block is byte-for-byte identical in both paths - only the top-level input field differs

**Error paths:**
- `len(audio.data) >= maxInlineBytes` + `objectStorage is None` → `SOURCE_TOO_LARGE` (no upload attempted, no operation created)
- Upload raises Exception → `OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR` (no operation created, no cleanup needed in finally)
- Operation failure after successful upload → object IS deleted in finally (no leak)

title: AsyncMock spec gotcha: methods not automatically async
content:
Testing gotcha discovered in Phase 3 STT implementation (tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_speechkit.py):

**Problem:** When creating `AsyncMock(spec=["upload", "delete", "aclose"])`, the methods specified in the spec list do NOT become AsyncMock objects. They remain regular MagicMock objects, which are not awaitable. This causes `'MagicMock' object can't be awaited` errors.

**Example that fails:**
```python
mockOs = AsyncMock(spec=["upload", "delete", "aclose"])
# Later:
await mockOs.aclose()  # TypeError: 'MagicMock' object can't be awaited
```

**Fix:** Explicitly assign AsyncMock objects to each method:
```python
mockOs = AsyncMock(spec=["upload", "delete", "aclose"])
mockOs.upload = AsyncMock(return_value="https://storage.yandexcloud.net/test-bucket/stt/fake-uuid")
mockOs.delete = AsyncMock()
mockOs.aclose = AsyncMock()
```

**Context:** This pattern is used in `_providerWithOs` fixture which creates a provider with boto3 mocked for `YandexObjectStorage`, then replaces `provider._objectStorage` with the test mock. This allows testing without hitting real S3 while preserving real initialization logic.

title: _bestEffortDeleteObject: best-effort cleanup pattern
content:
New helper method added to lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py in Phase 3:

```python
async def _bestEffortDeleteObject(self, objectUri: str) -> None:
    """Delete the staged object from Object Storage (best-effort, never raises).

    Args:
        objectUri: The URI of the object to delete.

    Returns:
        None
    """
    try:
        await self._objectStorage.delete(objectUri)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        logger.warning("Yandex STT best-effort object delete failed for %s: %s", objectUri, exc)
```

**Pattern characteristics:**
- Mirrors the existing `_bestEffortDelete` operation pattern
- Uses `except Exception` (NOT `except BaseException`) so `asyncio.CancelledError` propagates
- Logs warning on failure, returns None (never raises)
- Used in `transcribe()` finally block AFTER operation delete
- Ensures cleanup doesn't invalidate successful transcripts

**Invariant:** Best-effort cleanup must never raise. The `except Exception` guard (with `# noqa: BLE001`) is load-bearing - catching `BaseException` would swallow `asyncio.CancelledError`, breaking the never-raise contract for cancellation.

title: Type casting for Dict[str, object] test assertions
content:
When accessing values from a `Dict[str, object]` in tests (e.g., request body captured from httpx.MockTransport), pyright's strict type checking requires casting before further subscripting.

**Problem:** `capturedBody` is typed as `Dict[str, object]`, so `capturedBody["recognition_model"]` returns `object`, not a `Dict[str, object]`. Pyright rejects: `"__getitem__" method not defined on type "object"`

**Fix:** Use `cast()` from `typing` to assert the expected type:
```python
from typing import cast

# Before:
recognitionModel = capturedBody["recognition_model"]
assert recognitionModel["recognition_model"] == {...}  # pyright error

# After:
recognitionModel = cast(Dict[str, object], capturedBody["recognition_model"])
assert recognitionModel["recognition_model"] == {...}  # OK
```

**Context:** Pattern used in testYandexObjectStorageSubmitBodyHasUriNoContent (test 2) and other tests that inspect the submit body structure. The httpx.MockTransport pattern captures the body as `Dict[str, object]` because the provider's HTTP layer doesn't know the exact schema.

**Alternative:** Could use `assert isinstance(..., dict)` instead, but `cast()` is more concise when the assertion is implicit in the test logic.

title: STT v1.1 upload timeout structural enforcement pattern
content:
STT v1.1 Object Storage path uses a **structural enforcement pattern** to guarantee the upload operation runs OUTSIDE the operation budget timeout:

**Code pattern in `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py`:**
- Upload lives in a SEPARATE try block (lines 383-387) from the budgeted operation (lines 391-418)
- `self._objectStorage.upload(audio.data)` at line 384 runs BEFORE `async with asyncio.timeout(self._operationBudgetSeconds)` opens at line 394
- Upload has no finally; on failure, it returns immediately and never enters the operation try/finally
- This makes it IMPOSSIBLE for a future edit to accidentally pull upload under the timeout without restructuring

**Verification:**
- Test 7 (`testUploadOutsideBudgetNotBoundedByOperationTimeout`, lines 1499-1554) proves this with a 5× timing margin: budget=0.01s, upload sleeps 0.05s. If upload were inside budget, the timeout would interrupt → `TimeoutError` → `PROVIDER_ERROR`. Test asserts `FINAL` status, confirming upload survives.

**Rationale:** Upload is a staging operation (writes to Object Storage). The operation budget only covers the SpeechKit submit→poll→fetch→delete lifecycle. Upload MUST NOT be bounded by the operation timeout, or large files would fail before reaching SpeechKit.

This pattern is preferred over conventional reliance on developer discipline because it structurally guarantees the invariant.

title: STT v1.1 variable lifetime discipline for finally cleanup
content:
STT v1.1 Object Storage path requires precise variable initialization timing for correct cleanup in the finally block of the operation try block.

**Pattern in `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py` (lines 374, 390, 391, 410-418):**

1. `objectUri: Optional[str] = None` initialized at line 374 (BEFORE upload try block)
2. Upload succeeds → `objectUri` assigned at line 384 (inside upload try)
3. `operationId: Optional[str] = None` initialized at line 390 (BEFORE operation try block)
4. Submit succeeds → `operationId` assigned at line 395 (inside operation try)
5. Finally block at lines 410-418:
   - `if operationId is not None:` → delete operation (skip if submit never returned)
   - `if objectUri is not None:` → delete object (skip if upload failed)

**Edge case handled correctly:**
- Upload succeeds, `_submit` raises BEFORE returning → `operationId` stays `None` (from line 390), `objectUri` is set (from line 384)
- Finally correctly skips op-delete (operationId None), runs object-delete (objectUri set)
- No object leak even when submit fails

**Why initialization before try blocks matters:**
- If variables were initialized inside their respective try blocks, they'd be out of scope in the finally
- The finally block accesses both `operationId` and `objectUri` regardless of where failure occurred
- This pattern enables partial-failure cleanup across all permutations

**Test coverage:**
- Test 6 (`testObjectDeletedAfterOperationFailure`, lines 1465-1497) verifies object cleanup when operation fails after upload
- Test 4 (`testUploadFailureNoObjectDelete`, lines 1394-1423) verifies no object delete when upload fails (never assigned)

title: STT v1.1 recognition_model identity guarantee
content:
STT v1.1 Object Storage routing guarantees byte-for-byte equivalence of the `recognition_model` block between inline (content) and Object Storage (uri) submission paths through a **single-construction, shared-reference pattern**.

**Implementation in `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py` `_buildSubmitBody` (lines 499-531):**

1. Build `recognitionModel` dict ONCE at lines 517-527:
   - `model`: from `self._model`
   - `audio_format.container_audio.container_audio_type`: from `audio.container.toYandexSpeechKit()`
   - `language_restriction`: from `self._language`
   - `text_normalization`: from `self._textNormalization`

2. Return statements at lines 528-531:
   - `if objectUri is not None:` → `{"uri": objectUri, "recognition_model": recognitionModel}`
   - `else:` → `{"content": encodedContent, "recognition_model": recognitionModel}`
   - **Same `recognitionModel` object reference in both paths**

**Why single construction matters:**
- Guarantees structural identity - both paths submit identical recognition config
- Prevents drift: a future edit to recognition_model logic must update one location
- Avoids subtle bugs where different code paths would submit different recognition parameters

**Verification:**
- Test 2 (`testObjectStorageSubmitBodyCorrect`, lines 1314-1362) extracts the recognition_model from the captured submit body and asserts all fields match inline path expectations
- Line 1351-1361: asserts `model`, `container_audio.container_audio_type`, `language_restriction`, `text_normalization` are correct

title: STT v1.1 upload failure path: no finally, no object delete
content:
STT v1.1 Object Storage upload failure correctly SKIPS object cleanup because the upload try/except has NO finally, and returning from it never enters the operation try/finally.

**Implementation in `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py` (lines 383-387, 391):**

```python
# Upload try/except - NO finally
try:
    objectUri = await self._objectStorage.upload(audio.data)
except Exception:
    logger.exception("Yandex STT Object Storage upload failed")
    return self._errorResult(STTErrorCode.OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR)  # exits transcribe here

# Operation try/finally with cleanup
try:
    async with asyncio.timeout(self._operationBudgetSeconds):
        operationId = await self._submit(audio, objectUri=objectUri)
        recognitionBytes = await self._pollAndFetch(operationId)
    ...
finally:
    # objectUri is None if upload failed (never assigned), so object delete is skipped
    if operationId is not None:
        await self._bestEffortDelete(operationId)
    if objectUri is not None:
        await self._bestEffortDeleteObject(objectUri)
```

**Why this is correct:**
- `objectUri` is initialized to `None` at line 374
- Upload raises → assignment at line 384 never happens → `objectUri` stays `None`
- `return` at line 387 exits before entering operation try at line 391
- Finally at line 410 never runs, so object delete is never attempted
- Even if finally DID run, the `if objectUri is not None:` guard at line 417 would skip it

**Test verification:**
- Test 4 (`testUploadFailureNoObjectDelete`, lines 1394-1423) mocks `upload` to raise RuntimeError
- Line 1422: `mockOs.delete.assert_not_called()` — confirms no object delete attempt
- Line 1420: `result.status == STTResultStatus.ERROR` with `error.code == "object-storage-error"`

**Alternative considered but rejected:** Adding a finally to the upload try block. Rejected because there's nothing to clean up on upload failure (no object was created, no operation exists). The error result is sufficient.

title: STT v1.1 test timing margin for timeout verification
content:
STT v1.1 Test 7 (`testUploadOutsideBudgetNotBoundedByOperationTimeout`, lines 1499-1554) uses a **5× timing margin** to genuinely prove that upload runs outside the operation budget timeout.

**Test setup:**
- `provider._operationBudgetSeconds = 0.01` (10 milliseconds budget)
- Mock `upload` sleeps `await asyncio.sleep(0.05)` (50 milliseconds upload duration)
- This creates a scenario where upload duration > budget

**Verification logic:**
- If upload were INSIDE the budget, the 10ms timeout would fire during the 50ms sleep → `asyncio.TimeoutError` → caught at line 400 → `PROVIDER_ERROR` result
- Test asserts `result.status is STTResultStatus.FINAL` (line 1553) — meaning submit succeeded, so upload survived
- Test asserts `callOrder == ["upload", "submit"]` (line 1554) — upload actually ran
- Test asserts `postCount == 1` (line 1555) — submit was reached (not just upload)

**Why the margin matters:**
- 5× (10ms vs 50ms) is a safe, non-flaky margin across CI environments
- Narrow margins (e.g., 10ms budget, 11ms sleep) risk timing-dependent failures on slow runners
- The test proves the invariant structurally, not by luck

**Implementation note:**
- Test mutates `provider._operationBudgetSeconds` post-construction at line 1544 (reaches into private attribute)
- Works because `_providerWithOs` doesn't accept arbitrary overrides
- Could be cleaner with `**overrides` param on the test helper, but acceptable for verification

**Location:** `tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_speechkit.py:1499-1554`

title: STT v1.1 upload cancellation leak vector accepted by design
content:
STT v1.1 Object Storage upload can leak objects if cancelled mid-flight during `put_object`. This is an **accepted, documented leak vector** handled by the bucket's lifecycle TTL, not a bug.

**Leak scenario:**
1. `await self._objectStorage.upload(audio.data)` at line 384 calls boto3 `put_object`
2. `put_object` is in-flight (request sent to S3, response pending)
3. `asyncio.CancelledError` propagates (e.g., caller cancels, timeout fires)
4. Upload never returns → `objectUri` assignment at line 384 never completes
5. `objectUri` stays `None` (from line 374 initialization)
6. Function exits with CancelledError, never reaching finally (line 410)
7. Object MAY exist server-side, but we don't know its URI

**Why this is acceptable (per design `docs/design/stt-v1.1.md` §3.3):**
- Yandex Object Storage bucket has a lifecycle TTL (operator-configured, typically days)
- Leaked objects are reclaimed by the TTL automatically
- Leak window: only if cancellation happens during upload (small time window)
- Alternative (pre-generate key, catch CancelledError, delete) requires key to be captured before put_object, which `YandexObjectStorage.upload` already does (line 117: `key = f"{self._prefix}{uuid.uuid4()}"`), but the key is a local var lost on CancelledError
- Catching CancelledError to delete is complex: would need to store key in instance, re-enter upload handler on cancellation

**Why CancelledError must propagate (load-bearing):**
- All `except` blocks use `except Exception`, not `except BaseException`
- CancelledError is a `BaseException` subclass (since Python 3.8)
- Propagation is required for correct asyncio cancellation semantics
- Never-raise contract applies to business exceptions, not cancellation

**Upload try/except at line 385 uses `except Exception`:**
- Catches all business exceptions (network errors, permission errors, etc.) → `OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR`
- Allows CancelledError to propagate (not caught)
- Correct behavior: cancellation should abort the STT operation and bubble up to the caller

title: STT v1.1 boundary condition untested: exact threshold equality
content:
STT v1.1 has an **untested boundary condition** at `len(audio.data) == maxInlineBytes`. The code uses `>=` for routing to Object Storage, but tests only exercise `>` (above threshold, not at threshold).

**Implementation at `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py:379`:**
```python
if len(audio.data) >= self._maxInlineBytes:
    # Route to Object Storage path
```

**Test coverage gap:**
- `_largeAudio()` test helper (line 1372) returns `b"\x00" * 41943041` which is `maxInlineBytes + 1` (41943040 + 1)
- Tests 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 use `_largeAudio()` → all test `>` case
- No test for exact equality `len(audio.data) == 41943040`
- If code were changed to `>`, the exact-equality case would regress to inline path silently

**Risk assessment:**
- Low probability of regression (developer would likely notice the boundary change in code review)
- But a one-line parametrized test would lock the `>=` semantics:
  ```python
  @pytest.mark.parametrize("audioSize,expectedPath", [
      (maxInlineBytes - 1, "inline"),  # Below threshold
      (maxInlineBytes, "object-storage"),  # AT threshold (currently untested)
      (maxInlineBytes + 1, "object-storage"),  # Above threshold
  ])
  ```

**Recommendation:** Add a parametrized test at the exact boundary to catch a future `>` regression. This is polish, not a blocker.

title: STT v1.1 test wasteful double 40 MiB allocation
content:
STT v1.1 Test 2 (`testObjectStorageSubmitBodyCorrect`, line 1356) wastefully allocates a SECOND 40 MiB buffer just for assertion purposes.

**Wasteful pattern:**
```python
# Line 1342: First allocation, used in transcribe
await provider.transcribe(_largeAudio())

# Line 1356: Second allocation, just to read .data for assertion
mockOs.upload.assert_awaited_once_with(_largeAudio().data)
```

**Issue:**
- `_largeAudio()` returns `b"\x00" * 41943041` (40 MiB + 1 byte)
- Called TWICE → ~80 MiB allocated for a single test
- The `.data` is identical (test helper returns fresh data each call)

**Fix:**
```python
audio = _largeAudio()  # Allocate once
await provider.transcribe(audio)
mockOs.upload.assert_awaited_once_with(audio.data)  # Reuse
```

**Impact:**
- Negligible wall-clock cost (allocation is fast)
- Memory churn: 80 MiB → freed after test
- Tests 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 all call `_largeAudio()` at least once
- Cumulative across STT tests: minor but avoidable

**Root cause:** Test helper doesn't support creating audio once and reusing. Could extend `_providerWithOs` to accept a pre-created `audio` param, or callers should store the result.

**Recommendation:** Store `_largeAudio()` in a variable before calling `transcribe` to reduce memory churn. Minor optimization nit.

title: STT Phase 4: transcribe() UnboundLocalError gotcha with flag-gated result
content:
When restructuring `YandexSpeechKitProvider.transcribe()` to record stats on every exit path (Phase 4 gate-4), using a type annotation `result: TranscriptionResult` without initialization causes UnboundLocalError on the success path. The problem: early ERROR paths assign `result`, but the success path only parses into `recognitionBytes` after the try/except, leaving `result` unbound when later code tries to access `result.status`.

**Solution**: Use a boolean flag (`operationFailed = True` in except branches, stays False on success) and parse recognition bytes only on success. After the finally cleanup, a single `_recordStats` call covers both paths:
- Success path: parse recognition bytes → assign `result` → record → return
- Error path: except already assigned `result` → finally cleanup → record → return

This yields exactly two `_recordStats` call sites: early ERROR returns (SOURCE_TOO_LARGE, OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR) and one post-finally call. The finally block runs cleanup BEFORE stats recording, ensuring stats failure cannot interfere with object deletion (matches design §7 sequence diagram).

**Key pattern**: When restructuring control flow where a variable must be bound on multiple paths, use a flag rather than trying to branch on unbound state. Type annotations alone don't create values.

Location: `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py:280-470`

title: STT Phase 4: test helper must be async when it calls await
content:
When creating a test helper function that performs async cleanup (e.g., `await provider.aclose()`), the helper itself MUST be marked `async def`. If defined as a sync function containing `await`, calling it as `await _providerWithStats()` in tests triggers an "await allowed only within async function" error.

**Example bug** (original Phase 4 code):
```python
async def _providerWithStats(*, handler: ..., statsStorage: ..., **overrides: ...) -> YandexSpeechKitProvider:
    provider = _provider(handler=handler, **overrides)
    try:
        yield provider
    finally:
        await provider.aclose()  # Error: function not async
```

**Fix**: Change function signature to `async def`:
```python
async def _providerWithStats(*, handler: ..., statsStorage: ..., **overrides: ...) -> YandexSpeechKitProvider:
    provider = _provider(handler=handler, **overrides)
    try:
        yield provider
    finally:
        await provider.aclose()  # Works now
```

This pattern appears in test fixtures that manage provider lifecycle. The error is caught by linters but can slip in during refactoring.

Location: `tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_speechkit.py:1639-1651`

title: STT Phase 4: StatsStorage injection pattern mirrors lib/ai
content:
StatsStorage injection into STT providers mirrors the lib/ai pattern (see `lib/ai/abstract.py:850-887`):

**Constructor pattern** (Phase 4 gate-4):
```python
def __init__(self, ..., statsStorage: Optional[StatsStorage] = None) -> None:
    ...
    self.statsStorage: StatsStorage = (
        statsStorage if statsStorage is not None else NullStatsStorage()
    )
```

**Key points**:
- `statsStorage` is optional with `None` default
- Store as `self.statsStorage`, defaulting to `NullStatsStorage()` when not supplied
- Type annotation is concrete `StatsStorage`, not `Optional[StatsStorage]` (the default ensures it's never None at runtime)
- Import from `lib.stats.stats_storage`: `StatsStorage` (abstract), `NullStatsStorage` (no-op implementation)

**Usage in _recordStats**:
```python
async def _recordStats(
    self, *, consumerId: Optional[str], audio: ExtractedAudio,
    result: TranscriptionResult, elapsedSeconds: float
) -> None:
    try:
        await self.statsStorage.record(
            stats={...},
            consumerId=consumerId,
            labels={...}
        )
    except Exception:
        # Best-effort: log + swallow (never raises, except CancelledError)
        pass
```

**Why this pattern**: Enables global stats aggregation when no stats storage is wired (Phase 5 will inject real `DatabaseStatsStorage`), while ensuring the provider never crashes on stats recording failures. The lib/stt firewall is respected: only lib.* imports (no internal.*).

Location: `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py:1-140`, `lib/ai/abstract.py:850-887`

title: STT Phase 4: recording fake StatsStorage for testing
content:
When testing stats recording behavior, use a lightweight recording fake instead of the real `DatabaseStatsStorage`. This isolates the provider's stats recording logic from database concerns and makes tests deterministic.

**Recording fake implementation**:
```python
class _RecordingStatsStorage(StatsStorage):
    """Fake StatsStorage that records calls for assertion."""
    
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.records: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    
    async def record(
        self, *, stats: Dict[str, int], consumerId: Optional[str],
        labels: Dict[str, str]
    ) -> None:
        self.records.append({
            "stats": stats,
            "consumerId": consumerId,
            "labels": labels
        })
```

**Test coverage points** (Phase 4 gate-4):
1. **Success records stats**: Verify FINAL result → `record()` called with `status_FINAL`, `is_error=0`, correct `audio_duration_ms`, `elapsed_time >= 0`, labels include `generationType=stt`, `provider=yandex-speechkit`, `model=<provider's model>`, `status=FINAL`
2. **ERROR records stats**: Verify OS-disabled+over-threshold (SOURCE_TOO_LARGE) or upload-failure (OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR) → `record()` called with `is_error=1`, `status_ERROR`
3. **NullStatsStorage no-op**: Provider without `statsStorage` still succeeds, no crash
4. **Best-effort never raises**: Fake's `record()` raises → transcription still returns correct result (exception swallowed + logged)
5. **consumerId threading**: `stt(data, consumerId="chat-123")` → fake receives `consumerId="chat-123"`; `stt(data)` → receives `consumerId=None`
6. **Cleanup coexistence**: On OS path, both object delete (mockOs.delete awaited) AND stats recording happen (assert record called)

**Why this approach**: `DatabaseStatsStorage` requires DB setup, creates external dependencies, and makes tests slower. The fake is in-memory, allows precise assertions on what was recorded, and proves the contract without hitting the real storage layer.

Location: `tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_speechkit.py:1649-1688`

title: STT Phase 4: boundary test locks >= maxInlineBytes semantics
content:
Phase 3b introduced Object Storage routing based on audio size: `len(audio.data) >= maxInlineBytes` routes to OS, inline-only for smaller clips. Phase 4 added a boundary ride-along test to lock this semantics against future regression.

**Boundary test pattern**:
```python
async def testObjectStorageRoutingExactBoundary(...) -> None:
    provider = YandexSpeechKitProvider(
        ..., maxInlineBytes=8,  # Tiny threshold for testing
        objectStorage=mock_os, ...
    )
    audio = ExtractedAudio(
        data=b"x" * 8,  # Exactly maxInlineBytes
        durationMs=1000, ...
    )
    result = await provider.transcribe(audio)
    assert mock_os.upload.called  # Proves >= semantics
```

**Why this matters**:
- Without the test, a future refactor could change `>=` to `>` and break the documented contract
- The test constructs audio exactly at the boundary, forcing the decision logic through that path
- Existing `_largeAudio` test uses `maxInlineBytes+1` (above boundary), so this adds the edge case

**Related**: This is the STT counterpart to similar boundary tests elsewhere in the codebase that protect against off-by-one errors in routing/selection logic.

Location: `tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_speechkit.py:1812-1840`

title: STT Phase 4: consumerId threading is backward compatible
content:
The `consumerId` threading through `stt()` → `transcribe()` is a **backward-compatible contract evolution**:

**Signatures** (Phase 4 gate-4):
```python
# Abstract base
class AbstractSTTProvider(ABC):
    def stt(self, data: bytes, *, consumerId: Optional[str] = None) -> TranscriptionResult:
        ...
        return await self.transcribe(audio, *, consumerId=consumerId)

    @abstractmethod
    def transcribe(self, audio: ExtractedAudio, *, consumerId: Optional[str] = None) -> TranscriptionResult:
        ...
```

**Backward compatibility guarantees**:
- `consumerId` is **keyword-only** with `None` default
- Existing callers like `STTService.transcribeMedia` that call `provider.stt(data)` continue to work unchanged
- `consumerId=None` means "global rollup" (aggregated across all consumers)
- Phase 5 will wire `consumerId=str(chatId)` at the service layer, but the provider already accepts it

**Why keyword-only**: Forces callers to be explicit about the threading, prevents accidental positional passing. The `*` in the signature separates positional from keyword-only args.

**Impact on tests**: Existing golden tests and unit tests that call `stt(data)` without `consumerId` work unchanged. Only stub implementations needed signature updates to accept the new keyword-only param (e.g., `_StubProvider.transcribe` in `tests/lib/stt/test_abstract.py`).

Location: `lib/stt/abstract.py:104-120`, `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py:140`

title: STT record-exactly-once invariant implementation pattern
content:
The STT v1.1 statistics recording uses a **record-exactly-once invariant** in `YandexSpeechKitProvider.transcribe()` that every exit path must record stats exactly once (no zero-record, no double-record). This is implemented via a flag-gated single-exit refactor:

**Three record sites**:
1. **SOURCE_TOO_LARGE early return** (`yandex_speechkit.py:395-405`): Records inline, returns BEFORE entering the `try:/finally` block (lines 424-454). No cleanup conflict because no object upload attempted.
2. **OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR early return** (`yandex_speechkit.py:406-417`): Records inline, returns BEFORE `try:/finally`. Upload failed so `objectUri` stays `None` - no cleanup needed.
3. **Post-finally single record** (`yandex_speechkit.py:472`): Runs AFTER the `finally` cleanup (operation delete + object delete). Covers all other paths:
   - Success → FINAL/NO_SPEECH (operationFailed=False, parse succeeds)
   - Operation failure via _ProviderFailure (operationFailed=True, skips parse)
   - TimeoutError (operationFailed=True, skips parse)
   - Unexpected Exception (operationFailed=True, skips parse)
   - Parse-failure after operation success (operationFailed=False, parse sets ERROR)

**The `operationFailed` flag** (initialized False, set True only in the three operation-failure `except` branches) gates the parse block (`if not operationFailed:` at line 463) and ensures both success and operation-failure paths fall through to the single post-finally record without double-recording.

**Elapsed_time semantics**: Captured at `transcribe()` entry (`startTime = time.monotonic()` at line 389, before the staging `if`), computed at record point. For OS path this includes upload duration; for inline path it doesn't. Cleanup time (object/operation delete) is included because the post-finally record runs after the `finally` block - this is by-design per §5.3.

**Best-effort contract**: `_recordStats` (lines 852-898) wraps `await self._statsStorage.record(...)` in `try/except Exception` (not `BaseException`) so `CancelledError` propagates but other exceptions are swallowed with log. A raising `record()` cannot make `transcribe()` raise - the transcription result is still returned.

**Early-return vs cleanup ordering**: The two early-return paths return BEFORE entering the `try:` block, so they never enter the `finally` cleanup. This is correct: path (a) created no object and no operation; path (b) left `objectUri=None` because upload failed.

See design doc `docs/design/stt-v1.1.md` §5.2 (record-exactly-once warning), §5.3 (stats dict/labels), §7 (sequence diagram showing record after finally).

title: Backward compatibility: adding keyword-only parameters with defaults
content:
Adding a new keyword-only parameter with a default value to an existing method signature is backward-compatible and doesn't break existing callers.

**Pattern**: Change from `async def method(self, param)` to `async def method(self, param, *, newParam: Optional[Type] = None)`

**Why it works**:
- Keyword-only (`*,`) forces named argument passing, avoiding positional confusion
- Default value (`= None`) means existing callers can omit the argument
- No signature collision with subclasses - subclasses inheriting the method still work
- If a subclass overrides the method, it must either match the new signature OR be called in a way that never passes the new parameter (e.g., by also overriding the forwarding method)

**Example from STT Phase 4**:
- `AbstractSTTProvider.transcribe()` changed from `transcribe(self, audio)` to `transcribe(self, audio, *, consumerId: Optional[str] = None)`
- `AbstractSTTProvider.stt()` forwards with `consumerId=consumerId`
- Existing callers like `STTService.stt(data)` (no consumerId) still work because the default is used

**Gotcha**: Subclasses that override the method must be updated to match the new signature. In STT Phase 4, `tests/lib/stt/test_abstract.py` stubs were updated, but `tests/services/stt/test_transcribe.py:79` `FakeProvider.transcribe` was NOT updated - however, it's shielded because that class also overrides `stt()` which doesn't forward `consumerId`. This is a latent signature drift masked by `# type: ignore[override]`.

**Python typing**: This is Liskov-compatible as long as the subclass doesn't reject the keyword in its type signature.

title: STT stats dict and labels specification
content:
STT v1.1 statistics recording uses this exact stats dict and labels (mirroring lib/ai with STT-appropriate substitutions):

**Stats dict keys** (`yandex_speechkit.py:880-887`):
- `generation_stt: 1` - generation type identifier
- `request_count: 1` - transcription attempt counter
- `audio_duration_ms: audio.durationMs` - input audio length (STT analog of LLM token dimensions)
- `elapsed_time: elapsedSeconds` - wall-clock from transcribe() entry to record point
- `is_error: 1 if result.status is STTResultStatus.ERROR else 0` - error flag
- `f"status_{result.status.name}": 1` - per-status bucket (e.g., status_FINAL, status_NO_SPEECH, status_ERROR)

**Labels** (`yandex_speechkit.py:889-894`):
- `provider: "yandex-speechkit"` - provider identifier
- `generationType: "stt"` - generation type
- `status: result.status.name` - STTResultStatus enum name
- `model: self._model` - model name string

**Shape parity with lib/ai**:
- lib/ai uses `generation_{type}: 1`, `request_count: 1`, `is_error`, `status_{status.name}: 1`, `elapsed_time`
- lib/ai token dimensions (input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens) are replaced by `audio_duration_ms` for STT
- lib/ai labels include `modelName` and `modelId`; STT uses single `model` label

**Recording contract**: Called after result construction, best-effort (never raises via `except Exception`), via `StatsStorage.record(stats, consumerId, labels)`. StatsStorage defaults to `NullStatsStorage` when not injected.

See implementation: `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py` lines 852-898 (`_recordStats`).

title: STT Phase 4 test coverage gaps for stats recording
content:
After STT Phase 4 (gate-4 statistics recording) Gate-1 review, these test coverage gaps were identified as recommendations (non-blocking):

1. **NO_SPEECH stats not asserted at stats layer** (`tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_speechkit.py`):
   - Phase-1 test `testEmptyRecognitionBodyYieldsNoSpeech` (line 409) covers NO_SPEECH outcome
   - Phase-4 stats tests assert `status_FINAL` (Test 1, line 1700) and `status_ERROR` (Test 2, line 1739)
   - No test drives a NO_SPEECH outcome and asserts `stats.records[0]["stats"]["status_NO_SPEECH"] == 1` and `is_error == 0`
   - The generic construction `f"status_{result.status.name}": 1` covers NO_SPEECH, but it's untested at the stats layer

2. **Operation-failure-via-finally stats not asserted**:
   - Test 2 (ERROR records) drives SOURCE_TOO_LARGE early-return path (inline record site)
   - Test 6 (stats+cleanup) drives post-finally record on SUCCESS path
   - No Phase-4 stats test drives the post-finally record on an OPERATION FAILURE (paths d1/d2/d3 - PROVIDER_ERROR from operation error/timeout/maxPolls)
   - Existing operation-failure tests (`testOperationErrorYieldsProviderError` at line 352, timeout tests, maxPolls tests) verify the ERROR outcome but not the stats record
   - The post-finally record call is identical regardless of which branch set `result`, so low-risk, but a test would lock the `operationFailed` routing

3. **Signature drift in test stub** (`tests/services/stt/test_transcribe.py:79`):
   - `FakeProvider.transcribe` has signature `transcribe(self, audio)` not matching the abstract `transcribe(self, audio, *, consumerId=None)`
   - Masked by `# type: ignore[override]` and shielded because `FakeProvider` also overrides `stt()` which doesn't forward `consumerId`
   - Runtime safe (STTService calls `provider.stt(data)` which hits the `stt` override), but latent if future code calls `transcribe()` directly or removes the `stt` override
   - This file is outside declared Phase 4 scope but is a direct consequence of the abstract signature change

**Note**: These are test-coverage gaps, not correctness bugs. The record-exactly-once invariant holds by construction and was verified by trace during Gate-1 review.
